# 9. Validation with Zod

TypeScript types alone are not enough because AI and workers produce runtime data.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.schema.ts
```

Use Zod or a similar runtime validator.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import {
  AI_ASSET_KINDS,
  AI_CAPABILITIES,
  AI_EDITABLE_LEVELS,
  AI_LAYER_SOURCES,
  AI_LAYER_TYPES,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "./ai-layer.types";

const ConfidenceSchema = z.object({
  overall: z.number().min(0).max(1),

  classification: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  geometry: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  bbox: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  polygon: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  mask: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  alphaMatte: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  ocr: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  font: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  color: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  vectorization: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  zIndex: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  backgroundRepair: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  visualFidelity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
});

const BBoxSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
  width: z.number().nonnegative(),
  height: z.number().nonnegative(),
});

const PointSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
});

const GeminiBox1000Schema = z
  .tuple([z.number(), z.number(), z.number(), z.number()])
  .refine(
    ([yMin, xMin, yMax, xMax]) =>
      yMin >= 0 &&
      xMin >= 0 &&
      yMax <= 1000 &&
      xMax <= 1000 &&
      yMax >= yMin &&
      xMax >= xMin,
    "Invalid Gemini 0–1000 bbox"
  );

const TransformSchema = z.object({
  left: z.number(),
  top: z.number(),
  width: z.number().nonnegative(),
  height: z.number().nonnegative(),
  scaleX: z.number(),
  scaleY: z.number(),
  angle: z.number(),
  opacity: z.number().min(0).max(1),

  flipX: z.boolean().optional(),
  flipY: z.boolean().optional(),
  skewX: z.number().optional(),
  skewY: z.number().optional(),

  matrix: z
    .tuple([
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
    ])
    .optional(),

  originX: z.enum(["left", "center", "right"]),
  originY: z.enum(["top", "center", "bottom"]),
});

const GeometrySchema = z.object({
  coordinateSpace: z.literal("canvas_px"),

  bbox: BBoxSchema,

  renderBounds: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  polygon: z.array(PointSchema).optional(),

  originalBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  normalizedBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  geminiBox1000: GeminiBox1000Schema.optional(),

  transform: TransformSchema,
});

const AssetRefSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),

  kind: z.enum(AI_ASSET_KINDS),

  storagePath: z.string().optional(),

  url: z.string().url().optional(),

  urlExpiresAt: z.number().optional(),

  mimeType: z.string().optional(),

  width: z.number().positive().optional(),
  height: z.number().positive().optional(),

  sizeBytes: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  checksum: z
    .object({
      algorithm: z.enum(["sha256", "md5"]),
      value: z.string().min(1),
    })
    .optional(),

  metadata: z
    .object({
      contentType: z.string().optional(),
      cacheControl: z.string().optional(),
      createdBy: z.enum(AI_LAYER_SOURCES).optional(),
      layerId: z.string().optional(),
      jobId: z.string().optional(),
    })
    .optional(),
});

const FallbackSchema = z.object({
  strategy: z.enum([
    "none",
    "locked_reference",
    "original_crop",
    "raster_layer",
    "previous_version",
    "manual_user",
  ]),

  assetId: z.string().optional(),

  bbox: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  reason: z.string().optional(),

  visibleByDefault: z.boolean().optional(),
});

const TextPayloadSchema = z.object({
  value: z.string(),

  originalValue: z.string().optional(),

  language: z.string().optional(),

  fontFamily: z.string().optional(),
  fontSize: z.number().positive().optional(),
  fontWeight: z.union([z.string(), z.number()]).optional(),
  fontStyle: z.enum(["normal", "italic"]).optional(),

  lineHeight: z.number().positive().optional(),
  charSpacing: z.number().optional(),

  fill: z.string().optional(),
  stroke: z.string().optional(),
  strokeWidth: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  textAlign: z.enum(["left", "center", "right", "justify"]).optional(),

  source: z.enum(["ocr", "manual_user", "system"]),
});

const VectorPayloadSchema = z.object({
  primitive: z.enum([
    "rect",
    "rounded_rect",
    "circle",
    "ellipse",
    "line",
    "polygon",
    "path",
  ]),

  pathData: z.string().optional(),

  points: z.array(PointSchema).optional(),

  fill: z.string().optional(),
  stroke: z.string().optional(),
  strokeWidth: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  radius: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  opacity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
});

const RasterPayloadSchema = z.object({
  rgbaAssetId: z.string().min(1),

  maskAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  originalCropAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  crop: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  alphaMode: z.enum(["binary_mask", "soft_alpha", "matte"]).optional(),

  edgeQuality: z.enum(["high", "medium", "low", "unknown"]).optional(),
});

const GroupPayloadSchema = z.object({
  childLayerIds: z.array(z.string()),

  lockedChildren: z.boolean().optional(),

  semanticRole: z
    .enum([
      "button",
      "badge",
      "price_block",
      "menu_item",
      "logo_lockup",
      "social_handle",
      "header",
      "footer",
      "unknown",
    ])
    .optional(),
});

const LayerDecisionSchema = z.object({
  selectedFromObservationIds: z.array(z.string()),

  rejectedObservationIds: z.array(z.string()).optional(),

  strategy: z.enum([
    "use_editable_text",
    "use_vector",
    "use_masked_raster",
    "use_clean_background",
    "use_raster_fallback",
    "use_group",
    "use_locked_reference",
  ]),

  reasonCodes: z.array(z.string()),

  decidedBy: z.enum(["system", "manual_user"]),

  decidedAt: z.number(),
});

export const AiReconstructedLayerSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().min(1),

    jobId: z.string().min(1),
    designId: z.string().min(1),

    schemaVersion: z.literal(AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION),

    type: z.enum(AI_LAYER_TYPES),

    editableLevel: z.enum(AI_EDITABLE_LEVELS),

    name: z.string().min(1),

    visible: z.boolean(),
    locked: z.boolean(),

    zIndex: z.number().int(),

    geometry: GeometrySchema,

    confidence: ConfidenceSchema,

    capabilities: z.array(z.enum(AI_CAPABILITIES)),

    assetIds: z.array(z.string()),

    fallback: FallbackSchema,

    source: z.object({
      primary: z.enum(AI_LAYER_SOURCES),
      contributors: z.array(z.enum(AI_LAYER_SOURCES)),
    }),

    decision: LayerDecisionSchema,

    text: TextPayloadSchema.optional(),

    vector: VectorPayloadSchema.optional(),

    raster: RasterPayloadSchema.optional(),

    group: GroupPayloadSchema.optional(),

    metadata: z.object({
      createdAt: z.number(),
      updatedAt: z.number().optional(),

      modelVersion: z.string().optional(),
      pipelineVersion: z.string(),

      originalImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),
      normalizedImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),

      warnings: z.array(z.string()).optional(),

      userCorrected: z.boolean().optional(),

      tags: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    }),
  })
  .superRefine((layer, ctx) => {
    if (layer.editableLevel === "text_editable" && !layer.text) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: "text_editable layer must include text payload",
        path: ["text"],
      });
    }

    if (layer.editableLevel === "vector_editable" && !layer.vector) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: "vector_editable layer must include vector payload",
        path: ["vector"],
      });
    }

    if (
      ["raster_masked", "raster_clean_background", "raster_fallback"].includes(
        layer.editableLevel
      ) &&
      !layer.raster
    ) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: "raster layer must include raster payload",
        path: ["raster"],
      });
    }

    if (layer.editableLevel === "group_editable" && !layer.group) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: "group_editable layer must include group payload",
        path: ["group"],
      });
    }

    if (
      layer.type !== "locked_reference" &&
      layer.fallback.strategy === "none" &&
      layer.confidence.overall < 0.98
    ) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: "AI layer below near-perfect confidence must include fallback",
        path: ["fallback"],
      });
    }
  });

export type AiReconstructedLayerValidated = z.infer<
  typeof AiReconstructedLayerSchema
>;
```

---

# 10. Gemini model-output schema

This is **not** the full internal schema.

This is only what Gemini is allowed to return for layout analysis.

```txt
src/lib/ai-layers/model-output.schema.ts
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

export const GeminiLayoutElementSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),

  type: z.enum([
    "background",
    "photo_subject",
    "person",
    "product",
    "logo",
    "icon",
    "text",
    "shape",
    "decoration",
    "image_block",
    "shadow",
    "overlay",
    "unknown",
  ]),

  name: z.string(),

  /**
   * Gemini bounding box format:
   * [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]
   * normalized to 0–1000.
   */
  box_2d: z.tuple([z.number(), z.number(), z.number(), z.number()]),

  confidence: z.number().min(0).max(1),

  zIndexGuess: z.number().int(),

  description: z.string().optional(),

  editableHint: z.enum([
    "likely_text",
    "likely_vector",
    "likely_masked_raster",
    "likely_background",
    "unknown",
  ]),
});

export const GeminiLayoutResponseSchema = z.object({
  designType: z.string(),

  canvasSummary: z.string(),

  elements: z.array(GeminiLayoutElementSchema).max(40),

  warnings: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

export type GeminiLayoutResponse = z.infer<typeof GeminiLayoutResponseSchema>;
```

Then normalize this into internal observations:

```ts
import type {
  AiLayoutObservation,
  BBox,
  GeminiBox1000,
} from "./ai-layer.types";
import { geminiBox1000ToBBox } from "./geometry";
import type { GeminiLayoutResponse } from "./model-output.schema";

export function geminiLayoutToObservations(params: {
  response: GeminiLayoutResponse;
  jobId: string;
  imageWidth: number;
  imageHeight: number;
  modelName: string;
  promptVersion: string;
  promptHash: string;
  createdAt: number;
}): AiLayoutObservation[] {
  return params.response.elements.map((element): AiLayoutObservation => {
    const box = element.box_2d as GeminiBox1000;

    const bbox: BBox = geminiBox1000ToBBox(
      box,
      params.imageWidth,
      params.imageHeight
    );

    return {
      id: `obs_layout_${element.id}`,
      jobId: params.jobId,
      kind: "layout",
      source: "gemini_layout",
      createdAt: params.createdAt,

      model: {
        provider: "google_ai",
        modelName: params.modelName,
        promptVersion: params.promptVersion,
        promptHash: params.promptHash,
      },

      label: element.name,
      layerTypeGuess: element.type,
      bbox,
      geminiBox1000: box,
      zIndexGuess: element.zIndexGuess,
      description: element.description,

      confidence: {
        overall: element.confidence,
        classification: element.confidence,
        bbox: element.confidence,
      },

      warnings: params.response.warnings,
    };
  });
}
```

This preserves the source format and gives you absolute pixel coordinates.

---

# 11. OCR observation schema

Google Cloud Vision OCR supports text extraction from images and returns extracted text plus bounding boxes for words in `TEXT_DETECTION`; `DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION` returns a page/block/paragraph/word/symbol hierarchy for dense text. citeturn657573view0turn657573view1

Your OCR output should become observations, not layers.

```ts
export type NormalizedOcrWord = {
  id: string;
  text: string;
  bbox: BBox;
  polygon?: Polygon;

  confidence?: number;

  language?: string;

  blockIndex?: number;
  paragraphIndex?: number;
  wordIndex?: number;
};

export function ocrWordToObservation(params: {
  word: NormalizedOcrWord;
  jobId: string;
  createdAt: number;
  modelName: string;
}): AiOcrObservation {
  return {
    id: `obs_ocr_${params.word.id}`,
    jobId: params.jobId,
    kind: "ocr",
    source: "google_vision_ocr",
    createdAt: params.createdAt,

    model: {
      provider: "google_cloud_vision",
      modelName: params.modelName,
    },

    text: params.word.text,
    bbox: params.word.bbox,
    polygon: params.word.polygon,

    language: params.word.language,

    blockIndex: params.word.blockIndex,
    lineIndex: params.word.paragraphIndex,

    confidence: {
      overall: params.word.confidence ?? 0,
      ocr: params.word.confidence,
      bbox: params.word.confidence,
    },
  };
}
```

Later, your resolver groups words into text lines/text boxes.

Do not make each OCR word a Fabric text object.

# 12. Layer capability presets

Create:

```txt
src/lib/ai-layers/capabilities.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerCapability,
} from "./ai-layer.types";

export function capabilitiesForEditableLevel(
  editableLevel: AiEditableLevel
): AiLayerCapability[] {
  switch (editableLevel) {
    case "locked_reference":
      return ["hide", "restore_from_original"];

    case "text_editable":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "delete",
        "reorder",
        "edit_text",
        "edit_font",
        "recolor",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "vector_editable":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "delete",
        "reorder",
        "recolor",
        "edit_vector",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "raster_masked":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "delete",
        "reorder",
        "replace_asset",
        "edit_mask",
        "regenerate",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "raster_clean_background":
      return [
        "select",
        "hide",
        "replace_asset",
        "regenerate",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "raster_fallback":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "delete",
        "reorder",
        "replace_asset",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "group_editable":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "delete",
        "reorder",
        "ungroup",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "unknown_confidence":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "delete",
        "reorder",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    default:
      return ["select", "hide"];
  }
}
```

This keeps UX deterministic.

The UI does not need to infer behavior from layer type.

# 13. Layer invariants

Create:

```txt
src/lib/ai-layers/invariants.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  AiReconstructedLayer,
  AiReconstructionDocument,
} from "./ai-layer.types";

export function assertLayerInvariants(layer: AiReconstructedLayer): void {
  if (!layer.id) {
    throw new Error("Layer must have id");
  }

  if (!layer.name) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} must have name`);
  }

  if (layer.confidence.overall < 0 || layer.confidence.overall > 1) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} confidence.overall must be 0–1`);
  }

  if (layer.geometry.coordinateSpace !== "canvas_px") {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} must use canvas_px geometry`);
  }

  if (layer.geometry.bbox.width < 0 || layer.geometry.bbox.height < 0) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} bbox cannot have negative dimensions`);
  }

  if (layer.editableLevel === "text_editable" && !layer.text) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} is text_editable but has no text`);
  }

  if (layer.editableLevel === "vector_editable" && !layer.vector) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} is vector_editable but has no vector`);
  }

  if (
    ["raster_masked", "raster_clean_background", "raster_fallback"].includes(
      layer.editableLevel
    ) &&
    !layer.raster
  ) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} is raster but has no raster payload`);
  }

  if (
    layer.type !== "locked_reference" &&
    layer.confidence.overall < 0.98 &&
    layer.fallback.strategy === "none"
  ) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} needs fallback`);
  }
}

export function assertReconstructionDocumentInvariants(
  doc: AiReconstructionDocument
): void {
  const layerIds = new Set<string>();

  for (const layer of doc.layers) {
    assertLayerInvariants(layer);

    if (layerIds.has(layer.id)) {
      throw new Error(`Duplicate layer id: ${layer.id}`);
    }

    layerIds.add(layer.id);

    for (const assetId of layer.assetIds) {
      if (!doc.assets[assetId]) {
        throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} references missing asset ${assetId}`);
      }
    }

    if (
      layer.fallback.assetId &&
      !doc.assets[layer.fallback.assetId]
    ) {
      throw new Error(
        `Layer ${layer.id} references missing fallback asset ${layer.fallback.assetId}`
      );
    }
  }

  const zIndexes = doc.layers.map((layer) => layer.zIndex);
  const uniqueZIndexes = new Set(zIndexes);

  if (zIndexes.length !== uniqueZIndexes.size) {
    throw new Error("zIndex values must be unique in reconstruction document");
  }
}
```

This prevents garbage AI state from entering your editor.

# 15. Fabric metadata reservation

Even though Fabric manifest generation is the next point, reserve these fields now.

```ts
export type AiFabricMetadata = {
  aiLayerId: string;
  aiLayerType: AiLayerType;
  aiEditableLevel: AiEditableLevel;
  aiConfidence: AiConfidence;
  aiSource: AiLayerSource;
  aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
  aiSchemaVersion: typeof AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION;
};
```

When you convert internal layers into Fabric objects later, these fields must be attached to Fabric objects and included in serialization.

Prepare this file now:

```txt
src/lib/fabric/register-ai-custom-properties.ts
```

```ts
import { FabricObject } from "fabric";
import type {
  AiConfidence,
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerSource,
  AiLayerType,
} from "@/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.types";

declare module "fabric" {
  interface FabricObject {
    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiLayerSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;
  }

  interface SerializedObjectProps {
    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiLayerSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;
  }
}

export function registerAiFabricCustomProperties() {
  FabricObject.customProperties = [
    "aiLayerId",
    "aiLayerType",
    "aiEditableLevel",
    "aiConfidence",
    "aiSource",
    "aiFallbackAssetId",
    "aiSchemaVersion",
  ];
}
```

Call it once before loading/saving AI-generated Fabric documents.

# 16. What must be true after this step

After Step 1.1, your codebase should have:

```txt
src/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.types.ts
src/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.schema.ts
src/lib/ai-layers/model-output.schema.ts
src/lib/ai-layers/geometry.ts
src/lib/ai-layers/capabilities.ts
src/lib/ai-layers/invariants.ts
src/lib/fabric/register-ai-custom-properties.ts
```

And this must be true:

```txt
AI models do not output Fabric JSON directly.
AI models output observations.
Your system validates observations.
Your resolver creates AiReconstructionDocument.
Fabric conversion happens after this.
Every layer has type, editability, confidence, provenance, geometry, fallback.
Every asset is referenced, not embedded.
Every coordinate is normalized into canvas pixels.
```

---

# The hard rule for this step

Do not simplify this into:

```ts
{
  type: "image",
  src: "...",
  left: 100,
  top: 100
}
```

That is not a reconstruction system. That is just a Fabric import.

The correct abstraction is:

```txt
Layer = semantic decision + asset + geometry + confidence + fallback + provenance + capabilities
```

Once this schema is implemented, the next point is **Step 1.2 — define the Fabric manifest format generated from this internal schema**.

The next locked point is the Fabric manifest contract: a wrapper around Fabric’s own JSON, generated from your internal reconstruction document, with explicit canvas metadata.

# Step 1.2 — Define the Fabric manifest format

The next locked point is the **Fabric manifest contract**.

Your internal reconstruction document from Step 1.1 is the AI source of truth. The Fabric manifest is the **editor-loadable projection** of that document.

The hard separation is:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
= semantic reconstruction source of truth

AiFabricManifest
= editor import package

manifest.fabricJson
= the only object passed into canvas.loadFromJSON()
```

Do **not** call:

```ts
canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest)
```

Call:

```ts
canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest.fabricJson)
```

Fabric’s own docs say `loadFromJSON` expects JSON conforming to `fabric.Canvas#toJSON`, and that the call is async and should avoid race conditions by aborting older loading tasks. Fabric also documents that `toJSON` / `toObject` are the backbone of Fabric serialization, and `toObject` accepts extra properties to include in output. citeturn871230view0turn108725view0

---

# The core decision

The manifest must be a **wrapper around Fabric JSON**, not a modified Fabric JSON.

Correct:

```ts
{
  schemaVersion: "ai-fabric-manifest.v1",
  jobId: "...",
  designId: "...",
  canvas: {...},
  assets: {...},
  layerIndex: {...},
  fabricJson: {
    version: "...",
    objects: [...]
  }
}
```

Wrong:

```ts
{
  version: "...",
  objects: [...],
  jobId: "...",
  assets: {...},
  reconstruction: {...}
}
```

Why: Fabric may ignore, mutate, or fail to preserve top-level app metadata. Keep app metadata outside `fabricJson`. Only Fabric-renderable data goes inside `fabricJson`.

---

# Fabric-specific constraints to respect

Fabric object types are for Fabric deserialization, not your business logic. Current Fabric docs show class `type` values such as `Rect`, and explicitly warn not to build new app logic around the instance `type` accessor because it is legacy/deprecated behavior. Your editor logic should use `aiLayerType` and `aiEditableLevel`, not Fabric’s `type`. citeturn757913view1

Fabric custom properties must be registered if you want them to survive serialization. Fabric’s docs show the correct pattern: TypeScript module augmentation plus `FabricObject.customProperties = [...]`. They also warn that Fabric objects should not become your application data store, so only keep minimal AI identity metadata on Fabric objects. citeturn757913view0

For images, Fabric can initialize image objects from URL strings, so your manifest must resolve `storagePath` into browser-loadable URLs before import. Do not put `gs://...` paths in Fabric `src`. citeturn871230view1

For browser export, your asset URLs must be CORS-safe. Cross-origin images can taint the canvas, causing `toDataURL`, `toBlob`, and `getImageData` to throw `SecurityError`. GCS supports CORS configuration at the bucket level, so this belongs in the manifest loading contract from day one. citeturn706715search0turn706715search1turn706715search19

# 1. Fabric manifest types

```ts
// src/lib/ai-layers/fabric-manifest.types.ts

import type {
  AiAssetRef,
  AiConfidence,
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerSource,
  AiLayerType,
  AiReconstructionDocument,
  BBox,
} from "./ai-layer.types";

export const AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION =
  "ai-fabric-manifest.v1" as const;

export type FabricObjectJson = {
  type: string;

  version?: string;

  id?: string;
  name?: string;

  left?: number;
  top?: number;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  scaleX?: number;
  scaleY?: number;

  angle?: number;
  opacity?: number;

  originX?: "left" | "center" | "right";
  originY?: "top" | "center" | "bottom";

  visible?: boolean;
  selectable?: boolean;
  evented?: boolean;

  hasControls?: boolean;
  hasBorders?: boolean;

  lockMovementX?: boolean;
  lockMovementY?: boolean;
  lockScalingX?: boolean;
  lockScalingY?: boolean;
  lockRotation?: boolean;

  objectCaching?: boolean;
  perPixelTargetFind?: boolean;

  excludeFromExport?: boolean;

  /**
   * AI metadata.
   * Keep this minimal. The full source of truth stays in AiReconstructionDocument.
   */
  aiLayerId?: string;
  aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
  aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
  aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
  aiSource?: AiLayerSource;
  aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
  aiSchemaVersion?: string;

  [key: string]: unknown;
};

export type FabricRuntimeJson = {
  /**
   * Fabric library version used to generate this JSON.
   */
  version: string;

  /**
   * Fabric loadFromJSON does not reliably set canvas dimensions for your editor.
   * Always set dimensions from manifest.canvas before load.
   */
  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  objects: FabricObjectJson[];

  background?: string | null;
  backgroundColor?: string | null;

  backgroundImage?: FabricObjectJson;
  overlayImage?: FabricObjectJson;
  clipPath?: FabricObjectJson;

  [key: string]: unknown;
};

export type AiFabricLayerIndexEntry = {
  aiLayerId: string;

  objectIndex: number;

  zIndex: number;

  name: string;

  layerType: AiLayerType;
  editableLevel: AiEditableLevel;

  fabricObjectType: string;

  assetIds: string[];

  fallbackAssetId?: string;

  originalBBox?: BBox;
};

export type AiFabricManifestAsset = AiAssetRef & {
  /**
   * URL actually used by Fabric objects.
   * This should be browser-loadable and CORS-safe.
   */
  resolvedUrl?: string;
};

export type AiFabricManifest = {
  schemaVersion: typeof AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION;

  jobId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  createdAt: number;
  updatedAt: number;

  source: {
    reconstructionSchemaVersion: AiReconstructionDocument["schemaVersion"];
    reconstructionDocumentStoragePath?: string;

    originalImageAssetId?: string;
    normalizedImageAssetId?: string;
  };

  canvas: {
    width: number;
    height: number;

    originalWidth: number;
    originalHeight: number;

    normalizedWidth: number;
    normalizedHeight: number;

    unit: "px";

    backgroundColor?: string;
  };

  assets: Record<string, AiFabricManifestAsset>;

  layerIndex: Record<string, AiFabricLayerIndexEntry>;

  fabricJson: FabricRuntimeJson;

  reconstruction: {
    qualityScore?: number;
    visualMatchScore?: number;
    needsReview: boolean;
    warnings: string[];
  };

  runtime: {
    fabricVersion: string;

    /**
     * Useful when debugging JSON generated on server and loaded in browser.
     */
    generatedBy: "server" | "client" | "worker";

    pipelineVersion: string;
  };
};
```

# 2. Fabric object type map

Do **not** hand-maintain object type strings if you can avoid it. Derive them from the installed Fabric classes.

```ts
// src/lib/ai-layers/fabric-object-types.ts

import {
  Circle,
  Ellipse,
  FabricImage,
  Group,
  Line,
  Path,
  Polygon,
  Rect,
  Textbox,
} from "fabric";

export const FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES = {
  image: FabricImage.type,
  textbox: Textbox.type,
  rect: Rect.type,
  circle: Circle.type,
  ellipse: Ellipse.type,
  line: Line.type,
  polygon: Polygon.type,
  path: Path.type,
  group: Group.type,
} as const;
```

This keeps your manifest aligned with your installed Fabric major version.

# 3. Register AI custom properties safely

You already have a working editor, so do **not** overwrite existing custom properties. Merge yours into the existing Fabric list.

```ts
// src/lib/fabric/register-ai-custom-properties.ts

import { FabricObject } from "fabric";
import type {
  AiConfidence,
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerSource,
  AiLayerType,
} from "@/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.types";

export const AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES = [
  "id",
  "name",

  "aiLayerId",
  "aiLayerType",
  "aiEditableLevel",
  "aiConfidence",
  "aiSource",
  "aiFallbackAssetId",
  "aiSchemaVersion",
] as const;

declare module "fabric" {
  interface FabricObject {
    id?: string;
    name?: string;

    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiLayerSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;
  }

  interface SerializedObjectProps {
    id?: string;
    name?: string;

    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiLayerSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;
  }
}

export function registerAiFabricCustomProperties() {
  const existing = FabricObject.customProperties ?? [];

  FabricObject.customProperties = Array.from(
    new Set([...existing, ...AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES])
  );
}
```

Call this once before any AI manifest load or save:

```ts
registerAiFabricCustomProperties();
```

# 4. Raster asset coordinate policy

Use this rule from day one:

```txt
reference image        → full canvas PNG
clean background       → full canvas PNG
masked object layers   → cropped RGBA PNG
text fallback crops    → cropped RGBA PNG
```

For cropped object layers:

```txt
Fabric left/top = original bbox x/y
Fabric width/height = asset pixel width/height
Fabric scaleX/scaleY = rendered bbox size / asset pixel size
```

This avoids full-canvas transparent PNGs for every layer.

Example:

```txt
object bbox in canvas: x=300, y=180, width=420, height=560
layer PNG size:        width=420, height=560

Fabric:
left=300
top=180
width=420
height=560
scaleX=1
scaleY=1
```

If you export a layer asset at different resolution:

```txt
object bbox:     420 × 560
layer PNG:       840 × 1120

Fabric:
width=840
height=1120
scaleX=0.5
scaleY=0.5
```

Do not fake this with `width=bbox.width` if the actual image asset is a different size. Fabric image dimensions should represent the source image dimensions; visual sizing should happen through scale.

# 5. Convert one reconstructed layer into one Fabric object

```ts
// src/lib/ai-layers/to-fabric-object-json.ts

import type {
  AiAssetRef,
  AiReconstructedLayer,
  BBox,
} from "./ai-layer.types";
import type { FabricObjectJson } from "./fabric-manifest.types";
import { FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES } from "./fabric-object-types";

function round(value: number, digits = 4): number {
  const factor = 10 ** digits;
  return Math.round(value * factor) / factor;
}

function clamp01(value: number): number {
  return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value));
}

function getAsset(
  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>,
  assetId: string
): AiAssetRef {
  const asset = assets[assetId];

  if (!asset) {
    throw new Error(`Missing asset: ${assetId}`);
  }

  return asset;
}

function getAssetUrl(
  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>,
  assetId: string
): string {
  const asset = getAsset(assets, assetId);

  if (!asset.url) {
    throw new Error(
      `Asset ${assetId} has no resolved URL. Fabric cannot load storagePath directly.`
    );
  }

  return asset.url;
}

function baseFabricProps(layer: AiReconstructedLayer): FabricObjectJson {
  const t = layer.geometry.transform;

  const locked = layer.locked || layer.editableLevel === "locked_reference";

  const canMove = layer.capabilities.includes("move");
  const canResize = layer.capabilities.includes("resize");
  const canRotate = layer.capabilities.includes("rotate");

  return {
    id: layer.id,
    name: layer.name,

    left: round(t.left),
    top: round(t.top),

    width: round(t.width),
    height: round(t.height),

    scaleX: round(t.scaleX),
    scaleY: round(t.scaleY),

    angle: round(t.angle),
    opacity: clamp01(t.opacity),

    originX: t.originX,
    originY: t.originY,

    visible: layer.visible,

    selectable: !locked && layer.capabilities.includes("select"),
    evented: !locked,

    hasControls: !locked,
    hasBorders: !locked,

    lockMovementX: locked || !canMove,
    lockMovementY: locked || !canMove,
    lockScalingX: locked || !canResize,
    lockScalingY: locked || !canResize,
    lockRotation: locked || !canRotate,

    objectCaching: true,

    perPixelTargetFind:
      layer.editableLevel === "raster_masked" ||
      layer.editableLevel === "raster_fallback",

    excludeFromExport: false,

    aiLayerId: layer.id,
    aiLayerType: layer.type,
    aiEditableLevel: layer.editableLevel,
    aiConfidence: layer.confidence,
    aiSource: layer.source.primary,
    aiFallbackAssetId: layer.fallback.assetId,
    aiSchemaVersion: layer.schemaVersion,
  };
}

function imageObjectFromLayer(params: {
  layer: AiReconstructedLayer;
  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>;
}): FabricObjectJson {
  const { layer, assets } = params;

  if (!layer.raster) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} needs raster payload`);
  }

  const rgbaAsset = getAsset(assets, layer.raster.rgbaAssetId);
  const src = getAssetUrl(assets, layer.raster.rgbaAssetId);

  const bbox = layer.geometry.bbox;

  const sourceWidth = rgbaAsset.width ?? bbox.width;
  const sourceHeight = rgbaAsset.height ?? bbox.height;

  return {
    ...baseFabricProps(layer),

    type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.image,

    src,

    /**
     * Required for browser export reliability.
     * Your GCS/Firebase asset URLs must return valid CORS headers.
     */
    crossOrigin: "anonymous",

    width: round(sourceWidth),
    height: round(sourceHeight),

    scaleX: round(bbox.width / sourceWidth),
    scaleY: round(bbox.height / sourceHeight),

    left: round(bbox.x),
    top: round(bbox.y),

    filters: [],
  };
}

function textboxObjectFromLayer(layer: AiReconstructedLayer): FabricObjectJson {
  if (!layer.text) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} needs text payload`);
  }

  const bbox = layer.geometry.bbox;

  return {
    ...baseFabricProps(layer),

    type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.textbox,

    text: layer.text.value,

    left: round(bbox.x),
    top: round(bbox.y),

    width: round(bbox.width),

    fontFamily: layer.text.fontFamily ?? "Inter",
    fontSize: layer.text.fontSize ?? Math.max(12, bbox.height * 0.7),

    fontWeight: layer.text.fontWeight ?? "normal",
    fontStyle: layer.text.fontStyle ?? "normal",

    lineHeight: layer.text.lineHeight ?? 1.1,
    charSpacing: layer.text.charSpacing ?? 0,

    fill: layer.text.fill ?? "#000000",
    stroke: layer.text.stroke,
    strokeWidth: layer.text.strokeWidth ?? 0,

    textAlign: layer.text.textAlign ?? "left",

    splitByGrapheme: false,

    editable: true,
  };
}

function vectorObjectFromLayer(layer: AiReconstructedLayer): FabricObjectJson {
  if (!layer.vector) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} needs vector payload`);
  }

  const bbox = layer.geometry.bbox;
  const vector = layer.vector;
  const base = baseFabricProps(layer);

  const commonVectorProps = {
    fill: vector.fill ?? "transparent",
    stroke: vector.stroke,
    strokeWidth: vector.strokeWidth ?? 0,
    opacity: vector.opacity ?? base.opacity ?? 1,
  };

  switch (vector.primitive) {
    case "rect":
    case "rounded_rect":
      return {
        ...base,
        ...commonVectorProps,

        type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.rect,

        left: round(bbox.x),
        top: round(bbox.y),

        width: round(bbox.width),
        height: round(bbox.height),

        scaleX: 1,
        scaleY: 1,

        rx: vector.radius ?? 0,
        ry: vector.radius ?? 0,
      };

    case "circle": {
      const radius = Math.max(1, Math.min(bbox.width, bbox.height) / 2);

      return {
        ...base,
        ...commonVectorProps,

        type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.circle,

        left: round(bbox.x),
        top: round(bbox.y),

        radius: round(radius),

        width: round(radius * 2),
        height: round(radius * 2),

        scaleX: round(bbox.width / (radius * 2)),
        scaleY: round(bbox.height / (radius * 2)),
      };
    }

    case "ellipse":
      return {
        ...base,
        ...commonVectorProps,

        type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.ellipse,

        left: round(bbox.x),
        top: round(bbox.y),

        rx: round(bbox.width / 2),
        ry: round(bbox.height / 2),

        scaleX: 1,
        scaleY: 1,
      };

    case "line": {
      const p0 = vector.points?.[0] ?? { x: bbox.x, y: bbox.y };
      const p1 = vector.points?.[1] ?? {
        x: bbox.x + bbox.width,
        y: bbox.y + bbox.height,
      };

      return {
        ...base,
        ...commonVectorProps,

        type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.line,

        x1: round(p0.x),
        y1: round(p0.y),
        x2: round(p1.x),
        y2: round(p1.y),

        fill: undefined,
      };
    }

    case "polygon":
      return {
        ...base,
        ...commonVectorProps,

        type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.polygon,

        left: round(bbox.x),
        top: round(bbox.y),

        points:
          vector.points?.map((p) => ({
            x: round(p.x - bbox.x),
            y: round(p.y - bbox.y),
          })) ?? [],
      };

    case "path":
      if (!vector.pathData) {
        throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} path vector needs pathData`);
      }

      return {
        ...base,
        ...commonVectorProps,

        type: FABRIC_OBJECT_TYPES.path,

        left: round(bbox.x),
        top: round(bbox.y),

        path: vector.pathData,
      };

    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported vector primitive: ${vector.primitive}`);
  }
}

export function layerToFabricObjectJson(params: {
  layer: AiReconstructedLayer;
  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>;
}): FabricObjectJson | null {
  const { layer, assets } = params;

  switch (layer.editableLevel) {
    case "locked_reference":
    case "raster_masked":
    case "raster_clean_background":
    case "raster_fallback":
    case "unknown_confidence":
      return imageObjectFromLayer({ layer, assets });

    case "text_editable":
      return textboxObjectFromLayer(layer);

    case "vector_editable":
      return vectorObjectFromLayer(layer);

    case "group_editable":
      /**
       * Do not emit Fabric.Group by default unless your editor's group editing
       * semantics are already stable.
       *
       * The safer default is logical grouping in manifest.layerIndex.
       */
      return null;

    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported editable level: ${layer.editableLevel}`);
  }
}
```

# 6. Convert reconstruction document into Fabric manifest

```ts
// src/lib/ai-layers/to-fabric-manifest.ts

import { version as fabricVersion } from "fabric";

import type {
  AiAssetRef,
  AiReconstructionDocument,
} from "./ai-layer.types";
import {
  AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION,
  type AiFabricManifest,
  type AiFabricManifestAsset,
  type AiFabricLayerIndexEntry,
  type FabricObjectJson,
} from "./fabric-manifest.types";
import { layerToFabricObjectJson } from "./to-fabric-object-json";

export type ResolveFabricAssetUrl = (asset: AiAssetRef) => Promise<string>;

async function resolveManifestAssets(params: {
  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>;
  resolveAssetUrl: ResolveFabricAssetUrl;
}): Promise<Record<string, AiFabricManifestAsset>> {
  const resolved: Record<string, AiFabricManifestAsset> = {};

  for (const [assetId, asset] of Object.entries(params.assets)) {
    const needsUrl =
      asset.kind === "rgba_png" ||
      asset.kind === "original_image" ||
      asset.kind === "normalized_image" ||
      asset.kind === "svg" ||
      asset.kind === "preview_render";

    resolved[assetId] = {
      ...asset,
      resolvedUrl: needsUrl ? await params.resolveAssetUrl(asset) : asset.url,
      url: needsUrl ? await params.resolveAssetUrl(asset) : asset.url,
    };
  }

  return resolved;
}

export async function createAiFabricManifest(params: {
  doc: AiReconstructionDocument;

  resolveAssetUrl: ResolveFabricAssetUrl;

  generatedBy: "server" | "client" | "worker";
}): Promise<AiFabricManifest> {
  const { doc } = params;

  const resolvedAssets = await resolveManifestAssets({
    assets: doc.assets,
    resolveAssetUrl: params.resolveAssetUrl,
  });

  const sortedLayers = [...doc.layers].sort((a, b) => a.zIndex - b.zIndex);

  const objects: FabricObjectJson[] = [];
  const layerIndex: Record<string, AiFabricLayerIndexEntry> = {};

  for (const layer of sortedLayers) {
    const object = layerToFabricObjectJson({
      layer,
      assets: resolvedAssets,
    });

    /**
     * Logical-only groups may return null.
     */
    if (!object) continue;

    const objectIndex = objects.length;

    objects.push(object);

    layerIndex[layer.id] = {
      aiLayerId: layer.id,

      objectIndex,

      zIndex: layer.zIndex,

      name: layer.name,

      layerType: layer.type,
      editableLevel: layer.editableLevel,

      fabricObjectType: object.type,

      assetIds: layer.assetIds,

      fallbackAssetId: layer.fallback.assetId,

      originalBBox: layer.geometry.originalBBox,
    };
  }

  const now = Date.now();

  const manifest: AiFabricManifest = {
    schemaVersion: AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION,

    jobId: doc.jobId,
    designId: doc.designId,
    userId: doc.userId,

    createdAt: now,
    updatedAt: now,

    source: {
      reconstructionSchemaVersion: doc.schemaVersion,

      originalImageAssetId: doc.layers.find(
        (layer) => layer.type === "locked_reference"
      )?.raster?.rgbaAssetId,

      normalizedImageAssetId: doc.layers.find(
        (layer) => layer.metadata.normalizedImageAssetId
      )?.metadata.normalizedImageAssetId,
    },

    canvas: {
      width: doc.canvas.width,
      height: doc.canvas.height,

      originalWidth: doc.canvas.originalWidth,
      originalHeight: doc.canvas.originalHeight,

      normalizedWidth: doc.canvas.normalizedWidth,
      normalizedHeight: doc.canvas.normalizedHeight,

      unit: "px",

      backgroundColor: doc.canvas.backgroundColor,
    },

    assets: resolvedAssets,

    layerIndex,

    fabricJson: {
      version: fabricVersion,

      /**
       * Keep dimensions here for debug/export visibility,
       * but the loader must still set canvas dimensions from manifest.canvas.
       */
      width: doc.canvas.width,
      height: doc.canvas.height,

      background: doc.canvas.backgroundColor ?? "transparent",

      objects,
    },

    reconstruction: {
      qualityScore: doc.quality.visualMatchScore,
      visualMatchScore: doc.quality.visualMatchScore,
      needsReview: doc.quality.needsReview,
      warnings: doc.quality.warnings,
    },

    runtime: {
      fabricVersion,
      generatedBy: params.generatedBy,
      pipelineVersion: doc.pipeline.pipelineVersion,
    },
  };

  return manifest;
}
```

Small optimization: `resolveManifestAssets` above calls `resolveAssetUrl` twice. Use this instead:

```ts
async function resolveManifestAssets(params: {
  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>;
  resolveAssetUrl: ResolveFabricAssetUrl;
}): Promise<Record<string, AiFabricManifestAsset>> {
  const resolved: Record<string, AiFabricManifestAsset> = {};

  for (const [assetId, asset] of Object.entries(params.assets)) {
    const needsUrl =
      asset.kind === "rgba_png" ||
      asset.kind === "original_image" ||
      asset.kind === "normalized_image" ||
      asset.kind === "svg" ||
      asset.kind === "preview_render";

    const resolvedUrl = needsUrl
      ? await params.resolveAssetUrl(asset)
      : asset.url;

    resolved[assetId] = {
      ...asset,
      resolvedUrl,
      url: resolvedUrl,
    };
  }

  return resolved;
}
```

Use the optimized version.

# 7. Manifest validation

```ts
// src/lib/ai-layers/fabric-manifest.schema.ts

import { z } from "zod";
import { AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION } from "./fabric-manifest.types";

const BBoxSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
  width: z.number().nonnegative(),
  height: z.number().nonnegative(),
});

const FabricObjectJsonSchema = z
  .object({
    type: z.string().min(1),

    id: z.string().optional(),
    name: z.string().optional(),

    left: z.number().optional(),
    top: z.number().optional(),
    width: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
    height: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

    scaleX: z.number().optional(),
    scaleY: z.number().optional(),

    angle: z.number().optional(),
    opacity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

    visible: z.boolean().optional(),

    aiLayerId: z.string().optional(),
    aiLayerType: z.string().optional(),
    aiEditableLevel: z.string().optional(),
    aiSource: z.string().optional(),
    aiFallbackAssetId: z.string().optional(),
    aiSchemaVersion: z.string().optional(),
  })
  .passthrough();

const FabricRuntimeJsonSchema = z
  .object({
    version: z.string().min(1),
    width: z.number().positive().optional(),
    height: z.number().positive().optional(),
    background: z.union([z.string(), z.null()]).optional(),
    objects: z.array(FabricObjectJsonSchema),
  })
  .passthrough();

const ManifestAssetSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().min(1),
    kind: z.string().min(1),
    storagePath: z.string().optional(),
    url: z.string().url().optional(),
    resolvedUrl: z.string().url().optional(),
    mimeType: z.string().optional(),
    width: z.number().positive().optional(),
    height: z.number().positive().optional(),
    sizeBytes: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
  })
  .passthrough();

const LayerIndexEntrySchema = z.object({
  aiLayerId: z.string().min(1),
  objectIndex: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  zIndex: z.number().int(),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  layerType: z.string().min(1),
  editableLevel: z.string().min(1),
  fabricObjectType: z.string().min(1),
  assetIds: z.array(z.string()),
  fallbackAssetId: z.string().optional(),
  originalBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),
});

export const AiFabricManifestSchema = z
  .object({
    schemaVersion: z.literal(AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION),

    jobId: z.string().min(1),
    designId: z.string().min(1),
    userId: z.string().min(1),

    createdAt: z.number(),
    updatedAt: z.number(),

    source: z.object({
      reconstructionSchemaVersion: z.string().min(1),
      reconstructionDocumentStoragePath: z.string().optional(),
      originalImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),
      normalizedImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),
    }),

    canvas: z.object({
      width: z.number().positive(),
      height: z.number().positive(),

      originalWidth: z.number().positive(),
      originalHeight: z.number().positive(),

      normalizedWidth: z.number().positive(),
      normalizedHeight: z.number().positive(),

      unit: z.literal("px"),

      backgroundColor: z.string().optional(),
    }),

    assets: z.record(z.string(), ManifestAssetSchema),

    layerIndex: z.record(z.string(), LayerIndexEntrySchema),

    fabricJson: FabricRuntimeJsonSchema,

    reconstruction: z.object({
      qualityScore: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
      visualMatchScore: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
      needsReview: z.boolean(),
      warnings: z.array(z.string()),
    }),

    runtime: z.object({
      fabricVersion: z.string().min(1),
      generatedBy: z.enum(["server", "client", "worker"]),
      pipelineVersion: z.string().min(1),
    }),
  })
  .superRefine((manifest, ctx) => {
    if (manifest.fabricJson.objects.length === 0) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: "Fabric manifest must contain at least one Fabric object",
        path: ["fabricJson", "objects"],
      });
    }

    for (const [layerId, entry] of Object.entries(manifest.layerIndex)) {
      if (entry.aiLayerId !== layerId) {
        ctx.addIssue({
          code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
          message: "layerIndex key must match entry.aiLayerId",
          path: ["layerIndex", layerId],
        });
      }

      if (!manifest.fabricJson.objects[entry.objectIndex]) {
        ctx.addIssue({
          code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
          message: "layerIndex points to missing Fabric object",
          path: ["layerIndex", layerId, "objectIndex"],
        });
      }

      for (const assetId of entry.assetIds) {
        if (!manifest.assets[assetId]) {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            message: `Missing asset referenced by layerIndex: ${assetId}`,
            path: ["layerIndex", layerId, "assetIds"],
          });
        }
      }
    }
  });

export type AiFabricManifestValidated = z.infer<
  typeof AiFabricManifestSchema
>;
```

# 8. Load manifest into your existing Fabric editor

```ts
// src/lib/fabric/load-ai-fabric-manifest.ts

import type { Canvas, FabricObject } from "fabric";
import type { AiFabricManifest } from "@/lib/ai-layers/fabric-manifest.types";
import { AiFabricManifestSchema } from "@/lib/ai-layers/fabric-manifest.schema";
import { registerAiFabricCustomProperties } from "./register-ai-custom-properties";

export async function loadAiFabricManifest(params: {
  canvas: Canvas;
  manifest: AiFabricManifest;
  abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
}) {
  const { canvas } = params;

  const manifest = AiFabricManifestSchema.parse(params.manifest);

  registerAiFabricCustomProperties();

  canvas.clear();

  /**
   * Do this before loadFromJSON.
   * Do not rely on Fabric JSON to resize your editor canvas.
   */
  canvas.setDimensions({
    width: manifest.canvas.width,
    height: manifest.canvas.height,
  });

  await canvas.loadFromJSON(
    manifest.fabricJson,
    (_serializedObject: unknown, fabricObject: FabricObject) => {
      /**
       * Reviver hook:
       * use this for post-load normalization only.
       * Do not reconstruct missing AI data here.
       */
      fabricObject.set({
        dirty: true,
      });
    },
    params.abortSignal ? { signal: params.abortSignal } : undefined
  );

  for (const object of canvas.getObjects()) {
    object.setCoords();
  }

  canvas.requestRenderAll();

  return {
    objectCount: canvas.getObjects().length,
    layerIndex: manifest.layerIndex,
  };
}
```

Important runtime rule:

```ts
const controller = new AbortController();

await loadAiFabricManifest({
  canvas,
  manifest,
  abortSignal: controller.signal,
});

// when user imports another image before current one finishes
controller.abort();
```

Fabric specifically recommends aborting loading tasks before calling `loadFromJSON` again to prevent race conditions and unnecessary networking. citeturn871230view0

---

# 9. Save Fabric JSON without losing AI metadata

```ts
// src/lib/fabric/save-ai-fabric-json.ts

import type { Canvas } from "fabric";
import type { FabricRuntimeJson } from "@/lib/ai-layers/fabric-manifest.types";
import { AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES } from "./register-ai-custom-properties";

export function saveAiFabricRuntimeJson(canvas: Canvas): FabricRuntimeJson {
  /**
   * Use toObject with explicit custom props.
   * Do not depend only on JSON.stringify(canvas).
   */
  const json = canvas.toObject([...AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES]);

  return json as FabricRuntimeJson;
}
```

When autosaving user edits, save:

```ts
{
  fabricJson: saveAiFabricRuntimeJson(canvas),
  updatedAt: Date.now()
}
```

Do not regenerate the AI reconstruction document on every edit. User edits belong to the Fabric design state. AI observations belong to the reconstruction document.

---

# 10. CORS requirement for Firebase / GCS assets

Every image URL used inside `fabricJson.objects[].src` must be export-safe.

For GCS-backed Firebase Storage, configure bucket CORS for your editor origin:

```json
[
  {
    "origin": [
      "http://localhost:3000",
      "https://your-production-domain.com"
    ],
    "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
    "responseHeader": ["Content-Type", "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"],
    "maxAgeSeconds": 3600
  }
]
```

Apply it to the bucket:

```bash
gcloud storage buckets update gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME --cors-file=cors.json
```

If your assets are private, the clean pattern is:

```txt
canonical identity: storagePath
runtime loading: signed URL or authenticated asset proxy
Fabric src: resolved HTTPS URL
```

Never make this the canonical identity:

```txt
https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/...
```

Use it only as a runtime URL.

```json
      "width": 1080,
      "height": 1080
    },
    "clean_bg": {
      "id": "clean_bg",
      "kind": "rgba_png",

      "url": "https://cdn.example.com/clean_background.png",
```

# Non-negotiable manifest invariants

These should be enforced before loading into the editor:

```txt
manifest.fabricJson.objects.length > 0

every AI-visible Fabric object has aiLayerId

every aiLayerId in Fabric objects exists in layerIndex

every layerIndex objectIndex points to a real Fabric object

every image object has src as HTTPS URL

every image object uses crossOrigin: "anonymous"

no Fabric src uses gs:// storage paths

canvas dimensions are set from manifest.canvas before loadFromJSON

object order equals z-index order

locked_reference exists, even if hidden

full AI data stays outside Fabric JSON
```

---

# The architectural rule

The Fabric manifest is not your AI data model.

It is:

```txt
a deterministic editor projection
```

The internal reconstruction document remains the durable intelligence layer.

That lets you change segmentation models, OCR providers, Gemini prompts, background repair, vectorization, and export targets without breaking your editor or corrupting saved designs.

After this step is implemented, the pipeline has a stable contract:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
→ AiFabricManifest
→ manifest.fabricJson
→ canvas.loadFromJSON()
```

Next point is **Firebase / GCS data architecture**.

---

## ChatGPT Response 008

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 94a9cddc-dcad-4735-86bb-b8828bc044c1, 9a7843bf-4cbc-4ab6-b516-ab3e875d84f7, fc8ddd4a-7864-44fb-b7f6-fca79bad11ab -->

I’ll continue with the next locked point: Firebase/GCS storage architecture, keeping Firestore minimal except where storage paths need metadata references.

Key decisions now: separate immutable originals, derived AI artifacts, and mutable editor snapshots; use `workspaceId` as ownership root, and treat `storagePath` as the durable asset identity.

# Step 2.1 — Storage / GCS asset architecture

This step locks where every uploaded image, generated mask, extracted layer, fallback crop, manifest, preview, and export lives.

The rule:

```txt
Firestore = state and indexes
GCS / Firebase Storage = bytes
Fabric JSON = resolved editor document
storagePath = durable asset identity
signed URL / download URL = temporary runtime access
```

Do **not** use Firebase Storage as an unstructured file dump. For this feature, Storage becomes the asset backbone of the reconstruction system.

Cloud Storage for Firebase stores files in Google Cloud Storage buckets and can be accessed from Firebase client SDKs or privileged server environments via the Firebase Admin SDK / Google Cloud Storage APIs. That gives you the right split: client upload for originals, server-only writes for AI outputs, and backend-controlled URL resolution for Fabric loading. citeturn601775view3

---

# The storage contract

Every asset in the AI layer system must have this durable identity:

```ts
{
  assetId: string;
  bucket: string;
  storagePath: string;
  kind: AiAssetKind;
  contentType: string;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  sizeBytes?: number;
  checksum?: string;
  generation?: string;
  metageneration?: string;
}
```

Never use this as durable identity:

```txt
https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/...
https://storage.googleapis.com/...
signed-url-with-query-params
```

Those are runtime access URLs only.

Reason: Firebase Admin can generate non-expiring download URLs, and Firebase explicitly says anyone with that URL can permanently access the file. That is the wrong default for private user designs. citeturn390677view0

Use signed URLs for runtime access because Cloud Storage signed URLs are time-limited access grants to a specific resource. citeturn755669view1

---

# Bucket decision

Use **two buckets** from day one.

```txt
1. source bucket
2. asset bucket
```

Do not create a public bucket yet.

## 1. Source bucket

Purpose:

```txt
original uploads
normalized images
raw OCR outputs
raw Gemini outputs
raw masks
diagnostics
fallback crops
```

Example bucket:

```txt
yourapp-ai-source-prod.firebasestorage.app
```

Access:

```txt
private
server-readable
client writes only to upload landing zone
never directly public
no permanent download URLs
```

Cache behavior:

```txt
no-store
private
short-lived signed URLs only when needed
```

---

## 2. Asset bucket

Purpose:

```txt
editor-ready layer PNGs
editor-ready SVGs
clean backgrounds
Fabric manifests
preview renders
export renders
ZIP layer exports
```

Example bucket:

```txt
yourapp-ai-assets-prod.firebasestorage.app
```

Access:

```txt
private
server writes
client reads through signed URLs or URL resolver
CORS enabled
public access prevention enabled
```

Cache behavior:

```txt
immutable generated layer assets → long private cache
manifests/current state → no-cache
previews → medium cache
exports → medium/long private cache
```

Cloud Storage lets you create multiple buckets per Firebase project, each with its own location setting. Bucket location matters because Firebase recommends placing stored data close to users and services, and bucket location cannot be changed after provisioning. citeturn208277view0

---

# Location rule

Pick one primary region for:

```txt
Cloud Run AI worker
Firebase Storage buckets
Firestore database
server-side export worker
```

Do not scatter them.

For example:

```txt
AI worker: asia-south1
Storage: asia-south1
Firestore: asia-south1 / nearest supported location
```

Or:

```txt
AI worker: us-central1
Storage: us-central1
Firestore: us-central1
```

The exact region depends on where your users and Google AI workload actually run. The architecture rule is more important than the specific region:

```txt
Keep bytes close to compute.
Keep editor assets close to users.
Do not create cross-region read/write paths accidentally.
```

---

# Canonical path structure

Use this exact structure.

## Source bucket

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/source/original/{assetId}/original.{ext}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/source/normalized/{assetId}/normalized.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/raw/gemini-layout.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/raw/ocr.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/raw/segmentation.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/masks/{layerId}/{assetId}.mask.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/fallbacks/{layerId}/{assetId}.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/diagnostics/{assetId}.json
```

## Asset bucket

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/backgrounds/{assetId}.clean.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.editor.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.export.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/vectors/{layerId}/{assetId}.svg

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/manifests/{assetId}.reconstruction.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/ai/jobs/{jobId}/manifests/{assetId}.fabric-manifest.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/versions/{versionId}/fabric.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/versions/{versionId}/thumbnail.webp

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}/final.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}/layers.zip
```

Use `workspaceId` from day one, even if every user only has one personal workspace right now.

Bad long-term path:

```txt
users/{uid}/designs/{designId}/...
```

Better:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/...
```

Why: teams, agencies, shared designs, billing entities, and permissions can come later without moving every object.

---

# Upload landing zone

Client uploads should **not** write directly into canonical design paths.

Use a temporary landing zone:

```txt
client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/original.{ext}
```

Then your backend worker copies/normalizes it into:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/source/original/{assetId}/original.{ext}
```

Reason:

```txt
client-uploaded bytes are untrusted
canonical design assets should be server-verified
workspace permissions should be server-controlled
AI pipeline should only consume normalized canonical assets
```

---

# Object naming rules

Use generated IDs, not user filenames.

Good:

```txt
asset_01j2x9z6ms8k8qv3e4h7f2p9ab.editor.png
```

Bad:

```txt
my cool poster final final.png
```

Cloud Storage object names are flexible, but Google documents naming restrictions and considerations; object names cannot contain carriage return or line feed characters, cannot be `.` or `..`, and cannot start with `.well-known/acme-challenge/`. citeturn601775view0

Use:

```txt
lowercase
safe ASCII
no spaces
no user-provided filename in canonical path
assetId in filename
correct extension
```

---

# Asset kinds

Add these asset kinds to your schema.

```ts
export type AiAssetKind =
  | "original_image"
  | "normalized_image"
  | "rgba_png"
  | "editor_png"
  | "export_png"
  | "mask_png"
  | "svg"
  | "json"
  | "fabric_manifest"
  | "reconstruction_document"
  | "preview_render"
  | "final_export"
  | "zip_export"
  | "diagnostic"
  | "none";
```

Patch your `AiAssetRef` from Step 1.1:

```ts
export type AiAssetRef = {
  id: string;

  kind: AiAssetKind;

  bucket: string;

  storagePath: string;

  url?: string;
  urlExpiresAt?: number;

  mimeType?: string;

  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  sizeBytes?: number;

  generation?: string;
  metageneration?: string;

  checksum?: {
    algorithm: "sha256" | "md5";
    value: string;
  };

  cacheControl?: string;

  metadata?: {
    app?: string;
    workspaceId?: string;
    designId?: string;
    jobId?: string;
    layerId?: string;
    assetId?: string;
    assetKind?: AiAssetKind;
    schemaVersion?: string;
    pipelineVersion?: string;
    createdBy?: AiLayerSource;
  };
};
```

Important addition:

```txt
bucket
generation
metageneration
```

Cloud Storage objects have object data plus metadata, and Google documents that object name plus generation uniquely identifies an object within a bucket. Store generation when you upload assets. citeturn601775view0

---

# Never overwrite generated assets

Generated assets should be immutable.

Bad:

```txt
layers/layer_001.png
```

Good:

```txt
layers/layer_001/asset_01j2x9z6ms8k8qv3e4h7f2p9ab.editor.png
```

If the layer is regenerated, create a new asset:

```txt
layers/layer_001/asset_01j2xbv9vdm4q2x6x3fp93n8aa.editor.png
```

Then update the manifest or design version to point to the new `assetId`.

Use Cloud Storage preconditions on writes so a worker cannot accidentally overwrite an existing object. Google’s request preconditions are specifically designed to avoid unsafe writes and race conditions; `ifGenerationMatch` is the relevant generation precondition. citeturn771977view0

---

# Storage metadata policy

Every uploaded AI asset must include:

```ts
const metadata = {
  contentType: "image/png",
  cacheControl: "private, max-age=31536000, immutable",
  metadata: {
    app: "magic-layers",
    workspaceId,
    designId,
    jobId,
    layerId,
    assetId,
    assetKind: "editor_png",
    schemaVersion: "ai-reconstruction.v1",
    pipelineVersion: "pipeline.v1",
    createdBy: "segmentation"
  }
};
```

Cloud Storage `Cache-Control` metadata controls whether and how long objects can be cached by browser, internet, and Cloud Storage caches. citeturn755669view2

---

# Cache policy

Use this table.

| Asset | Cache-Control |
|---|---|
| original upload | `private, no-store` |
| normalized image | `private, no-store` |
| raw model output JSON | `private, no-store` |
| masks | `private, max-age=86400` |
| editor layer PNG | `private, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| export layer PNG | `private, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| SVG vector | `private, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| clean background | `private, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| reconstruction document | `private, no-cache` |
| Fabric manifest | `private, no-cache` |
| preview thumbnail | `private, max-age=86400` |
| final export | `private, max-age=604800` |

Why immutable cache works:

```txt
assets are never overwritten
new generation = new assetId = new path
old path can be cached safely
```

Do not use long cache on mutable paths like:

```txt
current/fabric.json
latest-preview.png
layer_001.png
```

---

# Runtime URL policy

Fabric needs browser-loadable URLs.

Your canonical asset object stores:

```txt
bucket
storagePath
assetId
```

At editor load time, backend resolves this into:

```txt
temporary signed HTTPS URL
```

Then your Fabric manifest gets:

```ts
{
  src: "https://storage.googleapis.com/...",
  crossOrigin: "anonymous"
}
```

Do not persist the signed URL as durable data.

Store this only as runtime data:

```ts
{
  url: signedUrl,
  urlExpiresAt: Date.now() + 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000
}
```

If the user reloads the editor tomorrow:

```txt
load manifest metadata
resolve URLs again
load Fabric
```

---

# CORS requirement

Because Fabric loads image assets into a browser canvas, your image responses must be CORS-safe. Firebase’s own Storage docs say you must configure CORS to download directly in the browser. citeturn755669view0

Use this for the asset bucket:

```json
[
  {
    "origin": [
      "http://localhost:3000",
      "https://yourdomain.com"
    ],
    "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
    "responseHeader": [
      "Content-Type",
      "Cache-Control",
      "Content-Disposition",
      "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"
    ],
    "maxAgeSeconds": 3600
  }
]
```

Apply:

```bash
gcloud storage buckets update gs://YOUR_ASSET_BUCKET --cors-file=cors.json
```

For the source bucket, you usually do **not** need browser CORS except for client upload landing zones.

---

# Public access prevention

Turn on public access prevention.

Private user designs should not become public because of one mistaken IAM binding or ACL. Cloud Storage public access prevention blocks public exposure through `allUsers` and `allAuthenticatedUsers`, while signed URLs still work because they grant scoped temporary access through service account permissions. citeturn601775view2

Bucket policy:

```txt
source bucket:
  public access prevention = enforced

asset bucket:
  public access prevention = enforced
```

Do not use public Firebase download URLs for private designs.

---

# Firebase Security Rules

Security rules should only allow direct client upload to the landing zone.

Everything canonical should be written by the backend worker.

```js
rules_version = '2';

service firebase.storage {
  match /b/{bucket}/o {
    function signedIn() {
      return request.auth != null;
    }

    function validUploadImage() {
      return request.resource.size < 25 * 1024 * 1024
        && request.resource.contentType.matches('image/(png|jpeg|webp)');
    }

    match /client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/{fileName} {
      allow create: if signedIn()
        && request.auth.uid == uid
        && validUploadImage();

      allow read, update, delete: if false;
    }

    match /{path=**} {
      allow read, write: if false;
    }
  }
}
```

Firebase Storage Security Rules can use Firebase Auth through `request.auth`, including `request.auth.uid`, and can validate uploaded data using fields such as `request.resource.size` and `request.resource.contentType`. citeturn807917view0turn807917view1

Do not let the client write here:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/...
```

That path is server-owned.

---

# App Check

Enable App Check for:

```txt
Cloud Storage
Cloud Run / Functions API endpoints
Firebase AI Logic if used from client
```

App Check helps prevent unauthorized clients from accessing backend resources and supports Cloud Storage for Firebase, Cloud Run, Cloud Firestore, Firebase AI Logic, and related Firebase services. It complements Firebase Auth; it does not replace authorization. citeturn601775view4

Use it as abuse reduction, not as your permission model.

Permission still comes from:

```txt
Firebase Auth
workspace membership
server-side access checks
signed URL issuance
```

---

# Lifecycle policy

Separate assets by retention class.

## Durable

Keep while design exists:

```txt
original image
normalized image
accepted layer PNGs
accepted SVGs
clean background
reconstruction document
Fabric manifest
design versions
final exports
```

## Diagnostic

Delete or archive after 30–90 days:

```txt
raw Gemini response
raw OCR response
raw segmentation output
debug renders
visual-diff heatmaps
failed masks
```

## Temporary

Delete after 1–7 days:

```txt
intermediate masks
worker scratch files
partial tiles
retry outputs
failed job artifacts
```

Cloud Storage lifecycle rules can delete objects when conditions match, and Cloud Storage soft delete retains deleted live objects for a retention window by default unless you disable it. citeturn601775view1

Example lifecycle policy:

```json
{
  "rule": [
    {
      "action": { "type": "Delete" },
      "condition": {
        "age": 7,
        "matchesPrefix": [
          "tmp/",
          "client-uploads/"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "action": { "type": "Delete" },
      "condition": {
        "age": 45,
        "matchesPrefix": [
          "workspaces/"
        ],
        "matchesSuffix": [
          ".diagnostic.json",
          ".debug.png",
          ".heatmap.png"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Do not enable Object Versioning by default. Your app already creates immutable asset paths. Object Versioning stores noncurrent versions and those versions are charged; Google recommends considering lifecycle management if versioning is enabled. citeturn771977view1

Use:

```txt
app-level versioned paths
soft delete
lifecycle rules
```

Not:

```txt
bucket-wide object versioning for every generated asset
```

---

# Cost control rule

This feature creates many files per input image:

```txt
original
normalized
clean background
N masks
N RGBA layers
N fallback crops
OCR JSON
Gemini JSON
manifest JSON
preview renders
exports
```

Firebase pricing shows Storage costs include stored GB, downloaded GB, upload operations, and download operations. Generated layer systems can become expensive mainly through repeated downloads and large PNG storage. citeturn755669view6

So enforce these now:

```txt
cropped RGBA layers, not full-canvas transparent PNGs
editor-resolution assets separate from export-resolution assets
immutable cached layer paths
no repeated manifest URL regeneration unless needed
delete temp artifacts
cap layer count
cap max image dimensions
cap max job artifacts
```

---

# Editor-resolution vs export-resolution assets

For every raster layer, support two variants.

```txt
editor asset:
  optimized for smooth Fabric editing
  max long edge: 2048 or 3072 px
  loaded into browser

export asset:
  higher fidelity
  used by server-side renderer
  not always loaded into browser
```

Path example:

```txt
layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.editor.png
layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.export.png
```

Schema:

```ts
export type AiRasterPayload = {
  editorAssetId: string;
  exportAssetId?: string;

  rgbaAssetId: string; // keep temporarily for backward compatibility

  maskAssetId?: string;
  originalCropAssetId?: string;

  crop?: BBox;

  alphaMode?: "binary_mask" | "soft_alpha" | "matte";

  edgeQuality?: "high" | "medium" | "low" | "unknown";
};
```

Fabric uses:

```txt
editorAssetId
```

Server export uses:

```txt
exportAssetId if available
else editorAssetId
```

This keeps the editor fast without throwing away export quality.

# `storage-buckets.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/storage/storage-buckets.ts

export type StorageBucketRole = "source" | "assets";

export type StorageBucketConfig = {
  sourceBucket: string;
  assetsBucket: string;
};

export function getStorageBucketConfig(): StorageBucketConfig {
  const sourceBucket = process.env.AI_SOURCE_BUCKET;
  const assetsBucket = process.env.AI_ASSETS_BUCKET;

  if (!sourceBucket) {
    throw new Error("Missing AI_SOURCE_BUCKET");
  }

  if (!assetsBucket) {
    throw new Error("Missing AI_ASSETS_BUCKET");
  }

  return {
    sourceBucket,
    assetsBucket,
  };
}

export function bucketForRole(role: StorageBucketRole): string {
  const config = getStorageBucketConfig();

  switch (role) {
    case "source":
      return config.sourceBucket;

    case "assets":
      return config.assetsBucket;

    default:
      throw new Error(`Unknown bucket role: ${role}`);
  }
}
```

Environment:

```env
AI_SOURCE_BUCKET=yourapp-ai-source-prod.firebasestorage.app
AI_ASSETS_BUCKET=yourapp-ai-assets-prod.firebasestorage.app
```

---

# `storage-paths.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/storage/storage-paths.ts

export type StoragePathBase = {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
};

export type JobStoragePathBase = StoragePathBase & {
  jobId: string;
};

export function clientUploadOriginalPath(params: {
  uid: string;
  uploadId: string;
  extension: "png" | "jpg" | "jpeg" | "webp";
}) {
  return `client-uploads/${params.uid}/${params.uploadId}/original.${params.extension}`;
}

export function originalImagePath(params: StoragePathBase & {
  assetId: string;
  extension: "png" | "jpg" | "jpeg" | "webp";
}) {
  return [
    "workspaces",
    params.workspaceId,
    "designs",
    params.designId,
    "source",
    "original",
    params.assetId,
    `original.${params.extension}`,
  ].join("/");
}

export function normalizedImagePath(params: StoragePathBase & {
  assetId: string;
}) {
  return [
    "workspaces",
    params.workspaceId,
    "designs",
    params.designId,
    "source",
    "normalized",
    params.assetId,
    "normalized.png",
  ].join("/");
}

export function rawModelOutputPath(params: JobStoragePathBase & {
  assetId: string;
  name: "gemini-layout" | "ocr" | "segmentation" | "matting" | "visual-diff";
}) {
  return [
    "workspaces",
    params.workspaceId,
    "designs",
    params.designId,
    "ai",
    "jobs",
    params.jobId,
    "raw",
    `${params.assetId}.${params.name}.json`,
  ].join("/");
}

export function maskPath(params: JobStoragePathBase & {
  layerId: string;
  assetId: string;
}) {
  return [
    "workspaces",
    params.workspaceId,
    "designs",
    params.designId,
    "ai",
    "jobs",
    params.jobId,
    "masks",
    params.layerId,
    `${params.assetId}.mask.png`,
  ].join("/");
}

export function fallbackCropPath(params: JobStoragePathBase & {
  layerId: string;
  assetId: string;
}) {
  return [
```

# `storage-cache-policy.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/storage/storage-cache-policy.ts

import type { AiAssetKind } from "@/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.types";

export function cacheControlForAssetKind(kind: AiAssetKind): string {
  switch (kind) {
    case "original_image":
    case "normalized_image":
    case "diagnostic":
      return "private, no-store";

    case "json":
    case "fabric_manifest":
    case "reconstruction_document":
      return "private, no-cache";

    case "mask_png":
      return "private, max-age=86400";

    case "rgba_png":
    case "editor_png":
    case "export_png":
    case "svg":
      return "private, max-age=31536000, immutable";

    case "preview_render":
      return "private, max-age=86400";

    case "final_export":
    case "zip_export":
      return "private, max-age=604800";

    default:
      return "private, no-cache";
  }
}
```

# `write-ai-asset.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/storage/write-ai-asset.ts

import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { getStorage } from "firebase-admin/storage";
import type {
  AiAssetKind,
  AiAssetRef,
  AiLayerSource,
} from "@/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.types";
import { cacheControlForAssetKind } from "./storage-cache-policy";

export type WriteAiAssetInput = {
  bucket: string;
  storagePath: string;

  bytes: Buffer;

  assetId: string;
  kind: AiAssetKind;

  contentType: string;

  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId?: string;
  layerId?: string;

  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  createdBy: AiLayerSource;

  schemaVersion: string;
  pipelineVersion: string;

  cacheControl?: string;
};

export async function writeAiAsset(
  input: WriteAiAssetInput
): Promise<AiAssetRef> {
  const bucket = getStorage().bucket(input.bucket);
  const file = bucket.file(input.storagePath);

  const sha256 = crypto
    .createHash("sha256")
    .update(input.bytes)
    .digest("hex");

  const cacheControl =
    input.cacheControl ?? cacheControlForAssetKind(input.kind);

  await file.save(input.bytes, {
    resumable: false,

    metadata: {
      contentType: input.contentType,
      cacheControl,

      metadata: {
        app: "magic-layers",
        workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
        designId: input.designId,
        jobId: input.jobId ?? "",
        layerId: input.layerId ?? "",
        assetId: input.assetId,
        assetKind: input.kind,
        schemaVersion: input.schemaVersion,
        pipelineVersion: input.pipelineVersion,
        createdBy: input.createdBy,
        sha256,
      },
    },

    /**
     * Create-only write.
     * Prevents accidental overwrite if two workers race.
     */
    preconditionOpts: {
      ifGenerationMatch: 0,
    },
  });

  const [metadata] = await file.getMetadata();

  return {
    id: input.assetId,
    kind: input.kind,

    bucket: input.bucket,
    storagePath: input.storagePath,

    mimeType: input.contentType,

    width: input.width,
    height: input.height,

    sizeBytes: Number(metadata.size ?? input.bytes.byteLength),

    generation: metadata.generation,
    metageneration: metadata.metageneration,

    cacheControl,

    checksum: {
      algorithm: "sha256",
      value: sha256,
    },

    metadata: {
      app: "magic-layers",
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      jobId: input.jobId,
      layerId: input.layerId,
      assetId: input.assetId,
      assetKind: input.kind,
      schemaVersion: input.schemaVersion,
      pipelineVersion: input.pipelineVersion,
      createdBy: input.createdBy,
    },
  };
}
```
