# `resolve-ai-asset-url.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/storage/resolve-ai-asset-url.ts

import { getStorage } from "firebase-admin/storage";
import type { AiAssetRef } from "@/lib/ai-layers/ai-layer.types";

export type ResolvedAssetUrl = {
  url: string;
  urlExpiresAt: number;
};

export async function resolveAiAssetSignedUrl(params: {
  asset: AiAssetRef;
  expiresInMs?: number;
}): Promise<ResolvedAssetUrl> {
  const expiresInMs = params.expiresInMs ?? 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
  const expiresAt = Date.now() + expiresInMs;

  if (!params.asset.bucket) {
    throw new Error(`Asset ${params.asset.id} missing bucket`);
  }

  if (!params.asset.storagePath) {
    throw new Error(`Asset ${params.asset.id} missing storagePath`);
  }

  const file = getStorage()
    .bucket(params.asset.bucket)
    .file(params.asset.storagePath);

  const [url] = await file.getSignedUrl({
    version: "v4",
    action: "read",
    expires: expiresAt,
  });

  return {
    url,
    urlExpiresAt: expiresAt,
  };
}
```

Your Fabric manifest generator from Step 1.2 should call this resolver.

---

# Client upload flow

The client only uploads the original to the landing zone.

```ts
// src/lib/storage/client-upload-original.ts

import {
  getStorage,
  ref,
  uploadBytesResumable,
  type UploadTask,
} from "firebase/storage";

export function uploadOriginalToLandingZone(params: {
  uid: string;
  uploadId: string;
  file: File;
}): UploadTask {
  const extension = extensionFromMime(params.file.type);

  const path = `client-uploads/${params.uid}/${params.uploadId}/original.${extension}`;

  const storage = getStorage();

  const fileRef = ref(storage, path);

  return uploadBytesResumable(fileRef, params.file, {
    contentType: params.file.type,
    customMetadata: {
      uploadId: params.uploadId,
      uid: params.uid,
      purpose: "magic-layers-original-upload",
    },
  });
}

function extensionFromMime(mime: string): "png" | "jpg" | "webp" {
  switch (mime) {
    case "image/png":
      return "png";

    case "image/jpeg":
      return "jpg";

    case "image/webp":
      return "webp";

    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported image MIME type: ${mime}`);
  }
}
```

After upload completes:

```txt
client tells backend uploadId
backend validates ownership
worker reads landing-zone file
worker verifies actual file type
worker writes canonical original
worker normalizes image
worker starts AI reconstruction
```

---

# Backend verification rule

Security Rules validate first-pass upload constraints.

The worker must still verify:

```txt
real MIME / magic bytes
image dimensions
pixel count
file size
malformed image
animated WebP / animated GIF rejection
EXIF stripping
orientation normalization
virus/malware scanning if needed later
```

Never trust client MIME alone.

---

# Fabric loading impact

When generating the Fabric manifest, image objects must receive runtime URLs:

```ts
{
  type: "Image",
  src: resolvedSignedUrl,
  crossOrigin: "anonymous",
  aiLayerId: layer.id,
  aiEditableLevel: layer.editableLevel
}
```

But the durable manifest should still preserve:

```ts
{
  assetId,
  bucket,
  storagePath
}
```

This means saved designs survive URL expiration.

---

# What goes into Firestore later

Not this:

```txt
base64 image
mask bytes
large Fabric JSON snapshots every second
signed URLs as permanent state
```

Only this:

```txt
assetId
bucket
storagePath
generation
mimeType
width
height
sizeBytes
checksum
current manifest assetId
job status
version pointer
```

Firestore structure is the next locked step. Storage is now only responsible for bytes.

---

# Non-negotiable invariants

Enforce these before connecting the AI pipeline:

```txt
No base64 assets in Firestore.

No base64 assets in Fabric JSON.

No public bucket for private user designs.

No permanent Firebase download URLs for private assets.

Every object has an assetId.

Every object has a canonical storagePath.

Every generated asset path is immutable.

Every write uses create-only behavior or unique path.

Every browser-loaded Fabric image has a CORS-safe HTTPS URL.

Every Fabric image URL can expire without breaking durable saved state.

Every AI job can be reconstructed from storagePath + asset metadata.

Every temp/intermediate asset has a lifecycle policy.

Every accepted layer asset is retained while the design exists.

Every original upload is preserved.

Every editor asset has optional export-quality equivalent.
```

---

Your repo should contain:


The storage layer is now ready for the next step: **Firestore data model and job state architecture**.

## ChatGPT Response 009

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 9bad06a9-b378-4430-9096-d20bd5dda30e, 51a7a80d-7655-44b8-b199-a9b64d0d05bd, bcc065fc-ae55-414a-b1ec-13c744d99baa -->

I’ll verify the research against primary sources, separate useful architecture from speculative claims, then replace our previous index with a cleaner plan if the evidence supports it.

The useful adjustment is the backbone: a LayerD-style decomposer should precede elementization for graphic designs, while Gemini remains for reasoning, routing, and QA—not pixel separation.

Yes, the research is helpful. But I would **not** adopt it as-is.

The useful core is this:

> The system should be a **raster-to-design-scene-graph reconstruction engine**, not a segmentation tool and not an SVG tracer.

That aligns with what we are building.

The weak part of the research is that it treats several research/backbone components as if they should become the product architecture. That is the wrong abstraction for your stack. Your durable architecture should remain:

```txt
Flat image
→ AI observations
→ canonical reconstruction document
→ Fabric manifest
→ existing Fabric editor
→ QA / fallback / repair
```

LayerD, Gemini, OCR, segmentation, vectorization, and inpainting are **replaceable engines** behind that contract.

---

# What I verified and what matters

Canva publicly positions Magic Layers as turning a flat design into an editable layout where users can select, move, edit text, change colors, and refine objects. Canva’s own press language says it analyzes structure, preserves layout relationships, restores text as live boxes, and separates components, not merely vector-tracing pixels. citeturn946761view0 citeturn946761view1

LayerD is directly relevant. It is an ICCV 2025 method for decomposing raster graphic designs into layers by iteratively extracting unoccluded foreground layers. The paper also explicitly says the problem is ill-posed, which supports our earlier rule: do not promise perfect original-source recovery. citeturn937293view0

LayerD’s repo is useful, but not enough alone. It provides a pipeline for decomposition, organization, SVG/PSD export, and text/vector/image classification; however, its OCR support is marked “coming soon,” so live editable text must remain your own separate subsystem. citeturn487002view1

CreatiParser is useful strategically, not as your day-one implementation. It confirms the right long-term direction: VLM-based text rendering protocols plus separate background/sticker layer generation. But it depends on a custom trained/fine-tuned architecture, not something you should build before your product contract is stable. citeturn612282view2

Google AI is useful for layout, object detection, and segmentation observations. Gemini docs now support normalized object boxes and segmentation masks, with `box_2d` coordinates normalized to `0–1000`, which fits our observation-schema approach. citeturn894441view1 citeturn894441view0

Fabric remains the right editor runtime, but not the source of truth. Fabric supports custom object properties, but those must be registered/serialized explicitly, which reinforces our internal-schema-first design. citeturn894441view3

---

# What we should take from the research

## Keep

1. **LayerD-style decomposition**
   
   Use iterative layer extraction / matting as one decomposition engine.

2. **Design-specific priors**
   
   Posters are not natural photos. Use flat-color ratio, hard edges, palette snapping, typography priors, alignment, and layout structure.

3. **Text as a rendering protocol**
   
   Do not just OCR text. Recover:

   ```txt
   string
   bbox
   font guess
   size
   weight
   color
   stroke
   shadow
   alignment
   rotation
   line height
   letter spacing
   fallback raster crop
   ```

4. **Render-diff validation**
   
   Before accepting editable text/vector, render it and compare against the original crop.

5. **Selective vectorization**
   
   Only vectorize high-confidence simple shapes/icons/logos. Do not vectorize photos, faces, food, products, or complex texture.

6. **Fallback-first UX**
   
   Every uncertain editable object needs a raster fallback.

7. **Quality gates**
   
   Recompose the generated Fabric document and compare it to the original before calling the job complete.

---

# What we should reject or modify

## Reject: “Use LayerD as the product backbone”

LayerD can be an engine. It should not define your schema, storage model, Fabric model, or UX.

Correct:

```txt
LayerD output → observations → resolver → your schema → Fabric
```

Wrong:

```txt
LayerD output → directly becomes your editor state
```

## Reject: “SVG/PSD as the real output”

SVG and PSD are exports. Your real product output is your own canonical design document plus Fabric projection.

Correct:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
→ AiFabricManifest
→ Fabric JSON
→ optional SVG/PSD/PNG/PDF exports
```

## Reject: “Train/fine-tune CreatiParser-style models early”

Not now. The text-rendering protocol idea is useful, but training Qwen/SDXL-style systems is not the first build. Your user-correction dataset must come first.

## Reject: “Fully editable everything”

The correct promise stays:

```txt
Editable where confident.
Faithful where uncertain.
Original preserved always.
```

## Modify: “Phased plan”

We will not use separate product phases. The day-one architecture must support the full long-term system, even if some engines are initially conservative.

---

# New plan index from scratch

This replaces the previous plan.

No phases. No separate stages. This is the strict master index we follow one point at a time.

---

## 0. Product contract and non-negotiable rules

Define exactly what the feature promises.

Core rule:

```txt
The first reconstructed render must visually match the original.
Editability is allowed only when confidence is high.
Fallback is mandatory when confidence is not high.
```

Output promise:

```txt
Flat image → editable Fabric design document with confidence and fallbacks.
```

Not:

```txt
Flat image → perfect original Canva/PSD source file.
```

---

## 1. Canonical reconstruction schema

Create the internal source of truth:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
AiReconstructedLayer
AiObservation
AiAssetRef
AiConfidence
AiFallback
AiLayerGeometry
AiLayerDecision
```

This schema must represent:

```txt
text
raster layers
vector candidates
clean background
groups
z-order
fallbacks
provenance
confidence
quality scores
```

AI models must not output Fabric JSON directly.

---

## 2. Fabric manifest contract

Create:

```txt
AiFabricManifest
```

This wraps:

```txt
fabricJson
assets
layerIndex
canvas
source reconstruction metadata
runtime metadata
```

Fabric receives only:

```ts
canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest.fabricJson)
```

The manifest remains a projection, not the source of truth.

---

## 3. Firebase/GCS asset model

Define immutable storage paths for:

```txt
original image
normalized image
raw model outputs
masks
RGBA layers
fallback crops
clean background
reconstruction document
Fabric manifest
previews
exports
```

Firestore stores metadata and job state only. Large JSON and image assets live in Storage/GCS. This is required because Firestore documents are capped at 1 MiB. citeturn894441view2

---

## 4. Firestore job and design state model

Define collections:

```txt
workspaces
designs
designVersions
aiLayerJobs
aiLayerJobEvents
assets
exports
```

Define job states:

```txt
created
uploaded
normalizing
observing
decomposing
recovering_text
elementizing
vectorizing
repairing_background
resolving_scene
generating_fabric
validating
completed
failed
cancelled
```

Even though the user experiences one action, backend state must be explicit.

---

## 5. Job orchestration

Use:

```txt
Next.js API = job creation / auth / editor routes
Cloud Run worker = heavy AI processing
Firebase Storage/GCS = files
Firestore = state
Google AI = layout/vision reasoning
Fabric editor = final interactive canvas
```

Do not run decomposition inside a Next.js request.

---

## 6. Upload and normalization

Every job starts with:

```txt
client upload
server verification
EXIF orientation fix
format normalization
sRGB conversion
dimension caps
noise cleanup
working-scale generation
original preservation
```

Outputs:

```txt
original asset
normalized asset
image metadata
perceptual hash
```

---

## 7. Routing and design diagnosis

Before decomposition, classify the input:

```txt
graphic poster
photo-heavy composite
menu/document-like design
logo/icon/flat illustration
AI-generated banner
mixed
```

Routing decides which engines get priority:

```txt
graphic design → LayerD-style decomposition + text recovery
photo-heavy → conservative object segmentation + background reconstruction
text-heavy → OCR/text protocol priority
flat illustration → vectorization priority
```

This is not a separate user-facing mode. It is internal routing.

---

## 8. Observation generation

Generate raw AI observations before creating layers.

Observation sources:

```txt
Gemini layout observations
Gemini object boxes
Gemini segmentation masks
OCR observations
LayerD raw RGBA layers
connected components
vector candidates
background repair candidates
palette observations
```

Observation rule:

```txt
Models observe.
Resolver decides.
Fabric displays.
```

---

## 9. Decomposition engine adapter

Create a common interface:

```ts
DecompositionEngine {
  run(input): Promise<DecompositionObservation[]>
}
```

Engines behind it:

```txt
Gemini segmentation
LayerD-style decomposition
SAM/BiRefNet-style masks if available
simple connected-components fallback
manual crop fallback
```

LayerD should enter here, not above the schema.

---

## 10. Text recovery system

Text must be independent from LayerD.

Inputs:

```txt
OCR results
Gemini layout text regions
text masks
original crops
```

Outputs:

```txt
editable text candidate
text raster fallback
font/style estimate
render validation score
```

Decision:

```txt
high confidence → fabric.Textbox
medium confidence → fabric.Textbox + visible fallback toggle
low confidence → raster fallback only
```

This is one of the highest-risk parts of the system. Text must never be silently rewritten.

---

## 11. Elementization

Convert raw RGBA layers and masks into actual design objects.

Process:

```txt
connected components
bbox extraction
rotated bbox if needed
contour extraction
small-component merge
duplicate removal
type classification
component-to-object conversion
```

Outputs:

```txt
text object candidates
shape candidates
raster object candidates
logo/icon candidates
decorations
groups
unknown objects
```

This is the bridge from “layers” to “editable design.”

---

## 12. Vector recovery

Only run vectorization on eligible components.

Eligibility:

```txt
flat color
clean alpha boundary
low texture entropy
limited color count
reasonable path complexity
not photographic
not live text
```

Engines:

```txt
Potrace for binary/monochrome shapes
VTracer for colored flat artwork
custom rect/circle/line detector
SVG path simplifier
```

Output decision:

```txt
vector_editable
or
raster_fallback
```

---

## 13. Raster layer generation

For photo/product/person/complex artwork:

```txt
apply alpha mask
crop to bbox
generate editor-resolution PNG
generate optional export-resolution PNG
store mask
store original crop fallback
```

Fabric uses editor PNGs. Server export can use export-resolution assets.

---

## 14. Clean background reconstruction

Create a background the user can expose when moving objects.

Input:

```txt
original image
combined foreground masks
text masks
object masks
```

Output:

```txt
clean_background.png
background confidence
background fallback
```

Use conservative repair. Do not let generative repair invent meaningful content.

---

## 15. Z-order resolver

Compute stack order from:

```txt
LayerD extraction order
Gemini layout guess
bbox overlap
mask overlap
object class
text priority
shadow/edge evidence
background priority
```

Default order:

```txt
locked reference
clean background
large shapes
decorations
image blocks
photo subjects/products
logos/icons
badges
headline text
small text
overlays
```

Manual reorder stays mandatory.

---

## 16. Group resolver

Detect semantic groups:

```txt
button = shape + text
badge = shape + text + decoration
menu item = text + price + divider
logo lockup = icon + wordmark
product group = product + shadow
headline block = text + background shape
```

Groups should be metadata-first. Do not overuse Fabric.Group until group editing behavior is stable.

---

## 17. Scene resolver

This is the central decision engine.

Inputs:

```txt
all observations
assets
confidence scores
routing result
quality thresholds
```

Output:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
```

The resolver decides:

```txt
which observations become layers
which are rejected
which become editable text
which become vectors
which stay raster
which require fallback
which need review
```

---

## 18. Fabric generator

Convert:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
→ AiFabricManifest
→ Fabric JSON
```

Mapping:

```txt
text_editable → fabric.Textbox
vector_editable → fabric.Rect / Circle / Path / Polygon / Line
raster_masked → fabric.Image
clean_background → fabric.Image
locked_reference → hidden locked fabric.Image
group metadata → layer panel grouping
```

Every Fabric object carries AI metadata:

```txt
aiLayerId
aiLayerType
aiEditableLevel
aiConfidence
aiFallbackAssetId
aiSource
```

---

## 19. Visual recomposition validator

After Fabric JSON is generated:

```txt
render Fabric reconstruction
compare to original
score pixel difference
score SSIM
score text exactness
score mask drift
score z-order conflicts
flag weak regions
```

The result updates:

```txt
quality.needsReview
quality.visualMatchScore
layer warnings
job warnings
```

---

## 20. Text safety validator

Special hard gate for text.

Checks:

```txt
OCR(original crop)
OCR(reconstructed render)
string equality / distance
bbox overlap
text mask IoU
visual crop difference
```

Rule:

```txt
If recovered text changes semantic content, block editable text and use raster fallback.
```

This prevents the most damaging class of failure.

---

## 21. User-facing layer panel

Your existing Fabric editor needs AI-specific layer UI:

```txt
name
type
editable level
confidence
fallback available
source
warning badge
visibility
lock
delete
duplicate
reorder
restore from original
```

AI reconstruction without a confidence-aware layer panel will feel broken.

---

## 22. Manual repair tools

Minimum repair tools:

```txt
restore from original
replace layer asset
regenerate selected layer
convert raster text to editable text
keep text as raster
split layer
merge layers
erase/restore mask
reorder layer
ungroup
```

These tools turn imperfect AI into a usable workflow.

---

## 23. Save/versioning model

Persist:

```txt
current Fabric JSON
current reconstruction pointer
asset references
user corrections
version snapshots
job metadata
```

Rules:

```txt
do not autosave huge JSON repeatedly to Firestore
do not store base64
store snapshots in GCS
store current pointers/state in Firestore
debounce client writes
```

---

## 24. Export system

Support in this order:

```txt
PNG preview
high-res PNG export
JPG export
SVG export
PDF export
ZIP layers export
PSD export later
```

PSD is useful, but it should not drive the system architecture.

---

## 25. Repair loop

Regenerate only the failing part.

Examples:

```txt
bad text → rerun OCR/text protocol on crop
bad mask → rerun segmentation on bbox
bad vector → downgrade to raster fallback
bad background → rerun background repair
bad z-order → recompute local stack order
```

Do not rerun the full job unless necessary.

---

## 26. Cost and latency controls

Hard limits from day one:

```txt
max image dimensions
max pixel count
max layer count
max OCR regions
max segmentation regions
max vector path count
max background repair area
max job runtime
max retries
```

Also:

```txt
deduplicate by image hash
cache immutable assets
use editor-resolution assets
generate export-resolution assets lazily
delete diagnostics by lifecycle policy
```

---

## 27. Feedback dataset

Store user corrections as structured signals:

```txt
deleted layer
merged layer
split layer
text edited
font changed
fallback restored
mask repaired
z-order changed
export completed
job abandoned
```

This becomes your private improvement loop.

---

# The corrected architecture

```txt
User uploads image
↓
Normalize image
↓
Generate observations
  - Gemini layout / boxes / masks
  - OCR
  - LayerD-style decomposition
  - connected components
  - vector candidates
↓
Resolve scene
↓
Create AiReconstructionDocument
↓
Generate assets
↓
Generate AiFabricManifest
↓
Load manifest.fabricJson into existing Fabric editor
↓
Validate visual match and text safety
↓
Expose confidence/fallback UX
↓
User edits
↓
Save versions and corrections
↓
Export
```

---

# The biggest architectural change from the pasted research

The pasted research says, effectively:

```txt
Find the best decomposition pipeline.
```

Our corrected version says:

```txt
Build a stable reconstruction contract.
Then plug decomposition engines behind it.
```

That is the right long-term move.

LayerD may improve. Gemini segmentation may improve. OCR models may change. Vectorizers may change. Your Fabric editor may evolve. The invariant should be:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument → AiFabricManifest → Fabric editor
```

That is the plan we should follow strictly from here.

Next point is **0. Product contract and non-negotiable rules**.

I’ll treat Step 0 as the binding product, legal, and technical contract before any schema or model work. I’ll verify public claims and research constraints, then lock the promise, invariants, failure boundaries, and acceptance gates.

# Step 0 — Product contract and non-negotiable rules

We are only locking **Step 0** here. No schema, Firebase model, workers, or Fabric conversion yet.

The correct product contract is:

> **Magic Layers converts a single flat still image into an editable Fabric design document by reconstructing likely design objects, while preserving the original visual appearance and providing fallbacks whenever reconstruction confidence is not high.**

The important phrase is **likely design objects**. A flattened raster image has lost source-layer truth. LayerD states this directly: graphic layer decomposition is ill-posed, there can be multiple valid decompositions, and even layer granularity can vary. That means your product must never claim exact original Canva/PSD/Figma recovery. It should claim high-fidelity editable reconstruction. citeturn145876view0

---

## 0.1 Market reality we should align with, but not blindly copy

Canva’s public promise is aggressive: flat designs become editable layouts; users can select, move, edit text, change colors, and avoid regenerating the whole image. Their newsroom says Magic Layers restores text as live boxes, separates elements, preserves layout structure, and is not just vector tracing. citeturn345566view1turn659282view0turn659282view1

The technical implication is clear:

```txt
Wrong target:
flat image → SVG trace

Correct target:
flat image → reconstructed design scene graph → Fabric editor
```

But Canva’s wording is too broad for your first version. Their own related Grab Text docs admit font matching is conditional: exact matching only works if the font exists in their library; otherwise they use the closest font. They also describe the safer approach as layering fresh editable text on top rather than destructively overwriting the original image. citeturn659282view3

That confirms our rule:

```txt
Editable text is not guaranteed.
Exact font recovery is not guaranteed.
Original text pixels must remain recoverable.
```

The Canva “Palestine” incident is the failure class to avoid: the feature reportedly changed visible text while converting an image into editable components, and Canva said the feature was not supposed to visibly alter designs. citeturn659282view7

So Step 0 must include a hard safety rule:

```txt
The system must never silently rewrite visible text.
```

---

# 0.2 Final public product promise

Use this externally:

> **Turn a flat image into editable layers. Move, resize, hide, replace, and edit recovered text or design elements where AI confidence is high. The original image is always preserved.**

Do **not** use:

```txt
“Perfectly converts any image into editable layers.”

“Recover the original Canva / PSD / Figma file.”

“Every object becomes fully editable.”

“Exact fonts, exact vectors, exact source layers.”

“AI recreates the original design file.”
```

The product is not source-file recovery. It is **faithful reconstruction with controlled editability**.

---

# 0.3 Input contract

Day-one input should be:

```ts
type MagicLayersInput = {
  kind: "single_flat_still_image";
  supportedMimeTypes: [
    "image/png",
    "image/jpeg",
    "image/webp"
  ];
};
```

Canva recommends JPEG and PNG for Magic Layers. Gemini’s image-understanding docs support PNG, JPEG, WEBP, HEIC, and HEIF, but for your product I would support only PNG/JPEG/WebP initially because those map cleanly to browser upload, Firebase Storage, and Fabric image loading. citeturn345566view1turn313491view0

Do not support in Step 0 contract:

```txt
multi-page PDF
animated GIF
video
PSD upload
Figma import
AI prompt-only generation
HTML import
presentation import
document layout import
```

Those are separate products or later import modes.

---

# 0.4 Output contract

The output is not “layers” in the casual sense. The output is:

```txt
A Fabric-loadable editable design document
+
a canonical reconstruction record
+
asset references
+
confidence/fallback metadata
```

At the product level, the user sees:

```txt
background
objects
text
shapes
images
logos/icons
decorations
groups
fallback layers
original reference
```

At the engineering level, every visible result must answer:

```txt
What is this layer?
How editable is it?
Where did it come from?
How confident are we?
What is the fallback?
```

If a layer cannot answer those five questions, it should not enter the editor as an AI-reconstructed layer.

---

# 0.5 The core invariant

This is the most important rule in the entire system:

```txt
The first reconstructed render must visually match the original image.
```

If visual fidelity and editability conflict, visual fidelity wins.

Correct behavior:

```txt
uncertain text → keep raster fallback
uncertain logo → keep raster fallback
uncertain vector shape → keep PNG
uncertain mask edge → preserve original crop
uncertain background repair → keep original background fallback
```

Wrong behavior:

```txt
force OCR text with wrong letters
force logo into bad vector path
hallucinate background content
split one object into nonsense pieces
invent missing elements
change wording
change brand marks
change semantic content
```

This is where most “AI layer” products will lose trust.

---

# 0.6 User-facing capability contract

The user can always do these after conversion:

```txt
select layer
move layer
resize layer
rotate layer
hide layer
lock layer
delete layer
duplicate layer
reorder layer
restore from original
```

The user can only do these when confidence is high:

```txt
edit text
change font
recolor vector shape
edit vector shape
replace subject/image
regenerate selected layer
regenerate background
```

That distinction must be visible in the UI. Do not let users discover model uncertainty by breaking the design.

---

# 0.7 Layer editability levels

These are the only editability levels allowed in the product contract:

```ts
type MagicLayerEditableLevel =
  | "locked_reference"
  | "text_editable"
  | "vector_editable"
  | "raster_masked"
  | "raster_clean_background"
  | "raster_fallback"
  | "group_editable"
  | "unknown_confidence";
```

Their meanings:

```txt
locked_reference
Original uploaded image. Hidden or locked. Used for compare, restore, QA, and repair.

text_editable
Fabric Textbox created from OCR + style estimation + validation.

vector_editable
Fabric vector object or path. Only for simple high-confidence shapes/icons.

raster_masked
Transparent PNG extracted from the image. Move/resize/rotate/edit mask, but not semantically editable.

raster_clean_background
Reconstructed background behind extracted objects.

raster_fallback
Faithful image crop used when semantic reconstruction is uncertain.

group_editable
Logical group of objects, such as badge, button, price block, product + shadow.

unknown_confidence
Detected visual entity with uncertain classification.
```

Do not let `layer.type` imply editability.

Bad:

```ts
{
  type: "text"
}
```

Correct:

```ts
{
  type: "text",
  editableLevel: "text_editable"
}
```

or:

```ts
{
  type: "text",
  editableLevel: "raster_fallback"
}
```

A text-looking area can be live text, logo lettering, stylized typography, corrupted AI text, handwriting, or an unreadable raster decoration. Those are not equivalent.

---

# 0.8 Non-negotiable product rules

## Rule 1 — Preserve the original image

Every AI job must include a locked original reference layer.

```txt
required:
original image asset
original dimensions
original hash
locked reference layer
restore path
```

The original image must never be overwritten, destructively modified, or replaced by generated content.

---

## Rule 2 — No silent semantic changes

Especially for text.

The system may extract, classify, and reconstruct text, but it must not “improve,” translate, rewrite, normalize, censor, correct, or substitute visible words.

Hard gate:

```txt
If OCR/reconstructed text differs semantically from original text,
do not expose it as editable text by default.
Use raster fallback.
Flag for user review.
```

This is not just quality. It is trust and safety.

---

## Rule 3 — Confidence must be explicit

Every reconstructed layer must carry confidence.

Minimum confidence dimensions:

```ts
type MagicLayerConfidence = {
  overall: number;
  classification?: number;
  bbox?: number;
  mask?: number;
  alpha?: number;
  ocr?: number;
  textStyle?: number;
  font?: number;
  color?: number;
  vector?: number;
  zIndex?: number;
  backgroundRepair?: number;
  visualFidelity?: number;
};
```

Do not use a single generic score. A layer can have correct OCR but poor font match, good bbox but bad mask, or good mask but wrong z-order.

---

## Rule 4 — Every uncertain layer needs fallback

Fallback is mandatory unless confidence is near-perfect.

```txt
text_editable → original text crop fallback
vector_editable → original raster crop fallback
raster_masked → original crop or reference fallback
clean_background → original background/reference fallback
unknown_confidence → fallback required
```

No fallback means no trust.

---

## Rule 5 — Editability must be earned

A layer becomes editable only after validation.

```txt
Text:
OCR confidence high
string preserved
bbox acceptable
rendered text close to original
font/style acceptable

Vector:
shape is simple
path count acceptable
color match acceptable
rendered vector close to original
not photographic
not text

Raster:
mask acceptable
edge quality acceptable
not duplicate noise
z-order plausible

Background:
repair does not visibly corrupt core content
does not invent semantic objects
```

The default should be conservative.

---

## Rule 6 — AI output must be constrained

Your Google AI / Gemini calls must return structured observations, not free-form editor instructions.

Firebase AI Logic and Gemini support structured JSON / enum output, which is exactly what we need for classification and observation extraction. citeturn345566view2turn659282view4

Bad:

```txt
“Here is the Fabric JSON.”
```

Correct:

```json
{
  "elements": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "box_2d": [120, 80, 230, 760],
      "confidence": 0.92,
      "zIndexGuess": 8
    }
  ]
}
```

Gemini’s object detection uses normalized `[ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]` coordinates scaled to `[0, 1000]`, which later must be converted to absolute pixels. citeturn313491view1turn313491view3

---

## Rule 7 — Fabric is runtime, not source of truth

Fabric is your editor/runtime projection.

It should not be the canonical AI reconstruction model.

Fabric does support custom properties, but its docs say they must be explicitly included in serialization; Fabric also warns not to build new application logic around the legacy object `type` value. citeturn659282view5turn659282view6

Correct architecture:

```txt
AI observations
→ canonical reconstruction document
→ Fabric manifest
→ canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest.fabricJson)
```

Wrong architecture:

```txt
AI directly writes Fabric JSON
→ editor treats it as truth
```

Fabric JSON is editable UI state. The reconstruction document is the durable intelligence layer.

---

# 0.9 Acceptance gates for Step 0

A Magic Layers job may be marked successful only when these are true:

```txt
original image preserved
first render visually matches original
all visible layers have type
all visible layers have editability level
all AI layers have confidence
all non-perfect layers have fallback
all text layers pass text safety gate
all image assets are restorable
all Fabric objects carry AI identity metadata later
low-confidence objects are visibly marked in UI
user can undo/restore AI reconstruction decisions
```

A job must be marked `needs_review` when:

```txt
text confidence is low
font confidence is low
vector render mismatch is high
background repair is suspicious
z-order conflicts are detected
visual diff exceeds threshold
too many unknown layers exist
important object is only partially extracted
```

A job must be marked `failed` or `fallback_only` when:

```txt
image cannot be decoded
image dimensions unsupported
normalization fails
original cannot be preserved
no meaningful layer extraction is possible
first render cannot approximate original
AI output violates schema
text safety validator detects semantic mutation
```

---

# 0.10 Product UX contract

The layer panel must expose AI uncertainty directly.

Each row should show:

```txt
Layer name
Layer type
Editable level
Confidence
Fallback indicator
Warning indicator
Source indicator
Visibility
Lock
Reorder
Restore
```

Example layer rows:

```txt
Headline
text · editable · 94%

Logo
logo · raster fallback · 61%

Product bottle
product · masked raster · 88%

Clean background
background · generated · 79%

Original reference
locked · source · 100%
```

Bad UI:

```txt
Layer 1
Layer 2
Layer 3
```

Good UI:

```txt
Headline — editable text — high confidence
Logo — raster fallback — low vector confidence
Person — masked image — medium edge confidence
```

This turns AI imperfection into controlled product behavior.

# 0.12 Step 0 definition of done

Step 0 is complete only when these decisions are accepted:

```txt
1. The feature is defined as reconstruction, not source-file recovery.

2. The public promise is conservative:
   editable where confident, faithful where uncertain.

3. The original image is always preserved as locked reference.

4. First render fidelity is higher priority than editability.

5. Text cannot be silently rewritten.

6. Every AI layer must have confidence, provenance, and fallback.

7. Fabric is the editor projection, not the canonical AI model.

8. AI model outputs must be schema-constrained observations.

9. Low-confidence layers remain useful through raster fallback.

10. UI must expose confidence and fallback state.
```

The locked Step 0 contract:

```txt
Flat image
→ faithful reconstructed design
→ editable where validated
→ fallback where uncertain
→ original always preserved
```

This is the foundation. Step 1 is **Canonical reconstruction schema**, but we should not enter it until this contract is treated as fixed.

# Step 1 — Canonical reconstruction schema

This step defines the **source of truth** for Magic Layers.

The canonical schema is **not Fabric JSON**, **not SVG**, **not PSD**, and **not raw model output**.

It is your internal durable representation:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
```

Everything else is derived from it:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
→ AiFabricManifest
→ Fabric JSON
→ editor
→ exports
```

The core reason is that raster-to-layer reconstruction is ambiguous. LayerD explicitly treats raster graphic layer decomposition as ill-posed: layer count, granularity, order, and even “correctness” can vary. So your system needs a schema that records evidence, decisions, confidence, fallbacks, and provenance, not just final objects. citeturn286188view0

---

# 1.1 Hard rule

The schema must separate:

```txt
observations
from
resolved layers
```

Correct:

```txt
Gemini says: "this looks like text"
OCR says: "SUMMER SALE"
LayerD says: "this RGBA region is frontmost"
Vectorizer says: "this looks like a rounded rectangle"
Resolver decides: "create editable Textbox with raster fallback"
```

Wrong:

```txt
Gemini returns Fabric JSON
Fabric JSON becomes source of truth
```

Gemini structured output can produce schema-constrained JSON, but Google’s own docs still say app code must validate outputs because schema-valid JSON does not guarantee semantically correct values. citeturn286188view1

---

# 1.2 What this schema must support long term

The schema must support these without migration pain:

```txt
Gemini layout observations
Gemini object boxes
Gemini segmentation masks
LayerD raster layers
OCR observations
text styling observations
vector candidates
connected components
clean background candidates
z-order evidence
group evidence
visual diff validation
text safety validation
manual user corrections
future trained model outputs
```

Do **not** design this around your first model stack. Design it around the invariant:

```txt
models observe
resolver decides
Fabric displays
user corrects
system learns
```

---

# 1.3 Why the schema must be richer than Fabric

Fabric is your editor runtime. It should not be your reconstruction truth.

Fabric supports custom object properties, but they must be explicitly registered and passed through serialization. Its docs also warn that object `type` is for Fabric serialization/deserialization and should not drive app logic. citeturn286188view2turn286188view3

So Fabric objects should carry only lightweight identity metadata:

```txt
aiLayerId
aiLayerType
aiEditableLevel
aiConfidence
aiFallbackAssetId
```

The full reconstruction record stays outside Fabric.

---

```ts
] as const;

export const AI_DECISION_STRATEGIES = [
  "use_locked_reference",
  "use_clean_background",
  "use_editable_text",
  "use_vector",
  "use_masked_raster",
  "use_raster_fallback",
  "use_group",
  "reject_duplicate",
  "reject_low_confidence",
] as const;
```

Important: Gemini object detection returns `box_2d` coordinates normalized to `[0, 1000]`, so the schema must preserve the raw Gemini box and the normalized pixel-space box. citeturn176009view0

---

# 1.7 Geometry helpers

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/schema/geometry.ts

import type { BBox, GeminiBox1000 } from "./reconstruction.types";

export function geminiBox1000ToBBox(
  box: GeminiBox1000,
  imageWidth: number,
  imageHeight: number
): BBox {
  const [yMin, xMin, yMax, xMax] = box;

  return {
    x: Math.round((xMin / 1000) * imageWidth),
    y: Math.round((yMin / 1000) * imageHeight),
    width: Math.round(((xMax - xMin) / 1000) * imageWidth),
    height: Math.round(((yMax - yMin) / 1000) * imageHeight),
  };
}

export function clampBBoxToCanvas(
  bbox: BBox,
  canvasWidth: number,
  canvasHeight: number
): BBox {
  const x = Math.max(0, Math.min(bbox.x, canvasWidth));
  const y = Math.max(0, Math.min(bbox.y, canvasHeight));

  return {
    x,
    y,
    width: Math.max(0, Math.min(bbox.width, canvasWidth - x)),
    height: Math.max(0, Math.min(bbox.height, canvasHeight - y)),
  };
}

export function bboxArea(bbox: BBox): number {
  return Math.max(0, bbox.width) * Math.max(0, bbox.height);
}

export function bboxIntersectionArea(a: BBox, b: BBox): number {
  const x1 = Math.max(a.x, b.x);
  const y1 = Math.max(a.y, b.y);
  const x2 = Math.min(a.x + a.width, b.x + b.width);
  const y2 = Math.min(a.y + a.height, b.y + b.height);

  return Math.max(0, x2 - x1) * Math.max(0, y2 - y1);
}

export function bboxIoU(a: BBox, b: BBox): number {
  const intersection = bboxIntersectionArea(a, b);
  const union = bboxArea(a) + bboxArea(b) - intersection;

  if (union <= 0) return 0;

  return intersection / union;
}
```

---

# 1.8 Asset reference

The canonical schema stores **references**, not bytes.

Firestore documents have a hard 1 MiB document size limit, so raw masks, base64 images, full model outputs, large SVGs, and previews should not be embedded inside Firestore documents. They must be referenced as assets. citeturn298492view0

```ts
export type AiAssetRef = {
  id: string;

  kind: AiAssetKind;

  /**
   * Storage-specific fields are deliberately generic here.
   * Step 3 will define exact Firebase/GCS storage paths.
   */
  bucket?: string;
  storagePath?: string;

  /**
   * Runtime URL only.
   * Never treat signed URLs or Firebase download URLs as canonical identity.
   */
  url?: string;
  urlExpiresAt?: number;

  mimeType?: string;

  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  sizeBytes?: number;

  checksum?: {
    algorithm: "sha256" | "md5";
    value: string;
  };

  metadata?: {
    workspaceId?: string;
    designId?: string;
    jobId?: string;
    layerId?: string;
    assetId?: string;
    source?: AiSource;
    createdAt?: number;
    schemaVersion?: string;
    pipelineVersion?: string;
  };
};
```

---

# 1.9 Confidence model

Do **not** use one score.

A layer can have excellent OCR and poor font match. A mask can have correct bbox and bad edge alpha. A background can be visually plausible but semantically risky.

```ts
export type AiConfidence = {
  overall: number;

  classification?: number;

  geometry?: number;
  bbox?: number;
  polygon?: number;

  mask?: number;
  alpha?: number;
  matte?: number;

  ocr?: number;
  textString?: number;
  textStyle?: number;
  font?: number;
  color?: number;

  vector?: number;
  pathSimplicity?: number;

  zIndex?: number;
  grouping?: number;

  backgroundRepair?: number;

  visualFidelity?: number;
  textSafety?: number;
};

export function clampConfidence(value: number | undefined): number | undefined {
  if (typeof value !== "number" || Number.isNaN(value)) return undefined;
  return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value));
}

export function computeOverallConfidence(confidence: AiConfidence): number {
  const values = Object.entries(confidence)
    .filter(([key]) => key !== "overall")
    .map(([, value]) => value)
    .filter((value): value is number => typeof value === "number");

  if (!values.length) return clampConfidence(confidence.overall) ?? 0;

  return values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / values.length;
}
```

---

# 1.10 Fallback model

Every uncertain layer needs a fallback.

Use an array, not a single fallback. Long term, a layer may have:

```txt
original crop
rasterized editable text
previous user-approved version
locked reference restore
manual replacement
```

```ts
export type AiFallback = {
  id: string;

  strategy:
    | "locked_reference"
    | "original_crop"
    | "raster_layer"
    | "rasterized_editable"
    | "previous_version"
    | "manual_user"
    | "none";

  assetId?: string;

  bbox?: BBox;

  reason: string;

  visibleByDefault: boolean;

  createdAt: number;
};
```

# 1.12 Observations

Observations are raw evidence.

They are not editor layers.

```ts

```

Text deserves a rich protocol because text reconstruction is not just OCR. De-rendering stylized text research treats raster text editing as recovering text, location, size, font, style, effects, and hidden background. CreatiParser follows the same direction by parsing text into a structured rendering protocol for reconstruction and editing. citeturn674926search1turn674926search0

LayerD is especially relevant here because it decomposes graphic designs into editable raster layers, and its project page explicitly describes graphic designs as containing typography, embellishments, vector shapes, and image materials. That supports keeping “RGBA layer observation” separate from final text/vector/raster objects. citeturn867101search12

# 1.14 Layer decision record

This is critical.

You need to know **why** the resolver exposed something as editable text, vector, raster, or fallback.

```ts
export type AiLayerDecision = {
  strategy: AiDecisionStrategy;

  selectedObservationIds: string[];

  rejectedObservationIds?: string[];

  reasonCodes: string[];

  thresholds?: Record<string, number>;

  decidedBy: "system" | "manual_user";

  decidedAt: number;
};
```

Example reason codes:

```txt
high_ocr_confidence
text_safety_passed
font_match_approximate
vector_render_diff_passed
mask_edge_low_confidence
background_hallucination_risk
duplicate_component_rejected
z_order_resolved_by_layerd_order
fallback_required
```

These reason codes later become debugging, analytics, and training data.

# 1.16 Groups as metadata-first

Do not force Fabric groups into the canonical schema.

Use logical groups first.

```ts
export type AiResolvedGroup = {
  id: string;

  name: string;

  role:
    | "button"
    | "badge"
    | "price_block"
    | "menu_item"
    | "logo_lockup"
    | "social_handle"
    | "headline_block"
    | "product_group"
    | "pattern"
    | "unknown";

  childLayerIds: string[];

  bbox: BBox;

  zIndexRange: {
    min: number;
    max: number;
  };

  confidence: AiConfidence;

  sourceObservationIds: string[];

  lockedChildren?: boolean;

  createdAt: number;
};
```

Reason: group semantics and editor grouping behavior are different. A badge may be logically grouped in the layer panel, but still remain individually editable as shape + text.

# 1.18 Capability resolver

Capabilities should come from `editableLevel`, not from `type`.

```ts
export function capabilitiesForEditableLevel(
  editableLevel: AiEditableLevel
): AiLayerCapability[] {
  switch (editableLevel) {
    case "locked_reference":
      return ["hide", "lock", "restore_from_original"];

    case "text_editable":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "delete",
        "duplicate",
        "reorder",
        "edit_text",
        "change_font",
        "recolor",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "vector_editable":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "delete",
        "duplicate",
        "reorder",
        "recolor",
        "edit_vector",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "raster_masked":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "delete",
        "duplicate",
        "reorder",
        "replace_asset",
        "crop",
        "edit_mask",
        "regenerate",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "raster_clean_background":
      return [
        "select",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "replace_asset",
        "regenerate",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "raster_fallback":
    case "unknown_confidence":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "delete",
        "duplicate",
        "reorder",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    case "group_editable":
      return [
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "delete",
        "duplicate",
        "reorder",
        "ungroup",
        "restore_from_original",
      ];

    default:
      return ["select", "hide"];
  }
}
```

# 1.19 Runtime validation with Zod

Use TypeScript for developer ergonomics and Zod for runtime validation. Zod is a TypeScript-first validation library designed to validate unknown data into typed values, which is exactly what you need for AI and worker outputs. citeturn686836search0

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/schema/reconstruction.zod.ts

import { z } from "zod";
import {
  AI_ASSET_KINDS,
  AI_DECISION_STRATEGIES,
  AI_EDITABLE_LEVELS,
  AI_LAYER_TYPES,
  AI_OBSERVATION_KINDS,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
  AI_SOURCES,
} from "./constants";

const BBoxSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
  width: z.number().nonnegative(),
  height: z.number().nonnegative(),
});

const PointSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
});

const ConfidenceSchema = z.object({
  overall: z.number().min(0).max(1),

  classification: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  geometry: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  bbox: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  polygon: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  mask: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  alpha: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  matte: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  ocr: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  textString: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  textStyle: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  font: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  color: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  vector: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  pathSimplicity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  zIndex: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  grouping: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  backgroundRepair: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  visualFidelity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
  textSafety: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
});

const GeminiBox1000Schema = z
  .tuple([z.number(), z.number(), z.number(), z.number()])
  .refine(
    ([yMin, xMin, yMax, xMax]) =>
      yMin >= 0 &&
      xMin >= 0 &&
      yMax <= 1000 &&
      xMax <= 1000 &&
      yMax >= yMin &&
      xMax >= xMin,
    "Invalid Gemini 0-1000 box"
  );

const TransformSchema = z.object({
  left: z.number(),
  top: z.number(),

  width: z.number().nonnegative(),
  height: z.number().nonnegative(),

  scaleX: z.number(),
  scaleY: z.number(),

  angle: z.number(),

  opacity: z.number().min(0).max(1),

  flipX: z.boolean().optional(),
  flipY: z.boolean().optional(),

  skewX: z.number().optional(),
  skewY: z.number().optional(),

  originX: z.enum(["left", "center", "right"]),
  originY: z.enum(["top", "center", "bottom"]),

  matrix: z
    .tuple([
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
      z.number(),
    ])
    .optional(),
});

const GeometrySchema = z.object({
  coordinateSpace: z.literal("canvas_px"),

  bbox: BBoxSchema,

  renderBounds: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  polygon: z.array(PointSchema).optional(),

  quad: z
    .tuple([PointSchema, PointSchema, PointSchema, PointSchema])
    .optional(),

  originalBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),
  normalizedBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),
  workingScaleBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  geminiBox1000: GeminiBox1000Schema.optional(),

  transform: TransformSchema,
});

const AssetRefSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),

  kind: z.enum(AI_ASSET_KINDS),

  bucket: z.string().optional(),
  storagePath: z.string().optional(),

  url: z.string().url().optional(),
  urlExpiresAt: z.number().optional(),

  mimeType: z.string().optional(),

  width: z.number().positive().optional(),
  height: z.number().positive().optional(),

  sizeBytes: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  checksum: z
    .object({
      algorithm: z.enum(["sha256", "md5"]),
      value: z.string().min(1),
    })
    .optional(),

  metadata: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional(),
});

const FallbackSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),

  strategy: z.enum([
    "locked_reference",
    "original_crop",
    "raster_layer",
    "rasterized_editable",
    "previous_version",
    "manual_user",
    "none",
  ]),

  assetId: z.string().optional(),

  bbox: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  reason: z.string().min(1),

  visibleByDefault: z.boolean(),

  createdAt: z.number(),
});

const ProvenanceSchema = z.object({
  primarySource: z.enum(AI_SOURCES),

  contributingSources: z.array(z.enum(AI_SOURCES)),

  model: z
    .object({
      provider: z.enum([
        "google_ai",
        "vertex_ai",
        "google_cloud_vision",
        "layerd",
        "custom",
        "system",
      ]),

      modelName: z.string().optional(),
      modelVersion: z.string().optional(),

      promptVersion: z.string().optional(),
      promptHash: z.string().optional(),

      rawOutputAssetId: z.string().optional(),
    })
    .optional(),

  createdAt: z.number(),

  pipelineVersion: z.string(),
});

const TextPayloadSchema = z.object({
  value: z.string(),

  originalValue: z.string().optional(),

  language: z.string().optional(),

  fontFamily: z.string().optional(),
  fontFallback: z.string().optional(),

  fontSize: z.number().positive(),

  fontWeight: z.union([z.string(), z.number()]).optional(),

  fontStyle: z.enum(["normal", "italic"]).optional(),

  lineHeight: z.number().positive().optional(),

  letterSpacingPx: z.number().optional(),

  fill: z.string().optional(),

  stroke: z.string().optional(),
  strokeWidth: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  shadow: z
    .object({
      color: z.string().optional(),
      offsetX: z.number().optional(),
      offsetY: z.number().optional(),
      blur: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
    })
    .optional(),

  textAlign: z.enum(["left", "center", "right", "justify"]).optional(),

  safety: z.object({
    originalOcrText: z.string().optional(),
    reconstructedText: z.string(),
    semanticMutationDetected: z.boolean(),
    roundTripOcrPassed: z.boolean().optional(),
  }),
});

const VectorPayloadSchema = z.object({
  primitive: z.enum([
    "rect",
    "rounded_rect",
    "circle",
    "ellipse",
    "line",
    "polygon",
    "path",
    "compound_path",
  ]),

  pathData: z.string().optional(),

  points: z.array(PointSchema).optional(),

  fill: z.string().optional(),

  stroke: z.string().optional(),

  strokeWidth: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  radius: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

  pathCount: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),

  sourceVectorAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  fallbackRasterAssetId: z.string().optional(),
});

const RasterPayloadSchema = z.object({
  editorAssetId: z.string().min(1),

  exportAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  maskAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  originalCropAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  crop: BBoxSchema.optional(),

  alphaMode: z.enum(["binary_mask", "soft_alpha", "matte"]).optional(),

  edgeQuality: z.enum(["high", "medium", "low", "unknown"]).optional(),

  canReplace: z.boolean().optional(),
  canCrop: z.boolean().optional(),
  canEditMask: z.boolean().optional(),
});

const BackgroundPayloadSchema = z.object({
  assetId: z.string().min(1),

  sourceImageAssetId: z.string().min(1),

  removedMaskAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  repairAreaRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  hallucinationRisk: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

  conservativeRepair: z.boolean(),
});

const GroupPayloadSchema = z.object({
  childLayerIds: z.array(z.string()),

  role: z.enum([
    "button",
    "badge",
    "price_block",
    "menu_item",
    "logo_lockup",
    "social_handle",
    "headline_block",
    "product_group",
    "pattern",
    "unknown",
  ]),

  lockedChildren: z.boolean().optional(),
});

const LayerDecisionSchema = z.object({
  strategy: z.enum(AI_DECISION_STRATEGIES),

  selectedObservationIds: z.array(z.string()),

  rejectedObservationIds: z.array(z.string()).optional(),

  reasonCodes: z.array(z.string()),

  thresholds: z.record(z.string(), z.number()).optional(),

  decidedBy: z.enum(["system", "manual_user"]),

  decidedAt: z.number(),
});

export const AiReconstructedLayerSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().min(1),

    schemaVersion: z.literal(AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION),

    jobId: z.string().min(1),
    designId: z.string().min(1),
    workspaceId: z.string().min(1),

    type: z.enum(AI_LAYER_TYPES),

    editableLevel: z.enum(AI_EDITABLE_LEVELS),

    name: z.string().min(1),

    visible: z.boolean(),

    locked: z.boolean(),

    zIndex: z.number().int(),

    geometry: GeometrySchema,

    confidence: ConfidenceSchema,

    capabilities: z.array(
      z.enum([
        "select",
        "move",
        "resize",
        "rotate",
        "hide",
        "lock",
        "delete",
        "duplicate",
        "reorder",
        "edit_text",
        "change_font",
        "recolor",
        "edit_vector",
        "replace_asset",
        "crop",
        "edit_mask",
        "regenerate",
        "restore_from_original",
        "ungroup",
      ])
    ),

    assetIds: z.array(z.string()),

    fallbacks: z.array(FallbackSchema),

    primaryFallbackId: z.string().optional(),

    provenance: ProvenanceSchema,

    decision: LayerDecisionSchema,

    text: TextPayloadSchema.optional(),

    vector: VectorPayloadSchema.optional(),

    raster: RasterPayloadSchema.optional(),

    background: BackgroundPayloadSchema.optional(),

    group: GroupPayloadSchema.optional(),

    metadata: z.object({
      createdAt: z.number(),
      updatedAt: z.number().optional(),

      originalImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),
      normalizedImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),

      warnings: z.array(z.string()).optional(),

      needsReview: z.boolean().optional(),

      userCorrected: z.boolean().optional(),

      userCorrectionType: z
        .enum([
          "text_changed",
          "font_changed",
          "mask_edited",
          "layer_deleted",
          "layer_split",
          "layer_merged",
          "z_order_changed",
          "fallback_restored",
          "asset_replaced",
        ])
        .optional(),
    }),
  })
  .superRefine((layer, ctx) => {
    if (layer.editableLevel === "text_editable" && !layer.text) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["text"],
        message: "text_editable layer must include text payload",
      });
    }

    if (layer.editableLevel === "vector_editable" && !layer.vector) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["vector"],
        message: "vector_editable layer must include vector payload",
      });
    }

    if (
      [
        "raster_masked",
        "raster_clean_background",
        "raster_fallback",
        "unknown_confidence",
      ].includes(layer.editableLevel) &&
      !layer.raster &&
      !layer.background
    ) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["raster"],
        message: "raster-like layer must include raster or background payload",
      });
    }

    if (layer.editableLevel === "group_editable" && !layer.group) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["group"],
        message: "group_editable layer must include group payload",
      });
    }

    if (
      layer.type !== "locked_reference" &&
      layer.confidence.overall < 0.98 &&
      layer.fallbacks.length === 0
    ) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["fallbacks"],
        message: "uncertain AI layer must include at least one fallback",
      });
    }

    if (
      layer.editableLevel === "text_editable" &&
      layer.text?.safety.semanticMutationDetected
    ) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["text", "safety"],
        message:
          "text_editable layer cannot have semanticMutationDetected=true",
      });
    }
  });

export const AiObservationSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().min(1),

    jobId: z.string().min(1),
    designId: z.string().min(1),

    kind: z.enum(AI_OBSERVATION_KINDS),

    source: z.enum(AI_SOURCES),

    model: z
      .object({
        provider: z.enum([
          "google_ai",
          "vertex_ai",
          "google_cloud_vision",
          "layerd",
          "custom",
          "system",
        ]),
        modelName: z.string().optional(),
        modelVersion: z.string().optional(),
        promptVersion: z.string().optional(),
        promptHash: z.string().optional(),
        rawOutputAssetId: z.string().optional(),
      })
      .optional(),

    confidence: ConfidenceSchema.optional(),

    createdAt: z.number(),

    warnings: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  })
  .passthrough();

export const AiReconstructionDocumentSchema = z
  .object({
    schemaVersion: z.literal(AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION),

    jobId: z.string().min(1),
    designId: z.string().min(1),
    workspaceId: z.string().min(1),
    userId: z.string().min(1),

    createdAt: z.number(),
    updatedAt: z.number(),

    sourceImage: z.object({
      originalAssetId: z.string().min(1),

      normalizedAssetId: z.string().optional(),

      mimeType: z.enum(["image/png", "image/jpeg", "image/webp"]),

      sha256: z.string().optional(),

      perceptualHash: z.string().optional(),

      width: z.number().positive(),
      height: z.number().positive(),

      uploadedAt: z.number(),
    }),

    canvas: z.object({
      width: z.number().positive(),
      height: z.number().positive(),

      originalWidth: z.number().positive(),
      originalHeight: z.number().positive(),

      normalizedWidth: z.number().positive(),
      normalizedHeight: z.number().positive(),

      unit: z.literal("px"),

      backgroundColor: z.string().optional(),

      dpi: z.number().positive().optional(),
    }),

    routing: z
      .object({
        canvasType: z.enum([
          "graphic_design",
          "photo_heavy_composite",
          "text_heavy_design",
          "menu_or_document",
          "logo_or_icon",
          "flat_illustration",
          "ai_generated_banner",
          "mixed",
          "unknown",
        ]),

        textDensity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

        flatColorRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

        photoRegionRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

        recommendedRoute: z.enum([
          "graphic_design_layer_decomposition",
          "photo_conservative_segmentation",
          "text_recovery_priority",
          "vectorization_priority",
          "fallback_only",
        ]),

        confidence: z.number().min(0).max(1),
      })
      .optional(),

    assets: z.record(z.string(), AssetRefSchema),

    observations: z.record(z.string(), AiObservationSchema),

    layers: z.array(AiReconstructedLayerSchema),

    groups: z.array(
      z.object({
        id: z.string().min(1),

        name: z.string().min(1),

        role: z.enum([
          "button",
          "badge",
          "price_block",
          "menu_item",
          "logo_lockup",
          "social_handle",
          "headline_block",
          "product_group",
          "pattern",
          "unknown",
        ]),

        childLayerIds: z.array(z.string()),

        bbox: BBoxSchema,

        zIndexRange: z.object({
          min: z.number().int(),
          max: z.number().int(),
        }),

        confidence: ConfidenceSchema,

        sourceObservationIds: z.array(z.string()),

        lockedChildren: z.boolean().optional(),

        createdAt: z.number(),
      })
    ),

    quality: z.object({
      visualMatchScore: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

      ssim: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

      rgbL1: z.number().min(0).optional(),

      lpips: z.number().min(0).optional(),

      textExactRate: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

      editableTextCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),

      vectorEditableCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),

      rasterLayerCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),

      fallbackLayerCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),

      unknownLayerCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),

      zOrderConflictCount: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),

      needsReview: z.boolean(),

      warnings: z.array(z.string()),
    }),

    pipeline: z.object({
      pipelineVersion: z.string().min(1),

      stepsCompleted: z.array(z.string()),

      modelsUsed: z.array(
        z.object({
          provider: z.enum([
            "google_ai",
            "vertex_ai",
            "google_cloud_vision",
            "layerd",
            "custom",
            "system",
          ]),
          modelName: z.string().optional(),
          modelVersion: z.string().optional(),
          promptVersion: z.string().optional(),
          promptHash: z.string().optional(),
          rawOutputAssetId: z.string().optional(),
        })
      ),

      warnings: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    }),

    audit: z.object({
      originalPreserved: z.boolean(),

      lockedReferenceLayerId: z.string().optional(),

      firstRenderValidated: z.boolean(),

      textSafetyValidated: z.boolean(),

      schemaValidated: z.boolean(),

      generatedAt: z.number(),
    }),
  })
  .superRefine((doc, ctx) => {
    const layerIds = new Set(doc.layers.map((layer) => layer.id));

    if (doc.layers.length === 0) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["layers"],
        message: "reconstruction document must include at least one layer",
      });
    }

    const lockedReferenceLayers = doc.layers.filter(
      (layer) => layer.type === "locked_reference"
    );

    if (lockedReferenceLayers.length !== 1) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["layers"],
        message: "document must include exactly one locked_reference layer",
      });
    }

    for (const layer of doc.layers) {
      for (const assetId of layer.assetIds) {
        if (!doc.assets[assetId]) {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            path: ["layers", layer.id, "assetIds"],
            message: `layer references missing asset: ${assetId}`,
          });
        }
      }

      for (const fallback of layer.fallbacks) {
        if (fallback.assetId && !doc.assets[fallback.assetId]) {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            path: ["layers", layer.id, "fallbacks"],
            message: `fallback references missing asset: ${fallback.assetId}`,
          });
        }
      }
    }

    for (const group of doc.groups) {
      for (const childLayerId of group.childLayerIds) {
        if (!layerIds.has(childLayerId)) {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            path: ["groups", group.id, "childLayerIds"],
            message: `group references missing layer: ${childLayerId}`,
          });
        }
      }
    }

    if (!doc.audit.originalPreserved) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["audit", "originalPreserved"],
        message: "original image must be preserved",
      });
    }
  });

export type AiReconstructionDocumentValidated = z.infer<
  typeof AiReconstructionDocumentSchema
>;
```

# 1.20 Invariants

Create hard checks outside Zod too. Zod validates shape. Invariants validate product truth.

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/schema/invariants.ts

import type {
  AiReconstructedLayer,
  AiReconstructionDocument,
} from "./reconstruction.types";

export function assertLayerInvariants(layer: AiReconstructedLayer): void {
  if (!layer.id) {
    throw new Error("Layer must have id");
  }

  if (!layer.name) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} must have name`);
  }

  if (layer.geometry.coordinateSpace !== "canvas_px") {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} must use canvas_px geometry`);
  }

  if (layer.confidence.overall < 0 || layer.confidence.overall > 1) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} confidence must be 0-1`);
  }

  if (layer.editableLevel === "text_editable") {
    if (!layer.text) {
      throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} is text_editable but has no text`);
    }

    if (layer.text.safety.semanticMutationDetected) {
      throw new Error(
        `Layer ${layer.id} cannot be editable text because semantic mutation was detected`
      );
    }
  }

  if (layer.editableLevel === "vector_editable" && !layer.vector) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} is vector_editable but has no vector`);
  }

  if (
    ["raster_masked", "raster_clean_background", "raster_fallback"].includes(
      layer.editableLevel
    ) &&
    !layer.raster &&
    !layer.background
  ) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} is raster-like but has no raster data`);
  }

  if (
    layer.type !== "locked_reference" &&
    layer.confidence.overall < 0.98 &&
    layer.fallbacks.length === 0
  ) {
    throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} requires fallback`);
  }
}

export function assertReconstructionDocumentInvariants(
  doc: AiReconstructionDocument
): void {
  const layerIds = new Set<string>();
  const zIndexes = new Set<number>();

  for (const layer of doc.layers) {
    assertLayerInvariants(layer);

    if (layerIds.has(layer.id)) {
      throw new Error(`Duplicate layer id: ${layer.id}`);
    }

    layerIds.add(layer.id);

    if (zIndexes.has(layer.zIndex)) {
      throw new Error(`Duplicate zIndex: ${layer.zIndex}`);
    }

    zIndexes.add(layer.zIndex);

    for (const assetId of layer.assetIds) {
      if (!doc.assets[assetId]) {
        throw new Error(`Layer ${layer.id} references missing asset ${assetId}`);
      }
    }
  }

  const referenceLayers = doc.layers.filter(
    (layer) => layer.type === "locked_reference"
  );

  if (referenceLayers.length !== 1) {
    throw new Error("Document must include exactly one locked reference layer");
  }

  if (!doc.audit.originalPreserved) {
    throw new Error("Original image preservation invariant failed");
  }

  for (const group of doc.groups) {
    for (const childLayerId of group.childLayerIds) {
      if (!layerIds.has(childLayerId)) {
        throw new Error(
          `Group ${group.id} references missing layer ${childLayerId}`
        );
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# 1.22 What must not enter this schema

Do not allow these:

```txt
base64 image data
raw mask bytes
raw PNG bytes
large full model responses inline
signed URLs as durable identity
Fabric object JSON as canonical data
SVG as canonical data
PSD layer data as canonical data
single generic confidence score
text layer without fallback
vector layer without fallback
model output without provenance
layer without decision record
layer without editableLevel
```

The schema should stay small enough to index, validate, migrate, and inspect. Large payloads are assets.

---

# 1.23 Acceptance criteria for Step 1

Step 1 is complete when these are true:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument exists.

Observations and resolved layers are separate.

Every layer has:
  id
  type
  editableLevel
  geometry
  zIndex
  confidence
  provenance
  decision
  fallbacks
  capabilities

Every asset is referenced, not embedded.

Every text_editable layer requires:
  text payload
  text safety state
  no semantic mutation
  fallback crop

Every vector_editable layer requires:
  vector payload
  render-confidence path
  fallback raster asset

Every uncertain non-reference layer requires fallback.

Exactly one locked_reference layer exists.

Zod validates runtime data.

Invariant checks reject unsafe documents.

No Fabric JSON exists in the canonical schema.
```

---

# 1.24 The locked Step 1 architecture

The canonical truth is:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
```

It contains:

```txt
source image metadata
canvas metadata
asset references
raw observations
resolved layers
logical groups
quality metrics
pipeline provenance
audit state
```

It does **not** contain:

```txt
Fabric runtime JSON
Firebase storage layout rules
job orchestration state
export format details
```

Those belong to later steps.

Step 1 is now locked as:

```txt
Models produce observations.
Resolver produces AiReconstructionDocument.
Fabric is generated later from AiReconstructionDocument.
```

## ChatGPT Response 012

<!-- assistant_message_ids: a0b653d3-eec0-4240-8915-ae5b1b267a81, a5f3e361-9f3b-4dc9-974d-e69772958bb3 -->

I’ll lock Step 2 only: the Fabric manifest contract, keeping Step 1’s reconstruction document as source of truth while defining the exact Fabric projection boundary.

# Step 2 — Fabric manifest contract

Step 2 defines the **editor import/export package**.

The canonical truth remains:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
```

The Fabric manifest is only the projection used by your existing Fabric editor:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
→ AiFabricManifest
→ manifest.fabricJson
→ canvas.loadFromJSON(...)
```

Do **not** make Fabric JSON the AI source of truth.

Fabric’s `loadFromJSON` expects JSON conforming to Fabric’s own `toJSON` shape, returns a `Promise<Canvas>`, and Fabric recommends aborting previous loading tasks before starting a new load to avoid race conditions and unnecessary networking. Also, `loadFromJSON` does not resize the canvas, so canvas dimensions must come from your manifest wrapper, not from Fabric JSON alone. citeturn846321view0turn367524view0

---

## 2.1 The hard rule

The manifest must be a **wrapper around Fabric JSON**, not modified Fabric JSON.

Correct:

```ts
{
  schemaVersion: "ai-fabric-manifest.v1",
  canvas: {...},
  assets: {...},
  layerIndex: {...},
  fabricJson: {
    version: "...",
    objects: [...]
  }
}
```

Wrong:

```ts
{
  version: "...",
  objects: [...],
  aiAssets: {...},
  aiLayers: {...},
  jobId: "..."
}
```

Reason: Fabric owns `fabricJson`. Your app owns `AiFabricManifest`.

---

# 2.2 What Step 2 must solve

This contract must solve five problems:

```txt
1. How Fabric loads AI-generated layers.
2. How your editor maps Fabric objects back to AI layers.
3. How image assets are resolved into browser-loadable URLs.
4. How AI metadata survives Fabric serialization.
5. How user edits are saved without corrupting the canonical reconstruction document.
```

Fabric can serialize custom object properties, but the docs are explicit: custom properties must be declared and included in serialization via `toObject` / `FabricObject.customProperties`. citeturn367524view1

---

# 2.3 Critical Fabric constraints

## Constraint 1 — `fabricJson` must be Fabric-compatible only

Fabric receives only this:

```ts
canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest.fabricJson)
```

Not this:

```ts
canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest)
```

---

## Constraint 2 — Set canvas dimensions outside Fabric JSON

Before loading:

```ts
canvas.setDimensions({
  width: manifest.canvas.width,
  height: manifest.canvas.height,
});
```

Fabric docs say `loadFromJSON` does not affect canvas size. citeturn367524view0

---

## Constraint 3 — Use Promise-based loading

Use:

```ts
await canvas.loadFromJSON(manifest.fabricJson);
canvas.requestRenderAll();
```

Not old callback-only patterns.

Fabric’s current docs show `loadFromJSON(...).then(...)` and define it as returning `Promise<Canvas>`. citeturn846321view0

---

## Constraint 4 — Abort stale loads

When user imports another image before the previous manifest finishes loading:

```ts
controller.abort();
```

Fabric recommends aborting loading tasks before calling `loadFromJSON` again. citeturn846321view0

---

## Constraint 5 — Browser image URLs must be CORS-safe

Every Fabric image object must use:

```ts
crossOrigin: "anonymous"
```

And the image response must include valid CORS headers.

MDN states that drawing a cross-origin image without CORS approval taints the canvas, and then `getImageData`, `toBlob`, `toDataURL`, and `captureStream` throw security errors. citeturn367524view2

This matters because your editor likely exports previews client-side.

---

## Constraint 6 — Do not use Fabric `type` for product logic

Fabric’s object `type` exists for Fabric serialization/deserialization. Fabric’s docs warn not to build new app logic around the instance `type` value. citeturn396449view1

Use this for app logic:

```ts
aiLayerType
aiEditableLevel
aiLayerId
```

Not:

```ts
object.type === "textbox"
```

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/fabric-manifest.types.ts
src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/fabric-manifest.zod.ts
src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/register-ai-fabric-properties.ts
```

No Firebase paths here. No Cloud Run. No model logic. This is only the Fabric projection boundary.
