# 2.5 Fabric manifest types

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/fabric-manifest.types.ts

import type {
  AiAssetRef,
  AiConfidence,
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerType,
  AiReconstructionDocument,
  AiSource,
  BBox,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

export const AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION =
  "ai-fabric-manifest.v1" as const;

export type FabricObjectJson = {
  type: string;

  version?: string;

  id?: string;
  name?: string;

  left?: number;
  top?: number;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  scaleX?: number;
  scaleY?: number;

  angle?: number;
  opacity?: number;

  originX?: "left" | "center" | "right";
  originY?: "top" | "center" | "bottom";

  visible?: boolean;

  selectable?: boolean;
  evented?: boolean;

  hasControls?: boolean;
  hasBorders?: boolean;

  lockMovementX?: boolean;
  lockMovementY?: boolean;
  lockScalingX?: boolean;
  lockScalingY?: boolean;
  lockRotation?: boolean;

  objectCaching?: boolean;
  perPixelTargetFind?: boolean;

  excludeFromExport?: boolean;

  /**
   * Required only for Fabric Image objects.
   */
  src?: string;
  crossOrigin?: "anonymous" | "use-credentials" | null;

  /**
   * AI identity metadata.
   * Keep this small.
   * Full reconstruction data stays in AiReconstructionDocument.
   */
  aiLayerId?: string;
  aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
  aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
  aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
  aiSource?: AiSource;
  aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
  aiSchemaVersion?: string;

  [key: string]: unknown;
};

export type FabricRuntimeJson = {
  /**
   * Fabric version used by the generator.
   * Do not hardcode. Pass from your installed Fabric package/app config.
   */
  version: string;

  /**
   * Included for diagnostics.
   * Loader still sets dimensions from manifest.canvas.
   */
  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  background?: string | null;
  backgroundColor?: string | null;

  objects: FabricObjectJson[];

  backgroundImage?: FabricObjectJson;
  overlayImage?: FabricObjectJson;
  clipPath?: FabricObjectJson;

  [key: string]: unknown;
};

export type AiFabricManifestAsset = AiAssetRef & {
  /**
   * Runtime URL used by Fabric.
   * This may expire.
   * Durable identity stays on asset.id/storagePath/bucket later.
   */
  resolvedUrl?: string;

  resolvedUrlExpiresAt?: number;
};

export type AiFabricLayerIndexEntry = {
  aiLayerId: string;

  /**
   * Index in fabricJson.objects.
   * Fabric object order is the draw stack.
   */
  objectIndex: number;

  zIndex: number;

  name: string;

  layerType: AiLayerType;
  editableLevel: AiEditableLevel;

  fabricObjectType: string;

  assetIds: string[];

  fallbackAssetIds: string[];

  primaryFallbackAssetId?: string;

  originalBBox?: BBox;
  canvasBBox: BBox;

  visible: boolean;
  locked: boolean;

  warnings?: string[];
};

export type AiFabricManifest = {
  schemaVersion: typeof AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION;

  jobId: string;
  designId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  userId: string;

  createdAt: number;
  updatedAt: number;

  source: {
    reconstructionSchemaVersion: AiReconstructionDocument["schemaVersion"];

    /**
     * Later, Step 3 defines exact GCS/Firebase paths.
     */
    reconstructionDocumentAssetId?: string;

    originalImageAssetId: string;
    normalizedImageAssetId?: string;
  };

  canvas: {
    width: number;
    height: number;

    originalWidth: number;
    originalHeight: number;

    normalizedWidth: number;
    normalizedHeight: number;

    unit: "px";

    backgroundColor?: string;
  };

  /**
   * Asset references needed by Fabric and layer panel.
   */
  assets: Record<string, AiFabricManifestAsset>;

  /**
   * Maps AI layer IDs to Fabric object indices.
   * This is what your layer panel should use.
   */
  layerIndex: Record<string, AiFabricLayerIndexEntry>;

  /**
   * The only object passed into canvas.loadFromJSON().
   */
  fabricJson: FabricRuntimeJson;

  reconstruction: {
    qualityScore?: number;
    visualMatchScore?: number;

    needsReview: boolean;

    warnings: string[];
  };

  runtime: {
    fabricVersion: string;

    generatedBy: "server" | "client" | "worker";

    pipelineVersion: string;

    manifestGeneratorVersion: string;
  };
};
```

---

# 2.6 Fabric JSON type registry

Use Fabric class static types for Fabric JSON generation, but do not use those type strings for product logic.

Fabric v6 moved to named imports such as `Canvas`, `Rect`, etc., and the upgrade docs warn that Fabric is now TypeScript-first. citeturn367524view4

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/fabric-json-types.ts

import {
  Circle,
  Ellipse,
  FabricImage,
  Group,
  Line,
  Path,
  Polygon,
  Rect,
  Textbox,
} from "fabric";

export const FABRIC_JSON_TYPES = {
  image: FabricImage.type,
  textbox: Textbox.type,
  rect: Rect.type,
  circle: Circle.type,
  ellipse: Ellipse.type,
  line: Line.type,
  polygon: Polygon.type,
  path: Path.type,
  group: Group.type,
} as const;
```

This is allowed because these values are for Fabric serialization only.

Your app logic still uses:

```ts
aiLayerType
aiEditableLevel
```

---

# 2.7 Register AI custom properties

This is mandatory.

Without this, your AI metadata may disappear when saving/loading Fabric JSON.

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/register-ai-fabric-properties.ts

import { FabricObject } from "fabric";
import type {
  AiConfidence,
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerType,
  AiSource,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

export const AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES = [
  "id",
  "name",

  "aiLayerId",
  "aiLayerType",
  "aiEditableLevel",
  "aiConfidence",
  "aiSource",
  "aiFallbackAssetId",
  "aiSchemaVersion",
] as const;

declare module "fabric" {
  interface FabricObject {
    id?: string;
    name?: string;

    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;
  }

  interface SerializedObjectProps {
    id?: string;
    name?: string;

    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;
  }
}

export function registerAiFabricCustomProperties() {
  const existing = FabricObject.customProperties ?? [];

  FabricObject.customProperties = Array.from(
    new Set([...existing, ...AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES])
  );
}
```

Important detail: merge with existing custom properties. Do **not** overwrite your current editor’s custom serialization fields.

---

# 2.8 Manifest validation

Use Zod to reject unsafe manifests before they enter your editor.

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/fabric-manifest.zod.ts

import { z } from "zod";
import { AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION } from "./fabric-manifest.types";

const BBoxSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
  width: z.number().nonnegative(),
  height: z.number().nonnegative(),
});

const ConfidenceSchema = z
  .object({
    overall: z.number().min(0).max(1),
  })
  .passthrough();

const FabricObjectJsonSchema = z
  .object({
    type: z.string().min(1),

    id: z.string().optional(),
    name: z.string().optional(),

    left: z.number().optional(),
    top: z.number().optional(),
    width: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
    height: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),

    scaleX: z.number().optional(),
    scaleY: z.number().optional(),

    angle: z.number().optional(),
    opacity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),

    visible: z.boolean().optional(),

    src: z.string().url().optional(),
    crossOrigin: z.enum(["anonymous", "use-credentials"]).nullable().optional(),

    aiLayerId: z.string().optional(),
    aiLayerType: z.string().optional(),
    aiEditableLevel: z.string().optional(),
    aiConfidence: ConfidenceSchema.optional(),
    aiSource: z.string().optional(),
    aiFallbackAssetId: z.string().optional(),
    aiSchemaVersion: z.string().optional(),
  })
  .passthrough();

const FabricRuntimeJsonSchema = z
  .object({
    version: z.string().min(1),

    width: z.number().positive().optional(),
    height: z.number().positive().optional(),

    background: z.union([z.string(), z.null()]).optional(),
    backgroundColor: z.union([z.string(), z.null()]).optional(),

    objects: z.array(FabricObjectJsonSchema),
  })
  .passthrough();

const ManifestAssetSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().min(1),
    kind: z.string().min(1),

    bucket: z.string().optional(),
    storagePath: z.string().optional(),

    url: z.string().url().optional(),
    urlExpiresAt: z.number().optional(),

    resolvedUrl: z.string().url().optional(),
    resolvedUrlExpiresAt: z.number().optional(),

    mimeType: z.string().optional(),

    width: z.number().positive().optional(),
    height: z.number().positive().optional(),

    sizeBytes: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
  })
  .passthrough();

const LayerIndexEntrySchema = z.object({
  aiLayerId: z.string().min(1),

  objectIndex: z.number().int().nonnegative(),

  zIndex: z.number().int(),

  name: z.string().min(1),

  layerType: z.string().min(1),
  editableLevel: z.string().min(1),

  fabricObjectType: z.string().min(1),

  assetIds: z.array(z.string()),
  fallbackAssetIds: z.array(z.string()),

  primaryFallbackAssetId: z.string().optional(),

  originalBBox: BBoxSchema.optional(),
  canvasBBox: BBoxSchema,

  visible: z.boolean(),
  locked: z.boolean(),

  warnings: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
});

export const AiFabricManifestSchema = z
  .object({
    schemaVersion: z.literal(AI_FABRIC_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION),

    jobId: z.string().min(1),
    designId: z.string().min(1),
    workspaceId: z.string().min(1),
    userId: z.string().min(1),

    createdAt: z.number(),
    updatedAt: z.number(),

    source: z.object({
      reconstructionSchemaVersion: z.string().min(1),
      reconstructionDocumentAssetId: z.string().optional(),
      originalImageAssetId: z.string().min(1),
      normalizedImageAssetId: z.string().optional(),
    }),

    canvas: z.object({
      width: z.number().positive(),
      height: z.number().positive(),

      originalWidth: z.number().positive(),
      originalHeight: z.number().positive(),

      normalizedWidth: z.number().positive(),
      normalizedHeight: z.number().positive(),

      unit: z.literal("px"),

      backgroundColor: z.string().optional(),
    }),

    assets: z.record(z.string(), ManifestAssetSchema),

    layerIndex: z.record(z.string(), LayerIndexEntrySchema),

    fabricJson: FabricRuntimeJsonSchema,

    reconstruction: z.object({
      qualityScore: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
      visualMatchScore: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
      needsReview: z.boolean(),
      warnings: z.array(z.string()),
    }),

    runtime: z.object({
      fabricVersion: z.string().min(1),
      generatedBy: z.enum(["server", "client", "worker"]),
      pipelineVersion: z.string().min(1),
      manifestGeneratorVersion: z.string().min(1),
    }),
  })
  .superRefine((manifest, ctx) => {
    if (manifest.fabricJson.objects.length === 0) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["fabricJson", "objects"],
        message: "Fabric manifest must include at least one Fabric object",
      });
    }

    for (const [layerId, entry] of Object.entries(manifest.layerIndex)) {
      if (entry.aiLayerId !== layerId) {
        ctx.addIssue({
          code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
          path: ["layerIndex", layerId],
          message: "layerIndex key must equal aiLayerId",
        });
      }

      const object = manifest.fabricJson.objects[entry.objectIndex];

      if (!object) {
        ctx.addIssue({
          code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
          path: ["layerIndex", layerId, "objectIndex"],
          message: "layerIndex points to missing Fabric object",
        });
        continue;
      }

      if (object.aiLayerId !== layerId) {
        ctx.addIssue({
          code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
          path: ["fabricJson", "objects", entry.objectIndex],
          message: "Fabric object aiLayerId must match layerIndex entry",
        });
      }

      for (const assetId of entry.assetIds) {
        if (!manifest.assets[assetId]) {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            path: ["layerIndex", layerId, "assetIds"],
            message: `Missing manifest asset: ${assetId}`,
          });
        }
      }
    }

    const hasLockedReference = manifest.fabricJson.objects.some(
      (object) => object.aiLayerType === "locked_reference"
    );

    if (!hasLockedReference) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        path: ["fabricJson", "objects"],
        message: "Fabric manifest must include a locked reference object",
      });
    }

    for (const [index, object] of manifest.fabricJson.objects.entries()) {
      const looksLikeImage =
        object.src !== undefined ||
        object.type.toLowerCase().includes("image");

      if (looksLikeImage) {
        if (!object.src || !/^https:\/\//.test(object.src)) {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            path: ["fabricJson", "objects", index, "src"],
            message: "Fabric image object must use HTTPS src",
          });
        }

        if (object.crossOrigin !== "anonymous") {
          ctx.addIssue({
            code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
            path: ["fabricJson", "objects", index, "crossOrigin"],
            message:
              "Fabric image object must use crossOrigin='anonymous' for export-safe canvas usage",
          });
        }
      }
    }
  });

export type AiFabricManifestValidated = z.infer<
  typeof AiFabricManifestSchema
>;
```

# 2.9 Load manifest into your existing Fabric editor

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/load-ai-fabric-manifest.ts

import type { Canvas, FabricObject } from "fabric";
import type { AiFabricManifest } from "./fabric-manifest.types";
import { AiFabricManifestSchema } from "./fabric-manifest.zod";
import { registerAiFabricCustomProperties } from "./register-ai-fabric-properties";

export async function loadAiFabricManifest(params: {
  canvas: Canvas;
  manifest: AiFabricManifest;
  abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
}) {
  const { canvas } = params;

  const manifest = AiFabricManifestSchema.parse(params.manifest);

  registerAiFabricCustomProperties();

  canvas.clear();

  canvas.setDimensions({
    width: manifest.canvas.width,
    height: manifest.canvas.height,
  });

  await canvas.loadFromJSON(
    manifest.fabricJson,
    (_serializedObject: unknown, fabricObject: FabricObject) => {
      fabricObject.set({
        dirty: true,
      });
    },
    params.abortSignal ? { signal: params.abortSignal } : undefined
  );

  for (const object of canvas.getObjects()) {
    object.setCoords();
  }

  canvas.requestRenderAll();

  return {
    objectCount: canvas.getObjects().length,
    layerIndex: manifest.layerIndex,
  };
}
```

Usage:

```ts
let currentManifestLoadController: AbortController | null = null;

export async function importMagicLayersManifest(
  canvas: Canvas,
  manifest: AiFabricManifest
) {
  currentManifestLoadController?.abort();

  currentManifestLoadController = new AbortController();

  return loadAiFabricManifest({
    canvas,
    manifest,
    abortSignal: currentManifestLoadController.signal,
  });
}
```

---

# 2.10 Save Fabric JSON without losing AI metadata

Use `toObject`, not plain `toJSON`, when you need custom properties.

Fabric docs state that `toObject(propertiesToInclude)` accepts additional properties, while `toJSON()` has its own signature and does not support additional properties. citeturn846321view2

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-manifest/save-ai-fabric-json.ts

import type { Canvas } from "fabric";
import type { FabricRuntimeJson } from "./fabric-manifest.types";
import { AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES } from "./register-ai-fabric-properties";

export function saveAiFabricRuntimeJson(canvas: Canvas): FabricRuntimeJson {
  const json = canvas.toObject([...AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES]);

  return json as FabricRuntimeJson;
}
```

Autosave should save edited Fabric state:

```ts
const fabricJson = saveAiFabricRuntimeJson(canvas);
```

But it should **not** mutate the original `AiReconstructionDocument`.

Correct split:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
= AI reconstruction evidence and decisions

FabricRuntimeJson
= current editable editor state after user changes
```

---

# 2.11 Required AI metadata on every Fabric object

Every AI-generated Fabric object must include:

```ts
{
  id: layer.id,
  name: layer.name,

  aiLayerId: layer.id,
  aiLayerType: layer.type,
  aiEditableLevel: layer.editableLevel,
  aiConfidence: layer.confidence,
  aiSource: layer.provenance.primarySource,
  aiFallbackAssetId: layer.primaryFallbackId,
  aiSchemaVersion: layer.schemaVersion
}
```

This is the bridge between your editor and the canonical reconstruction document.

Do not attach the whole layer object to Fabric.

Bad:

```ts
fabricObject.set({
  aiLayer: fullAiReconstructedLayer
});
```

Good:

```ts
fabricObject.set({
  aiLayerId,
  aiLayerType,
  aiEditableLevel,
  aiConfidence,
});
```

Full reconstruction data belongs in `AiReconstructionDocument`.

---

# 2.12 Image object contract

A Fabric image object generated by Magic Layers must use:

```ts
{
  type: FABRIC_JSON_TYPES.image,
  src: "https://resolved-runtime-url.example/layer.png",
  crossOrigin: "anonymous",

  left,
  top,
  width,
  height,
  scaleX,
  scaleY,

  aiLayerId,
  aiLayerType,
  aiEditableLevel
}
```

Fabric Image can be initialized from a URL string, and `FabricImage.fromURL` creates an image instance from a URL. citeturn396449view0turn396449view3

Important asset rule:

```txt
asset.storagePath / asset.id = durable identity
object.src = temporary runtime URL
```

Do not put this inside Fabric JSON:

```txt
gs://...
firebase storage internal path
unsigned private path
base64 PNG
```

Fabric needs browser-loadable URLs. Your durable asset model comes later in Step 3.

---

# 2.13 Object order contract

Fabric draw stack is object-order based. The manifest must sort objects by `zIndex` before generating `fabricJson.objects`.

Bottom to top:

```txt
locked reference
clean background
large shapes
decorations
image blocks
photo subjects/products
logos/icons
badges
headline text
small text
overlays
```

Technical rule:

```ts
fabricJson.objects = layers
  .filter(layer => layerShouldRenderInFabric(layer))
  .sort((a, b) => a.zIndex - b.zIndex)
  .map(layerToFabricObjectJson);
```

Fabric exposes stack operations such as `bringObjectToFront`, `sendObjectToBack`, and `moveObjectTo`, which confirms stack order is an explicit Fabric concern. citeturn608244view0

---

# 2.14 Groups contract

Do **not** force Fabric groups at this layer.

For now:

```txt
groups live in manifest.layerIndex / AiReconstructionDocument.groups
Fabric objects remain individually editable
Layer panel can display logical groups
```

Only generate `fabric.Group` when your existing editor already handles:

```txt
group selection
ungroup
child editing
group serialization
z-order inside group
autosave/undo behavior
```

Default:

```txt
logical groups, not Fabric.Group
```

This avoids corrupting editability.

# 2.16 Manifest invariants

Before loading into Fabric, these must be true:

```txt
manifest.schemaVersion is valid

manifest.fabricJson.objects is non-empty

canvas dimensions exist in manifest.canvas

canvas dimensions are set before loadFromJSON

fabricJson is passed to loadFromJSON, not the whole manifest

every AI Fabric object has aiLayerId

every aiLayerId exists in layerIndex

every layerIndex.objectIndex points to the correct Fabric object

object order follows zIndex ascending

locked_reference object exists

image objects use HTTPS src

image objects use crossOrigin: "anonymous"

Fabric image src is runtime URL, not durable storage identity

custom AI Fabric properties are registered before load/save

saved Fabric JSON includes AI custom properties

full AiReconstructionDocument is not embedded inside Fabric objects

groups are metadata-first unless group editing is already stable
```

```txt
Firebase/GCS storage paths
```

```txt
How the editor receives and preserves the reconstructed design.
```

```txt
Fabric is the editor projection.
```

## ChatGPT Response 013

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 77cb6c5d-b714-44af-8f5d-da2ac806c10d, cf9af243-9385-408c-9115-1036c5ef0f85, 2ac1d684-1295-4d2f-9f39-19cf1d202834 -->

I’m moving strictly into Step 3: the Firebase/GCS durable asset model, using primary docs and avoiding Firestore job state, orchestration, workers, or model adapters.

The key storage decisions are immutable generated assets and durable identity as `bucket + storagePath + generation`. Runtime access should use signed URLs or an authenticated proxy, not non-expiring Firebase download URLs.

# Step 3 — Firebase/GCS asset model

This step defines **where bytes live**, how they are identified, how the Fabric editor receives them, and how they are retained or deleted.

The locked rule:

```txt
Firestore = metadata, state, indexes, pointers
GCS / Firebase Storage = all bytes
Fabric JSON = runtime editor projection
signed URLs = temporary access
bucket + storagePath + generation = durable asset identity
```

Do **not** store images, masks, base64 strings, large SVGs, raw AI responses, or large Fabric snapshots in Firestore. Firestore documents are capped at 1 MiB, so the storage model must assume all heavy artifacts live in GCS/Firebase Storage. citeturn283432view4

---

# 3.1 The asset identity contract

Every file produced by Magic Layers must have a durable asset identity:

```ts
type DurableAssetIdentity = {
  assetId: string;
  bucket: string;
  storagePath: string;
  generation?: string;
  metageneration?: string;
  checksum?: {
    algorithm: "sha256" | "md5";
    value: string;
  };
};
```

Do **not** use these as durable identity:

```txt
signed URL
Firebase download URL
https://storage.googleapis.com/...
https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/...
base64 blob
public CDN URL
```

A signed URL is deliberately temporary: anyone holding it can use it while it is active. citeturn775261view0 Firebase Admin can also generate non-expiring download URLs, and Firebase explicitly says anyone with such a URL can permanently access the file, so those should not be your default for private user designs. citeturn775261view1

The durable identity is:

```txt
assetId + bucket + storagePath + generation
```

Cloud Storage object generations uniquely identify object versions, while metageneration tracks metadata updates for a specific generation. citeturn283432view7

---

# 3.2 Bucket model

Use **two buckets**, not one public bucket and not per-user buckets.

```txt
MAGIC_LAYERS_SOURCE_BUCKET
MAGIC_LAYERS_ASSETS_BUCKET
```

Firebase Storage is backed by Google Cloud Storage buckets and can be accessed by Firebase client SDKs, Firebase Admin SDK, and Google Cloud Storage APIs. citeturn283432view0 Firebase also supports multiple buckets in one app/project, each with its own location. citeturn117327view0

## Bucket 1 — source bucket

Purpose:

```txt
raw user upload
canonical original
normalized image
raw AI model outputs
raw OCR output
raw Gemini output
raw LayerD output
intermediate masks
diagnostics
temporary artifacts
```

Access policy:

```txt
private
client can only create upload landing-zone files
server can read/write canonical files
no public URLs
no permanent download URLs
short lifecycle for temporary/debug files
```

## Bucket 2 — assets bucket

Purpose:

```txt
editor-visible reference image
clean background
accepted layer PNGs
fallback crops
accepted masks
SVG/vector assets
reconstruction documents
Fabric manifests
preview renders
version snapshots
exports
ZIP layer exports
```

Access policy:

```txt
private
server writes
client reads through signed URLs or an authenticated proxy
CORS enabled for editor origins
public access prevention enforced
uniform bucket-level access enabled
```

Uniform bucket-level access is recommended because it disables object ACLs and makes IAM the uniform access-control system, reducing accidental exposure through ACLs. citeturn399456view0 Public access prevention should be enforced because it blocks accidental `allUsers` or `allAuthenticatedUsers` exposure, while still allowing signed URLs because signed URLs operate through scoped service account permissions. citeturn236518view0

---

# 3.3 Region rule

Put these in the same primary geography unless you have a hard residency reason not to:

```txt
Cloud Run worker
Firestore database
source bucket
assets bucket
export worker
```

When provisioning a Firebase Storage bucket, you choose a location, and Firebase recommends storing data close to users and services that need it. Firebase’s current docs also state that once a bucket is provisioned, its location setting cannot be changed. citeturn117327view1

For India-heavy usage, a practical default is:

```txt
asia-south1 or nearby supported Google Cloud region
```

For global product-first simplicity, choose one primary region now and add regional buckets later only when latency, residency, or cost forces it.

Do **not** create per-user buckets.

---

# 3.4 Default bucket naming note

For new Firebase projects, the default Cloud Storage bucket name format is now:

```txt
PROJECT_ID.firebasestorage.app
```

Legacy default buckets created before September 2024 may use:

```txt
PROJECT_ID.appspot.com
```

Firebase documents this distinction directly. citeturn117327view0

Use environment variables instead of hardcoding either format:

```env
MAGIC_LAYERS_SOURCE_BUCKET=your-source-bucket.firebasestorage.app
MAGIC_LAYERS_ASSETS_BUCKET=your-assets-bucket.firebasestorage.app
```

# 3.6 Update `AiAssetRef`

Patch the Step 1 `AiAssetRef`:

```ts
export type AiAssetStorageRole = "source" | "assets";

export type AiAssetRef = {
  id: string;

  kind: AiAssetKind;

  storageRole: AiAssetStorageRole;

  bucket: string;

  storagePath: string;

  /**
   * Runtime only.
   * Do not treat this as durable identity.
   */
  url?: string;
  urlExpiresAt?: number;

  height?: number;
```

Cloud Storage supports custom metadata, but it has size limits and storage cost implications, so custom metadata should stay small and operational. Do not use object metadata as your main application database. citeturn283432view3

# 3.7 Canonical storage paths

Use `workspaces`, not `users`, in every canonical path.

Reason:

```txt
personal account today
team workspace tomorrow
agency workspace later
enterprise workspace eventually
```

## Source bucket paths

```txt
client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/original.{ext}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/source/original/{assetId}/original.{ext}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/source/normalized/{assetId}/normalized.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/raw/gemini-layout/{assetId}.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/raw/ocr/{assetId}.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/raw/segmentation/{assetId}.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/raw/layerd/{assetId}.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/intermediate/masks/{assetId}.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/diagnostics/{assetId}.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/diagnostics/{assetId}.png

tmp/magic-layers/{jobId}/{assetId}
```

## Assets bucket paths

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/reference/{assetId}.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/background/{assetId}.clean.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.editor.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.export.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/layers/{layerId}/{assetId}.mask.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/fallbacks/{layerId}/{assetId}.crop.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/vectors/{layerId}/{assetId}.svg

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/manifests/{assetId}.reconstruction.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/manifests/{assetId}.fabric-manifest.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/versions/{versionId}/fabric.json

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/versions/{versionId}/thumbnail.webp

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}/final.png

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}/final.jpg

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}/layers.zip
```

Object names in Cloud Storage can contain valid Unicode, but there are restrictions: no carriage return or line feed, no `.` or `..`, cannot start with `.well-known/acme-challenge/`, and flat namespace object names are limited to 1–1024 bytes when UTF-8 encoded. Use lowercase safe ASCII IDs and never use user-provided filenames in canonical paths. citeturn283432view5

# 3.8 Object naming rules

Use generated IDs:

```txt
asset_01jz7k5f7vdn8h2ef0q2m4c92v.editor.png
asset_01jz7k6p4cfv3mrd9mm3qde71a.mask.png
asset_01jz7k7b8m2f6tk9n35whq2f4j.reconstruction.json
```

Do not use:

```txt
summer sale final.png
layer 1.png
user-uploaded-filename.jpg
logo.png
background.png
```

Rule:

```txt
human-readable folder prefix
machine-stable assetId filename
correct extension
no spaces
no user filenames
no overwrites
```

---

# 3.9 Immutable asset rule

Generated assets are immutable.

Bad:

```txt
layers/layer_001.png
```

Good:

```txt
layers/layer_001/asset_01jz7k5f7vdn8h2ef0q2m4c92v.editor.png
```

If a layer is regenerated:

```txt
layers/layer_001/asset_new.editor.png
```

Then the reconstruction document or design version points to the new asset.

Use create-only writes with generation preconditions. Cloud Storage supports request preconditions to prevent writes from applying to unexpected object states, and `ifGenerationMatch: 0` only proceeds when no live object with that name exists. citeturn100460view0

---

# 3.10 Runtime URL policy

The canonical asset stores:

```txt
bucket
storagePath
generation
assetId
```

The editor receives:

```txt
temporary HTTPS signed URL
```

Flow:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
→ asset refs with bucket/storagePath
→ URL resolver hydrates temporary signed URLs
→ AiFabricManifest runtime response
→ Fabric loads images
```

Do **not** persist signed URLs inside the canonical reconstruction document.

Do **not** persist signed URL enriched Fabric manifests as durable truth.

Correct:

```txt
stored durable manifest:
  asset refs only

runtime manifest returned to editor:
  asset refs + resolved signed URLs
```

Signed URLs are appropriate here because the editor needs browser-loadable URLs but your assets should remain private. citeturn775261view0

---

# 3.11 CORS policy for Fabric

Every Fabric image loaded from GCS must be export-safe.

Your Fabric image objects use:

```ts
crossOrigin: "anonymous"
```

Your bucket must return CORS headers for your app origins. Firebase’s web download docs state that browser direct downloads require bucket CORS configuration. citeturn283432view1 Cloud Storage supports bucket-level CORS configuration for browser access from specific origins. citeturn283432view2

This matters because if a cross-origin image is drawn into a canvas without CORS approval, the canvas becomes tainted and browser APIs like `toBlob()`, `toDataURL()`, and `getImageData()` can throw `SecurityError`. citeturn201986search0

Use restricted origins, not wildcard, for private editor assets.

`cors.assets.json`:

```json
[
  {
    "origin": [
      "http://localhost:3000",
      "https://app.yourdomain.com"
    ],
    "method": ["GET", "HEAD"],
    "responseHeader": [
      "Content-Type",
      "Cache-Control",
      "Content-Disposition",
      "Content-Length",
      "ETag"
    ],
    "maxAgeSeconds": 3600
  }
]
```

Source bucket usually does not need browser CORS if only server reads it. If you ever serve the normalized reference directly from the source bucket into Fabric, apply the same CORS policy there too. Cleaner default: copy an editor reference image into the assets bucket.

---

# 3.12 Editor-resolution versus export-resolution assets

Every raster layer should support two variants:

```txt
editor PNG
export PNG
```

Editor PNG:

```txt
optimized for Fabric performance
cropped to bbox
transparent RGBA
max long edge: 2048–3072 px
```

Export PNG:

```txt
higher resolution
used by server-side export
can be generated lazily
not always loaded in browser
```

Schema usage:

```ts
raster: {
  editorAssetId: "asset_layer_001_editor",
  exportAssetId: "asset_layer_001_export",
  maskAssetId: "asset_layer_001_mask",
  originalCropAssetId: "asset_layer_001_crop"
}
```

Fabric should load:

```txt
editorAssetId
```

Server export should prefer:

```txt
exportAssetId
```

Fallback:

```txt
editorAssetId
```

This keeps the editor smooth without destroying final export quality.

---

# 3.13 Cache policy

Because generated asset paths are immutable, accepted editor assets can be cached aggressively.

```ts
export function cacheControlForAssetKind(kind: AiAssetKind): string {
  switch (kind) {
    case "original_image":
    case "normalized_image":
    case "raw_model_output_json":
    case "raw_ocr_output_json":
    case "raw_layout_output_json":
    case "raw_segmentation_output_json":
    case "diagnostic":
    case "temporary":
      return "private, no-store";

    case "reconstruction_document":
    case "fabric_manifest":
    case "fabric_runtime_json":
      return "private, no-cache";

    case "intermediate_mask_png":
      return "private, max-age=86400";

    case "editor_reference_image":
    case "accepted_mask_png":
    case "rgba_png":
    case "editor_png":
    case "export_png":
    case "original_crop":
    case "fallback_crop":
    case "clean_background":
    case "svg":
      return "private, max-age=31536000, immutable";

    case "preview_render":
    case "thumbnail":
    case "diff_heatmap":
      return "private, max-age=86400";

    case "final_export":
    case "zip_export":
      return "private, max-age=604800";

    default:
      return "private, no-cache";
  }
}
```

Cloud Storage object metadata controls response behavior such as `Cache-Control` and `Content-Type`. citeturn998986search24

---

# 3.14 Lifecycle policy

Do not retain all intermediate artifacts forever.

Durable while design exists:

```txt
raw original
normalized image
editor reference image
accepted layer assets
fallback crops
clean background
accepted masks
reconstruction document
Fabric manifest
version snapshots
final exports
```

Delete after short retention:

```txt
tmp files
failed job scratch
intermediate masks
debug renders
raw model outputs if not needed for audit
visual-diff heatmaps
```

Cloud Storage lifecycle rules can delete objects by conditions such as age, prefix, and suffix. Lifecycle changes may take up to 24 hours to go into effect, so they are not immediate cleanup guarantees. citeturn283432view6

`lifecycle.source.json`:

```json
{
  "rule": [
    {
      "action": { "type": "Delete" },
      "condition": {
        "age": 3,
        "matchesPrefix": ["tmp/"]
      }
    },
    {
      "action": { "type": "Delete" },
      "condition": {
        "age": 7,
        "matchesPrefix": ["client-uploads/"]
      }
    },
    {
      "action": { "type": "Delete" },
      "condition": {
        "age": 45,
        "matchesPrefix": ["workspaces/"],
        "matchesSuffix": [
          ".diagnostic.json",
          ".debug.png",
          ".heatmap.png"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Do not enable Object Versioning by default. Your app already creates immutable paths. Object Versioning keeps noncurrent versions and those versions are charged; Google recommends soft delete over Object Versioning for protection against accidental or malicious deletion in many cases. citeturn599677view0

---

# 3.15 Client upload landing zone

Client uploads should go only here:

```txt
client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/original.{ext}
```

Then server verifies and copies into canonical source paths.

Why:

```txt
client bytes are untrusted
canonical paths are server-owned
workspace permission must be server-decided
AI pipeline should only consume verified normalized assets
```

Firebase Storage Rules can use `request.auth.uid` and validate upload metadata such as `request.resource.size` and `request.resource.contentType`. citeturn117327view2

`storage.rules`:

```js
rules_version = '2';

service firebase.storage {
  match /b/{bucket}/o {
    function signedIn() {
      return request.auth != null;
    }

    function validOriginalUpload() {
      return request.resource.size < 30 * 1024 * 1024
        && request.resource.contentType.matches('image/(png|jpeg|webp)');
    }

    match /client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/{fileName} {
      allow create: if signedIn()
        && request.auth.uid == uid
        && validOriginalUpload();

      allow read, update, delete: if false;
    }

    match /{path=**} {
      allow read, write: if false;
    }
  }
}
```

Enable App Check for client-facing Storage access. App Check supports Cloud Storage for Firebase and rejects requests without valid attestation when enforcement is enabled, but it does not replace Auth or server-side authorization. citeturn117327view3

---

# 3.16 Backend verification rule

Security Rules are first-pass checks only.

The backend must still verify:

```txt
actual MIME via magic bytes
decode validity
image dimensions
pixel count
file size
EXIF orientation
animated WebP rejection if unsupported
color profile normalization
malformed image rejection
perceptual hash
sha256 hash
```

Never trust:

```txt
client MIME type
file extension
user-provided filename
client-provided dimensions
client-provided hash
```

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/storage/storage-buckets.ts

export type MagicStorageRole = "source" | "assets";

export type MagicStorageBucketConfig = {
  sourceBucket: string;
  assetsBucket: string;
};

export function getMagicStorageBucketConfig(): MagicStorageBucketConfig {
  const sourceBucket = process.env.MAGIC_LAYERS_SOURCE_BUCKET;
  const assetsBucket = process.env.MAGIC_LAYERS_ASSETS_BUCKET;

  if (!sourceBucket) {
    throw new Error("Missing MAGIC_LAYERS_SOURCE_BUCKET");
  }

  if (!assetsBucket) {
    throw new Error("Missing MAGIC_LAYERS_ASSETS_BUCKET");
  }

  return {
    sourceBucket,
    assetsBucket,
  };
}

export function bucketForMagicStorageRole(role: MagicStorageRole): string {
  const config = getMagicStorageBucketConfig();

  switch (role) {
    case "source":
      return config.sourceBucket;

    case "assets":
      return config.assetsBucket;

    default:
      throw new Error(`Unknown storage role: ${role satisfies never}`);
  }
}
```

# 3.20 `write-ai-asset.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/storage/write-ai-asset.ts

import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { getStorage } from "firebase-admin/storage";

import type {
  AiAssetKind,
  AiAssetRef,
  AiSource,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import type { MagicStorageRole } from "./storage-buckets";
import { cacheControlForAssetKind } from "./cache-control";

export type WriteAiAssetInput = {
  storageRole: MagicStorageRole;

  bucket: string;
  storagePath: string;

  bytes: Buffer;

  assetId: string;
  kind: AiAssetKind;

  contentType: string;

  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId?: string;
  layerId?: string;

  width?: number;
  height?: number;

  source: AiSource;

  schemaVersion: string;
  pipelineVersion: string;

  sourceAssetId?: string;
  parentAssetId?: string;

  cacheControl?: string;
};

export async function writeAiAsset(
  input: WriteAiAssetInput
): Promise<AiAssetRef> {
  const bucket = getStorage().bucket(input.bucket);
  const file = bucket.file(input.storagePath);

  const sha256 = crypto
    .createHash("sha256")
    .update(input.bytes)
    .digest("hex");

  const cacheControl =
    input.cacheControl ?? cacheControlForAssetKind(input.kind);

  await file.save(input.bytes, {
    resumable: false,

    metadata: {
      contentType: input.contentType,
      cacheControl,

      metadata: {
        app: "magic-layers",

        workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
        designId: input.designId,
        jobId: input.jobId ?? "",
        layerId: input.layerId ?? "",

        assetId: input.assetId,
        assetKind: input.kind,

        source: input.source,

        schemaVersion: input.schemaVersion,
        pipelineVersion: input.pipelineVersion,

        sourceAssetId: input.sourceAssetId ?? "",
        parentAssetId: input.parentAssetId ?? "",

        sha256,
      },
    },

    /**
     * Create-only write. Prevents accidental overwrite.
     */
    preconditionOpts: {
      ifGenerationMatch: 0,
    },
  });

  const [metadata] = await file.getMetadata();

  return {
    id: input.assetId,

    kind: input.kind,

    storageRole: input.storageRole,

    bucket: input.bucket,
    storagePath: input.storagePath,

    mimeType: input.contentType,

    width: input.width,
    height: input.height,

    sizeBytes: Number(metadata.size ?? input.bytes.byteLength),

    generation:
      typeof metadata.generation === "string"
        ? metadata.generation
        : undefined,

    metageneration:
      typeof metadata.metageneration === "string"
        ? metadata.metageneration
        : undefined,

    cacheControl,

    checksum: {
      algorithm: "sha256",
      value: sha256,
    },

    metadata: {
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      jobId: input.jobId,
      layerId: input.layerId,

      assetId: input.assetId,
      assetKind: input.kind,

      source: input.source,

      schemaVersion: input.schemaVersion,
      pipelineVersion: input.pipelineVersion,

      sourceAssetId: input.sourceAssetId,
      parentAssetId: input.parentAssetId,

      createdAt: Date.now(),
    },
  };
}
```

# 3.21 `resolve-ai-asset-url.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/storage/resolve-ai-asset-url.ts

import { getStorage } from "firebase-admin/storage";
import type { AiAssetRef } from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

export type ResolveAiAssetUrlInput = {
  asset: AiAssetRef;

  expiresInMs?: number;

  /**
   * Optional override for download filename.
   */
  responseDisposition?: string;

  /**
   * Optional response content type override.
   */
  responseType?: string;
};

export type ResolvedAiAssetUrl = {
  url: string;
  urlExpiresAt: number;
};

export async function resolveAiAssetSignedUrl(
  input: ResolveAiAssetUrlInput
): Promise<ResolvedAiAssetUrl> {
  const expiresInMs = input.expiresInMs ?? 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
  const urlExpiresAt = Date.now() + expiresInMs;

  if (!input.asset.bucket) {
    throw new Error(`Asset ${input.asset.id} is missing bucket`);
  }

  if (!input.asset.storagePath) {
    throw new Error(`Asset ${input.asset.id} is missing storagePath`);
  }

  const file = getStorage()
    .bucket(input.asset.bucket)
    .file(input.asset.storagePath);

  const [url] = await file.getSignedUrl({
    version: "v4",
    action: "read",
    expires: urlExpiresAt,
    responseDisposition: input.responseDisposition,
    responseType: input.responseType,
  });

  return {
    url,
    urlExpiresAt,
  };
}
```

# 3.22 `client-upload-original.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/storage/client-upload-original.ts

import {
  getStorage,
  ref,
  uploadBytesResumable,
  type UploadTask,
} from "firebase/storage";

export function uploadOriginalToLandingZone(input: {
  uid: string;
  uploadId: string;
  file: File;
}): UploadTask {
  const extension = extensionFromMime(input.file.type);

  const storage = getStorage();

  const path = `client-uploads/${input.uid}/${input.uploadId}/original.${extension}`;

  const storageRef = ref(storage, path);

  return uploadBytesResumable(storageRef, input.file, {
    contentType: input.file.type,
    customMetadata: {
      purpose: "magic-layers-original-upload",
      uid: input.uid,
      uploadId: input.uploadId,
    },
  });
}

function extensionFromMime(mimeType: string): "png" | "jpg" | "webp" {
  switch (mimeType) {
    case "image/png":
      return "png";

    case "image/jpeg":
      return "jpg";

    case "image/webp":
      return "webp";

    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported image MIME type: ${mimeType}`);
  }
}
```

# 3.23 What goes into Firestore later

Step 4 will define the Firestore collections, but Step 3 already locks the rule.

Firestore may store:

```txt
assetId
kind
bucket
storagePath
generation
metageneration
mimeType
width
height
sizeBytes
checksum
createdAt
current manifest pointer
current reconstruction pointer
```

Firestore must not store:

```txt
base64 images
PNG bytes
mask bytes
raw model responses
large SVG path dumps
signed URLs as permanent state
large autosave snapshots every second
```

---

# 3.24 Cost control implications

This feature creates many files per design:

```txt
original image
normalized image
working scale image
clean background
N masks
N layer PNGs
N fallback crops
raw OCR JSON
raw Gemini JSON
raw decomposition JSON
reconstruction JSON
Fabric manifest
preview render
exports
```

Cloud Storage pricing is based on stored data, processing/operations, and network usage, so this system must reduce unnecessary asset size, repeated downloads, and object churn. citeturn148695search0

Hard rules:

```txt
crop layer PNGs to bbox
do not create full-canvas transparent PNGs for every layer
separate editor and export assets
generate export-resolution assets lazily where possible
cache immutable accepted assets
delete temporary artifacts by lifecycle
dedupe uploads by perceptual hash + sha256 where possible
do not store signed URL manifests as durable state
```

---

# 3.25 Non-negotiable invariants

Step 3 is only valid if these are true:

```txt
No base64 assets in Firestore.

No base64 assets in Fabric JSON.

No public buckets for private designs.

No permanent Firebase download URLs for private editor assets.

Every asset has assetId.

Every durable asset has bucket + storagePath.

Every accepted asset path is immutable.

Every generated write uses create-only semantics.

Every browser-loaded Fabric image uses a CORS-safe HTTPS URL.

Every signed URL can expire without breaking saved designs.

Every raw original is preserved.

Every editor-visible raster layer has an editor asset.

Every export-quality raster layer can be separate from editor asset.

Every temporary artifact has a lifecycle policy.

Every canonical path uses workspaceId/designId.

Every client upload enters through a landing zone.

Every canonical asset is server-owned.

Every asset can be traced back to workspaceId, designId, jobId, layerId, source, schemaVersion, and pipelineVersion.
```

```txt
Raw bytes and generated assets live in GCS/Firebase Storage.

AiReconstructionDocument stores asset references.

AiFabricManifest receives runtime signed URLs.

Durable identity is bucket + storagePath + generation, never URL.
```

# Step 4 — Firestore job and design state model

Firestore is **not** the storage layer and not the AI processing layer.

Firestore’s role is:

```txt
ownership
job state
current pointers
small indexes
progress UI
audit trail
version pointers
cost counters
```

Large objects stay in GCS because Firestore documents have a hard 1 MiB document limit. citeturn729125search0

---

## 4.1 Core rule

Use Firestore for **state and pointers only**.

Do not store:

```txt
base64 images
mask bytes
PNG bytes
large Fabric JSON autosaves
raw Gemini responses
raw OCR responses
large SVG paths
signed URLs as durable data
```

Store:

```txt
assetId
bucket
storagePath
generation
status
owner ids
currentManifestAssetId
currentReconstructionAssetId
currentVersionId
small quality scores
small counters
timestamps
```

---

## 4.2 Collections

Use this structure:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/versions/{versionId}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/aiLayerJobs/{jobId}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/aiLayerJobs/{jobId}/events/{eventId}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/assets/{assetId}

workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}
```

Avoid global top-level `aiLayerJobs/{jobId}` unless you need admin queue views. Workspace nesting keeps security rules simpler.

---

## 4.3 `workspaces/{workspaceId}`

```ts
type WorkspaceDoc = {
  id: string;

  ownerUserId: string;

  memberUserIds: string[];

  plan: "free" | "starter" | "pro" | "team" | "enterprise";

  magicLayers: {
    enabled: boolean;
    monthlyJobLimit: number;
    monthlyJobCount: number;
    maxImageMegapixels: number;
    maxLayerCount: number;
  };

  createdAt: Timestamp;
  updatedAt: Timestamp;
};
```

Keep membership small here. If teams become large later, move members to:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}
```

---

## 4.4 `designs/{designId}`

This is the current design pointer.

```ts
type DesignDoc = {
  id: string;

  workspaceId: string;
  ownerUserId: string;

  title: string;

  source: {
    kind: "magic_layers" | "blank" | "template" | "manual_upload";

    | "draft"
    | "processing"
    | "ready"
```

Do not put full Fabric JSON here.

## 4.5 `versions/{versionId}`

Versions point to immutable snapshots in GCS.

```ts
type DesignVersionDoc = {
  id: string;

  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;

  source:
    | "magic_layers_initial"
    | "user_autosave"
    | "manual_save"
    | "export_checkpoint"
    | "repair_result";

  fabricJsonAssetId: string;
  thumbnailAssetId?: string;

  reconstructionAssetId?: string;
  fabricManifestAssetId?: string;

  parentVersionId?: string;

  stats: {
    objectCount: number;
    layerCount: number;
    textObjectCount: number;
    imageObjectCount: number;
    vectorObjectCount: number;
  };

  createdByUserId: string;
  createdAt: Timestamp;
};
```

Autosave should not create one version per keystroke. Use debounced current state plus periodic snapshots.

## 4.6 `aiLayerJobs/{jobId}`

This is the central job document.

```ts
type AiLayerJobDoc = {
  id: string;

  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  status:
    | "created"
    | "uploaded"
    | "normalizing"
    | "observing"
    | "decomposing"
    | "recovering_text"
    | "elementizing"
    | "vectorizing"
    | "repairing_background"
    | "resolving_scene"
    | "generating_fabric"
    | "validating"
    | "completed"
    | "failed"
    | "cancelled";

  progress: {
    percent: number;
    label: string;
    currentStep: string;
  };

  input: {
    uploadId: string;
    uploadPath: string;
    originalAssetId?: string;
    normalizedAssetId?: string;
    sha256?: string;
    perceptualHash?: string;
    mimeType?: "image/png" | "image/jpeg" | "image/webp";
    width?: number;
    height?: number;
  };

  output?: {
    reconstructionAssetId?: string;
    fabricManifestAssetId?: string;
    previewAssetId?: string;
    initialVersionId?: string;
  };

  quality?: {
    visualMatchScore?: number;
    textExactRate?: number;
    needsReview?: boolean;
    warnings?: string[];
  };

  cost: {
    geminiCalls: number;
    ocrCalls: number;
    segmentationCalls: number;
    storageWriteBytes: number;
    storageReadBytes: number;
    firestoreWrites: number;
  };

  error?: {
    code: string;
    message: string;
    retryable: boolean;
    failedStep?: string;
  };

  createdAt: Timestamp;
  updatedAt: Timestamp;
  startedAt?: Timestamp;
  completedAt?: Timestamp;
};
```

Job IDs should be random/auto IDs, not sequential. Firestore best practices warn against sequential document IDs because they can cause hotspots. citeturn729125search1

## 4.7 `aiLayerJobs/{jobId}/events/{eventId}`

Use events for debugging and progress history.

```ts
type AiLayerJobEventDoc = {
  id: string;

  type:
    | "status_changed"
    | "step_started"
    | "step_completed"
    | "asset_created"
    | "warning"
    | "error"
    | "cost_update"
    | "quality_update";

  step?: string;

  message: string;

  assetId?: string;

  metadata?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;

  createdAt: Timestamp;
};
```

Do not write too many events. Aggregate noisy worker logs into GCS diagnostics. Firestore pricing is operation-based, so event spam becomes cost. citeturn729125search15

Firestore asset index for GCS files.

## 4.10 Security model

Client can read only workspace-owned metadata.

Client should not write canonical AI outputs.

Allowed client writes:

```txt
create upload request / job request
update lightweight editor current pointer if authorized
create manual save/version request
create export request
```

Server-only writes:

```txt
job status transitions
asset index docs
reconstruction output pointers
quality scores
cost counters
completion/failure
```

Security rules must stay simple. Firestore rules have document access call limits for rules evaluation, including 10 for single-document/query requests and 20 for multi-document/transactions/batches. citeturn729125search20

---

## 4.11 Index strategy

Needed queries:

```txt
designs by workspaceId + updatedAt desc

aiLayerJobs by designId + createdAt desc

aiLayerJobs by workspaceId + status + createdAt desc

assets by designId + kind + createdAt desc

versions by designId + createdAt desc

exports by designId + createdAt desc
```

Do not index high-cardinality noisy fields unless queried.

Do not create indexes for:

```txt
error.message
progress.label
large metadata maps
warnings arrays
raw model ids
```

---

## 4.12 Cost rules

Firestore cost control:

```txt
No per-layer live updates during processing.

No logs as Firestore documents unless user-visible.

No full Fabric JSON in documents.

No autosave on every Fabric object movement.

Debounce autosave.

Store autosave snapshots in GCS.

Use one job doc for live progress.

Use event docs only for meaningful milestones.
```

Target write shape per job:

```txt
1 job create
8–15 job status updates
N asset index writes
1 design update
1 version write
5–20 event writes max
```

---

## 4.13 Locked Step 4 architecture

```txt
Firestore owns:
  workspace access
  design pointer
  job status
  asset index
  version pointer
  export status
  small counters

GCS owns:
  images
  masks
  manifests
  Fabric JSON
  raw AI outputs
  previews
  exports

Workers own:
  state transitions
  asset creation
  output pointers

Client owns:
  upload initiation
  editor interaction
  debounced save requests
```

Step 4 is complete when these collections, document shapes, security boundaries, and indexes are defined.

## ChatGPT Response 015

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 7d232cbb-a3fa-4dad-a445-baf615cf3b2b, 507fd72e-69c9-4e56-a96d-05a5e607522f, 8b0802f6-11dc-43c2-a3ba-725835818e10 -->

I’ll lock Step 5 to orchestration only: API boundaries, queueing, worker ownership, retries, cancellation, idempotency, and state transitions. Default path: Cloud Tasks to authenticated Cloud Run; Pub/Sub stays secondary for fan-out.

Important refinement: Cloud Tasks should dispatch/start the work, not hold the full AI pipeline open. Long decomposition should run in Cloud Run Jobs or a worker flow beyond a single task deadline.

# Step 5 — Job orchestration

Step 5 locks how a user action becomes a reliable AI reconstruction job.

The correct orchestration model is:

```txt
Client
→ Next.js API
→ Firestore job doc
→ Cloud Tasks queue
→ private Cloud Run dispatcher
→ Cloud Run Job worker
→ Firestore progress + GCS assets
→ Fabric manifest ready
```

The hard rule:

```txt
Next.js never performs AI decomposition.
Cloud Tasks never waits for the full decomposition.
Cloud Run Job owns heavy processing.
Firestore owns state.
GCS owns bytes.
```

Cloud Tasks HTTP tasks have a default 10-minute deadline and a maximum 30-minute deadline, so they should dispatch work, not hold the entire AI job open. Cloud Run services can run HTTP requests up to 60 minutes, but Google explicitly warns that long requests need idempotency and retry tolerance. Cloud Run Jobs are the better primitive for run-to-completion AI processing because they execute tasks until completion and support much longer task timeouts. citeturn523257view1turn872093view4turn523257view0

---

## 5.1 Final orchestration decision

Use **Cloud Tasks + Cloud Run Jobs**.

Not:

```txt
Client → Next.js API → process image synchronously
```

Not:

```txt
Client → Next.js API → Cloud Run service waits for full AI job
```

Not:

```txt
Firestore trigger watches job docs and starts processing implicitly
```

Correct:

```txt
Next.js API creates job state.
Cloud Tasks controls dispatch and rate limits.
Cloud Run dispatcher starts Cloud Run Job.
Cloud Run Job performs heavy AI work.
```

Reason:

```txt
Cloud Tasks gives queueing, retries, deduplication, rate limits.
Cloud Run Job gives long-running batch execution.
Firestore gives user-visible progress.
GCS gives durable artifact storage.
```

Cloud Tasks supports reliable HTTP target dispatch and configurable rate/concurrency control, while Cloud Run Jobs can be executed programmatically and can receive runtime overrides such as arguments, environment variables, task count, and timeout. citeturn523257view1turn872093view0turn722889view0

---

# 5.2 System flow

```txt
1. Client uploads image to Storage landing zone.

2. Client calls:
   POST /api/magic-layers/jobs

3. Next.js API:
   - verifies Firebase Auth ID token
   - verifies App Check token
   - checks workspace permission
   - checks quota
   - creates design/job docs
   - enqueues Cloud Task
   - returns jobId/designId immediately

4. Cloud Tasks calls:
   POST /tasks/magic-layers/dispatch

5. Cloud Run dispatcher:
   - verifies IAM invocation
   - claims job idempotently
   - starts Cloud Run Job execution
   - stores Cloud Run execution name
   - returns 2xx to Cloud Tasks

6. Cloud Run Job worker:
   - reads job doc
   - reads input assets from GCS
   - runs step machine
   - writes outputs to GCS
   - updates Firestore progress
   - writes reconstruction + Fabric manifest pointers
   - marks completed / failed / cancelled

7. Client watches Firestore job/design docs.
```

The user sees one smooth action. Internally, the system is queued, resumable, auditable, and cancellable.

---

# 5.3 Services

You need four runtime surfaces.

```txt
Next.js API
Public user-facing API.

Cloud Tasks queue
Durable dispatch and rate limiting.

Cloud Run dispatcher service
Small private HTTP service. Starts Cloud Run Job executions.

Cloud Run Job worker
Heavy AI processing container.
```

Do **not** collapse dispatcher and worker into one HTTP service. That would reintroduce request-timeout coupling.

---

# 5.4 Required endpoints

## Public endpoint

```txt
POST /api/magic-layers/jobs
```

Purpose:

```txt
create job
create design if needed
enqueue dispatch task
return immediately
```

Request:

```ts

  workspaceId: string;

  /**
   * Existing design if importing into an existing canvas.
   * If omitted, API creates a new design.
   */
  designId?: string;

  uploadId: string;

  /**
   * Must be client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/original.ext
   */
```

```ts
  status: "uploaded";

```

```txt
GET /api/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}
```

This can return the job doc, but in the editor you should primarily use a Firestore listener for progress.

Cloud Run supports cancelling running job executions through console, gcloud, client libraries, and REST API. citeturn941293view1

## Internal dispatcher endpoint

```txt
POST /tasks/magic-layers/dispatch
```

Only Cloud Tasks should call this.

Payload:

# 5.5 Job doc orchestration patch

Patch the Step 4 `AiLayerJobDoc` with this field:

```ts
type AiLayerJobOrchestration = {
  kind: "initial_reconstruction";

  dispatch: {
    state:
      | "pending"
      | "enqueued"
      | "dispatching"
      | "execution_started"
      | "dispatch_failed";

    queueName?: string;
    taskName?: string;

    dispatchAttemptCount: number;

    lastDispatchError?: {
      code: string;
      message: string;
    };
  };

  execution: {
    backend: "cloud_run_job";

    cloudRunJobName?: string;
    cloudRunExecutionName?: string;

    executionStartedAt?: Timestamp;
    executionCompletedAt?: Timestamp;

    workerAttemptCount: number;

    heartbeatAt?: Timestamp;
  };

  cancellation: {
    cancelRequested: boolean;
    cancelRequestedAt?: Timestamp;
    cancelledAt?: Timestamp;
    cancelReason?: string;
  };

  idempotency: {
```
