```ts
    requestId: string;
    dedupeKey: string;
  };
};
```

Full job patch:

```ts
type AiLayerJobDoc = {
  // Step 4 fields...

  orchestration: AiLayerJobOrchestration;
};
```

Do not add a new top-level job status like `queued`. Step 4 status remains the product-visible state. Orchestration state is internal.

---

# 5.6 Allowed job status transitions

Use a hard status machine.

```ts
export const MAGIC_LAYER_JOB_STATUSES = [
  "created",
  "uploaded",
  "normalizing",
  "observing",
  "decomposing",
  "recovering_text",
  "elementizing",
  "vectorizing",
  "repairing_background",
  "resolving_scene",
  "generating_fabric",
  "validating",
  "completed",
  "failed",
  "cancelled",
] as const;

export type MagicLayerJobStatus =
  (typeof MAGIC_LAYER_JOB_STATUSES)[number];

export const ALLOWED_JOB_TRANSITIONS: Record<
  MagicLayerJobStatus,
  MagicLayerJobStatus[]
> = {
  created: ["uploaded", "cancelled", "failed"],

  uploaded: ["normalizing", "cancelled", "failed"],

  normalizing: ["observing", "cancelled", "failed"],

  observing: ["decomposing", "recovering_text", "cancelled", "failed"],

  decomposing: ["recovering_text", "elementizing", "cancelled", "failed"],

  recovering_text: ["elementizing", "cancelled", "failed"],

  elementizing: ["vectorizing", "repairing_background", "cancelled", "failed"],

  vectorizing: ["repairing_background", "resolving_scene", "cancelled", "failed"],

  repairing_background: ["resolving_scene", "cancelled", "failed"],

  resolving_scene: ["generating_fabric", "cancelled", "failed"],

  generating_fabric: ["validating", "cancelled", "failed"],

  validating: ["completed", "cancelled", "failed"],

  completed: [],

  failed: [],

  cancelled: [],
};

export function assertValidJobTransition(
  from: MagicLayerJobStatus,
  to: MagicLayerJobStatus
) {
  if (!ALLOWED_JOB_TRANSITIONS[from]?.includes(to)) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid Magic Layers job transition: ${from} → ${to}`);
  }
}
```

All state transitions should happen from server code using Firestore transactions where concurrent workers could race. Firestore transactions provide serializable isolation, and server client libraries use the database’s concurrency controls, so this is the right primitive for claiming and transitioning jobs. citeturn523257view6

---

# 5.7 Client → Next.js API contract

The Next.js API route must run in Node.js runtime, not Edge runtime.

```ts
export const runtime = "nodejs";
```

Responsibilities:

```txt
verify Firebase Auth
verify App Check
validate upload path
check workspace membership
check quota
create job/design docs
enqueue Cloud Task
return immediately
```

Firebase Admin SDK can verify Firebase ID tokens and return the authenticated `uid`. Firebase App Check can be verified on custom backends using the Admin SDK, and failed App Check requests should be rejected. citeturn259952view0turn523257view5

---

## Example API skeleton

```ts
// src/app/api/magic-layers/jobs/route.ts

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getAuth } from "firebase-admin/auth";
import { getAppCheck } from "firebase-admin/app-check";
import { getFirestore, FieldValue } from "firebase-admin/firestore";
import { enqueueMagicLayersDispatchTask } from "@/lib/magic-layers/orchestration/enqueue-magic-layers-dispatch-task";
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";

export const runtime = "nodejs";

type CreateMagicLayersJobRequest = {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId?: string;
  uploadId: string;
  uploadPath: string;
  idempotencyKey: string;
};

export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  const authHeader = req.headers.get("authorization") ?? "";
  const idToken = authHeader.startsWith("Bearer ")
    ? authHeader.slice("Bearer ".length)
    : null;

  if (!idToken) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "missing_auth_token" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  const appCheckToken = req.headers.get("x-firebase-appcheck");

  if (!appCheckToken) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "missing_app_check" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  const [decodedAuth] = await Promise.all([
    getAuth().verifyIdToken(idToken),
    getAppCheck().verifyToken(appCheckToken),
  ]);

  const userId = decodedAuth.uid;

  const body = (await req.json()) as CreateMagicLayersJobRequest;

  validateCreateMagicLayersJobRequest(body, userId);

  const db = getFirestore();

  const designId = body.designId ?? db.collection("_").doc().id;
  const jobId = db.collection("_").doc().id;

  const requestId = createHash("sha256")
    .update(`${userId}:${body.workspaceId}:${body.idempotencyKey}`)
    .digest("hex");

  const dedupeKey = createHash("sha256")
    .update(`magic-layers:${body.workspaceId}:${designId}:${requestId}`)
    .digest("hex");

  const workspaceRef = db.doc(`workspaces/${body.workspaceId}`);
  const designRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${body.workspaceId}/designs/${designId}`
  );
  const jobRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${body.workspaceId}/designs/${designId}/aiLayerJobs/${jobId}`
  );
  const idempotencyRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${body.workspaceId}/idempotencyKeys/${requestId}`
  );

  let existing:
    | {
        jobId: string;
        designId: string;
      }
    | undefined;

  await db.runTransaction(async (tx) => {
    const [workspaceSnap, idemSnap] = await Promise.all([
      tx.get(workspaceRef),
      tx.get(idempotencyRef),
    ]);

    if (!workspaceSnap.exists) {
      throw new Error("workspace_not_found");
    }

    const workspace = workspaceSnap.data()!;

    if (
      workspace.ownerUserId !== userId &&
      !workspace.memberUserIds?.includes(userId)
    ) {
      throw new Error("workspace_forbidden");
    }

    if (idemSnap.exists) {
      const idem = idemSnap.data()!;
      existing = {
        jobId: idem.jobId,
        designId: idem.designId,
      };
      return;
    }

    tx.set(designRef, {
      id: designId,
      workspaceId: body.workspaceId,
      ownerUserId: userId,

      title: "Untitled design",

      source: {
        kind: "magic_layers",
      },

      canvas: {
        width: 0,
        height: 0,
        unit: "px",
      },

      current: {
        updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      },

      status: "processing",

      createdAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    tx.set(jobRef, {
      id: jobId,

      workspaceId: body.workspaceId,
      designId,
      userId,

      status: "uploaded",

      progress: {
        percent: 0,
        label: "Queued",
        currentStep: "uploaded",
      },

      input: {
        uploadId: body.uploadId,
        uploadPath: body.uploadPath,
      },

      cost: {
        geminiCalls: 0,
        ocrCalls: 0,
        segmentationCalls: 0,
        storageWriteBytes: 0,
        storageReadBytes: 0,
        firestoreWrites: 1,
      },

      orchestration: {
        kind: "initial_reconstruction",

        dispatch: {
          state: "pending",
          dispatchAttemptCount: 0,
        },

        execution: {
          backend: "cloud_run_job",
          workerAttemptCount: 0,
        },

        cancellation: {
          cancelRequested: false,
        },

        idempotency: {
          idempotencyKey: body.idempotencyKey,
          requestId,
          dedupeKey,
        },
      },

      createdAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    tx.set(idempotencyRef, {
      id: requestId,
      jobId,
      designId,
      userId,
      createdAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
  });

  if (existing) {
    return NextResponse.json({
      jobId: existing.jobId,
      designId: existing.designId,
      status: "uploaded",
    });
  }

  await enqueueMagicLayersDispatchTask({
    jobId,
    designId,
    workspaceId: body.workspaceId,
    userId,
    requestId,
  });

  await jobRef.update({
    "orchestration.dispatch.state": "enqueued",
    updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
  });

  return NextResponse.json(
    {
      jobId,
      designId,
      status: "uploaded",
    },
    { status: 202 }
  );
}

function validateCreateMagicLayersJobRequest(
  body: CreateMagicLayersJobRequest,
  userId: string
) {
  if (!body.workspaceId) throw new Error("missing_workspaceId");
  if (!body.uploadId) throw new Error("missing_uploadId");
  if (!body.uploadPath) throw new Error("missing_uploadPath");
  if (!body.idempotencyKey) throw new Error("missing_idempotencyKey");

  const expectedPrefix = `client-uploads/${userId}/${body.uploadId}/`;

  if (!body.uploadPath.startsWith(expectedPrefix)) {
    throw new Error("invalid_upload_path");
  }
}
```

---

# 5.8 Cloud Tasks enqueue contract

Use one primary queue first:

```txt
magic-layers-dispatch
```

Queue responsibilities:

```txt
smooth traffic spikes
rate-limit expensive AI jobs
retry dispatch failures
dedupe double-clicks / duplicate API attempts
protect Cloud Run worker capacity
```

Cloud Tasks supports configurable rate limits, including max dispatches per second and max concurrent dispatches. It also separates rate limits from retry configuration. citeturn872093view0turn872093view1

---

## Queue config

Start conservative:

```bash
gcloud tasks queues create magic-layers-dispatch \
  --location="$REGION" \
  --max-dispatches-per-second=1 \
  --max-concurrent-dispatches=5 \
  --max-attempts=5 \
  --min-backoff=10s \
  --max-backoff=300s \
  --max-doublings=4
```

Increase only after measuring:

```txt
average job duration
Gemini/API rate limits
Cloud Run Job concurrency
GCS egress/read patterns
Firestore write load
failure rate
```

---

## Enqueue function

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/orchestration/enqueue-magic-layers-dispatch-task.ts

import { CloudTasksClient } from "@google-cloud/tasks";
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";

const client = new CloudTasksClient();

export type EnqueueMagicLayersDispatchTaskInput = {
  jobId: string;
  designId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  userId: string;
  requestId: string;
};

export async function enqueueMagicLayersDispatchTask(
  input: EnqueueMagicLayersDispatchTaskInput
) {
  const projectId = requiredEnv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT");
  const location = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_TASKS_LOCATION");
  const queue = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_TASKS_QUEUE");
  const dispatcherUrl = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_DISPATCHER_URL");
  const invokerServiceAccount = requiredEnv(
    "MAGIC_LAYERS_TASKS_INVOKER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"
  );

  const parent = client.queuePath(projectId, location, queue);

  /**
   * Explicit task IDs enable Cloud Tasks deduplication.
   * Use a hash prefix, not sequential IDs.
   */
  const taskId = `ml-${createHash("sha256")
    .update(input.jobId)
    .digest("hex")
    .slice(0, 32)}`;

  const taskName = client.taskPath(projectId, location, queue, taskId);

  const payload = {
    jobId: input.jobId,
    designId: input.designId,
    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    userId: input.userId,
    kind: "initial_reconstruction",
    requestId: input.requestId,
    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };

  try {
    const [task] = await client.createTask({
      parent,
      task: {
        name: taskName,
        httpRequest: {
          httpMethod: "POST",
          url: `${dispatcherUrl}/tasks/magic-layers/dispatch`,
          headers: {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
          },
          body: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).toString("base64"),

          oidcToken: {
            serviceAccountEmail: invokerServiceAccount,
            audience: dispatcherUrl,
          },
        },

        /**
         * Dispatcher must only start Cloud Run Job and return.
         * It must not perform the full AI job.
         */
        dispatchDeadline: {
          seconds: 300,
        },
      },
    });

    return {
      taskName: task.name!,
      deduplicated: false,
    };
  } catch (error) {
    if (isAlreadyExistsError(error)) {
      return {
        taskName,
        deduplicated: true,
      };
    }

    throw error;
  }
}

function requiredEnv(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) throw new Error(`Missing env: ${name}`);
  return value;
}

function isAlreadyExistsError(error: unknown): boolean {
  const maybe = error as { code?: number; message?: string };

  return (
    maybe.code === 6 ||
    maybe.message?.includes("ALREADY_EXISTS") === true
  );
}
```

Explicit Cloud Tasks task IDs enable deduplication, but Google recommends avoiding sequential task IDs because they can increase latency and error rates; hashed IDs are appropriate here. citeturn625554view0

---

# 5.9 Dispatcher contract

The dispatcher is a small private Cloud Run service.

It does **not** run AI.

It does:

```txt
parse dispatch payload
claim job
start Cloud Run Job
save execution name
return 2xx
```

Cloud Tasks can attach an OIDC token when calling Cloud Run, and the Cloud Run service should require IAM authentication rather than being public. citeturn872093view3turn523257view3

---

## Dispatcher logic

```ts
// services/magic-layers-dispatcher/src/server.ts

import express from "express";
import { GoogleAuth } from "google-auth-library";
import { getFirestore, FieldValue } from "firebase-admin/firestore";

const app = express();

app.use(express.json({ limit: "64kb" }));

app.post("/tasks/magic-layers/dispatch", async (req, res) => {
  const payload = parseDispatchPayload(req.body);

  const claim = await claimJobForCloudRunExecution(payload);

  if (claim.action === "ignore") {
    return res.status(200).json({
      ignored: true,
      reason: claim.reason,
    });
  }

  const execution = await startMagicLayersCloudRunJob({
    jobId: payload.jobId,
    designId: payload.designId,
    workspaceId: payload.workspaceId,
    userId: payload.userId,
  });

  await saveCloudRunExecutionName({
    workspaceId: payload.workspaceId,
    designId: payload.designId,
    jobId: payload.jobId,
    executionName: execution.executionName,
  });

  return res.status(200).json({
    started: true,
    executionName: execution.executionName,
  });
});

export default app;

type DispatchPayload = {
  jobId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;
  kind: "initial_reconstruction";
  requestId: string;
  createdAt: number;
};

function parseDispatchPayload(value: unknown): DispatchPayload {
  const payload = value as DispatchPayload;

  if (!payload.jobId) throw new Error("missing_jobId");
  if (!payload.workspaceId) throw new Error("missing_workspaceId");
  if (!payload.designId) throw new Error("missing_designId");
  if (!payload.userId) throw new Error("missing_userId");
  if (payload.kind !== "initial_reconstruction") {
    throw new Error("invalid_kind");
  }

  return payload;
}

async function claimJobForCloudRunExecution(payload: DispatchPayload): Promise<
  | { action: "start" }
  | { action: "ignore"; reason: string }
> {
  const db = getFirestore();

  const jobRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${payload.workspaceId}/designs/${payload.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${payload.jobId}`
  );

  return db.runTransaction(async (tx) => {
    const snap = await tx.get(jobRef);

    if (!snap.exists) {
      return {
        action: "ignore",
        reason: "job_not_found",
      };
    }

    const job = snap.data()!;

    if (job.status === "completed") {
      return {
        action: "ignore",
        reason: "already_completed",
      };
    }

    if (job.status === "cancelled") {
      return {
        action: "ignore",
        reason: "already_cancelled",
      };
    }

    if (job.orchestration?.execution?.cloudRunExecutionName) {
      return {
        action: "ignore",
        reason: "execution_already_started",
      };
    }

    if (job.orchestration?.cancellation?.cancelRequested) {
      tx.update(jobRef, {
        status: "cancelled",
        "progress.percent": 100,
        "progress.label": "Cancelled",
        "orchestration.cancellation.cancelledAt":
          FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
        updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      });

      return {
        action: "ignore",
        reason: "cancel_requested",
      };
    }

    tx.update(jobRef, {
      "orchestration.dispatch.state": "dispatching",
      "orchestration.dispatch.dispatchAttemptCount":
        FieldValue.increment(1),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    return {
      action: "start",
    };
  });
}

async function startMagicLayersCloudRunJob(input: {
  jobId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;
}): Promise<{ executionName: string }> {
  const projectId = requiredEnv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT");
  const region = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_CLOUD_RUN_REGION");
  const jobName = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_WORKER_JOB_NAME");

  const auth = new GoogleAuth({
    scopes: ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"],
  });

  const client = await auth.getClient();

  const url = `https://run.googleapis.com/v2/projects/${projectId}/locations/${region}/jobs/${jobName}:run`;

  const response = await client.request<{
    name: string;
    metadata?: {
      name?: string;
    };
  }>({
    url,
    method: "POST",
    data: {
      overrides: {
        containerOverrides: [
          {
            env: [
              { name: "MAGIC_LAYERS_JOB_ID", value: input.jobId },
              { name: "MAGIC_LAYERS_WORKSPACE_ID", value: input.workspaceId },
              { name: "MAGIC_LAYERS_DESIGN_ID", value: input.designId },
              { name: "MAGIC_LAYERS_USER_ID", value: input.userId },
            ],
          },
        ],

        /**
         * One job input per execution.
         * Later, selected layer repair can use same mechanism.
         */
        taskCount: 1,

        /**
         * Set by expected job class.
         * This is orchestration only; actual model decisions come later.
         */
        timeout: "3600s",
      },
    },
  });

  return {
    executionName:
      response.data.metadata?.name ?? response.data.name,
  };
}

async function saveCloudRunExecutionName(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
  executionName: string;
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${input.workspaceId}/designs/${input.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${input.jobId}`
    )
    .update({
      "orchestration.dispatch.state": "execution_started",
      "orchestration.execution.cloudRunJobName": requiredEnv(
        "MAGIC_LAYERS_WORKER_JOB_NAME"
      ),
      "orchestration.execution.cloudRunExecutionName": input.executionName,
      "orchestration.execution.executionStartedAt":
        FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
}

function requiredEnv(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) throw new Error(`Missing env: ${name}`);
  return value;
}
```

---

# 5.10 Worker contract

The Cloud Run Job worker owns the real AI pipeline.

It must:

```txt
read jobId from env
load job doc
check cancellation
run steps in order
write assets to GCS
update Firestore status/progress
write reconstruction document
write Fabric manifest
mark completed
```

It must **not** depend on in-memory state surviving.

It must be safe to retry or resume.

Cloud Run Jobs can configure task timeout and retries; failed tasks can be retried, and if retries are exhausted the execution is marked failed. citeturn523257view0

---

## Worker main skeleton

```ts
// services/magic-layers-worker/src/main.ts

import { getFirestore, FieldValue } from "firebase-admin/firestore";

const STEP_SEQUENCE = [
  "normalizing",
  "observing",
  "decomposing",
  "recovering_text",
  "elementizing",
  "vectorizing",
  "repairing_background",
  "resolving_scene",
  "generating_fabric",
  "validating",
] as const;

type WorkerStep = (typeof STEP_SEQUENCE)[number];

async function main() {
  const jobId = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_JOB_ID");
  const workspaceId = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_WORKSPACE_ID");
  const designId = requiredEnv("MAGIC_LAYERS_DESIGN_ID");

  const context = {
    jobId,
    workspaceId,
    designId,
  };

  try {
    await markWorkerStarted(context);

    await runStep(context, "normalizing", async () => {
      // Step 6 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "observing", async () => {
      // Step 8 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "decomposing", async () => {
      // Step 9 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "recovering_text", async () => {
      // Step 10 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "elementizing", async () => {
      // Step 11 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "vectorizing", async () => {
      // Step 12 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "repairing_background", async () => {
      // Step 14 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "resolving_scene", async () => {
      // Step 17 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "generating_fabric", async () => {
      // Step 18 owns implementation.
    });

    await runStep(context, "validating", async () => {
      // Steps 19 and 20 own implementation.
    });

    await markCompleted(context);
  } catch (error) {
    await markFailed(context, error);
    throw error;
  }
}

async function runStep(
  context: {
    jobId: string;
    workspaceId: string;
    designId: string;
  },
  step: WorkerStep,
  fn: () => Promise<void>
) {
  await throwIfCancelled(context);

  await transitionToStep(context, step);

  /**
   * Later steps must make this idempotent:
   * if step outputs already exist and match schema, skip.
   */
  await fn();

  await markStepCompleted(context, step);

  await throwIfCancelled(context);
}

async function transitionToStep(
  context: {
    workspaceId: string;
    designId: string;
    jobId: string;
  },
  step: WorkerStep
) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${context.workspaceId}/designs/${context.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${context.jobId}`
    )
    .update({
      status: step,
      progress: progressForStep(step),
      "orchestration.execution.heartbeatAt": FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
}

function progressForStep(step: WorkerStep) {
  const order = STEP_SEQUENCE.indexOf(step);
  const percent = Math.round((order / STEP_SEQUENCE.length) * 100);

  return {
    percent,
    currentStep: step,
    label: labelForStep(step),
  };
}

function labelForStep(step: WorkerStep) {
  switch (step) {
    case "normalizing":
      return "Preparing image";
    case "observing":
      return "Analyzing design";
    case "decomposing":
      return "Separating layers";
    case "recovering_text":
      return "Recovering text";
    case "elementizing":
      return "Finding design objects";
    case "vectorizing":
      return "Rebuilding shapes";
    case "repairing_background":
      return "Reconstructing background";
    case "resolving_scene":
      return "Resolving layout";
    case "generating_fabric":
      return "Preparing editor";
    case "validating":
      return "Checking reconstruction";
  }
}

async function throwIfCancelled(context: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  const snap = await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${context.workspaceId}/designs/${context.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${context.jobId}`
    )
    .get();

  const job = snap.data();

  if (job?.orchestration?.cancellation?.cancelRequested) {
    await snap.ref.update({
      status: "cancelled",
      "progress.percent": 100,
      "progress.label": "Cancelled",
      "orchestration.cancellation.cancelledAt":
        FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    throw new Error("job_cancelled");
  }
}

async function markWorkerStarted(context: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${context.workspaceId}/designs/${context.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${context.jobId}`
    )
    .update({
      startedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      "orchestration.execution.workerAttemptCount":
        FieldValue.increment(1),
      "orchestration.execution.heartbeatAt": FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
}

async function markStepCompleted(
  context: {
    workspaceId: string;
    designId: string;
    jobId: string;
  },
  step: WorkerStep
) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${context.workspaceId}/designs/${context.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${context.jobId}`
    )
    .update({
      [`steps.${step}.status`]: "completed",
      [`steps.${step}.completedAt`]: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      "orchestration.execution.heartbeatAt": FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
}

async function markCompleted(context: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${context.workspaceId}/designs/${context.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${context.jobId}`
    )
    .update({
      status: "completed",
      "progress.percent": 100,
      "progress.label": "Ready",
      completedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      "orchestration.execution.executionCompletedAt":
        FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
}

async function markFailed(
  context: {
    workspaceId: string;
    designId: string;
    jobId: string;
  },
  error: unknown
) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${context.workspaceId}/designs/${context.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${context.jobId}`
    )
    .update({
      status: "failed",
      error: {
        code: "worker_failed",
        message:
          error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown worker error",
        retryable: true,
      },
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });
}

function requiredEnv(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) throw new Error(`Missing env: ${name}`);
  return value;
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

This skeleton intentionally does not implement normalization, observation, decomposition, OCR, vectorization, or validation. Those belong to later steps.

---

# 5.11 Retry policy

Retries must happen at safe boundaries only.

Use this policy:

```txt
Cloud Tasks retries dispatcher startup failures.
Cloud Run Job does not blindly repeat expensive AI calls.
Worker steps retry individual transient API calls.
Full job retry requires idempotent step resume.
```

Recommended initial Cloud Run Job setting:

```txt
--max-retries=0
```

Why:

```txt
full job retries can duplicate AI calls
duplicate AI calls increase cost
duplicate asset writes create confusing outputs
manual retry is safer until resume logic is mature
```

Once step-level idempotency is implemented:

```txt
--max-retries=1
```

Cloud Run Jobs support retry configuration, but the architecture must assume a worker can be restarted after partially writing outputs. citeturn523257view0

---

# 5.12 Idempotency rules

Every orchestration layer needs idempotency.

## API idempotency

Client sends:

```txt
idempotencyKey
```

Server stores:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/idempotencyKeys/{requestId}
```

Repeated requests return the same:

```txt
jobId
designId
```

---

## Cloud Tasks idempotency

Task ID is deterministic:

```txt
ml-{sha256(jobId).slice(0, 32)}
```

Cloud Tasks explicit task IDs enable deduplication, but hashed IDs are preferred over sequential IDs. citeturn625554view0

---

## Dispatcher idempotency

Dispatcher must not start two Cloud Run executions for the same job.

Claim condition:

```txt
if cloudRunExecutionName exists → return 2xx ignore
if completed/cancelled → return 2xx ignore
otherwise start execution
```

---

## Worker idempotency

Each step must eventually support:

```txt
if expected output assets already exist and schema validates → skip step
otherwise run step
```

This is mandatory before enabling aggressive worker retries.

---

# 5.13 Cancellation

Cancellation has two layers.

## Soft cancellation

Worker checks this field before and after every expensive step:

```ts
orchestration.cancellation.cancelRequested === true
```

Then it marks:

```txt
status = cancelled
```

## Hard cancellation

If Cloud Run execution already exists:

```txt
POST /api/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/cancel
→ set cancelRequested
→ call Cloud Run execution cancel API
```

Cloud Run cancellation stops the current job execution and preserves execution data/logs. citeturn941293view1

---

# 5.14 Security and IAM

Use least-privilege service accounts.

```txt
next-api-sa
  - Firestore read/write for workspace/design/job metadata
  - Cloud Tasks Enqueuer
  - Storage read on client upload landing zone
  - Storage write to canonical source paths if API performs copy

cloud-tasks-invoker-sa
  - Cloud Run Invoker on magic-layers-dispatcher only

magic-layers-dispatcher-sa
  - Firestore read/write job docs
  - Cloud Run Developer or narrower permissions to execute the worker job
  - no Storage access required unless needed for validation

magic-layers-worker-sa
  - Firestore read/write job/design/assets
  - Storage read/write source/assets buckets
  - Google AI / Vertex AI permissions
  - Secret Manager access if model keys are stored there
```

Cloud Run services should require IAM authentication for private internal endpoints, not public access. citeturn523257view3

---

# 5.15 Deployment shape

## Dispatcher service

```bash
gcloud run deploy magic-layers-dispatcher \
  --image="$DISPATCHER_IMAGE" \
  --region="$REGION" \
  --service-account="magic-layers-dispatcher-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --no-allow-unauthenticated
```

Allow Cloud Tasks to invoke it:

```bash
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding magic-layers-dispatcher \
  --region="$REGION" \
  --member="serviceAccount:cloud-tasks-invoker-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/run.invoker"
```

---

## Worker job

```bash
gcloud run jobs create magic-layers-worker \
  --image="$WORKER_IMAGE" \
  --region="$REGION" \
  --service-account="magic-layers-worker-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --memory="8Gi" \
  --cpu="4" \
  --task-timeout="3600s" \
  --max-retries="0"
```

Cloud Run Jobs default to 10 minutes but can be configured up to 168 hours for non-GPU jobs; GPU task timeout is limited to 1 hour. citeturn523257view0

---

# 5.16 Progress update policy

Do not write progress every second.

Write Firestore progress only on:

```txt
job created
task enqueued
worker started
step started
step completed
warning created
job completed
job failed
job cancelled
```

For long-running steps:

```txt
heartbeat every 60 seconds
```

Do not stream logs into Firestore. Put detailed logs in Cloud Logging and diagnostics in GCS.

---

# 5.17 Failure handling

Classify failures into three categories.

```ts
type MagicLayersFailureClass =
  | "permanent_input_failure"
  | "retryable_infrastructure_failure"
  | "retryable_model_failure";
```

## Permanent input failure

Examples:

```txt
unsupported MIME
image decode failure
image too large
upload missing
workspace forbidden
```

Action:

```txt
mark failed
return 2xx from dispatcher if encountered there
do not retry
```

## Retryable infrastructure failure

Examples:

```txt
temporary GCS read failure
Firestore contention
Cloud Run Job start failure
network timeout
```

Action:

```txt
Cloud Tasks may retry dispatcher
worker may retry specific operation
```

## Retryable model failure

Examples:

```txt
Gemini temporary failure
OCR timeout
segmentation service unavailable
```

Action:

```txt
retry inside step with bounded attempts
if exhausted, mark failed or fallback_only later
```

Do not let Cloud Tasks repeatedly re-run an expensive model job because one model call failed.

---

# 5.18 Stuck job recovery

Because Firestore job creation and Cloud Tasks enqueue are not one atomic transaction, you need a recovery path.

Add a lightweight sweeper later in the same orchestration layer:

```txt
scheduled every 5 minutes
find jobs with orchestration.dispatch.state = pending
older than 2 minutes
status = uploaded
enqueue dispatch task again
```

Because task IDs are deterministic, re-enqueue is safe.

Also detect stale executions:

```txt
status not completed/failed/cancelled
heartbeatAt older than threshold
cloudRunExecutionName exists
```

Then either:

```txt
mark needs investigation
or enqueue explicit retry after checking Cloud Run execution state
```

Do not guess completion from missing heartbeat alone.

---

# 5.19 What goes into the Cloud Task body

Allowed:

```txt
jobId
workspaceId
designId
userId
kind
requestId
createdAt
```

Not allowed:

```txt
image bytes
signed URLs
Fabric JSON
reconstruction document
raw Gemini response
OCR response
mask data
large config
```

The worker reads all durable state from Firestore and GCS.

# 5.21 Non-negotiable invariants

```txt
Next.js API returns immediately after enqueue.

No AI decomposition runs inside Next.js.

Cloud Tasks dispatches, but does not own full job execution.

Cloud Tasks payload contains only IDs.

Cloud Run dispatcher starts the Cloud Run Job and returns 2xx quickly.

Cloud Run Job owns heavy processing.

Every job has an idempotency key.

Every Cloud Task has a deterministic hashed task ID.

Dispatcher never starts duplicate Cloud Run executions.

Worker can survive restart or retry.

Worker writes progress only at step boundaries or heartbeat intervals.

All job status transitions are server-controlled.

All public API calls verify Firebase Auth.

All public API calls verify App Check.

Internal dispatcher is private and IAM-protected.

Cancellation is both soft flag and hard Cloud Run execution cancel.

No signed URLs are stored as durable job state.

No generated bytes are stored in Firestore.
```

## ChatGPT Response 016

<!-- assistant_message_ids: e8d70b71-3e1f-4e10-8b6d-3d415b541e44, 27596393-871e-4d4b-af3b-2a81a0606b6a, 12916ac0-e0e8-4ced-8de7-302e66a491dd -->

I’ll keep Step 6 strictly to upload verification and deterministic normalization. The worker must turn the landing-zone upload into canonical original, normalized analysis, and editor reference assets.

The key invariant is that the normalized image becomes the fixed coordinate and pixel contract for every later AI observation, mask, crop, and Fabric placement.

# Step 6 — Upload and normalization

Step 6 converts an **untrusted client upload** into the stable image basis for the whole Magic Layers pipeline.

Locked rule:

```txt
Client upload is not the source of truth.

Canonical original + normalized image + working-scale images
are the source inputs for all later AI steps.
```

Nothing in this step does OCR, segmentation, routing, vectorization, background repair, or Fabric generation.

---

## 6.1 What Step 6 must produce

Input:

```txt
client-uploads/{uid}/{uploadId}/original.{ext}
```

Output:

```txt
canonical original image
normalized PNG
editor reference image
working-scale images
normalization report JSON
Firestore job/design updates
asset index docs
```

The core result is:

```txt
canvas_px = normalized_px
```

All later geometry is measured against the normalized canvas.

---

## 6.2 Why this step matters

Magic Layers fails early if image normalization is inconsistent.

Common failure cases:

```txt
JPEG orientation ignored
CMYK/P3 image rendered differently in browser
client MIME lies
huge JPEG causes memory blowup
animated WebP sneaks in
AI sees one size but Fabric uses another
OCR uses a rotated crop
masks generated on one scale are applied to another
```

Firebase Storage lets clients upload files with metadata like `contentType`, but that metadata is user-controlled and must not be trusted as final validation. Firebase’s docs show upload metadata support, while OWASP explicitly warns not to trust the `Content-Type` header and recommends extension allowlists, generated filenames, file-size limits, and server-side file-type validation. citeturn255183view0turn797898search0

---

# 6.3 Final normalization policy

Use this from day one:

```ts
export const MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY = {
  maxUploadBytes: 30 * 1024 * 1024,

  /**
   * This is intentionally far below Sharp's default safety limit.
   * 50MP RGBA decode is already expensive enough.
   */
  maxDecodePixels: 50_000_000,

  minDimensionPx: 64,

  /**
   * Fabric canvas and canonical AI coordinate space.
   */
  maxCanvasLongEdge: 4096,

  /**
   * Gemini/Firebase AI Logic larger images are scaled/padded to max 3072×3072,
   * so keep a Gemini-oriented working scale at 3072 long edge.
   */
  workingScales: {
    route: 768,
    layout: 1536,
    ai: 3072,
  },

  supportedMimeTypes: [
    "image/png",
    "image/jpeg",
    "image/webp",
  ] as const,

  output: {
    normalizedMimeType: "image/png",
    pngCompressionLevel: 9,
    adaptiveFiltering: true,
  },
} as const;
```

Firebase AI Logic’s Gemini image input docs list PNG, JPEG, and WebP as supported image MIME types. The same docs say larger images are scaled and padded to fit a maximum 3072×3072 resolution while preserving aspect ratio, which is why this step creates a 3072 long-edge AI working image separately from the 4096 long-edge normalized canvas. citeturn778328view0

---

# 6.4 Hard product decisions

## Decision 1 — preserve original bytes, but do not process from landing zone

The landing-zone upload is temporary and untrusted.

The worker must copy verified original bytes into canonical storage:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/source/original/{assetId}/original.{ext}
```

Only after:

```txt
path ownership verified
size verified
magic bytes verified
image decoded successfully
dimensions accepted
animation/multipage rejected
```

---

## Decision 2 — normalized PNG becomes the canonical canvas

The normalized PNG defines:

```txt
canvas.width
canvas.height
canvas_px coordinate system
locked reference dimensions
AI geometry basis
```

This means later objects, masks, OCR boxes, and Fabric positions use:

```txt
normalized_px === canvas_px
```

Do **not** use original raw dimensions as Fabric canvas dimensions when the image is very large.

---

## Decision 3 — no visual enhancement here

Do **not** do this in Step 6:

```txt
denoise
sharpen
super-resolution
contrast enhancement
background cleanup
OCR cleanup
AI repair
upscale
```

Step 6 must be deterministic and conservative.

Allowed transformations only:

```txt
decode
auto-orient
convert to sRGB
strip metadata
resize down if too large
encode PNG
create working scales
```

Sharp supports EXIF-based auto orientation and input pixel limits. Its docs also state that metadata dimensions do not take later operations like rotate/resize into account, so you must read final dimensions from the normalized output, not only from input metadata. citeturn987127view0turn399474view1

---

## Decision 4 — strip metadata from normalized/editor assets

The raw original keeps original bytes.

Normalized/editor/working images should strip EXIF/XMP/IPTC/ICC metadata by default and store only controlled metadata in Firestore/GCS asset records.

Sharp’s default behavior, when metadata preservation is not requested, is to convert output to device-independent sRGB and strip metadata, including ICC profile removal. That is the behavior we want for normalized assets. citeturn399474view0

---

# 6.5 Output assets

Step 6 creates these assets.

```txt
original_image
  unchanged verified original bytes
  source bucket
  no-store

normalized_image
  auto-oriented sRGB PNG
  source bucket
  no-store

editor_reference_image
  same pixels as normalized image
  assets bucket
  CORS-loadable for Fabric
  immutable cache

working_scale_image: route
  max long edge 768
  source bucket

working_scale_image: layout
  max long edge 1536
  source bucket

working_scale_image: ai
  max long edge 3072
  source bucket

diagnostic / normalization_report
  JSON with metadata, hashes, dimensions, transform info
  source bucket
```

The editor reference image is intentionally duplicated into the assets bucket because Fabric needs browser-loadable, CORS-safe HTTPS URLs later.

Cloud Storage object metadata controls response headers like `Cache-Control` and `Content-Type`, so these assets must be uploaded with explicit metadata instead of relying on defaults. citeturn255183view3

---

# 6.6 Normalization algorithm

The worker does this:

```txt
1. Load job doc.
2. Re-verify upload path.
3. Read landing-zone object metadata.
4. Enforce max upload bytes.
5. Download bytes.
6. Detect file type by magic bytes.
7. Decode with Sharp.
8. Verify decoded MIME matches allowed type.
9. Reject animated/multipage images.
10. Reject invalid dimensions.
11. Compute sha256.
12. Copy verified original to canonical source path.
13. Auto-orient.
14. Convert to sRGB.
15. Downscale to maxCanvasLongEdge if needed.
16. Encode normalized PNG.
17. Read final normalized dimensions.
18. Compute perceptual hash.
19. Save normalized image.
20. Save editor reference image.
21. Save working-scale images.
22. Save normalization report.
23. Create Firestore asset index docs.
24. Patch job input fields.
25. Patch design canvas fields.
```

Use magic-byte detection as a first pass only. The `file-type` package detects binary file types from magic numbers, but its own docs state that this is a best-effort hint and does not guarantee the file is valid or safe. Decode validation is still mandatory. citeturn197051search0

# 6.9 Hash helper

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/normalization/image-hash.ts
```

```ts
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import sharp from "sharp";

export function sha256Hex(buffer: Buffer): string {
  return crypto.createHash("sha256").update(buffer).digest("hex");
}

/**
 * Simple 64-bit difference hash.
 * Good enough for upload dedupe and near-duplicate clustering.
 * Not a security hash.
 */
export async function computeDHash(buffer: Buffer): Promise<string> {
  const raw = await sharp(buffer, {
    failOn: "warning",
    limitInputPixels: 4096 * 4096,
  })
    .resize(9, 8, {
      fit: "fill",
    })
    .greyscale()
    .raw()
    .toBuffer();

  let bits = "";

  for (let y = 0; y < 8; y++) {
    for (let x = 0; x < 8; x++) {
      const left = raw[y * 9 + x];
      const right = raw[y * 9 + x + 1];
      bits += left > right ? "1" : "0";
    }
  }

  return bits
    .match(/.{1,4}/g)!
    .map((chunk) => parseInt(chunk, 2).toString(16))
    .join("")
    .padStart(16, "0");
}
```

# 6.10 Normalization implementation

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/normalization/normalize-magic-layers-upload.ts
```

```ts
import { getStorage } from "firebase-admin/storage";
import { fileTypeFromBuffer } from "file-type";
import sharp from "sharp";

import {
  AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "../schema/constants";

import type {
  AiAssetRef,
  AiSource,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import { bucketForMagicStorageRole } from "../storage/storage-buckets";

import {
  canonicalOriginalPath,
  cleanBackgroundPath,
  editorReferenceImagePath,
  normalizedImagePath,
  normalizationReportPath,
  workingScaleImagePath,
} from "../storage/storage-paths";

import { writeAiAsset } from "../storage/write-ai-asset";

import { MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY } from "./normalization-policy";
import {
  computeDHash,
  sha256Hex,
} from "./image-hash";

import type {
  MagicLayersNormalizationResult,
  MagicLayersRawImageMetadata,
  MagicLayersSupportedImageMime,
  MagicLayersWorkingScaleKind,
} from "./normalization.types";

export type NormalizeMagicLayersUploadInput = {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
  userId: string;

  uploadId: string;
  uploadPath: string;
};

export async function normalizeMagicLayersUpload(
  input: NormalizeMagicLayersUploadInput
): Promise<MagicLayersNormalizationResult> {
  assertValidLandingZonePath(input);

  const sourceBucket = bucketForMagicStorageRole("source");
  const assetsBucket = bucketForMagicStorageRole("assets");

  const uploadFile = getStorage()
    .bucket(sourceBucket)
    .file(input.uploadPath);

  const [exists] = await uploadFile.exists();

  if (!exists) {
    throw normalizationError("upload_missing", "Upload object does not exist");
  }

  const [uploadMetadata] = await uploadFile.getMetadata();

  const uploadSizeBytes = Number(uploadMetadata.size ?? 0);

  if (
    !Number.isFinite(uploadSizeBytes) ||
    uploadSizeBytes <= 0
  ) {
    throw normalizationError("upload_empty", "Upload object is empty");
  }

  if (
    uploadSizeBytes >
    MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxUploadBytes
  ) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "upload_too_large",
      `Upload exceeds ${MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxUploadBytes} bytes`
    );
  }

  const [inputBuffer] = await uploadFile.download();

  const detected = await fileTypeFromBuffer(inputBuffer);

  if (!detected) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "file_type_unknown",
      "Could not detect file type from magic bytes"
    );
  }

  if (!isSupportedMime(detected.mime)) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "unsupported_mime",
      `Unsupported MIME type: ${detected.mime}`
    );
  }

  const sha256 = sha256Hex(inputBuffer);

  const inputImage = sharp(inputBuffer, {
    failOn: "warning",
    limitInputPixels:
      MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxDecodePixels,
    animated: false,
  });

  const metadata = await inputImage.metadata();

  if (!metadata.width || !metadata.height) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "invalid_dimensions",
      "Image metadata missing width or height"
    );
  }

  if (
    metadata.width < MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.minDimensionPx ||
    metadata.height < MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.minDimensionPx
  ) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "image_too_small",
      "Image is below minimum supported dimensions"
    );
  }

  const pixels = metadata.width * metadata.height;

  if (
    pixels >
    MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxDecodePixels
  ) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "image_too_large",
      "Image exceeds maximum decode pixel count"
    );
  }

  const pages = metadata.pages ?? 1;

  if (pages > 1) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "animated_or_multipage_unsupported",
      "Animated or multipage images are not supported for Magic Layers"
    );
  }

  const sharpMime = metadata.mediaType ?? mimeFromSharpFormat(metadata.format);

  if (sharpMime && sharpMime !== detected.mime) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "mime_mismatch",
      `Magic-byte MIME ${detected.mime} does not match decoded MIME ${sharpMime}`
    );
  }

  const rawMeta: MagicLayersRawImageMetadata = {
    detectedMimeType: detected.mime as MagicLayersSupportedImageMime,
    sharpFormat: metadata.format,
    sharpMediaType: metadata.mediaType,
    width: metadata.width,
    height: metadata.height,
    orientation: metadata.orientation,
    pages,
    hasAlpha: metadata.hasAlpha,
    hasProfile: metadata.hasProfile,
    colourSpace: metadata.space,
    channels: metadata.channels,
    sizeBytes: uploadSizeBytes,
  };

  const oriented = orientedDimensions({
    width: metadata.width,
    height: metadata.height,
    orientation: metadata.orientation,
  });

  const canvasSize = fitInsideMaxLongEdge(
    oriented.width,
    oriented.height,
    MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxCanvasLongEdge
  );

  const originalAssetId = stableAssetId(input.jobId, "original");
  const normalizedAssetId = stableAssetId(input.jobId, "normalized");
  const editorReferenceAssetId = stableAssetId(
    input.jobId,
    "editor-reference"
  );

  const originalExtension = extensionForMime(
    detected.mime as MagicLayersSupportedImageMime
  );

  const originalAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "source",
    bucket: sourceBucket,
    storagePath: canonicalOriginalPath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      assetId: originalAssetId,
      extension: originalExtension,
    }),

    bytes: inputBuffer,

    assetId: originalAssetId,
    kind: "original_image",

    contentType: detected.mime,

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,

    width: metadata.width,
    height: metadata.height,

    source: "original_upload",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    cacheControl: "private, no-store",
  });

  const normalizedPipeline = sharp(inputBuffer, {
    failOn: "warning",
    limitInputPixels:
      MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxDecodePixels,
    autoOrient: true,
    animated: false,
  })
    .toColourspace("srgb")
    .resize({
      width: canvasSize.width,
      height: canvasSize.height,
      fit: "inside",
      withoutEnlargement: true,
    })
    .png({
      compressionLevel:
        MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.output
          .pngCompressionLevel,
      adaptiveFiltering:
        MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.output
          .adaptiveFiltering,
    });

  const {
    data: normalizedBuffer,
    info: normalizedInfo,
  } = await normalizedPipeline.toBuffer({
    resolveWithObject: true,
  });

  const perceptualDHash = await computeDHash(normalizedBuffer);

  const normalizedAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "source",
    bucket: sourceBucket,
    storagePath: normalizedImagePath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      assetId: normalizedAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: normalizedBuffer,

    assetId: normalizedAssetId,
    kind: "normalized_image",

    contentType: "image/png",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,

    width: normalizedInfo.width,
    height: normalizedInfo.height,

    source: "normalizer",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    sourceAssetId: originalAsset.id,

    cacheControl: "private, no-store",
  });

  const editorReferenceAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "assets",
    bucket: assetsBucket,
    storagePath: editorReferenceImagePath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      jobId: input.jobId,
      assetId: editorReferenceAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: normalizedBuffer,

    assetId: editorReferenceAssetId,
    kind: "editor_reference_image",

    contentType: "image/png",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,

    width: normalizedInfo.width,
    height: normalizedInfo.height,

    source: "normalizer",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    sourceAssetId: normalizedAsset.id,

    cacheControl: "private, max-age=31536000, immutable",
  });

  const workingScales = await createWorkingScales({
    input,
    sourceBucket,
    normalizedBuffer,
    normalizedWidth: normalizedInfo.width,
    normalizedHeight: normalizedInfo.height,
    normalizedAsset,
  });

  const resultWithoutReport = {
    jobId: input.jobId,
    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    userId: input.userId,

    original: {
      asset: originalAsset,
      metadata: rawMeta,
    },

    normalized: {
      asset: normalizedAsset,
      width: normalizedInfo.width,
      height: normalizedInfo.height,
      mimeType: "image/png" as const,
    },

    editorReference: {
      asset: editorReferenceAsset,
    },

    workingScales,

    hashes: {
      sha256,
      perceptualDHash,
    },

    transform: {
      rawWidth: metadata.width,
      rawHeight: metadata.height,

      orientedOriginalWidth: oriented.width,
      orientedOriginalHeight: oriented.height,

      canvasWidth: normalizedInfo.width,
      canvasHeight: normalizedInfo.height,

      scaleFromOrientedOriginalX:
        normalizedInfo.width / oriented.width,
      scaleFromOrientedOriginalY:
        normalizedInfo.height / oriented.height,

      orientationApplied: Boolean(metadata.orientation),
    },

    warnings: buildNormalizationWarnings({
      rawMeta,
      normalizedWidth: normalizedInfo.width,
      normalizedHeight: normalizedInfo.height,
      orientedWidth: oriented.width,
      orientedHeight: oriented.height,
    }),

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };

  const reportAssetId = stableAssetId(input.jobId, "normalization-report");

  const reportBuffer = Buffer.from(
    JSON.stringify(resultWithoutReport, null, 2),
    "utf8"
  );

  const reportAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "source",
    bucket: sourceBucket,
    storagePath: normalizationReportPath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      jobId: input.jobId,
      assetId: reportAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: reportBuffer,

    assetId: reportAssetId,
    kind: "diagnostic",

    contentType: "application/json",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,

    source: "normalizer",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    sourceAssetId: normalizedAsset.id,

    cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
  });

  return {
    ...resultWithoutReport,
    reportAsset,
  };
}

async function createWorkingScales(input: {
  input: NormalizeMagicLayersUploadInput;
  sourceBucket: string;
  normalizedBuffer: Buffer;
  normalizedWidth: number;
  normalizedHeight: number;
  normalizedAsset: AiAssetRef;
}) {
  const output = {} as Record<
    MagicLayersWorkingScaleKind,
    {
      asset: AiAssetRef;
      width: number;
      height: number;
      maxLongEdge: number;
    }
  >;

  const entries = Object.entries(
    MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.workingScales
  ) as [MagicLayersWorkingScaleKind, number][];

  for (const [scaleKind, maxLongEdge] of entries) {
    const size = fitInsideMaxLongEdge(
      input.normalizedWidth,
      input.normalizedHeight,
      maxLongEdge
    );

    /**
     * Reuse normalized asset when already small enough.
     */
    if (
      input.normalizedWidth <= maxLongEdge &&
      input.normalizedHeight <= maxLongEdge
    ) {
      output[scaleKind] = {
        asset: input.normalizedAsset,
        width: input.normalizedWidth,
        height: input.normalizedHeight,
        maxLongEdge,
      };

      continue;
    }

    const assetId = stableAssetId(
      input.input.jobId,
      `working-${scaleKind}`
    );

    const {
      data,
      info,
    } = await sharp(input.normalizedBuffer, {
      failOn: "warning",
      limitInputPixels:
        MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.maxDecodePixels,
    })
      .resize({
        width: size.width,
        height: size.height,
        fit: "inside",
        withoutEnlargement: true,
      })
      .png({
        compressionLevel:
          MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.output
            .pngCompressionLevel,
        adaptiveFiltering:
          MAGIC_LAYERS_NORMALIZATION_POLICY.output
            .adaptiveFiltering,
      })
      .toBuffer({
        resolveWithObject: true,
      });

    const asset = await writeAiAsset({
      storageRole: "source",
      bucket: input.sourceBucket,
      storagePath: workingScaleImagePath({
        workspaceId: input.input.workspaceId,
        designId: input.input.designId,
        jobId: input.input.jobId,
        scaleKind,
        assetId,
      }),

      bytes: data,

      assetId,
      kind: "working_scale_image",

      contentType: "image/png",

      workspaceId: input.input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.input.designId,
      jobId: input.input.jobId,

      width: info.width,
      height: info.height,

      source: "normalizer",

      schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
      pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

      sourceAssetId: input.normalizedAsset.id,

      cacheControl: "private, max-age=86400",
    });

    output[scaleKind] = {
      asset,
      width: info.width,
      height: info.height,
      maxLongEdge,
    };
  }

  return output;
}

function assertValidLandingZonePath(
  input: NormalizeMagicLayersUploadInput
) {
  const expectedPrefix =
    `client-uploads/${input.userId}/${input.uploadId}/`;

  if (!input.uploadPath.startsWith(expectedPrefix)) {
    throw normalizationError(
      "invalid_upload_path",
      "Upload path does not belong to authenticated user/uploadId"
    );
  }
}

function isSupportedMime(
  mime: string
): mime is MagicLayersSupportedImageMime {
  return (
    mime === "image/png" ||
    mime === "image/jpeg" ||
    mime === "image/webp"
  );
}

function mimeFromSharpFormat(format?: string): string | undefined {
  switch (format) {
    case "jpeg":
    case "jpg":
      return "image/jpeg";

    case "png":
      return "image/png";

    case "webp":
      return "image/webp";

    default:
      return undefined;
  }
}

function extensionForMime(
  mime: MagicLayersSupportedImageMime
): "png" | "jpg" | "webp" {
  switch (mime) {
    case "image/png":
      return "png";

    case "image/jpeg":
      return "jpg";

    case "image/webp":
      return "webp";
  }
}

function orientedDimensions(input: {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  orientation?: number;
}) {
  /**
   * EXIF orientations 5, 6, 7, 8 swap width/height.
   */
  if (
    input.orientation === 5 ||
    input.orientation === 6 ||
    input.orientation === 7 ||
    input.orientation === 8
  ) {
    return {
      width: input.height,
      height: input.width,
    };
  }

  return {
    width: input.width,
    height: input.height,
  };
}

function fitInsideMaxLongEdge(
  width: number,
  height: number,
  maxLongEdge: number
) {
  const longEdge = Math.max(width, height);

  if (longEdge <= maxLongEdge) {
    return {
      width,
      height,
    };
  }

  const scale = maxLongEdge / longEdge;

  return {
    width: Math.max(1, Math.round(width * scale)),
    height: Math.max(1, Math.round(height * scale)),
  };
}

function stableAssetId(jobId: string, label: string) {
  return `asset_${jobId}_${label}`
    .replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "_")
    .toLowerCase();
}

function buildNormalizationWarnings(input: {
  rawMeta: MagicLayersRawImageMetadata;
  orientedWidth: number;
  orientedHeight: number;
  normalizedWidth: number;
  normalizedHeight: number;
}) {
  const warnings: string[] = [];

  if (input.rawMeta.orientation && input.rawMeta.orientation !== 1) {
    warnings.push("exif_orientation_applied");
  }

  if (
    input.normalizedWidth < input.orientedWidth ||
    input.normalizedHeight < input.orientedHeight
  ) {
    warnings.push("image_downscaled_for_canvas");
  }

  if (input.rawMeta.hasProfile) {
    warnings.push("icc_profile_converted_to_srgb_and_stripped");
  }

  if (input.rawMeta.hasAlpha) {
    warnings.push("input_alpha_preserved");
  }

  return warnings;
}

function normalizationError(code: string, message: string) {
  const error = new Error(message) as Error & { code: string };
  error.code = code;
  return error;
}
```

Remove the unused `cleanBackgroundPath` import if your TypeScript linter enforces no unused imports.

# 6.11 Firestore patch after normalization

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/normalization/apply-normalization-result.ts
```

```ts
import {
  FieldValue,
  getFirestore,
} from "firebase-admin/firestore";

import type {
  MagicLayersNormalizationResult,
} from "./normalization.types";

export async function applyNormalizationResult(
  result: MagicLayersNormalizationResult
) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  const designRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${result.workspaceId}/designs/${result.designId}`
  );

  const jobRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${result.workspaceId}/designs/${result.designId}/aiLayerJobs/${result.jobId}`
  );

  const assetRefs = [
    result.original.asset,
    result.normalized.asset,
    result.editorReference.asset,
    result.workingScales.route.asset,
    result.workingScales.layout.asset,
    result.workingScales.ai.asset,
    result.reportAsset,
  ];

  const batch = db.batch();

  for (const asset of dedupeAssets(assetRefs)) {
    const assetRef = db.doc(
      `workspaces/${result.workspaceId}/designs/${result.designId}/assets/${asset.id}`
    );

    batch.set(
      assetRef,
      {
        id: asset.id,

        workspaceId: result.workspaceId,
        designId: result.designId,
        jobId: result.jobId,

        kind: asset.kind,

        storageRole: asset.storageRole,

        bucket: asset.bucket,
        storagePath: asset.storagePath,

        generation: asset.generation,
        metageneration: asset.metageneration,

        mimeType: asset.mimeType,

        width: asset.width,
        height: asset.height,
        sizeBytes: asset.sizeBytes,

        checksum: asset.checksum,

        source: asset.metadata.source,

        retained: true,

        createdAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      },
      { merge: true }
    );
  }

  batch.update(jobRef, {
    "input.originalAssetId": result.original.asset.id,
    "input.normalizedAssetId": result.normalized.asset.id,
    "input.editorReferenceAssetId": result.editorReference.asset.id,

    "input.mimeType": result.original.metadata.detectedMimeType,
    "input.width": result.normalized.width,
    "input.height": result.normalized.height,

    "input.sha256": result.hashes.sha256,
    "input.perceptualHash": result.hashes.perceptualDHash,

    "input.normalizationReportAssetId": result.reportAsset.id,

    "input.workingScaleAssetIds.route":
      result.workingScales.route.asset.id,
    "input.workingScaleAssetIds.layout":
      result.workingScales.layout.asset.id,
    "input.workingScaleAssetIds.ai":
      result.workingScales.ai.asset.id,

    "input.transform": result.transform,

    "progress.percent": 10,
    "progress.label": "Image prepared",
    "progress.currentStep": "normalizing",

    updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
  });

  batch.update(designRef, {
    "source.originalAssetId": result.original.asset.id,
    "source.currentNormalizedAssetId": result.normalized.asset.id,

    "canvas.width": result.normalized.width,
    "canvas.height": result.normalized.height,
    "canvas.unit": "px",

    updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
  });

  await batch.commit();
}

function dedupeAssets<T extends { id: string }>(assets: T[]): T[] {
  const map = new Map<string, T>();

  for (const asset of assets) {
    map.set(asset.id, asset);
  }

  return [...map.values()];
}
```

# 6.15 Non-negotiable invariants

Step 6 is valid only if:

```txt
Client upload path is re-verified server-side.

Client MIME is not trusted.

Magic-byte MIME is checked.

Image decode succeeds.

Decoded MIME is allowed.

Animated/multipage images are rejected.

Original verified bytes are copied to canonical source storage.

Normalized image is auto-oriented.

Normalized image is converted to sRGB.

Normalized/editor assets do not preserve EXIF/XMP/IPTC metadata.

Normalized canvas dimensions are recorded.

canvas_px equals normalized_px.

Original-to-canvas scale is recorded.

Editor reference image exists in assets bucket.

Working-scale images exist or intentionally alias normalized asset.

SHA-256 is computed from original bytes.

Perceptual hash is computed from normalized pixels.

Firestore job input fields are patched.

Firestore design canvas fields are patched.

Asset index docs exist.

No base64 is written to Firestore.

No AI model call happens in this step.

No visual enhancement happens in this step.
```

## ChatGPT Response 017

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 2c9fa9f0-ca21-43ef-9938-ee05f4fb4ff0, e23fbcf5-40c9-4cb4-bb0e-806f90e6c74f -->

Step 7 is the internal routing diagnosis: it chooses the safest engine priorities and budgets before expensive extraction, without creating layers, OCR, masks, or Fabric objects.

# Step 7 — Routing and design diagnosis

Step 7 decides **how the image should be reconstructed** before expensive decomposition begins.

The locked rule:

```txt
Do not run one universal reconstruction pipeline for every image.
Diagnose the image first.
Route it to the safest reconstruction strategy.
```

This step still does **not** create final layers, OCR text objects, masks, vectors, background repair, or Fabric JSON.

It only produces:

```txt
routing diagnosis
route confidence
local image metrics
optional Gemini routing judgment
routing report asset
Firestore job/design patch
```

---

## 7.1 Why routing exists

A restaurant poster, a product photo, a menu screenshot, a logo, and an AI-generated banner should not enter the same layer pipeline.

Wrong:

```txt
normalized image
→ segmentation
→ masks
→ Fabric
```

Correct:

```txt
normalized image
→ routing diagnosis
→ choose reconstruction strategy
→ generate observations
→ resolve scene
```

LayerD is directly relevant for graphic designs because it decomposes raster graphic designs by repeatedly extracting foreground layers and completing backgrounds, and its project page explicitly relies on graphic-design priors like flat-color layers. That makes it useful for posters and AI banners, but not automatically ideal for photo-heavy images. citeturn269344search2turn269344search10

Gemini is useful here as a classifier and layout reasoner because its image-understanding docs support image classification and object-detection-style visual reasoning. Its bounding boxes use normalized `0–1000` coordinates when object detection is requested, but Step 7 should not ask for detailed layer boxes yet. citeturn541707search1

# 7.4 Route taxonomy

Use the existing Step 1 enum:

```ts
type MagicLayersRecommendedRoute =
  | "graphic_design_layer_decomposition"
  | "photo_conservative_segmentation"
  | "text_recovery_priority"
  | "vectorization_priority"
  | "fallback_only";
```

Meaning:

```txt
graphic_design_layer_decomposition
Poster, flyer, social banner, thumbnail, AI graphic, ad creative.
Use LayerD-style decomposition + OCR + vectorization + background repair.

photo_conservative_segmentation
Mostly photographic image with some foreground objects.
Use conservative object masks. Avoid aggressive layer splitting.

text_recovery_priority
Menu, document-like design, price list, dense text creative.
Prioritize OCR/text recovery. Use raster fallback heavily.

vectorization_priority
Logo, icon, flat illustration, simple graphic, badge.
Prioritize shape detection/vectorization. Avoid unnecessary inpainting.

fallback_only
No safe editable reconstruction route.
Create locked reference + maybe clean background/fallback only.
```

Do **not** expose this route name to the user. This is internal pipeline routing.

# 7.5 Canvas type taxonomy

Keep this from Step 1:

```ts
type MagicLayersCanvasType =
  | "graphic_design"
  | "photo_heavy_composite"
  | "text_heavy_design"
  | "menu_or_document"
  | "logo_or_icon"
  | "flat_illustration"
  | "ai_generated_banner"
  | "mixed"
  | "unknown";
```

Important distinction:

```txt
canvasType = what this image appears to be
recommendedRoute = how the system should process it
```

Example:

```json
{
  "canvasType": "mixed",
  "recommendedRoute": "graphic_design_layer_decomposition"
}
```

A mixed poster with product photo + text + badges should still route to graphic-design reconstruction.

# 7.6 Local metrics

Step 7 should compute local image metrics before calling any model.

Model-only routing is too unstable. The model should confirm or refine the deterministic diagnosis, not replace it.

```ts
export type MagicLayersRoutingLocalMetrics = {
  width: number;
  height: number;

  aspectRatio: number;

  megapixels: number;

  hasAlpha: boolean;

  entropy: number;

  sharpness?: number;

  dominantColor?: string;

  estimatedPaletteSize: number;

  topPaletteCoverage: number;

  flatColorRatio: number;

  edgeDensity: number;

  smallComponentDensity: number;

  largeComponentDensity: number;

  textLikeComponentDensity: number;

  photoTextureRatio: number;

  backgroundUniformity: number;

  transparencyRatio?: number;

  documentLikeScore: number;

  logoIconScore: number;

  graphicDesignScore: number;

  photoHeavyScore: number;
};
```

Sharp exposes pixel-derived image statistics including entropy, sharpness, and dominant sRGB color, which makes it useful for quick local diagnosis before model calls. citeturn541707search7

---

# 7.7 Metric interpretation

Use these heuristics.

```txt
High flatColorRatio
  likely poster / vector graphic / logo / UI / menu

High photoTextureRatio
  likely natural photo or photo-heavy design

High textLikeComponentDensity
  likely poster/menu/document/text-heavy creative

High topPaletteCoverage
  likely flat design, logo, icon, simple illustration

High edgeDensity + low palette size
  likely typography / vector art / icon

Low edgeDensity + high texture entropy
  likely photo

Square-ish + low palette + centered content
  likely logo/icon

Tall or document-like + many text components
  likely menu/document
```

These are not final classifications. They are routing evidence.

## `compute-routing-local-metrics.ts`

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/routing/compute-routing-local-metrics.ts

import sharp from "sharp";
import { MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY } from "./routing-policy";
import type {
  MagicLayersRoutingLocalMetrics,
} from "./routing.types";

type RgbaPixel = {
  r: number;
  g: number;
  b: number;
  a: number;
};

export async function computeRoutingLocalMetrics(
  imageBuffer: Buffer
): Promise<MagicLayersRoutingLocalMetrics> {
  const prepared = sharp(imageBuffer, {
    failOn: "warning",
    limitInputPixels: 4096 * 4096,
  })
    .ensureAlpha()
    .resize({
      width: MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.routeImageMaxLongEdge,
      height: MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.routeImageMaxLongEdge,
      fit: "inside",
      withoutEnlargement: true,
    });

  const stats = await prepared.clone().stats();

  const {
    data,
    info,
  } = await prepared
    .clone()
    .raw()
    .toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

  const width = info.width;
  const height = info.height;
  const pixelCount = width * height;

  const pixels = readRgbaPixels(data);

  const alphaStats = computeAlphaStats(pixels);

  const palette = computeQuantizedPalette(
    pixels,
    MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics
      .paletteQuantizationBitsPerChannel
  );

  const edgeDensity = computeEdgeDensity(pixels, width, height);

  const components = computeApproxConnectedComponents({
    pixels,
    width,
    height,
    edgeDensity,
  });

  const topPaletteCoverage = palette.topCoverage;
  const estimatedPaletteSize = palette.estimatedPaletteSize;

  const flatColorRatio = clamp01(
    topPaletteCoverage * 0.7 +
      (estimatedPaletteSize < 24 ? 0.2 : 0) +
      (stats.entropy < 4.8 ? 0.1 : 0)
  );

  const photoTextureRatio = clamp01(
    normalizeRange(stats.entropy, 4.2, 7.6) * 0.55 +
      normalizeRange(edgeDensity, 0.08, 0.34) * 0.25 +
      (estimatedPaletteSize > 72 ? 0.2 : 0)
  );

  const backgroundUniformity = estimateBackgroundUniformity({
    pixels,
    width,
    height,
  });

  const aspectRatio = width / height;

  const documentLikeScore = clamp01(
    components.textLikeComponentDensity * 2.2 +
      (aspectRatio < 0.82 ? 0.15 : 0) +
      (flatColorRatio > 0.5 ? 0.15 : 0) -
      photoTextureRatio * 0.35
  );

  const logoIconScore = clamp01(
    (aspectRatio > 0.75 && aspectRatio < 1.35 ? 0.22 : 0) +
      topPaletteCoverage * 0.38 +
      flatColorRatio * 0.28 +
      backgroundUniformity * 0.12 -
      photoTextureRatio * 0.35
  );

  const graphicDesignScore = clamp01(
    flatColorRatio * 0.42 +
      components.textLikeComponentDensity * 1.1 +
      backgroundUniformity * 0.16 +
      (photoTextureRatio < 0.55 ? 0.15 : 0)
  );

  const photoHeavyScore = clamp01(
    photoTextureRatio * 0.74 +
      (flatColorRatio < 0.45 ? 0.18 : 0) +
      (components.largeComponentDensity > 0.18 ? 0.08 : 0)
  );

  return {
    width,
    height,

    aspectRatio,
    megapixels: pixelCount / 1_000_000,

    hasAlpha: !stats.isOpaque,
    transparencyRatio: alphaStats.transparencyRatio,

    entropy: stats.entropy,
    sharpness: stats.sharpness,

    dominantColor: stats.dominant
      ? rgbToHex(stats.dominant.r, stats.dominant.g, stats.dominant.b)
      : undefined,

    estimatedPaletteSize,
    topPaletteCoverage,
    flatColorRatio,

    edgeDensity,

    smallComponentDensity: components.smallComponentDensity,
    largeComponentDensity: components.largeComponentDensity,
    textLikeComponentDensity: components.textLikeComponentDensity,

    photoTextureRatio,

    backgroundUniformity,

    documentLikeScore,
    logoIconScore,
    graphicDesignScore,
    photoHeavyScore,
  };
}

function readRgbaPixels(data: Buffer): RgbaPixel[] {
  const pixels: RgbaPixel[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i += 4) {
    pixels.push({
      r: data[i],
      g: data[i + 1],
      b: data[i + 2],
      a: data[i + 3],
    });
  }

  return pixels;
}

function computeAlphaStats(pixels: RgbaPixel[]) {
  let transparent = 0;

  for (const p of pixels) {
    if (p.a < 250) transparent++;
  }

  return {
    transparencyRatio: transparent / pixels.length,
  };
}

function computeQuantizedPalette(
  pixels: RgbaPixel[],
  bitsPerChannel: number
) {
  const shift = 8 - bitsPerChannel;

  const bins = new Map<number, number>();

  let visible = 0;

  for (const p of pixels) {
    if (p.a < 16) continue;

    visible++;

    const key =
      ((p.r >> shift) << (bitsPerChannel * 2)) |
      ((p.g >> shift) << bitsPerChannel) |
      (p.b >> shift);

    bins.set(key, (bins.get(key) ?? 0) + 1);
  }

  const counts = [...bins.values()].sort((a, b) => b - a);

  const topN = counts.slice(0, 12).reduce((sum, count) => sum + count, 0);

  return {
    estimatedPaletteSize: bins.size,
    topCoverage: visible > 0 ? topN / visible : 0,
  };
}

function computeEdgeDensity(
  pixels: RgbaPixel[],
  width: number,
  height: number
) {
  let edges = 0;
  let total = 0;

  const threshold = MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.edgeThreshold;

  for (let y = 1; y < height; y++) {
    for (let x = 1; x < width; x++) {
      const current = luminance(pixels[y * width + x]);
      const left = luminance(pixels[y * width + x - 1]);
      const top = luminance(pixels[(y - 1) * width + x]);

      const diff = Math.max(
        Math.abs(current - left),
        Math.abs(current - top)
      );

      if (diff > threshold) edges++;

      total++;
    }
  }

  return total > 0 ? edges / total : 0;
}

/**
 * Fast approximation only.
 * Real connected components happen in Step 11.
 */
function computeApproxConnectedComponents(input: {
  pixels: RgbaPixel[];
  width: number;
  height: number;
  edgeDensity: number;
}) {
  const {
    pixels,
    width,
    height,
  } = input;

  const visited = new Uint8Array(width * height);

  const minArea =
    MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.componentMinAreaRatio *
    width *
    height;

  const smallArea =
    MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.componentSmallAreaRatio *
    width *
    height;

  const largeArea =
    MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.componentLargeAreaRatio *
    width *
    height;

  let smallComponents = 0;
  let largeComponents = 0;
  let textLikeComponents = 0;

  const maxComponentsToScan = 500;
  let scannedComponents = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < pixels.length; i++) {
    if (visited[i]) continue;

    const p = pixels[i];

    if (p.a < 16) {
      visited[i] = 1;
      continue;
    }

    const component = floodFillSimilar({
      pixels,
      width,
      height,
      startIndex: i,
      visited,
    });

    if (component.area < minArea) continue;

    scannedComponents++;

    if (component.area < smallArea) {
      smallComponents++;
    }

    if (component.area > largeArea) {
      largeComponents++;
    }

    const aspectRatio =
      component.bbox.width / Math.max(1, component.bbox.height);

    const areaRatio = component.area / (width * height);

    const isTextLike =
      aspectRatio >=
        MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.textLikeAspectRatioMin &&
      aspectRatio <=
        MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.textLikeAspectRatioMax &&
      areaRatio <=
        MAGIC_LAYERS_ROUTING_POLICY.localMetrics.textLikeAreaMaxRatio;

    if (isTextLike) {
      textLikeComponents++;
    }

    if (scannedComponents >= maxComponentsToScan) {
      break;
    }
  }

  const normalizer = Math.max(1, scannedComponents);

  return {
    smallComponentDensity: smallComponents / normalizer,
    largeComponentDensity: largeComponents / normalizer,
    textLikeComponentDensity: textLikeComponents / normalizer,
  };
}

function floodFillSimilar(input: {
  pixels: RgbaPixel[];
  width: number;
  height: number;
  startIndex: number;
  visited: Uint8Array;
}) {
  const {
    pixels,
    width,
    height,
    startIndex,
    visited,
  } = input;

  const start = pixels[startIndex];

  const stack = [startIndex];

  visited[startIndex] = 1;

  let area = 0;

  let minX = width;
  let minY = height;
  let maxX = 0;
  let maxY = 0;

  while (stack.length) {
    const index = stack.pop()!;

    const x = index % width;
    const y = Math.floor(index / width);

    area++;

    minX = Math.min(minX, x);
    minY = Math.min(minY, y);
    maxX = Math.max(maxX, x);
    maxY = Math.max(maxY, y);

    for (const next of [
      index - 1,
      index + 1,
      index - width,
      index + width,
    ]) {
      if (next < 0 || next >= pixels.length) continue;
      if (visited[next]) continue;

      const p = pixels[next];

      if (p.a < 16) {
        visited[next] = 1;
        continue;
      }

      if (colorDistance(start, p) <= 34) {
        visited[next] = 1;
        stack.push(next);
      }
    }
  }

  return {
    area,
    bbox: {
      x: minX,
      y: minY,
      width: maxX - minX + 1,
      height: maxY - minY + 1,
    },
  };
}

function estimateBackgroundUniformity(input: {
  pixels: RgbaPixel[];
  width: number;
  height: number;
}) {
  const {
    pixels,
    width,
    height,
  } = input;

  const sample: RgbaPixel[] = [];

  for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
    sample.push(pixels[x]);
    sample.push(pixels[(height - 1) * width + x]);
  }

  for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    sample.push(pixels[y * width]);
    sample.push(pixels[y * width + width - 1]);
  }

  if (sample.length === 0) return 0;

  const palette = computeQuantizedPalette(sample, 4);

  return palette.topCoverage;
}

function luminance(p: RgbaPixel) {
  return 0.2126 * p.r + 0.7152 * p.g + 0.0722 * p.b;
}

function colorDistance(a: RgbaPixel, b: RgbaPixel) {
  return Math.sqrt(
    (a.r - b.r) ** 2 +
      (a.g - b.g) ** 2 +
      (a.b - b.b) ** 2
  );
}

function normalizeRange(value: number, min: number, max: number) {
  if (value <= min) return 0;
  if (value >= max) return 1;
  return (value - min) / (max - min);
}

function clamp01(value: number) {
  return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value));
}

function rgbToHex(r: number, g: number, b: number) {
  return `#${[r, g, b]
    .map((v) => Math.round(v).toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("")}`;
}
```

This approximate component scan is only for routing. Step 11 will do real elementization.
