## ChatGPT Response 019

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 01ba9ee9-819e-479f-a895-a7892d8d3b07, 273a667c-05f8-438d-a138-fb8b10550f24 -->

Step 9 is the model-adapter boundary: LayerD, SAM/Gemini masks, SAM2, or future RGBA-layer models must append observations, never own editor state.

# Step 9 — Decomposition engine adapter

Step 9 creates the **common adapter layer** for decomposition engines.

The locked rule:

```txt
Decomposition engines do not create final layers.
Decomposition engines produce decomposition observations.
The scene resolver later decides what becomes text, vector, raster, group, or fallback.
```

This is where LayerD, Gemini segmentation, SAM/BiRefNet-style masks, and fallback deterministic extractors become interchangeable.

LayerD is directly relevant, but it must not define your product architecture. Its public paper/project describes raster graphic decomposition as iterative extraction of unoccluded foreground layers, and also says the problem is ill-posed because multiple decompositions can be valid. That is exactly why our adapter must output evidence, not final editor state. citeturn427731view0turn427731view1

---

## 9.1 What Step 9 owns

Step 9 owns:

```txt
decomposition engine interface
engine selection based on routing
engine run records
raw decomposition asset storage
RGBA layer observations
mask observations
z-order observations
background candidate observations
decomposition report asset
observation bundle update
Firestore decomposition summary
```

Step 9 does **not** own:

```txt
final raster layers
editable text decisions
vector acceptance
background repair acceptance
scene resolving
Fabric JSON
visual validation
text safety validation
```

Those come later.

---

# 9.2 Core architecture decision

Use this architecture:

```txt
Node worker
→ DecompositionEngine adapter
→ engine-specific implementation
→ raw outputs
→ normalized AiObservation records
→ updated AiObservationBundle
```

Do **not** let any model write directly into:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument.layers
Fabric JSON
design versions
```

Correct:

```txt
LayerD output → rgba_layer observations
Gemini masks → mask observations
SAM/BiRefNet masks → mask observations
connected components → component/mask observations
```

Wrong:

```txt
LayerD output → final Fabric layers
Gemini mask → accepted layer
SAM mask → accepted product object
```

---

# 9.3 Engine taxonomy

Use this engine set from day one:

```ts
export type DecompositionEngineName =
  | "layerd_graphic_design"
  | "gemini_segmentation_proposals"
  | "sam_prompted_masks"
  | "birefnet_subject_matte"
  | "connected_components_fallback"
  | "manual_crop_fallback";
```

Meaning:

```txt
layerd_graphic_design
Best for posters, flyers, social banners, AI-generated graphics, flat/vector-heavy designs.
Produces raw RGBA layer candidates and ordering evidence.

gemini_segmentation_proposals
Semantic mask proposals from Gemini. Useful for products, people, logos, icons, image blocks.
Not trusted as final masks.

sam_prompted_masks
Prompted segmentation from bounding boxes/points derived from Gemini layout/OCR.
Useful when you need pixel masks around known regions.

birefnet_subject_matte
High-resolution foreground/top-layer matte candidate.
Useful for person/product/photo subject extraction and possible top-layer matting.

connected_components_fallback
Deterministic flat-region decomposition.
Useful for simple logos, icons, flat shapes, and when model calls fail.

manual_crop_fallback
Creates no semantic layers. Provides locked reference + crop/manual tooling path.
```

SAM 2 is a promptable segmentation foundation model for images and videos, so it fits this adapter as a mask proposal engine, not as a design-understanding system. citeturn427731view2 BiRefNet is an official high-resolution dichotomous image segmentation implementation, so it fits foreground/top-layer matte proposals, not scene reconstruction. citeturn427731view3 Gemini segmentation can return JSON with `box_2d`, `mask`, and `label`, but Google’s own best-practice prompt still frames this as segmentation output, not layered design reconstruction. citeturn427731view4

---

# 9.4 Route-to-engine matrix

Use the route from Step 7.

```ts
export const DECOMPOSITION_ENGINE_PLAN_BY_ROUTE = {
  graphic_design_layer_decomposition: [
    "layerd_graphic_design",
    "gemini_segmentation_proposals",
    "connected_components_fallback",
  ],

  photo_conservative_segmentation: [
    "gemini_segmentation_proposals",
    "sam_prompted_masks",
    "birefnet_subject_matte",
  ],

  text_recovery_priority: [
    "connected_components_fallback",
    "gemini_segmentation_proposals",
  ],

  vectorization_priority: [
    "connected_components_fallback",
    "gemini_segmentation_proposals",
  ],

  fallback_only: [
    "manual_crop_fallback",
  ],
} as const;
```

Important behavior:

```txt
LayerD is not run for photo-heavy images by default.
SAM/BiRefNet are not used as graphic-design scene parsers.
Gemini segmentation is semantic proposal evidence only.
Connected components are fallback evidence only.
```

# 9.5 Engine output contract

Every engine returns the same structure.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/decomposition/decomposition-engine.types.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  AiAssetRef,
  AiObservation,
  AiRoutingDiagnosis,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import type {
  AiObservationBundle,
} from "../observations/observation-bundle.types";

export const AI_DECOMPOSITION_PASS_SCHEMA_VERSION =
  "ai-decomposition-pass.v1" as const;

export type DecompositionEngineName =
  | "layerd_graphic_design"
  | "gemini_segmentation_proposals"
  | "sam_prompted_masks"
  | "birefnet_subject_matte"
  | "connected_components_fallback"
  | "manual_crop_fallback";

export type DecompositionEngineBackend =
  | "node_local"
  | "python_subprocess"
  | "cloud_run_job"
  | "external_http"
  | "system";

export type DecompositionEngineRunStatus =
  | "skipped"
  | "completed"
  | "failed";

export type DecompositionEngineInput = {
  jobId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  canvas: {
    width: number;
    height: number;
    unit: "px";
  };

  routing: {
    diagnosis: AiRoutingDiagnosis;
    recommendedRoute:
      | "graphic_design_layer_decomposition"
      | "photo_conservative_segmentation"
      | "text_recovery_priority"
      | "vectorization_priority"
      | "fallback_only";
  };

  assets: {
    normalized: AiAssetRef;
    editorReference: AiAssetRef;
    routeScale: AiAssetRef;
    layoutScale: AiAssetRef;
    aiScale: AiAssetRef;
  };

  observationBundle: AiObservationBundle;

  limits: {
    maxCandidateLayers: number;
    maxMaskCandidates: number;
    maxRuntimeMs: number;
    maxOutputAssetBytes: number;
  };

  options: {
    conservative: boolean;
    allowGpu: boolean;
    allowRemoteEngine: boolean;
    dryRun?: boolean;
  };
};

export type DecompositionEngineOutput = {
  engineName: DecompositionEngineName;

  backend: DecompositionEngineBackend;

  status: DecompositionEngineRunStatus;

  observations: AiObservation[];

  assets: Record<string, AiAssetRef>;

  rawOutputAssetId?: string;

  reportAssetId?: string;

  metrics: {
    candidateLayerCount: number;
    maskCandidateCount: number;
    rgbaLayerCount: number;
    backgroundCandidateCount: number;

    runtimeMs: number;

    outputBytes: number;

    averageConfidence?: number;
  };

  warnings: string[];

  error?: {
    code: string;
    message: string;
    retryable: boolean;
  };
};

export type DecompositionEngine = {
  name: DecompositionEngineName;

  backend: DecompositionEngineBackend;

  shouldRun(input: DecompositionEngineInput): boolean;

  run(input: DecompositionEngineInput): Promise<DecompositionEngineOutput>;
};

export type DecompositionEngineRunRecord = {
  name: DecompositionEngineName;

  backend: DecompositionEngineBackend;

  status: DecompositionEngineRunStatus;

  observationCount: number;

  rawOutputAssetId?: string;
  reportAssetId?: string;

  metrics: DecompositionEngineOutput["metrics"];

  warnings: string[];

  startedAt: number;
  completedAt?: number;

  error?: {
    code: string;
    message: string;
    retryable: boolean;
  };
};

export type AiDecompositionPass = {
  schemaVersion: typeof AI_DECOMPOSITION_PASS_SCHEMA_VERSION;

  jobId: string;
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  sourceObservationBundleAssetId: string;

  outputObservationBundleAssetId: string;

  engineRuns: DecompositionEngineRunRecord[];

  observationsAdded: {
    total: number;
    mask: number;
    rgbaLayer: number;
    backgroundCandidate: number;
    zOrder: number;
    component: number;
  };

  assetsCreated: string[];

  warnings: string[];

  createdAt: number;
};
```

---

# 9.6 Engine execution boundary

Use a strict process boundary for heavy engines.

For day one, support two execution modes:

```txt
node_local
  deterministic connected-components fallback
  manual crop fallback

python_subprocess or cloud_run_job
  LayerD
  SAM/BiRefNet
```

The long-term default should be:

```txt
Node worker orchestrates.
Python/GPU engines run behind adapters.
All input/output is via GCS asset references and JSON reports.
```

Do not bind your Node worker directly to Python model APIs. LayerD’s official repo exposes a high-level Python pipeline that can decompose, organize, and export SVG/PSD, but in your system it should be wrapped behind an adapter and converted to observations. citeturn497368search0

For GPU engines on Cloud Run Jobs, remember the current task-timeout constraint: Cloud Run Jobs can run much longer for CPU tasks, but GPU tasks are capped at one hour. citeturn583806search1turn583806search2

---

# 9.7 Engine artifact rule

Engine outputs are raw/intermediate unless accepted later.

Store engine outputs in the **source bucket** first:

```txt
workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/magic-layers/jobs/{jobId}/decomposition/{engineName}/{engineRunId}/...
```

Only later accepted editor assets go to the assets bucket.

Raw engine outputs:

```txt
rgba candidates
mask candidates
engine report JSON
raw stdout/stderr summary
engine metadata JSON
```

Accepted editor assets come later:

```txt
editor_png
export_png
accepted_mask_png
clean_background
```

This prevents bad engine outputs from becoming product-visible assets prematurely.

# 9.9 LayerD adapter contract

LayerD should enter through an adapter like this:

```txt
normalized image
→ LayerD Python engine
→ raw RGBA candidate layers
→ optional raw background candidate
→ extraction order metadata
→ AiRgbaLayerObservation[]
→ AiZOrderObservation[]
→ optional AiBackgroundCandidateObservation
```

LayerD is strongest for graphic-design images. Do not run it blindly on photo-heavy composites. Its project describes graphic designs as containing typography, embellishments, vector shapes, and image materials, and LayerD decomposes them for layer-level edits and downstream post-processing such as OCR/vectorization. citeturn497368search4

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/decomposition/layerd-engine-adapter.ts
```

```ts
import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks";

import type {
  AiObservation,
  AiRgbaLayerObservation,
  AiZOrderObservation,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import {
  AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "../schema/constants";

import {
  bucketForMagicStorageRole,
} from "../storage/storage-buckets";

import {
  decompositionEngineReportPath,
  decompositionRawRgbaLayerPath,
} from "../storage/storage-paths";

import {
  writeAiAsset,
} from "../storage/write-ai-asset";

import type {
  DecompositionEngine,
  DecompositionEngineInput,
  DecompositionEngineOutput,
} from "./decomposition-engine.types";

export const layerdGraphicDesignEngine: DecompositionEngine = {
  name: "layerd_graphic_design",

  backend: process.env.MAGIC_LAYERS_LAYERD_BACKEND === "cloud_run_job"
    ? "cloud_run_job"
    : "python_subprocess",

  shouldRun(input) {
    return (
      input.routing.recommendedRoute ===
        "graphic_design_layer_decomposition" &&
      input.options.allowGpu &&
      input.limits.maxCandidateLayers > 0
    );
  },

  async run(input): Promise<DecompositionEngineOutput> {
    const started = performance.now();

    const engineRunId = stableEngineRunId(input.jobId, this.name);

    try {
      const rawLayerDResult = await runLayerDEngineProcess({
        input,
        engineRunId,
      });

      const observations: AiObservation[] = [];
      const assets: DecompositionEngineOutput["assets"] = {};
      const sourceBucket = bucketForMagicStorageRole("source");

      let totalBytes = 0;

      for (let i = 0; i < rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers.length; i++) {
        const raw = rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers[i];

        const assetId = stableAssetId(
          input.jobId,
          `layerd-rgba-${i}`
        );

        const asset = await writeAiAsset({
          storageRole: "source",
          bucket: sourceBucket,
          storagePath: decompositionRawRgbaLayerPath({
            workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
            designId: input.designId,
            jobId: input.jobId,
            engineName: this.name,
            engineRunId,
            layerIndex: i,
            assetId,
          }),

          bytes: raw.bytes,

          assetId,
          kind: "raw_rgba_layer_png" as any,

          contentType: "image/png",

          workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
          designId: input.designId,
          jobId: input.jobId,

          width: raw.width,
          height: raw.height,

          source: "layerd",

          schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
          pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

          sourceAssetId: input.assets.normalized.id,

          cacheControl: "private, no-store",
        });

        assets[asset.id] = asset;
        totalBytes += raw.bytes.byteLength;

        const observation: AiRgbaLayerObservation = {
          id: `obs_layerd_rgba_${String(i).padStart(3, "0")}`,

          jobId: input.jobId,
          designId: input.designId,

          kind: "rgba_layer",

          source: "layerd",

          createdAt: Date.now(),

          model: {
            provider: "layerd",
            modelName: rawLayerDResult.engineVersion,
          },

          rgbaAssetId: asset.id,

          maskAssetId: raw.maskAssetId,

          bbox: raw.bbox,

          extractionOrder: raw.extractionOrder,

          frontToBackIndex: raw.frontToBackIndex,

          labelGuess: raw.labelGuess,

          confidence: {
            overall: raw.confidence ?? 0.7,
            mask: raw.confidence ?? 0.7,
            visualFidelity: raw.confidence ?? 0.7,
          },

          warnings: raw.warnings ?? [],
        };

        observations.push(observation);
      }

      /**
       * LayerD extraction order is useful z-order evidence.
       * It is still not the final editor z-order.
       */
      const ordered = rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers
        .map((_, index) => ({
          id: `obs_layerd_rgba_${String(index).padStart(3, "0")}`,
          frontToBackIndex:
            rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers[index].frontToBackIndex ?? index,
        }))
        .sort((a, b) => a.frontToBackIndex - b.frontToBackIndex);

      for (let i = 0; i < ordered.length - 1; i++) {
        const zObservation: AiZOrderObservation = {
          id: `obs_layerd_z_${i}_${i + 1}`,

          jobId: input.jobId,
          designId: input.designId,

          kind: "z_order",

          source: "layerd",

          createdAt: Date.now(),

          frontLayerId: ordered[i].id,
          backLayerId: ordered[i + 1].id,

          relation: "in_front_of",

          evidence: "layerd_order",

          confidence: {
            overall: 0.75,
            zIndex: 0.75,
          },
        };

        observations.push(zObservation);
      }

      const reportAssetId = stableAssetId(
        input.jobId,
        "layerd-report"
      );

      const reportAsset = await writeAiAsset({
        storageRole: "source",
        bucket: sourceBucket,
        storagePath: decompositionEngineReportPath({
          workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
          designId: input.designId,
          jobId: input.jobId,
          engineName: this.name,
          engineRunId,
          assetId: reportAssetId,
        }),

        bytes: Buffer.from(
          JSON.stringify(rawLayerDResult.report, null, 2),
          "utf8"
        ),

        assetId: reportAssetId,
        kind: "raw_decomposition_report_json" as any,

        contentType: "application/json",

        workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
        designId: input.designId,
        jobId: input.jobId,

        source: "layerd",

        schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

        sourceAssetId: input.assets.normalized.id,

        cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
      });

      assets[reportAsset.id] = reportAsset;

      const runtimeMs = Math.round(performance.now() - started);

      return {
        engineName: this.name,
        backend: this.backend,
        status: "completed",

        observations,

        assets,

        reportAssetId: reportAsset.id,

        metrics: {
          candidateLayerCount: rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers.length,
          maskCandidateCount: rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers.filter(
            (layer) => Boolean(layer.maskAssetId)
          ).length,
          rgbaLayerCount: rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers.length,
          backgroundCandidateCount:
            rawLayerDResult.backgroundCandidate ? 1 : 0,
          runtimeMs,
          outputBytes: totalBytes,
          averageConfidence: average(
            rawLayerDResult.rgbaLayers.map(
              (layer) => layer.confidence ?? 0.7
            )
          ),
        },

        warnings: rawLayerDResult.warnings,
      };
    } catch (error) {
      return {
        engineName: this.name,
        backend: this.backend,
        status: "failed",

        observations: [],
        assets: {},

        metrics: {
          candidateLayerCount: 0,
          maskCandidateCount: 0,
          rgbaLayerCount: 0,
          backgroundCandidateCount: 0,
          runtimeMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
          outputBytes: 0,
        },

        warnings: ["layerd_engine_failed"],

        error: {
          code: "layerd_engine_failed",
          message:
            error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown LayerD error",
          retryable: true,
        },
      };
    }
  },
};
```

The function `runLayerDEngineProcess(...)` is intentionally a boundary. It should be implemented either as:

```txt
python subprocess
or
separate Cloud Run Job/service
```

Do not mix LayerD internals into your TypeScript reconstruction code.

---

# 9.10 LayerD process response contract

The Python engine should output a JSON manifest like this:

```ts
type LayerDEngineProcessResult = {
  engineName: "layerd_graphic_design";

  engineVersion: string;

  rgbaLayers: {
    localPath: string;
    bytes: Buffer;

    width: number;
    height: number;

    bbox: {
      x: number;
      y: number;
      width: number;
      height: number;
    };

    extractionOrder: number;
    frontToBackIndex: number;

    confidence?: number;

    maskAssetId?: string;

    labelGuess?: string;

    warnings?: string[];
  }[];

  backgroundCandidate?: {
    localPath: string;
    width: number;
    height: number;
    confidence?: number;
  };

  report: Record<string, unknown>;

  warnings: string[];
};
```

Do not rely on LayerD SVG/PSD output as your canonical state.

Correct:

```txt
LayerD RGBA layers → AiRgbaLayerObservation
LayerD ordering → AiZOrderObservation
LayerD optional background → AiBackgroundCandidateObservation
```

Wrong:

```txt
LayerD SVG → Fabric import
LayerD PSD → canonical design state
```

SVG/PSD are export or diagnostic formats, not your source of truth.

---

# 9.11 Gemini segmentation adapter

Gemini segmentation belongs here as an engine only if Step 8 did not already run it.

In this step, Gemini segmentation should be bounded and semantic:

```txt
Give segmentation masks for prominent editable candidates:
products, people, logos, icons, image blocks, large decorations.
```

Do not ask:

```txt
Give every layer.
Reconstruct the design.
Create editable objects.
```

Google’s Gemini image docs state that object-detection boxes use `[ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]` normalized to `0–1000` and must be de-scaled to image size, which remains the coordinate rule for this adapter. citeturn427731view5

Output:

```txt
AiMaskObservation[]
raw_gemini_segmentation_output_json
raw_mask_png assets if masks are base64 PNG
```

Core adapter behavior:

```ts
export const geminiSegmentationProposalEngine: DecompositionEngine = {
  name: "gemini_segmentation_proposals",
  backend: "external_http",

  shouldRun(input) {
    return (
      input.routing.recommendedRoute !== "fallback_only" &&
      input.limits.maxMaskCandidates > 0
    );
  },

  async run(input) {
    /**
     * Implementation may reuse Step 8's Gemini segmentation generator.
     * If observationBundle already contains Gemini mask observations,
     * return skipped/completed with zero new observations.
     */
    const existing = Object.values(
      input.observationBundle.observations
    ).filter(
      (obs) =>
        obs.kind === "mask" &&
        obs.source === "gemini_segmentation"
    );

    if (existing.length > 0) {
      return {
        engineName: "gemini_segmentation_proposals",
        backend: "external_http",
        status: "skipped",
        observations: [],
        assets: {},
        metrics: {
          candidateLayerCount: 0,
          maskCandidateCount: 0,
          rgbaLayerCount: 0,
          backgroundCandidateCount: 0,
          runtimeMs: 0,
          outputBytes: 0,
        },
        warnings: ["gemini_segmentation_already_present"],
      };
    }

    /**
     * Actual call should use the Step 8 segmentation generator.
     * Keep one implementation path.
     */
    return runGeminiSegmentationAsDecompositionEngine(input);
  },
};
```

Important: keep only one Gemini segmentation implementation. Do not duplicate prompt logic in multiple places.

---

# 9.12 SAM prompted mask adapter

SAM/SAM2 should consume existing observations:

```txt
Gemini layout boxes
OCR text boxes
routing decision
```

It should not do semantic classification itself.

Input prompts:

```txt
bbox prompts from layout observations
optional point prompts at bbox center
negative prompts later if needed
```

Output:

```txt
AiMaskObservation[]
raw_mask_png assets
```

Adapter shape:

```ts
export const samPromptedMasksEngine: DecompositionEngine = {
  name: "sam_prompted_masks",
  backend: "python_subprocess",

  shouldRun(input) {
    return (
      input.routing.recommendedRoute ===
        "photo_conservative_segmentation" ||
      input.routing.recommendedRoute ===
        "graphic_design_layer_decomposition"
    );
  },

  async run(input) {
    const layoutBoxes = Object.values(
      input.observationBundle.observations
    ).filter(
      (obs) =>
        obs.kind === "layout" &&
        obs.bbox &&
        [
          "person",
          "product",
          "photo_subject",
          "logo",
          "icon",
          "image_block",
        ].includes(obs.layerTypeGuess)
    );

    const prompts = layoutBoxes
      .slice(0, input.limits.maxMaskCandidates)
      .map((obs) => ({
        observationId: obs.id,
        bbox: obs.bbox!,
        label: obs.label,
        layerTypeGuess: obs.layerTypeGuess,
      }));

    if (prompts.length === 0) {
      return skippedOutput({
        engineName: "sam_prompted_masks",
        backend: "python_subprocess",
        reason: "no_prompt_boxes",
      });
    }

    return runSamEngineProcess({
      input,
      prompts,
    });
  },
};
```

SAM mask quality is later evaluated in Step 13/17. This adapter only creates candidate masks.

---

# 9.13 BiRefNet matte adapter

BiRefNet should be used as a foreground/top-layer matte candidate engine.

Use it for:

```txt
person/product/photo subject
large foreground object
possible top-most subject
```

Do not use it for:

```txt
dense text extraction
vector shape reconstruction
complete design scene parsing
```

Adapter shape:

```ts
export const birefnetSubjectMatteEngine: DecompositionEngine = {
  name: "birefnet_subject_matte",
  backend: "python_subprocess",

  shouldRun(input) {
    return (
      input.routing.recommendedRoute ===
        "photo_conservative_segmentation" ||
      input.routing.recommendedRoute ===
        "graphic_design_layer_decomposition"
    );
  },

  async run(input) {
    const foregroundHints = Object.values(
      input.observationBundle.observations
    ).filter(
      (obs) =>
        obs.kind === "layout" &&
        ["person", "product", "photo_subject"].includes(
          obs.layerTypeGuess
        )
    );

    if (foregroundHints.length === 0) {
      return skippedOutput({
        engineName: "birefnet_subject_matte",
        backend: "python_subprocess",
        reason: "no_foreground_hints",
      });
    }

    return runBiRefNetEngineProcess({
      input,
      hints: foregroundHints.slice(0, 8),
    });
  },
};
```

BiRefNet outputs should become:

```txt
AiMaskObservation
```

or, if the engine already creates RGBA:

```txt
AiRgbaLayerObservation
```

Still not final layers.

---

# 9.14 Connected-components fallback engine

This engine is deterministic and should run when:

```txt
route = vectorization_priority
route = text_recovery_priority
route = graphic_design_layer_decomposition
or all model engines fail
```

It is useful for:

```txt
flat colors
simple shapes
logos/icons
large solid blocks
badges
simple decorations
```

It is weak for:

```txt
photos
hair
shadows
soft transparency
complex illustrations
```

Adapter shape:

```ts
export const connectedComponentsFallbackEngine: DecompositionEngine = {
  name: "connected_components_fallback",
  backend: "node_local",

  shouldRun(input) {
    return input.routing.recommendedRoute !== "fallback_only";
  },

  async run(input) {
    /**
     * This should use normalized/editorReference image.
     * It creates only component/mask observations.
     * Real elementization is Step 11, so keep this conservative.
     */
    return runConnectedComponentsDecomposition(input);
  },
};
```

This fallback should only extract high-confidence flat regions. It must not flood the observation bundle with tiny noise.

---

# 9.15 Manual crop fallback engine

This engine exists so the job can still produce a usable editor import when decomposition is unsafe.

```ts
export const manualCropFallbackEngine: DecompositionEngine = {
  name: "manual_crop_fallback",
  backend: "system",

  shouldRun(input) {
    return input.routing.recommendedRoute === "fallback_only";
  },

  async run(input) {
    return {
      engineName: "manual_crop_fallback",
      backend: "system",
      status: "completed",

      observations: [
        {
          id: "obs_manual_fallback_reference_only",
          jobId: input.jobId,
          designId: input.designId,
          kind: "layout",
          source: "system",
          createdAt: Date.now(),

          label: "Original reference",
          layerTypeGuess: "locked_reference",
          editableHint: "likely_background",

          bbox: {
            x: 0,
            y: 0,
            width: input.canvas.width,
            height: input.canvas.height,
          },

          zIndexGuess: 0,

          description:
            "Fallback-only route. No safe automatic decomposition was selected.",

          confidence: {
            overall: 1,
            classification: 1,
            bbox: 1,
          },
        },
      ],

      assets: {},

      metrics: {
        candidateLayerCount: 1,
        maskCandidateCount: 0,
        rgbaLayerCount: 0,
        backgroundCandidateCount: 0,
        runtimeMs: 0,
        outputBytes: 0,
        averageConfidence: 1,
      },

      warnings: ["fallback_only_decomposition"],
    };
  },
};
```

This is not failure. It is a safe degradation mode.

# 9.16 Decomposition pass runner

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/decomposition/run-decomposition-pass.ts
```

```ts
import {
  AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "../schema/constants";

import type {
  AiObservation,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import type {
  AiObservationBundle,
} from "../observations/observation-bundle.types";

import {
  bucketForMagicStorageRole,
} from "../storage/storage-buckets";

import {
  decompositionPassReportPath,
  observationBundlePath,
} from "../storage/storage-paths";

import {
  writeAiAsset,
} from "../storage/write-ai-asset";

import {
  enginePlanForRoute,
} from "../routing/route-engine-policy";

import type {
  DecompositionEngine,
  DecompositionEngineInput,
  DecompositionEngineRunRecord,
  AiDecompositionPass,
} from "./decomposition-engine.types";

import {
  layerdGraphicDesignEngine,
} from "./layerd-engine-adapter";

import {
  geminiSegmentationProposalEngine,
} from "./gemini-segmentation-engine-adapter";

import {
  samPromptedMasksEngine,
} from "./sam-prompted-masks-engine-adapter";

import {
  birefnetSubjectMatteEngine,
} from "./birefnet-subject-matte-engine-adapter";

import {
  connectedComponentsFallbackEngine,
} from "./connected-components-fallback-engine";

import {
  manualCropFallbackEngine,
} from "./manual-crop-fallback-engine";

export type RunDecompositionPassInput = {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
  userId: string;

  observationBundle: AiObservationBundle;

  sourceObservationBundleAssetId: string;
};

export async function runDecompositionPass(
  input: RunDecompositionPassInput
): Promise<{
  updatedBundle: AiObservationBundle;
  updatedBundleAssetId: string;
  decompositionPass: AiDecompositionPass;
  decompositionPassAssetId: string;
}> {
  const route =
    input.observationBundle.routing.diagnosis.recommendedRoute;

  const enginePlan = enginePlanForRoute(route);

  const context: DecompositionEngineInput = {
    jobId: input.jobId,
    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    userId: input.userId,

    canvas: input.observationBundle.canvas,

    routing: {
      diagnosis: input.observationBundle.routing.diagnosis,
      recommendedRoute: route,
    },

    assets: resolveCoreAssets(input.observationBundle),

    observationBundle: input.observationBundle,

    limits: {
      maxCandidateLayers: enginePlan.maxCandidateLayers,
      maxMaskCandidates: enginePlan.maxCandidateLayers,
      maxRuntimeMs: 12 * 60 * 1000,
      maxOutputAssetBytes: 512 * 1024 * 1024,
    },

    options: {
      conservative: true,
      allowGpu: true,
      allowRemoteEngine: true,
    },
  };

  const engines = selectDecompositionEngines(route);

  const engineRuns: DecompositionEngineRunRecord[] = [];

  const allNewObservations: AiObservation[] = [];
  const allNewAssets = {
    ...input.observationBundle.assets,
  };

  const warnings: string[] = [];

  for (const engine of engines) {
    const startedAt = Date.now();

    if (!engine.shouldRun(context)) {
      engineRuns.push({
        name: engine.name,
        backend: engine.backend,
        status: "skipped",
        observationCount: 0,
        metrics: emptyMetrics(),
        warnings: ["engine_should_run_false"],
        startedAt,
        completedAt: Date.now(),
      });

      continue;
    }

    const result = await engine.run(context);

    for (const [assetId, asset] of Object.entries(result.assets)) {
      allNewAssets[assetId] = asset;
    }

    for (const observation of result.observations) {
      allNewObservations.push(observation);
    }

    warnings.push(...result.warnings);

    engineRuns.push({
      name: result.engineName,
      backend: result.backend,
      status: result.status,
      observationCount: result.observations.length,
      rawOutputAssetId: result.rawOutputAssetId,
      reportAssetId: result.reportAssetId,
      metrics: result.metrics,
      warnings: result.warnings,
      startedAt,
      completedAt: Date.now(),
      error: result.error,
    });

    /**
     * If LayerD produced enough RGBA candidates for graphic design,
     * avoid over-running extra engines unless route needs them.
     */
    if (
      result.engineName === "layerd_graphic_design" &&
      result.status === "completed" &&
      result.metrics.rgbaLayerCount >= 3 &&
      route === "graphic_design_layer_decomposition"
    ) {
      /**
       * Keep Gemini/CC evidence if already present from Step 8,
       * but do not force extra expensive engines.
       */
    }
  }

  const updatedObservations = {
    ...input.observationBundle.observations,
  };

  for (const observation of allNewObservations) {
    updatedObservations[observation.id] = observation;
  }

  const updatedBundle: AiObservationBundle = {
    ...input.observationBundle,

    assets: allNewAssets,

    observations: updatedObservations,

    generatorRuns: input.observationBundle.generatorRuns,

    counts: countObservationKinds(Object.values(updatedObservations)),

    warnings: [
      ...input.observationBundle.warnings,
      ...warnings,
    ],

    updatedAt: Date.now(),
  };

  const updatedBundleAssetId = stableAssetId(
    input.jobId,
    "observation-bundle-after-decomposition"
  );

  const updatedBundleAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "source",
    bucket: bucketForMagicStorageRole("source"),
    storagePath: observationBundlePath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      jobId: input.jobId,
      assetId: updatedBundleAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: Buffer.from(
      JSON.stringify(updatedBundle, null, 2),
      "utf8"
    ),

    assetId: updatedBundleAssetId,
    kind: "observation_bundle_json" as any,

    contentType: "application/json",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,

    source: "system",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
  });

  const decompositionPassAssetId = stableAssetId(
    input.jobId,
    "decomposition-pass"
  );

  const decompositionPass: AiDecompositionPass = {
    schemaVersion: "ai-decomposition-pass.v1",

    jobId: input.jobId,
    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    userId: input.userId,

    sourceObservationBundleAssetId:
      input.sourceObservationBundleAssetId,

    outputObservationBundleAssetId: updatedBundleAsset.id,

    engineRuns,

    observationsAdded: countAddedObservations(allNewObservations),

    assetsCreated: Object.keys(allNewAssets).filter(
      (assetId) => !input.observationBundle.assets[assetId]
    ),

    warnings,

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };

  const decompositionPassAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "source",
    bucket: bucketForMagicStorageRole("source"),
    storagePath: decompositionPassReportPath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      jobId: input.jobId,
      assetId: decompositionPassAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: Buffer.from(
      JSON.stringify(decompositionPass, null, 2),
      "utf8"
    ),

    assetId: decompositionPassAssetId,
    kind: "decomposition_pass_json" as any,

    contentType: "application/json",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,

    source: "system",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
  });

  return {
    updatedBundle,
    updatedBundleAssetId: updatedBundleAsset.id,
    decompositionPass,
    decompositionPassAssetId: decompositionPassAsset.id,
  };
}

function selectDecompositionEngines(
  route: DecompositionEngineInput["routing"]["recommendedRoute"]
): DecompositionEngine[] {
  switch (route) {
    case "graphic_design_layer_decomposition":
      return [
        layerdGraphicDesignEngine,
        geminiSegmentationProposalEngine,
        connectedComponentsFallbackEngine,
      ];

    case "photo_conservative_segmentation":
      return [
        geminiSegmentationProposalEngine,
        samPromptedMasksEngine,
        birefnetSubjectMatteEngine,
      ];

    case "text_recovery_priority":
      return [
        connectedComponentsFallbackEngine,
        geminiSegmentationProposalEngine,
      ];

    case "vectorization_priority":
      return [
        connectedComponentsFallbackEngine,
        geminiSegmentationProposalEngine,
      ];

    case "fallback_only":
      return [manualCropFallbackEngine];
  }
}
```

```ts
}
```

# 9.19 Decomposition observation acceptance gates

Before adding engine output to the observation bundle:

```txt
image asset exists
asset is readable
bbox is inside canvas
mask dimensions are valid
RGBA dimensions are valid
observation id is stable
observation source is correct
confidence exists
raw output report exists
output size is under limit
candidate count is under limit
```

Reject or downgrade if:

```txt
mask is empty
mask covers almost whole canvas without being background
RGBA layer has no alpha variation
bbox area is tiny noise
duplicate IoU with existing observation is too high
engine output exceeds max candidate count
engine output has missing dimensions
engine output cannot be decoded
```

Use conservative defaults:

```ts
export const MAGIC_LAYERS_DECOMPOSITION_POLICY = {
  maxCandidateLayers: 40,

  maxMaskCandidates: 40,

  minMaskAreaRatio: 0.0005,

  maxNonBackgroundMaskAreaRatio: 0.92,

  duplicateMaskIoUThreshold: 0.92,

  minRgbaVisibleAlphaRatio: 0.001,

  maxRawEngineOutputBytes: 512 * 1024 * 1024,

  layerd: {
    enabled: true,
    maxIterations: 30,
    onlyForRoutes: ["graphic_design_layer_decomposition"],
  },

  sam: {
    enabled: true,
    maxPromptBoxes: 24,
  },

  birefnet: {
    enabled: true,
    maxForegroundHints: 8,
  },

  connectedComponents: {
    enabled: true,
    maxComponents: 80,
    minComponentAreaRatio: 0.0004,
  },
} as const;
```

# 9.20 Duplicate suppression

Duplicate candidate masks are common.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/decomposition/dedupe-mask-observations.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  AiMaskObservation,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import {
  bboxIoU,
} from "../schema/geometry";

export function dedupeMaskObservations(
  masks: AiMaskObservation[]
): AiMaskObservation[] {
  const accepted: AiMaskObservation[] = [];

  for (const mask of masks.sort(
    (a, b) =>
      (b.confidence?.overall ?? 0) -
      (a.confidence?.overall ?? 0)
  )) {
    const duplicate = accepted.find(
      (existing) => bboxIoU(existing.bbox, mask.bbox) > 0.92
    );

    if (duplicate) {
      accepted.push({
        ...mask,
        duplicateOfObservationId: duplicate.id,
        warnings: [
          ...(mask.warnings ?? []),
          "duplicate_mask_candidate",
        ],
      });

      continue;
    }

    accepted.push(mask);
  }

  return accepted;
}
```

This is bbox-only dedupe. Later, Step 13 can do mask-pixel IoU.

---

# 9.21 Engine failure policy

A failed engine should not automatically fail the job.

Rules:

```txt
If LayerD fails on graphic design:
  continue with Gemini segmentation + connected components.

If Gemini segmentation fails:
  continue with LayerD/SAM/BiRefNet if available.

If SAM/BiRefNet fails:
  continue with Gemini/layout observations.

If all decomposition engines fail:
  keep observation bundle
  mark decomposition needs_review
  continue only if fallback path can still create locked reference.
```

Fail the job only when:

```txt
no locked reference exists
normalized image is missing
all decomposition paths fail and fallback cannot be produced
engine output corrupts required state
GCS write fails for required reports
```

---

# 9.22 What Step 9 must not do

Do not add:

```txt
final layer acceptance
mask edge refinement
alpha matting finalization
text editing
font matching
vector tracing acceptance
background clean layer acceptance
Fabric objects
visual diff scoring
PSD export
```

Step 9 only extracts **candidate layer/mask evidence**.

# 9.24 Non-negotiable invariants

Step 9 is valid only if:

```txt
Every decomposition engine uses the same adapter interface.

Every engine output becomes AiObservation records.

No engine output becomes AiReconstructedLayer.

No engine output becomes Fabric JSON.

LayerD is route-gated.

SAM/BiRefNet are treated as mask/matte engines, not design parsers.

Gemini segmentation is treated as semantic proposal evidence only.

Raw engine outputs are stored in GCS.

Firestore stores only summaries and pointers.

Every output observation has provenance.

Every output observation uses canvas_px geometry.

Every raw asset has assetId, bucket, storagePath, source, schemaVersion, pipelineVersion.

Engine failures are isolated.

Partial decomposition is allowed.

Fallback-only path remains valid.

The observation bundle is updated immutably by creating a new bundle asset.
```

# 9.25 Definition of done

Step 9 is complete when:

```txt
DecompositionEngine interface exists.

Route-to-engine selection exists.

LayerD adapter exists behind a process boundary.

Gemini segmentation adapter is unified with Step 8 segmentation logic.

SAM/BiRefNet adapters are defined as mask/matte proposal engines.

Connected-components fallback exists.

Manual fallback exists.

Decomposition pass runner updates the observation bundle.

Decomposition pass report is stored in GCS.

Firestore points to the updated observation bundle.

No final layers are created.

No Fabric JSON is created.
```

Locked Step 9 architecture:

```txt
ObservationBundle
→ route-selected decomposition engines
→ raw RGBA/mask/z-order/background observations
→ updated ObservationBundle
→ decomposition pass report
→ Firestore pointer update
```

## ChatGPT Response 020

<!-- assistant_message_ids: c7a76f02-1d43-403e-9ec2-a61c28cb8709, 104bd42c-7ab3-4a03-ae5a-228813583ef4 -->

Step 10 is the first high-risk trust subsystem: OCR and style recovery only create text evidence, while editable text is earned later through grouping, render validation, and preservation checks.

# Step 10 — Text recovery system

Step 10 turns raw OCR/layout evidence into **validated editable-text candidates**.

The locked rule:

```txt
OCR does not create editable text.
Text recovery creates text candidates.
The scene resolver later decides whether a candidate becomes text_editable or raster_fallback.
```

This is the highest-risk subsystem in Magic Layers because wrong text destroys trust faster than a bad mask.

---

## 10.1 What Step 10 owns

Step 10 owns:

```txt
OCR word grouping
text region construction
line/block reconstruction
text crop generation
raster fallback crop generation
font/style estimation
text color estimation
stroke/shadow heuristic detection
render-back validation
text mutation detection
text candidate observations
text recovery report
updated observation bundle
Firestore text recovery summary
```

Step 10 does **not** own:

```txt
Fabric Textbox creation
final layer acceptance
final z-order
background repair
scene resolving
export rendering
```

Fabric `Textbox` is still the eventual editor target, but Fabric’s docs matter here: `Textbox` wraps lines automatically and adjusts height based on wrapping. That means reconstructed poster typography can drift unless width, font, font size, line height, and spacing are validated before promotion to live text. citeturn835791view1

---

# 10.2 Why text recovery is separate from OCR

OCR only answers:

```txt
What characters are visible?
Where are they approximately?
```

Editable design text requires:

```txt
string
bbox
line breaks
reading order
font family
font weight
font size
letter spacing
line height
fill
stroke
shadow
rotation
alignment
fallback crop
render similarity
text safety
```

Research on de-rendering stylized text frames raster text editing as recovering rendering parameters: text, location, size, font, style, effects, and hidden background. It also explicitly describes the problem as OCR + background inpainting + styling recognition, not OCR alone. citeturn835791view3

So the product rule is:

```txt
OCR evidence + style estimation + render validation
→ text candidate

text candidate + scene resolver thresholds
→ maybe text_editable
```

---

# 10.3 Inputs

Step 10 consumes the current `AiObservationBundle` after Step 9.

Required inputs:

```txt
normalized image asset
editor reference image asset
ai working scale image asset
OCR observations
Gemini layout text observations
decomposition mask/RGBA observations
routing diagnosis
canvas dimensions
```

Useful observation kinds:

```txt
ocr
layout
mask
rgba_layer
palette
routing
group_candidate
z_order
```

Step 10 should never read:

```txt
client upload path
raw OCR response directly
raw Gemini response directly
```

It reads normalized observations and asset references.

Step 10 appends new observations to the observation bundle:

```txt
text_candidate observations
text_style observations
quality observations
group_candidate observations if text lines form blocks
```

It creates assets:

```txt

```

It updates Firestore:

```txt
job.input.observationBundleAssetId
job.textRecovery.summary
progress
```

It does **not** create:

```txt
AiReconstructedLayer
AiFabricManifest
Fabric JSON
```

```ts
    maxRenderRgbL1ForLiveText: 0.18,
    maxEditDistanceRatioForLiveText: 0.02,

    minTextSafetyForLiveText: 1,

    minFontConfidenceForLiveText: 0.45,

  },

  cost: {
    renderValidateOnlyTopN: 80,
    roundTripOcrOnlyWhenAmbiguous: true,
  },
} as const;
```

These thresholds are intentionally conservative. A visually faithful raster fallback is preferable to a wrong editable text object.

---

# 10.8 Text recovery algorithm

Step 10 runs this sequence:

```txt
1. Load observation bundle.
2. Collect OCR word observations.
3. Collect Gemini layout text observations.
4. Filter low-confidence OCR noise.
5. Cluster OCR words into lines.
6. Merge lines into text blocks using layout regions.
7. Build text candidate records.
8. Extract fallback crop from normalized image.
9. Estimate style.
10. Render candidate text back to image.
11. Compare render against original crop.
12. Detect text mutation.
13. Mark candidate as live_text_candidate / needs_review / raster_only.
14. Append text_candidate + quality observations.
15. Save updated observation bundle.
16. Save text recovery report.
17. Patch Firestore.
```

Cloud Vision’s `TEXT_DETECTION` is optimized for sparse text and returns word-level text with bounding boxes plus a structural hierarchy, while `DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION` is optimized for dense text/document-like images and returns the `fullTextAnnotation` hierarchy. That is why Step 8 produced OCR observations, and Step 10 consumes them rather than calling OCR again. citeturn835791view0

# 10.9 Text grouping

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/text-recovery/group-ocr-words.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  AiLayoutObservation,
  AiOcrObservation,
  BBox,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import {
  bboxIntersectionArea,
  bboxArea,
} from "../schema/geometry";

import {
  MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY,
} from "./text-recovery-policy";

export type OcrWordForGrouping = {
  id: string;
  text: string;
  bbox: BBox;
  confidence: number;
  language?: string;
};

export type TextLineGroup = {
  id: string;
  wordIds: string[];
  text: string;
  bbox: BBox;
  confidence: number;
  baselineY: number;
};

export type TextBlockGroup = {
  id: string;
  lineIds: string[];
  wordIds: string[];
  text: string;
  bbox: BBox;
  confidence: number;
  sourceLayoutObservationIds: string[];
};

export function groupOcrWordsIntoTextBlocks(input: {
  ocrObservations: AiOcrObservation[];
  textLayoutObservations: AiLayoutObservation[];
}): TextBlockGroup[] {
  const words = input.ocrObservations
    .map((obs): OcrWordForGrouping => ({
      id: obs.id,
      text: obs.text,
      bbox: obs.bbox,
      confidence: obs.confidence?.ocr ?? obs.confidence?.overall ?? 0,
      language: obs.language,
    }))
    .filter(
      (word) =>
        word.text.trim().length > 0 &&
        word.confidence >=
          MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.minOcrWordConfidence
    );

  const lines = groupWordsIntoLines(words);

  const blocks = mergeLinesIntoBlocks({
    lines,
    textLayoutObservations: input.textLayoutObservations,
  });

  return blocks;
}

function groupWordsIntoLines(words: OcrWordForGrouping[]): TextLineGroup[] {
  const sorted = [...words].sort((a, b) => {
    const dy = centerY(a.bbox) - centerY(b.bbox);
    if (Math.abs(dy) > Math.min(a.bbox.height, b.bbox.height) * 0.7) {
      return dy;
    }
    return a.bbox.x - b.bbox.x;
  });

  const lines: OcrWordForGrouping[][] = [];

  for (const word of sorted) {
    const matchingLine = lines.find((line) => {
      const lineBox = unionBBoxes(line.map((w) => w.bbox));
      const avgHeight =
        line.reduce((sum, w) => sum + w.bbox.height, 0) / line.length;

      return (
        Math.abs(centerY(word.bbox) - centerY(lineBox)) <=
        avgHeight *
          MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.lineGrouping
            .maxBaselineDeltaRatio
      );
    });

    if (matchingLine) {
      matchingLine.push(word);
    } else {
      lines.push([word]);
    }
  }

  return lines.map((line, index): TextLineGroup => {
    const ordered = [...line].sort((a, b) => a.bbox.x - b.bbox.x);

    const text = joinWordsWithEstimatedSpaces(ordered);

    const bbox = unionBBoxes(ordered.map((w) => w.bbox));

    return {
      id: `text_line_${index}`,
      wordIds: ordered.map((w) => w.id),
      text,
      bbox,
      confidence:
        ordered.reduce((sum, w) => sum + w.confidence, 0) /
        Math.max(1, ordered.length),
      baselineY: centerY(bbox),
    };
  });
}

function mergeLinesIntoBlocks(input: {
  lines: TextLineGroup[];
  textLayoutObservations: AiLayoutObservation[];
}): TextBlockGroup[] {
  const textLayouts = input.textLayoutObservations.filter(
    (obs) => obs.layerTypeGuess === "text"
  );

  const assigned = new Set<string>();
  const blocks: TextBlockGroup[] = [];

  for (const layout of textLayouts) {
    if (!layout.bbox) continue;

    const matchingLines = input.lines.filter((line) => {
      const intersection = bboxIntersectionArea(line.bbox, layout.bbox!);
      const ratio = intersection / Math.max(1, bboxArea(line.bbox));

      return (
        ratio >= MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.minLayoutOverlapIoU
      );
    });

    if (!matchingLines.length) continue;

    for (const line of matchingLines) {
      assigned.add(line.id);
    }

    const orderedLines = matchingLines.sort(
      (a, b) => a.bbox.y - b.bbox.y
    );

    blocks.push({
      id: `text_block_layout_${layout.id}`,
      lineIds: orderedLines.map((line) => line.id),
      wordIds: orderedLines.flatMap((line) => line.wordIds),
      text: orderedLines.map((line) => line.text).join("\n"),
      bbox: unionBBoxes(orderedLines.map((line) => line.bbox)),
      confidence:
        orderedLines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.confidence, 0) /
        Math.max(1, orderedLines.length),
      sourceLayoutObservationIds: [layout.id],
    });
  }

  const unassigned = input.lines.filter((line) => !assigned.has(line.id));

  for (const line of unassigned) {
    blocks.push({
      id: `text_block_line_${line.id}`,
      lineIds: [line.id],
      wordIds: line.wordIds,
      text: line.text,
      bbox: line.bbox,
      confidence: line.confidence,
      sourceLayoutObservationIds: [],
    });
  }

  return blocks;
}

function joinWordsWithEstimatedSpaces(words: OcrWordForGrouping[]) {
  if (words.length === 0) return "";

  const parts = [words[0].text];

  for (let i = 1; i < words.length; i++) {
    const prev = words[i - 1];
    const current = words[i];

    const gap = current.bbox.x - (prev.bbox.x + prev.bbox.width);
    const avgCharWidth =
      prev.bbox.width / Math.max(1, prev.text.length);

    parts.push(gap > avgCharWidth * 0.6 ? " " : "");
    parts.push(current.text);
  }

  return parts.join("");
}

function centerY(bbox: BBox) {
  return bbox.y + bbox.height / 2;
}

function unionBBoxes(boxes: BBox[]): BBox {
  const x1 = Math.min(...boxes.map((b) => b.x));
  const y1 = Math.min(...boxes.map((b) => b.y));
  const x2 = Math.max(...boxes.map((b) => b.x + b.width));
  const y2 = Math.max(...boxes.map((b) => b.y + b.height));

  return {
    x: x1,
    y: y1,
    width: x2 - x1,
    height: y2 - y1,
  };
}
```

This grouping is intentionally simple. More advanced typography reconstruction can later use baseline fitting, rotated boxes, character-level grouping, and learned text de-rendering.

# 10.10 Fallback crop generation

Every text candidate needs a raster fallback crop.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/text-recovery/create-text-fallback-crop.ts
```

```ts
import sharp from "sharp";

import type {
  BBox,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import {
  MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY,
} from "./text-recovery-policy";

export async function createTextFallbackCrop(input: {
  normalizedImageBuffer: Buffer;
  bbox: BBox;
  canvasWidth: number;
  canvasHeight: number;
}): Promise<{
  cropBuffer: Buffer;
  cropBBox: BBox;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}> {
  const padding = Math.max(
    MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.crop.minPaddingPx,
    Math.min(
      MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.crop.maxPaddingPx,
      Math.round(
        Math.max(input.bbox.width, input.bbox.height) *
          MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.crop.paddingRatio
      )
    )
  );

  const cropBBox = {
    x: Math.max(0, input.bbox.x - padding),
    y: Math.max(0, input.bbox.y - padding),
    width: Math.min(
      input.canvasWidth - Math.max(0, input.bbox.x - padding),
      input.bbox.width + padding * 2
    ),
    height: Math.min(
      input.canvasHeight - Math.max(0, input.bbox.y - padding),
      input.bbox.height + padding * 2
    ),
  };

  const {
    data,
    info,
  } = await sharp(input.normalizedImageBuffer, {
    failOn: "warning",
  })
    .extract({
      left: cropBBox.x,
      top: cropBBox.y,
      width: cropBBox.width,
      height: cropBBox.height,
    })
    .png({
      compressionLevel: 9,
      adaptiveFiltering: true,
    })
    .toBuffer({
      resolveWithObject: true,
    });

  return {
    cropBuffer: data,
    cropBBox,
    width: info.width,
    height: info.height,
  };
}
```

This fallback crop is what protects the product when font matching, OCR, or style recovery is weak.

# 10.11 Text style estimation

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/text-recovery/estimate-text-style.ts
```

```ts
import sharp from "sharp";

import type {
  BBox,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

import {
  MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY,
} from "./text-recovery-policy";

export type EstimatedTextStyle = {
  fontFamilyGuess: string;
  fontFallback: string;

  fontCandidates: {
    family: string;
    confidence: number;
    source: "heuristic" | "font_catalog";
  }[];

  fontSizePx: number;

  fontWeight: string | number;

  fontStyle: "normal" | "italic";

  lineHeight: number;

  letterSpacingPx: number;

  fill: string;

  stroke?: string;
  strokeWidth?: number;

  shadow?: {
    color?: string;
    offsetX?: number;
    offsetY?: number;
    blur?: number;
  };

  textAlign: "left" | "center" | "right" | "justify";

  angle: number;

  confidence: {
    font: number;
    color: number;
    style: number;
  };
};

export async function estimateTextStyle(input: {
  cropBuffer: Buffer;
  candidateText: string;
  candidateBBox: BBox;
  lineCount: number;
}): Promise<EstimatedTextStyle> {
  const stats = await sharp(input.cropBuffer)
    .ensureAlpha()
    .stats();

  /**
   * Approximation:
   * For poster text, dominant non-background contrast color often approximates fill.
   * Later versions should use a text mask or alpha matte.
   */
  const fill = stats.dominant
    ? rgbToHex(
        stats.dominant.r,
        stats.dominant.g,
        stats.dominant.b
      )
    : "#000000";

  const fontSizePx = clamp(
    Math.round(
      input.candidateBBox.height /
        Math.max(1, input.lineCount) *
        0.78
    ),
    MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.style.minFontSizePx,
    MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.style.maxFontSizePx
  );

  const estimatedWeight = estimateFontWeightFromTextAndSize({
    text: input.candidateText,
    bbox: input.candidateBBox,
  });

  const family = chooseDefaultFontFamily(input.candidateText);

  return {
    fontFamilyGuess: family,
    fontFallback:
      MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.style.defaultFontFallback,

    fontCandidates: [
      {
        family,
        confidence: 0.42,
        source: "heuristic",
      },
      {
        family:
          MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.style.defaultFontFamily,
        confidence: 0.35,
        source: "font_catalog",
      },
    ],

    fontSizePx,

    fontWeight: estimatedWeight,

    fontStyle: "normal",

    lineHeight: 1.1,

    letterSpacingPx: 0,

    fill,

    textAlign: "left",

    angle: 0,

    confidence: {
      font: 0.4,
      color: 0.65,
      style: 0.48,
    },
  };
}

function chooseDefaultFontFamily(text: string) {
  const upperRatio =
    text.replace(/[^A-Z]/g, "").length /
    Math.max(1, text.replace(/[^A-Za-z]/g, "").length);

  if (upperRatio > 0.7) return "Montserrat";

  return MAGIC_LAYERS_TEXT_RECOVERY_POLICY.style.defaultFontFamily;
}

function estimateFontWeightFromTextAndSize(input: {
  text: string;
  bbox: BBox;
}) {
  const upperRatio =
    input.text.replace(/[^A-Z]/g, "").length /
    Math.max(1, input.text.replace(/[^A-Za-z]/g, "").length);

  if (upperRatio > 0.7 && input.bbox.height > 40) {
    return 700;
  }

  return 400;
}

function rgbToHex(r: number, g: number, b: number) {
  return `#${[r, g, b]
    .map((v) => Math.round(v).toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("")}`;
}

function clamp(value: number, min: number, max: number) {
  return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, value));
}
```

This first implementation is heuristic. The architecture leaves room for a real font classifier later.

For font availability, use a controlled font catalog. Google Fonts’ Developer API exposes metadata for font families, variants, subsets, axes, and files; cache that metadata server-side and only output font families you can actually render/export. citeturn951516view0

Font identification from images is possible but should be treated as approximate. DeepFont reports top-5 font identification above 80% on its dataset and produces similar-font suggestions, which is useful evidence but still not a guarantee of exact original font recovery. citeturn951516view1

# 10.12 Text safety normalization

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/text-recovery/text-safety.ts
```

```ts
export function normalizeTextForSafety(value: string): string {
  return value
    .normalize("NFKC")
    .replace(/[“”]/g, '"')
    .replace(/[‘’]/g, "'")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim();
}

export function levenshteinDistance(a: string, b: string): number {
  const dp = Array.from({ length: a.length + 1 }, () =>
    Array<number>(b.length + 1).fill(0)
  );

  for (let i = 0; i <= a.length; i++) dp[i][0] = i;
  for (let j = 0; j <= b.length; j++) dp[0][j] = j;

  for (let i = 1; i <= a.length; i++) {
    for (let j = 1; j <= b.length; j++) {
      const cost = a[i - 1] === b[j - 1] ? 0 : 1;

      dp[i][j] = Math.min(
        dp[i - 1][j] + 1,
        dp[i][j - 1] + 1,
        dp[i - 1][j - 1] + cost
      );
    }
  }

  return dp[a.length][b.length];
}

export function computeEditDistanceRatio(input: {
  original: string;
  candidate: string;
}) {
  const original = normalizeTextForSafety(input.original);
  const candidate = normalizeTextForSafety(input.candidate);

  const distance = levenshteinDistance(original, candidate);

  return distance / Math.max(1, original.length);
}

export function detectSemanticTextMutation(input: {
  originalOcrText: string;
  candidateText: string;
}) {
  const original = normalizeTextForSafety(input.originalOcrText);
  const candidate = normalizeTextForSafety(input.candidateText);

  if (original === candidate) {
    return false;
  }

  const ratio = computeEditDistanceRatio({
    original,
    candidate,
  });

  /**
   * Any meaningful substitution blocks automatic live text.
   * Scene resolver can still expose "convert to editable text" manually.
   */
  return ratio > 0.02;
}
```

No Gemini call should be allowed to “improve” this text. Gemini may classify layout or help choose among OCR alternatives later, but it must not rewrite visible content.

# 10.13 Render validation

Render validation answers:

```txt
If we render this candidate as editable text, does it visually cover the original text well enough?
```

Use a `TextRenderer` interface so you can later swap the renderer:

```txt
initial: SVG rendered through sharp
better: @napi-rs/canvas / Skia with registered fonts
best: same server renderer used for exports
```

Create:

```ts
  EstimatedTextStyle,
} from "./estimate-text-style";

export type RenderTextCandidateInput = {
  text: string;

  width: number;
  height: number;

  style: EstimatedTextStyle;
};

export type RenderTextCandidateResult = {
```

SVG renderer:

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/text-recovery/svg-text-candidate-renderer.ts

import sharp from "sharp";
import type {
  TextCandidateRenderer,
} from "./text-renderer.types";

export const svgTextCandidateRenderer: TextCandidateRenderer = {
  name: "sharp_svg_text_renderer",

  async render(input) {
    const escapedText = escapeXml(input.text);

    const lines = escapedText.split("\n");

    const lineHeight =
      input.style.fontSizePx *
      (input.style.lineHeight ?? 1.1);

    const svgTextLines = lines
      .map((line, index) => {
        const y =
          input.style.fontSizePx + index * lineHeight;

        return `<tspan x="0" y="${y}">${line}</tspan>`;
      })
      .join("");

    const svg = `
      <svg width="${input.width}" height="${input.height}"
           xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
        <text
          x="0"
          y="0"
          font-family="${escapeXml(input.style.fontFamilyGuess)}"
          font-size="${input.style.fontSizePx}"
          font-weight="${input.style.fontWeight ?? 400}"
          fill="${input.style.fill}"
          letter-spacing="${input.style.letterSpacingPx ?? 0}">
          ${svgTextLines}
        </text>
      </svg>
    `;

    const pngBuffer = await sharp(Buffer.from(svg))
      .png()
      .toBuffer();

    return {
      pngBuffer,
      width: input.width,
      height: input.height,
    };
  },
};

function escapeXml(value: string) {
  return value
    .replace(/&/g, "&amp;")
    .replace(/</g, "&lt;")
    .replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
    .replace(/"/g, "&quot;");
}
```

This renderer is acceptable for first-pass validation, not for final quality guarantees. The scene resolver should still be conservative.

# 10.14 Pixel comparison

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/text-recovery/validate-text-render.ts
```

```ts
import sharp from "sharp";

export type TextRenderValidationMetrics = {
  rgbL1: number;
  maskIoU: number;
};

export async function validateRenderedTextAgainstCrop(input: {
  originalCropBuffer: Buffer;
  renderedCandidateBuffer: Buffer;
}): Promise<TextRenderValidationMetrics> {
  const original = await sharp(input.originalCropBuffer)
    .ensureAlpha()
    .raw()
    .toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

  const rendered = await sharp(input.renderedCandidateBuffer)
    .resize(original.info.width, original.info.height, {
      fit: "fill",
    })
    .ensureAlpha()
    .raw()
    .toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

  let rgbDiff = 0;
  let rgbCount = 0;

  let maskIntersection = 0;
  let maskUnion = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < original.data.length; i += 4) {
    const oa = original.data[i + 3];
    const ra = rendered.data[i + 3];

    const originalTextLike = isNonBackgroundPixel(
      original.data[i],
      original.data[i + 1],
      original.data[i + 2],
      oa
    );

    const renderedTextLike = ra > 16;

    if (originalTextLike && renderedTextLike) {
      maskIntersection++;
    }

    if (originalTextLike || renderedTextLike) {
      maskUnion++;
    }

    if (renderedTextLike || originalTextLike) {
      rgbDiff +=
        Math.abs(original.data[i] - rendered.data[i]) / 255 +
        Math.abs(original.data[i + 1] - rendered.data[i + 1]) / 255 +
        Math.abs(original.data[i + 2] - rendered.data[i + 2]) / 255;

      rgbCount += 3;
    }
  }

  return {
    rgbL1: rgbCount > 0 ? rgbDiff / rgbCount : 1,
    maskIoU: maskUnion > 0 ? maskIntersection / maskUnion : 0,
  };
}

/**
 * Conservative approximation.
 * Later replace with text mask from decomposition/OCR crop.
 */
function isNonBackgroundPixel(
  r: number,
  g: number,
  b: number,
  a: number
) {
  if (a < 16) return false;

  const luminance = 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b;

  return luminance < 245;
}
```

This is imperfect because it lacks a true text mask. It is still useful as a gate. Better Step 10 versions should generate a text mask using OCR polygons, connected components inside text regions, or a text segmentation model.
