# 21.23 What Step 21 must not do

Do not:

```txt
write autosave snapshots
mutate AiReconstructionDocument
call AI repair
restore fallback directly
regenerate background
regenerate layer
create Fabric.Group by default
store panel expansion state in Firestore
write signed URLs
change reconstruction confidence
mark job ready/failed
```

The panel controls the current editor runtime. It does not revise the reconstruction truth.

# 21.24 Definition of done

Step 21 is complete when:

```txt
Layer panel renders from runtime manifest + Fabric canvas.

Rows show layer name, type, editable level, confidence, fallback, warnings.

Panel display order is front-to-back.

Canvas stack order remains bottom-to-top.

Selecting a row selects the Fabric object.

Selecting on canvas highlights the row.

Visibility toggle works.

Lock toggle works.

Rename works locally.

Delete works locally.

Duplicate works locally.

Bring to front / send to back works.

Locked reference remains bottom-most.

Logical groups display without Fabric.Group.

Group row selection creates ActiveSelection, not Fabric.Group.

Dirty state is set for real edits only.

No autosave happens yet.

No reconstruction document mutation happens.
```

Locked Step 21 architecture:

```txt
AiFabricRuntimeManifest
+ Fabric canvas runtime
→ derived LayerPanelModel
→ user commands
→ Fabric object mutations
→ local dirty state
```

Step 22 defines controlled runtime editing in Fabric: users can mutate objects, but AI identity, provenance, lock rules, and autosave compatibility must survive every edit.

# Step 22 — Editor editing behavior and AI metadata preservation

Step 22 defines how users edit the generated Fabric scene **without corrupting AI identity, provenance, fallbacks, or future autosave**.

The locked rule:

```txt
Editor edits mutate Fabric runtime objects.
They do not mutate AiReconstructionDocument.
They do not regenerate Fabric manifests.
They do not call AI repair.
```

This step is the runtime editing guardrail layer.

Fabric events are useful for listening to changes, but Fabric’s own docs warn not to treat events as your app’s main message system. So editor actions should go through explicit commands first; Fabric events should be used for synchronization, dirty-state detection, and safety checks. citeturn633441view0

---

# 22.1 What Step 22 owns

Step 22 owns:

```txt
editing command boundary
AI metadata preservation
runtime object invariants
manual object identity
duplicate object identity
object lock enforcement
transform normalization
selection/edit event capture
local dirty event queue
safe Fabric serialization support
editor runtime validation
```

Step 22 does **not** own:

```txt
autosave writes
Firestore versioning
repair loops
fallback restoration execution
AI regeneration
export
visual validation
canonical reconstruction mutation
```

Step 23 will persist edits. Step 25 will handle repair/fallback workflows.

---

# 22.2 Core rule

Every Fabric object must be one of:

```txt
1. reconstruction_layer
   Came from AiReconstructionDocument.

2. duplicate
   User duplicated an AI-generated object.

3. manual_object
   User created/imported something manually in the editor.
```

These states must be explicit.

Never allow an anonymous Fabric object to exist in the canvas.

Wrong:

```ts
canvas.add(new fabric.Rect(...));
```

Correct:

```ts
const rect = new Rect(...);
attachManualObjectAiMetadata(rect);
canvas.add(rect);
```

---

# 22.3 Critical Fabric facts

Fabric custom properties must be declared and registered for serialization. Fabric’s docs show that custom properties need TypeScript declarations and must be passed through `toObject`; otherwise they can disappear during save/load. citeturn633441view1

Fabric’s `type` is for serialization/deserialization and Fabric class identity; Fabric explicitly says not to use it to drive application logic. Use your AI metadata fields instead. citeturn633441view2

Fabric object flags such as `selectable`, `evented`, `hasControls`, `lockMovementX`, `lockMovementY`, `lockRotation`, and `visible` are the correct runtime controls for lock/visibility behavior. citeturn633441view3

```ts
// src/lib/magic-layers/fabric-generator/register-ai-fabric-properties.ts

import { FabricObject } from "fabric";

import type {
  AiConfidence,
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiSource,
  AiLayerType,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

export const AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES = [
  "id",
  "name",

  "aiLayerId",
  "aiParentLayerId",
  "aiLayerType",
  "aiEditableLevel",
  "aiConfidence",
  "aiSource",
  "aiFallbackAssetId",
  "aiSourceAssetId",
  "aiSchemaVersion",

  "aiRuntimeKind",
  "aiCreatedByEditor",
  "aiDirty",
] as const;

export type AiFabricRuntimeKind =
  | "reconstruction_layer"
  | "duplicate"
  | "manual_object";

declare module "fabric" {
  interface FabricObject {
    id?: string;
    name?: string;

    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiParentLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSourceAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;

    aiRuntimeKind?: AiFabricRuntimeKind;
    aiCreatedByEditor?: boolean;
    aiDirty?: boolean;
  }

  interface SerializedObjectProps {
    id?: string;
    name?: string;

    aiLayerId?: string;
    aiParentLayerId?: string;
    aiLayerType?: AiLayerType;
    aiEditableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
    aiConfidence?: AiConfidence;
    aiSource?: AiSource;
    aiFallbackAssetId?: string;
    aiSourceAssetId?: string;
    aiSchemaVersion?: string;

    aiRuntimeKind?: AiFabricRuntimeKind;
    aiCreatedByEditor?: boolean;
    aiDirty?: boolean;
  }
}

export function registerAiFabricCustomProperties() {
  const existing = FabricObject.customProperties ?? [];

  FabricObject.customProperties = Array.from(
    new Set([...existing, ...AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES])
  );
}
```

One correction from Step 18: use `AiSource`, not `AiLayerSource`, unless your Step 1 schema explicitly defines `AiLayerSource`.

```ts
  | "text_changed"
  | "style_changed"
  | "metadata_repaired";

export type MagicFabricObjectSnapshot = {
  layerId: string;

  parentLayerId?: string;

  runtimeKind:
    | "reconstruction_layer"
    | "duplicate"
    | "manual_object";

  editableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;
```

# 22.7 Object snapshot helper

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/fabric-object-snapshot.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
  FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  MagicFabricObjectSnapshot,
} from "./editor-behavior.types";

export function snapshotFabricObject(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;
  object: FabricObject;
}): MagicFabricObjectSnapshot | undefined {
  const { canvas, object } = input;

  if (!object.aiLayerId) return undefined;

  const stackIndex = canvas.getObjects().indexOf(object);

  return {
    layerId: object.aiLayerId,

    parentLayerId: object.aiParentLayerId,

    runtimeKind: object.aiRuntimeKind ?? "reconstruction_layer",

    layerType: object.aiLayerType,

    editableLevel: object.aiEditableLevel,

    name: object.name,

    visible: object.visible,

    locked: isFabricObjectLocked(object),

    left: object.left,
    top: object.top,

    width: object.width,
    height: object.height,

    scaleX: object.scaleX,
    scaleY: object.scaleY,

    angle: object.angle,
    opacity: object.opacity,

    fill: (object as any).fill,
    stroke: (object as any).stroke,
    strokeWidth: (object as any).strokeWidth,

    text: (object as any).text,

    src: (object as any).src,

    stackIndex,
  };
}

export function isFabricObjectLocked(object: FabricObject) {
  return Boolean(
    object.lockMovementX &&
      object.lockMovementY &&
      object.lockScalingX &&
      object.lockScalingY &&
      object.lockRotation
  );
}
```

# 22.8 AI metadata preservation helper

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/ai-fabric-runtime-metadata.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

import {
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "../schema/constants";

import type {
  AiEditableLevel,
  AiLayerType,
} from "../schema/reconstruction.types";

export function isAiFabricObject(
  object: FabricObject
): boolean {
  return Boolean(object.aiLayerId);
}

export function attachManualObjectAiMetadata(input: {
  object: FabricObject;

  layerType?: AiLayerType;

  editableLevel?: AiEditableLevel;

  name?: string;
}) {
  const layerId = createManualLayerId();

  input.object.set({
    id: layerId,

    name:
      input.name ??
      input.object.name ??
      "Manual layer",

    aiLayerId: layerId,

    aiLayerType: input.layerType ?? "unknown",

    aiEditableLevel: input.editableLevel ?? "unknown_confidence",

    aiConfidence: {
      overall: 1,
    },

    aiSource: "manual_user",

    aiSchemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,

    aiRuntimeKind: "manual_object",

    aiCreatedByEditor: true,

    aiDirty: true,
  });
}

export function attachDuplicateObjectAiMetadata(input: {
  object: FabricObject;

  sourceObject: FabricObject;
}) {
  const layerId = createDuplicateLayerId(
    input.sourceObject.aiLayerId ?? "unknown"
  );

  input.object.set({
    id: layerId,

    name: `${input.sourceObject.name ?? "Layer"} copy`,

    aiLayerId: layerId,

    aiParentLayerId: input.sourceObject.aiLayerId,

    aiLayerType: input.sourceObject.aiLayerType,

    aiEditableLevel: input.sourceObject.aiEditableLevel,

    aiConfidence: input.sourceObject.aiConfidence,

    aiSource: "manual_user",

    aiFallbackAssetId: input.sourceObject.aiFallbackAssetId,

    aiSourceAssetId: input.sourceObject.aiSourceAssetId,

    aiSchemaVersion: input.sourceObject.aiSchemaVersion,

    aiRuntimeKind: "duplicate",

    aiCreatedByEditor: true,

    aiDirty: true,
  });
}

export function repairMissingAiMetadata(input: {
  object: FabricObject;
}) {
  if (input.object.aiLayerId) return false;

  attachManualObjectAiMetadata({
    object: input.object,
  });

  return true;
}

function createManualLayerId() {
  return `manual_layer_${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
}

function createDuplicateLayerId(parentLayerId: string) {
  return `duplicate_layer_${parentLayerId}_${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
}
```

Manual objects and duplicates become editor-runtime objects. They are not automatically added to `AiReconstructionDocument`.

# 22.9 Lock policy

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/apply-runtime-lock-policy.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
  FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

export function applyRuntimeLockPolicy(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;
}) {
  for (const object of input.canvas.getObjects()) {
    if (object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
      lockFabricObject(object);
      object.set({
        visible: object.visible ?? false,
        selectable: false,
        evented: false,
      });
    }
  }

  keepLockedReferenceAtBack(input.canvas);
}

export function lockFabricObject(object: FabricObject) {
  object.set({
    selectable: false,
    evented: false,

    hasControls: false,
    hasBorders: false,

    lockMovementX: true,
    lockMovementY: true,

    lockScalingX: true,
    lockScalingY: true,

    lockRotation: true,
  });

  object.setCoords();
}

export function unlockFabricObject(object: FabricObject) {
  if (object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
    return;
  }

  object.set({
    selectable: true,
    evented: true,

    hasControls: true,
    hasBorders: true,

    lockMovementX: false,
    lockMovementY: false,

    lockScalingX: false,
    lockScalingY: false,

    lockRotation: false,
  });

  object.setCoords();
}

export function keepLockedReferenceAtBack(canvas: Canvas) {
  const reference = canvas
    .getObjects()
    .find((object) => object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference");

  if (!reference) return;

  canvas.sendObjectToBack(reference);
}
```

The locked reference layer must never drift above editable layers.

# 22.10 Normalize object after edit

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/normalize-object-after-edit.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

import {
  MAGIC_LAYERS_EDITOR_BEHAVIOR_POLICY,
} from "./editor-behavior-policy";

export function normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(
  object: FabricObject
) {
  object.set({
    scaleX: clamp(
      object.scaleX ?? 1,
      MAGIC_LAYERS_EDITOR_BEHAVIOR_POLICY.transforms.minScale,
      MAGIC_LAYERS_EDITOR_BEHAVIOR_POLICY.transforms.maxScale
    ),

    scaleY: clamp(
      object.scaleY ?? 1,
      MAGIC_LAYERS_EDITOR_BEHAVIOR_POLICY.transforms.minScale,
      MAGIC_LAYERS_EDITOR_BEHAVIOR_POLICY.transforms.maxScale
    ),

    opacity: clamp01(object.opacity ?? 1),

    aiDirty: true,
  });

  if (
    MAGIC_LAYERS_EDITOR_BEHAVIOR_POLICY.transforms
      .callSetCoordsAfterMutation
  ) {
    object.setCoords();
  }
}

function clamp(value: number, min: number, max: number) {
  return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, value));
}

function clamp01(value: number) {
  return clamp(value, 0, 1);
}
```

This protects against invalid scale/opacity values and keeps Fabric controls in sync after mutations.

# 22.11 Runtime invariant checker

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/assert-editor-runtime-invariants.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  AiFabricRuntimeManifest,
} from "../fabric-generator/fabric-generator.types";

export function assertEditorRuntimeInvariants(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;
  manifest: AiFabricRuntimeManifest;
}) {
  const objects = input.canvas.getObjects();

  const layerIds = new Set<string>();

  let lockedReferenceCount = 0;

  for (const [index, object] of objects.entries()) {
    if (!object.aiLayerId) {
      throw new Error(
        `Fabric object at index ${index} is missing aiLayerId`
      );
    }

    if (layerIds.has(object.aiLayerId)) {
      throw new Error(
        `Duplicate aiLayerId in Fabric canvas: ${object.aiLayerId}`
      );
    }

    layerIds.add(object.aiLayerId);

    if (object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
      lockedReferenceCount++;

      if (index !== 0) {
        throw new Error("locked_reference must be bottom-most Fabric object");
      }

      if (
        object.selectable !== false ||
        object.evented !== false ||
        object.lockMovementX !== true ||
        object.lockMovementY !== true ||
        object.lockScalingX !== true ||
        object.lockScalingY !== true ||
        object.lockRotation !== true
      ) {
        throw new Error("locked_reference object is not fully locked");
      }
    }
  }

  if (lockedReferenceCount !== 1) {
    throw new Error(
      `Expected exactly one locked_reference object, found ${lockedReferenceCount}`
    );
  }

  for (const [layerId, entry] of Object.entries(input.manifest.layerIndex)) {
    const object = objects[entry.objectIndex];

    if (!object) {
      /**
       * This can happen after user deletion.
       * It is not fatal for runtime editing, but it must not happen immediately after load.
       */
      continue;
    }

    if (object.aiLayerId !== layerId) {
      throw new Error(
        `Layer index mismatch: ${layerId} points to ${object.aiLayerId}`
      );
    }
  }
}
```

Run this immediately after loading a runtime manifest and again before autosave in Step 23.

# 22.12 Bind Fabric editor behavior

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/bind-magic-layer-editor-behavior.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
  FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  AiFabricRuntimeManifest,
} from "../fabric-generator/fabric-generator.types";

import type {
  MagicEditorBehaviorBindings,
  MagicEditorEditEvent,
  MagicEditorRuntimeState,
} from "./editor-behavior.types";

import {
  snapshotFabricObject,
} from "./fabric-object-snapshot";

import {
  repairMissingAiMetadata,
} from "./ai-fabric-runtime-metadata";

import {
  applyRuntimeLockPolicy,
  keepLockedReferenceAtBack,
} from "./apply-runtime-lock-policy";

import {
  normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit,
} from "./normalize-object-after-edit";

import {
  assertEditorRuntimeInvariants,
} from "./assert-editor-runtime-invariants";

export function bindMagicLayerEditorBehavior(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;

  manifest: AiFabricRuntimeManifest;

  isLoading?: boolean;

  onDirty?: () => void;

  onEditEvent?: (event: MagicEditorEditEvent) => void;

  onRuntimeInvariantError?: (error: Error) => void;
}): MagicEditorBehaviorBindings {
  const state: MagicEditorRuntimeState = {
    isLoading: input.isLoading ?? false,

    isApplyingCommand: false,

    dirty: false,

    editEvents: [],

    lastSnapshotByLayerId: new Map(),
  };

  applyRuntimeLockPolicy({
    canvas: input.canvas,
  });

  for (const object of input.canvas.getObjects()) {
    const snapshot = snapshotFabricObject({
      canvas: input.canvas,
      object,
    });

    if (snapshot) {
      state.lastSnapshotByLayerId.set(snapshot.layerId, snapshot);
    }
  }

  try {
    assertEditorRuntimeInvariants({
      canvas: input.canvas,
      manifest: input.manifest,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    input.onRuntimeInvariantError?.(error as Error);
  }

  const handleObjectAdded = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target) return;

    const repaired = repairMissingAiMetadata({
      object: event.target,
    });

    event.target.setCoords();

    if (state.isLoading) return;

    emitEditEvent({
      type: repaired ? "metadata_repaired" : "object_added",
      object: event.target,
      source: repaired ? "system" : "user",
      state,
      canvas: input.canvas,
      onDirty: input.onDirty,
      onEditEvent: input.onEditEvent,
    });
  };

  const handleObjectRemoved = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target?.aiLayerId) return;

    if (state.isLoading) return;

    const before =
      state.lastSnapshotByLayerId.get(event.target.aiLayerId);

    const editEvent: MagicEditorEditEvent = {
      id: createEditEventId(),
      type: "object_removed",
      layerId: event.target.aiLayerId,
      at: Date.now(),
      source: "user",
      before,
      coalescingKey: `remove:${event.target.aiLayerId}`,
    };

    state.editEvents.push(editEvent);
    state.dirty = true;

    input.onDirty?.();
    input.onEditEvent?.(editEvent);

    state.lastSnapshotByLayerId.delete(event.target.aiLayerId);
  };

  const handleObjectModified = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target) return;

    normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(event.target);

    keepLockedReferenceAtBack(input.canvas);

    emitEditEvent({
      type: "object_modified",
      object: event.target,
      source: "user",
      state,
      canvas: input.canvas,
      onDirty: input.onDirty,
      onEditEvent: input.onEditEvent,
    });
  };

  const handleObjectMoving = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target) return;

    if (event.target.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
      event.target.set({
        left: 0,
        top: 0,
      });
    }
  };

  const handleObjectScaling = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target) return;

    if (event.target.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
      event.target.set({
        scaleX: 1,
        scaleY: 1,
      });
    }
  };

  const handleObjectRotating = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target) return;

    if (event.target.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
      event.target.set({
        angle: 0,
      });
    }
  };

  const handleTextChanged = (event: { target?: FabricObject }) => {
    if (!event.target) return;

    if (event.target.aiEditableLevel !== "text_editable") return;

    normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(event.target);

    emitEditEvent({
      type: "text_changed",
      object: event.target,
      source: "user",
      state,
      canvas: input.canvas,
      onDirty: input.onDirty,
      onEditEvent: input.onEditEvent,
    });
  };

  input.canvas.on("object:added", handleObjectAdded);
  input.canvas.on("object:removed", handleObjectRemoved);
  input.canvas.on("object:modified", handleObjectModified);
  input.canvas.on("object:moving", handleObjectMoving);
  input.canvas.on("object:scaling", handleObjectScaling);
  input.canvas.on("object:rotating", handleObjectRotating);
  input.canvas.on("text:changed", handleTextChanged);

  return {
    dispose() {
      input.canvas.off("object:added", handleObjectAdded);
      input.canvas.off("object:removed", handleObjectRemoved);
      input.canvas.off("object:modified", handleObjectModified);
      input.canvas.off("object:moving", handleObjectMoving);
      input.canvas.off("object:scaling", handleObjectScaling);
      input.canvas.off("object:rotating", handleObjectRotating);
      input.canvas.off("text:changed", handleTextChanged);
    },

    getState() {
      return state;
    },

    clearEvents() {
      state.editEvents = [];
      state.dirty = false;
    },
  };
}

function emitEditEvent(input: {
  type: MagicEditorEditEvent["type"];

  object: FabricObject;

  source: MagicEditorEditEvent["source"];

  state: MagicEditorRuntimeState;

  canvas: Canvas;

  onDirty?: () => void;

  onEditEvent?: (event: MagicEditorEditEvent) => void;
}) {
  if (!input.object.aiLayerId) return;

  const before =
    input.state.lastSnapshotByLayerId.get(input.object.aiLayerId);

  const after = snapshotFabricObject({
    canvas: input.canvas,
    object: input.object,
  });

  if (!after) return;

  const event: MagicEditorEditEvent = {
    id: createEditEventId(),
    type: input.type,
    layerId: input.object.aiLayerId,
    at: Date.now(),
    source: input.source,
    before,
    after,
    coalescingKey: `${input.type}:${input.object.aiLayerId}`,
  };

  input.state.lastSnapshotByLayerId.set(
    input.object.aiLayerId,
    after
  );

  input.state.editEvents.push(event);
  input.state.dirty = true;

  input.onDirty?.();
  input.onEditEvent?.(event);
}

function createEditEventId() {
  return `edit_${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
}
```

Important boundary:

```txt
This captures local edit events.
It does not write them anywhere.
```

Step 23 consumes these events for autosave/versioning.

# 22.13 Duplicate object safely

Patch Step 21 duplicate behavior to use Step 22 metadata helper.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/duplicate-fabric-object-preserving-ai.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
  FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

import {
  AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES,
} from "../fabric-generator/register-ai-fabric-properties";

import {
  attachDuplicateObjectAiMetadata,
} from "./ai-fabric-runtime-metadata";

export async function duplicateFabricObjectPreservingAi(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;

  object: FabricObject;
}) {
  if (input.object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
    return undefined;
  }

  const cloned = await input.object.clone([
    ...AI_FABRIC_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES,
  ]);

  attachDuplicateObjectAiMetadata({
    object: cloned,
    sourceObject: input.object,
  });

  cloned.set({
    left: (input.object.left ?? 0) + 16,
    top: (input.object.top ?? 0) + 16,
  });

  cloned.setCoords();

  input.canvas.add(cloned);
  input.canvas.setActiveObject(cloned);
  input.canvas.requestRenderAll();

  return cloned;
}
```

Duplicate must not reuse the original `aiLayerId`.


```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
} from "fabric";

export function assertAllFabricObjectsHaveAiIdentity(
  canvas: Canvas
) {
  for (const [index, object] of canvas.getObjects().entries()) {
    if (!object.aiLayerId) {
      throw new Error(
        `Cannot save Fabric runtime: object at index ${index} is missing aiLayerId`
      );
    }

    if (!object.aiEditableLevel) {
      throw new Error(
        `Cannot save Fabric runtime: object ${object.aiLayerId} is missing aiEditableLevel`
      );
    }

    if (!object.aiRuntimeKind) {
      throw new Error(
        `Cannot save Fabric runtime: object ${object.aiLayerId} is missing aiRuntimeKind`
      );
    }
  }
}
```


```ts
  | {
      type: "set_transform";
      layerId: string;

        left?: number;

      };
    }

      visible: boolean;
    }
  | {
```

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/editor-behavior/run-magic-editor-command.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  MagicEditorCommand,
} from "./magic-editor-command.types";

import {
  getFabricObjectByLayerId,
} from "../layer-panel/fabric-layer-lookup";

import {
  lockFabricObject,
  unlockFabricObject,
} from "./apply-runtime-lock-policy";

import {
  normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit,
} from "./normalize-object-after-edit";

export function runMagicEditorCommand(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;

  command: MagicEditorCommand;
}) {
  const object = getFabricObjectByLayerId({
    canvas: input.canvas,
    layerId: input.command.layerId,
  });

  if (!object) return;

  if (object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference") {
    return;
  }

  switch (input.command.type) {
    case "set_transform":
      object.set(input.command.transform);
      break;

    case "set_text":
      if (object.aiEditableLevel !== "text_editable") return;
      object.set({
        text: input.command.text,
        aiDirty: true,
      } as any);
      break;

    case "set_style":
      object.set({
        ...input.command.style,
        aiDirty: true,
      } as any);
      break;

    case "set_visibility":
      object.set({
        visible: input.command.visible,
        aiDirty: true,
      });
      break;

    case "set_locked":
      if (input.command.locked) {
        lockFabricObject(object);
      } else {
        unlockFabricObject(object);
      }
      object.set({
        aiDirty: true,
      });
      break;

    case "rename":
      object.set({
        name: input.command.name.trim(),
        aiDirty: true,
      });
      break;
  }

  normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(object);

  input.canvas.requestRenderAll();
}
```

This command boundary makes Step 23 autosave and Step 25 repair safer.

# 22.17 Text editing rule

When the user edits text:

```txt
Fabric object text changes.
aiLayerId stays the same.
aiEditableLevel stays text_editable.
aiDirty becomes true.
text safety status from reconstruction is no longer authoritative for user-edited text.
```

Do **not** mutate:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument.layers[].text.value
```

in Step 22.

The edited text becomes part of runtime Fabric JSON in Step 23.

Important state:

```txt
AI-generated text safety validated source text.
User-edited text is user-owned content.
```

So after user edits a text object:

```txt
show “edited” state
remove “AI unsafe” warning if it was user-corrected only in runtime
do not claim original reconstruction text safety anymore for that object
```

Actual persistence rules come in Step 23.

---

# 22.18 Vector editing rule

Vector edits should mutate Fabric primitive/path properties only.

Allowed:

```txt
fill
stroke
strokeWidth
opacity
transform
path point editing later
```

Not allowed in Step 22:

```txt
regenerate vector
re-vectorize raster
replace source SVG
claim validation still passed
```

After vector edit:

```txt
aiDirty = true
visual validation metrics from reconstruction are stale for this runtime object
```

Do not change the canonical vector candidate.

---

# 22.19 Raster editing rule

Raster edits allowed in Step 22:

```txt
move
scale
rotate
opacity
visibility
lock
crop UI hooks if your editor already supports crop
```

Not Step 22:

```txt
replace image asset
edit mask
restore fallback
regenerate matte
background repair
```

Those are Step 25-level repair/replacement flows because they create new assets and may need revalidation.

---

# 22.20 Group editing rule

Logical groups support:

```txt
select as group
multi-select children
move active selection
show group row
rename group locally
collapse/expand group row
```

Do not create `fabric.Group`.

Fabric has programmatic selection/group demos, but real Fabric groups affect selection, child targeting, transforms, and serialization behavior. Use `ActiveSelection` for temporary multi-selection; use metadata groups for layer panel structure. citeturn917833view0turn633441view3

---

# 22.21 Manual object rule

When users create new shapes/text/images manually:

```txt
aiRuntimeKind = manual_object
aiSource = manual_user
aiEditableLevel = unknown_confidence or matching tool type
aiConfidence.overall = 1
aiCreatedByEditor = true
aiDirty = true
```

Manual objects are not part of the AI reconstruction truth.

Later Step 23 stores them in Fabric runtime JSON.

A future “commit to design version” can promote them into a saved design version, but not back into the original reconstruction document.

---

# 22.22 Deleted object rule

When a user deletes an AI layer:

```txt
Fabric object is removed.
AiReconstructionDocument remains unchanged.
Layer panel no longer shows the object from runtime canvas.
Autosave later records the deletion in Fabric runtime JSON.
```

Do not remove the layer from:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument.layers
```

The reconstruction document is the original AI-generated snapshot.

---

# 22.23 Runtime metadata staleness

After user edits an object, these AI fields still identify provenance:

```txt
aiLayerId
aiParentLayerId
aiLayerType
aiEditableLevel
aiSourceAssetId
aiFallbackAssetId
aiSchemaVersion
```

But these fields may become stale as quality indicators:

```txt
aiConfidence
visualMatchScore
textSafetyLevel
vector validation
mask validation
```

So the UI should treat:

```txt
aiDirty = true
```

as meaning:

```txt
AI validation metrics describe the generated object before user edits.
```

That distinction protects trust.

---

# 22.24 Event coalescing rule

Step 22 can collect local edit events, but Step 23 owns saving.

Event coalescing should happen later like this:

```txt
many object:moving events
→ one transform delta

many text:changed events
→ one text delta after debounce

many style changes
→ one style delta
```

Step 22 only emits events with `coalescingKey`.

Do not write every Fabric event to Firestore.

After Step 18 runtime manifest load:

# Step 25 — Fallback restoration, repair loops, and targeted regeneration

Step 25 defines how the editor fixes unsafe or weak AI outputs **without corrupting the original reconstruction truth**.

The locked rule:

```txt
Repair creates new runtime state and/or new repair assets.
Repair does not silently rewrite the original AiReconstructionDocument.
Repair does not mutate the original AI reconstruction snapshot.
```

This is the step where users can do things like:

```txt
restore raster fallback for unsafe text
restore original crop
replace product image
regenerate clean background
rerun mask for one object
rerun vectorization for one shape
convert one raster text crop to editable text
```

Fabric image replacement can be done at runtime because `FabricImage.setSrc()` loads and sets a new image source, and Fabric recommends aborting previous loading tasks before calling it to prevent race conditions. citeturn765467view0 User replacement assets should be uploaded to Cloud Storage as files/blobs with explicit metadata; Firebase’s web SDK supports `uploadBytes()` from `Blob`/`File`, and Cloud Storage metadata controls fields such as `contentType`. citeturn451030view2 For generative repair, Gemini image editing can add/remove/modify image elements and supports semantic masking, but it must remain a guarded repair path because it can alter meaning. citeturn437366view2turn437366view1

---

## 25.1 What Step 25 owns

Step 25 owns:

```txt
fallback restoration
runtime repair patches
targeted repair requests
repair request Firestore docs
repair worker routing
repair asset generation
repair patch generation
repair result versioning
runtime canvas patch application
repair provenance
repair audit state
```

Step 25 does **not** own:

```txt
autosave core logic
full reconstruction pipeline
automatic scene mutation without user/system repair request
export
collaboration
original reconstruction overwrite
```

Step 23 persists repaired runtime state after patches are applied.

---

# 25.2 Repair categories

Use four repair classes.

```txt
local_runtime_repair
  no AI
  no server worker
  applies existing fallback/runtime asset to Fabric canvas

asset_replacement
  user uploads a new asset
  server stores it
  runtime object source is replaced

targeted_ai_repair
  server worker regenerates one target asset/candidate
  returns a runtime patch

full_reconstruction_retry
  reruns larger pipeline when targeted repair is insufficient
```

Day-one supported actions:

```txt
restore_fallback
downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback
replace_raster_asset
regenerate_clean_background
remask_raster_layer
revectorize_shape
convert_raster_text_to_editable
```

Do not start with arbitrary “AI fix this design.” That creates uncontrollable state.

---

# 25.3 Repair decision matrix

| Problem | Default repair |
|---|---|
| Unsafe editable text | `downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback` |
| Weak text font/style | `restore_fallback` or `convert_raster_text_to_editable` manually |
| Bad vector shape | `restore_fallback` or `revectorize_shape` |
| Bad product/person mask | `remask_raster_layer` |
| Bad clean background | `regenerate_clean_background` |
| User wants a new product/photo | `replace_raster_asset` |
| Many objects wrong | `full_reconstruction_retry` |
| Visual validation failed catastrophically | fallback-only or full reconstruction retry |

Strong rule:

```txt
If text safety failed, repair must not “trust” editable text.
First repair is raster fallback.
```

# 25.5 Repair patch asset

A repair result should be a **patch**, not a full silent overwrite.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/repair/repair.types.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  FabricObjectJson,
  FabricRuntimeJson,
} from "../fabric-generator/fabric-generator.types";

export const AI_REPAIR_PATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION =
  "ai-repair-patch.v1" as const;

export type MagicRepairPatchOp =
  | {
      op: "replace_image_src";
      layerId: string;
      assetId: string;
      width?: number;
      height?: number;
      preserveTransform: true;
      reason: string;
    }
  | {
      op: "replace_object";
      layerId: string;
      object: FabricObjectJson;
      reason: string;
    }
  | {
      op: "set_object_props";
      layerId: string;
      props: Record<string, unknown>;
      reason: string;
    }
  | {
      op: "remove_object";
      layerId: string;
      reason: string;
    }
  | {
      op: "add_object";
      object: FabricObjectJson;
      insertAboveLayerId?: string;
      insertBelowLayerId?: string;
      reason: string;
    }
  | {
      op: "mark_review_resolved";
      layerId: string;
      reason: string;
    };

export type MagicRepairPatch = {
  schemaVersion: typeof AI_REPAIR_PATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION;

  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  repairRequestId: string;

  baseRevision: number;

  repairType:
    | "restore_fallback"
    | "downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback"
    | "replace_raster_asset"
    | "regenerate_clean_background"
    | "remask_raster_layer"
    | "revectorize_shape"
    | "convert_raster_text_to_editable"
    | "full_reconstruction_retry";

  targetLayerId?: string;

  ops: MagicRepairPatchOp[];

  repairedAssetIds: string[];

  warnings: string[];

  createdAt: number;
};
```

Repair patches are applied to the **current Fabric runtime**, then Step 23 autosaves the resulting runtime snapshot.

```ts
  return joinPath([
    repairRequestRootPath(input),
    `${input.assetId}.repair-report.json`,
  ]);
}

export function repairedAssetPath(
  input: WorkspaceDesignPathInput & {
    repairRequestId: string;
    layerId: string;
    assetId: string;
    extension: "png" | "svg" | "json" | "webp";
  }
) {
  return joinPath([
    repairRequestRootPath(input),
    "assets",
    input.layerId,
    `${input.assetId}.${input.extension}`,
  ]);
}
```

Set explicit `Cache-Control` and `Content-Type` on every repair asset. Cloud Storage object metadata controls how objects are handled when accessed, including cache behavior. citeturn451030view3

---

# 25.9 Client-side fallback restoration

This is the fastest repair path.

It uses existing fallback assets from:

```txt
manifest.layerIndex[layerId].primaryFallbackAssetId
```

or:

```txt
layer.fallbacks[].assetId
```

## For image-like objects

Use `FabricImage.setSrc(...)`.

```txt
existing Fabric image object
→ hydrate fallback asset URL
→ setSrc(fallbackUrl)
→ update aiSourceAssetId
→ mark aiDirty
→ autosave later
```

## For text objects

Unsafe editable text needs a raster fallback object:

```txt
textbox object
→ remove textbox
→ insert FabricImage fallback crop at same transform
→ keep same aiLayerId
→ aiEditableLevel = raster_fallback
→ aiRuntimeKind = reconstruction_layer
→ mark aiDirty
```

This preserves layer panel identity while switching runtime representation.

```ts
export async function requestRuntimeAssetUrl(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  assetId: string;
  idToken: string;
  appCheckToken: string;
}) {
  const response = await fetch(
    `/api/workspaces/${input.workspaceId}/designs/${input.designId}/asset-runtime-url`,
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        Authorization: `Bearer ${input.idToken}`,
        "x-firebase-appcheck": input.appCheckToken,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        assetId: input.assetId,
      }),
    }
  );

  const body = await response.json();

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(body.error ?? "asset_url_failed");
  }

  return body as {
    url: string;
    urlExpiresAt: number;
  };
}
```

# 25.11 Apply fallback restoration in Fabric

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/repair/apply-fallback-restoration.ts
```

```ts
import {
  FabricImage,
  type Canvas,
  type FabricObject,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  AiFabricRuntimeManifest,
} from "../fabric-generator/fabric-generator.types";

import {
  getFabricObjectByLayerId,
} from "../layer-panel/fabric-layer-lookup";

import {
  normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit,
} from "../editor-behavior/normalize-object-after-edit";

export async function applyFallbackRestoration(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;

  manifest: AiFabricRuntimeManifest;

  layerId: string;

  fallbackAssetId?: string;

  resolveAssetUrl: (assetId: string) => Promise<{
    url: string;
    urlExpiresAt: number;
  }>;

  repairMode:
    | "restore_fallback"
    | "downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback";
}) {
  const object = getFabricObjectByLayerId({
    canvas: input.canvas,
    layerId: input.layerId,
  });

  if (!object) {
    throw new Error(`missing_fabric_object_${input.layerId}`);
  }

  const layerIndex = input.manifest.layerIndex[input.layerId];

  if (!layerIndex) {
    throw new Error(`missing_layer_index_${input.layerId}`);
  }

  const fallbackAssetId =
    input.fallbackAssetId ??
    layerIndex.primaryFallbackAssetId ??
    layerIndex.fallbackAssetIds[0];

  if (!fallbackAssetId) {
    throw new Error(`missing_fallback_asset_${input.layerId}`);
  }

  const resolved = await input.resolveAssetUrl(fallbackAssetId);

  const isImageObject =
    String(object.type).toLowerCase().includes("image");

  if (isImageObject && "setSrc" in object) {
    await (object as any).setSrc(resolved.url, {
      crossOrigin: "anonymous",
    });

    object.set({
      aiSourceAssetId: fallbackAssetId,
      aiFallbackAssetId: fallbackAssetId,
      aiDirty: true,
    });

    normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(object);
    input.canvas.requestRenderAll();

    return {
      layerId: input.layerId,
      fallbackAssetId,
      replacedObject: false,
    };
  }

  /**
   * Textbox/vector → raster fallback image replacement.
   */
  const replacement = await FabricImage.fromURL(
    resolved.url,
    {
      crossOrigin: "anonymous",
    }
  );

  copyPlacementAndAiIdentity({
    source: object,
    target: replacement,
    fallbackAssetId,
  });

  const index = input.canvas.getObjects().indexOf(object);

  input.canvas.remove(object);
  input.canvas.insertAt(index, replacement);
  input.canvas.setActiveObject(replacement);

  replacement.setCoords();

  input.canvas.requestRenderAll();

  return {
    layerId: input.layerId,
    fallbackAssetId,
    replacedObject: true,
  };
}

function copyPlacementAndAiIdentity(input: {
  source: FabricObject;
  target: FabricImage;
  fallbackAssetId: string;
}) {
  const source = input.source;

  input.target.set({
    id: source.id,
    name: source.name,

    left: source.left,
    top: source.top,

    width: source.width,
    height: source.height,

    scaleX: source.scaleX,
    scaleY: source.scaleY,

    angle: source.angle,
    opacity: source.opacity,

    originX: source.originX,
    originY: source.originY,

    visible: source.visible,

    selectable: source.selectable,
    evented: source.evented,

    aiLayerId: source.aiLayerId,
    aiParentLayerId: source.aiParentLayerId,

    aiLayerType: source.aiLayerType,

    aiEditableLevel: "raster_fallback",

    aiConfidence: {
      ...(source.aiConfidence ?? {}),
      overall: Math.max(0.7, source.aiConfidence?.overall ?? 0),
    },

    aiSource: "manual_user",

    aiFallbackAssetId: input.fallbackAssetId,
    aiSourceAssetId: input.fallbackAssetId,

    aiSchemaVersion: source.aiSchemaVersion,

    aiRuntimeKind: source.aiRuntimeKind ?? "reconstruction_layer",

    aiCreatedByEditor: false,
    aiDirty: true,

    crossOrigin: "anonymous",
  });
}
```

This is local runtime repair. Step 23 persists it.

# 25.12 Repair patch application

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/repair/apply-repair-patch-to-canvas.ts
```

```ts
import {
  FabricImage,
  type Canvas,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  MagicRepairPatch,
} from "./repair.types";

import {
  getFabricObjectByLayerId,
} from "../layer-panel/fabric-layer-lookup";

import {
  normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit,
} from "../editor-behavior/normalize-object-after-edit";

export async function applyRepairPatchToCanvas(input: {
  canvas: Canvas;

  patch: MagicRepairPatch;

  resolveAssetUrl: (assetId: string) => Promise<{
    url: string;
    urlExpiresAt: number;
  }>;
}) {
  for (const op of input.patch.ops) {
    switch (op.op) {
      case "replace_image_src": {
        const object = getFabricObjectByLayerId({
          canvas: input.canvas,
          layerId: op.layerId,
        });

        if (!object) {
          throw new Error(`patch_missing_object_${op.layerId}`);
        }

        const resolved = await input.resolveAssetUrl(op.assetId);

        if ("setSrc" in object) {
          await (object as any).setSrc(resolved.url, {
            crossOrigin: "anonymous",
          });

          object.set({
            aiSourceAssetId: op.assetId,
            aiDirty: true,
          });

          normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(object);
        } else {
          const replacement = await FabricImage.fromURL(
            resolved.url,
            {
              crossOrigin: "anonymous",
            }
          );

          replacement.set({
            ...object.toObject(),
            src: resolved.url,
            crossOrigin: "anonymous",
            aiSourceAssetId: op.assetId,
            aiDirty: true,
          });

          const index = input.canvas.getObjects().indexOf(object);
          input.canvas.remove(object);
          input.canvas.insertAt(index, replacement);
        }

        break;
      }

      case "set_object_props": {
        const object = getFabricObjectByLayerId({
          canvas: input.canvas,
          layerId: op.layerId,
        });

        if (!object) {
          throw new Error(`patch_missing_object_${op.layerId}`);
        }

        object.set({
          ...op.props,
          aiDirty: true,
        } as any);

        normalizeFabricObjectAfterEdit(object);
        break;
      }

      case "remove_object": {
        const object = getFabricObjectByLayerId({
          canvas: input.canvas,
          layerId: op.layerId,
        });

        if (object) {
          input.canvas.remove(object);
        }

        break;
      }

      case "add_object": {
        /**
         * Day-one: add_object should be avoided unless the object is image/text/vector JSON
         * already hydrated by the caller.
         */
        throw new Error("add_object_patch_not_enabled_client_side");

      }

      case "replace_object":
        throw new Error("replace_object_patch_not_enabled_client_side");

      case "mark_review_resolved": {
        const object = getFabricObjectByLayerId({
          canvas: input.canvas,
          layerId: op.layerId,
        });

        if (object) {
          object.set({
            aiDirty: true,
          });
        }

        break;
      }
    }
  }

  input.canvas.requestRenderAll();
}
```

Start with `replace_image_src` and `set_object_props`. Add `replace_object` only after testing.

---

# 25.13 User replacement upload

For product/image replacement:

```txt
user chooses file
→ upload landing-zone or direct repair upload
→ server verifies/normalizes image
→ creates user_replacement_asset
→ returns repair patch replace_image_src
→ client applies patch
→ Step 23 autosaves
```

Do not let browser-local blob URLs become durable state.

Client file upload can use Firebase Storage `uploadBytes()` for `Blob`/`File`, but server must still verify and normalize the asset before accepting it as a design asset. Firebase Storage supports file/blob upload from web clients, and metadata can include `contentType`. citeturn451030view2

```ts
import {
  FieldValue,
  getFirestore,
} from "firebase-admin/firestore";

export async function createRepairRequest(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  repairType:
    | "restore_fallback"
    | "downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback"
    | "replace_raster_asset"
    | "regenerate_clean_background"
    | "remask_raster_layer"
    | "revectorize_shape"
    | "convert_raster_text_to_editable"
    | "full_reconstruction_retry";

  target: {
    layerId?: string;
    objectId?: string;
    groupId?: string;
    bbox?: {
      x: number;
      y: number;
      width: number;
      height: number;
    };
  };

  input: {
    baseRevision: number;
    runtimeSnapshotAssetId?: string;
    reconstructionAssetId?: string;
    fabricManifestTemplateAssetId?: string;
    uploadedAssetId?: string;
    prompt?: string;
    constraints?: Record<string, unknown>;
  };
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  const ref = db
    .collection(
      `workspaces/${input.workspaceId}/designs/${input.designId}/repairRequests`
    )
    .doc();

  await ref.set({
    id: ref.id,

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    userId: input.userId,

    status: "queued",

    repairType: input.repairType,

    target: input.target,

    input: input.input,

    progress: {
      percent: 0,
      label: "Repair queued",
    },

    createdAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
  });

  return {
    repairRequestId: ref.id,
  };
}
```

# 25.15 Repair request API

Create:

```txt
src/app/api/workspaces/[workspaceId]/designs/[designId]/repair-requests/route.ts
```

```ts
import {
  NextRequest,
  NextResponse,
} from "next/server";

import {
  createRepairRequest,
} from "@/lib/magic-layers/repair/create-repair-request";

export const runtime = "nodejs";

export async function POST(
  req: NextRequest,
  context: {
    params: Promise<{
      workspaceId: string;
      designId: string;
    }>;
  }
) {
  const {
    workspaceId,
    designId,
  } = await context.params;

  const user = await verifyUserAndAppCheck(req);
  await assertWorkspaceAccess({ workspaceId, userId: user.uid });

  const body = await req.json();

  const result = await createRepairRequest({
    workspaceId,
    designId,
    userId: user.uid,

    repairType: body.repairType,
    target: body.target,
    input: body.input,
  });

  /**
   * Enqueue worker:
   * Cloud Tasks / PubSub / callable worker entry.
   */
  await enqueueRepairWorker({
    workspaceId,
    designId,
    repairRequestId: result.repairRequestId,
  });

  return NextResponse.json(result);
}
```

Use the same auth/App Check pattern from Step 24.

# 25.16 Repair worker dispatcher

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/repair/run-repair-request.ts
```

```ts
import {
  FieldValue,
  getFirestore,
} from "firebase-admin/firestore";

import type {
  MagicRepairPatch,
} from "./repair.types";

export async function runRepairRequest(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  repairRequestId: string;
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  const ref = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${input.workspaceId}/designs/${input.designId}/repairRequests/${input.repairRequestId}`
  );

  const snap = await ref.get();

  if (!snap.exists) {
    throw new Error("repair_request_not_found");
  }

  const request = snap.data()!;

  await ref.update({
    status: "running",
    "progress.percent": 10,
    "progress.label": "Repair running",
    updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
  });

  try {
    let patch: MagicRepairPatch;

    switch (request.repairType) {
      case "regenerate_clean_background":
        patch = await repairCleanBackground(request);
        break;

      case "remask_raster_layer":
        patch = await repairRasterMask(request);
        break;

      case "revectorize_shape":
        patch = await repairVectorShape(request);
        break;

      case "convert_raster_text_to_editable":
        patch = await repairTextConversion(request);
        break;

      case "replace_raster_asset":
        patch = await repairReplaceRasterAsset(request);
        break;

      case "downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback":
      case "restore_fallback":
        patch = await repairExistingFallback(request);
        break;

      case "full_reconstruction_retry":
        patch = await repairFullReconstructionRetry(request);
        break;

      default:
        throw new Error(`unsupported_repair_type:${request.repairType}`);
    }

    const output = await persistRepairPatch({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      repairRequestId: input.repairRequestId,
      patch,
    });

    await ref.update({
      status: "completed",
      output: {
        repairPatchAssetId: output.patchAsset.id,
        repairedAssetIds: patch.repairedAssetIds,
      },
      "progress.percent": 100,
      "progress.label": "Repair completed",
      completedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    return output;
  } catch (error) {
    await ref.update({
      status: "failed",
      error: {
        code: "repair_failed",
        message:
          error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown repair error",
        retryable: true,
      },
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    throw error;
  }
}
```

The individual repair functions should reuse prior pipeline modules in target-bounded mode.

# 25.17 Persist repair patch

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/repair/persist-repair-patch.ts
```

```ts
import {
  AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "../schema/constants";

import {
  bucketForMagicStorageRole,
} from "../storage/storage-buckets";

import {
  repairPatchPath,
  repairRequestReportPath,
} from "../storage/storage-paths";

import {
  writeAiAsset,
} from "../storage/write-ai-asset";

import type {
  MagicRepairPatch,
} from "./repair.types";

export async function persistRepairPatch(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  repairRequestId: string;
  patch: MagicRepairPatch;
}) {
  validateRepairPatch(input.patch);

  const patchAssetId = stableAssetId(
    input.repairRequestId,
    "repair-patch"
  );

  const patchAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "assets",
    bucket: bucketForMagicStorageRole("assets"),
    storagePath: repairPatchPath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      repairRequestId: input.repairRequestId,
      assetId: patchAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: Buffer.from(
      JSON.stringify(input.patch, null, 2),
      "utf8"
    ),

    assetId: patchAssetId,
    kind: "repair_patch_json" as any,

    contentType: "application/json",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,

    source: "system",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
  });

  const reportAssetId = stableAssetId(
    input.repairRequestId,
    "repair-report"
  );

  const reportAsset = await writeAiAsset({
    storageRole: "source",
    bucket: bucketForMagicStorageRole("source"),
    storagePath: repairRequestReportPath({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      repairRequestId: input.repairRequestId,
      assetId: reportAssetId,
    }),

    bytes: Buffer.from(
      JSON.stringify(
        {
          repairRequestId: input.repairRequestId,
          patchAssetId: patchAsset.id,
          repairedAssetIds: input.patch.repairedAssetIds,
          warnings: input.patch.warnings,
          createdAt: Date.now(),
        },
        null,
        2
      ),
      "utf8"
    ),

    assetId: reportAssetId,
    kind: "repair_request_report_json" as any,

    contentType: "application/json",

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,

    source: "system",

    schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

    sourceAssetId: patchAsset.id,

    cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
  });

  return {
    patchAsset,
    reportAsset,
  };
}

function validateRepairPatch(patch: MagicRepairPatch) {
  for (const op of patch.ops) {
    if ("assetId" in op) {
      if (/^https?:\/\//.test(op.assetId)) {
        throw new Error("repair_patch_asset_id_contains_url");
      }
    }
  }
}

function stableAssetId(repairRequestId: string, label: string) {
  return `asset_${repairRequestId}_${label}_${crypto.randomUUID()}`
    .replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "_")
    .toLowerCase();
}
```

Remove `as any` after patching asset kind enum.

---

# 25.18 Repair: existing fallback

This is a server-produced patch for clients that want all repairs to flow through the repair request system.

```ts
async function repairExistingFallback(request: any): Promise<MagicRepairPatch> {
  const layerId = request.target.layerId;

  const fallbackAssetId =
    request.input.constraints?.fallbackAssetId;

  if (!layerId || !fallbackAssetId) {
    throw new Error("missing_layer_or_fallback_asset");
  }

  return {
    schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",

    workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
    designId: request.designId,
    repairRequestId: request.id,

    baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,

    repairType: request.repairType,

    targetLayerId: layerId,

    ops: [
      {
        op: "replace_image_src",
        layerId,
        assetId: fallbackAssetId,
        preserveTransform: true,
        reason:
          request.repairType === "downgrade_text_to_raster_fallback"
            ? "Unsafe or weak editable text downgraded to raster fallback"
            : "Layer restored from fallback asset",
      },
      {
        op: "set_object_props",
        layerId,
        props: {
          aiEditableLevel: "raster_fallback",
          aiDirty: true,
        },
        reason: "Runtime layer now uses fallback representation",
      },
    ],

    repairedAssetIds: [fallbackAssetId],

    warnings: [],

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}
```

For text fallback, if the current Fabric object is a Textbox, the client `applyFallbackRestoration(...)` handles object replacement.

# 25.19 Repair: replace raster asset

Use when user uploads a new image for a product/person/image block.

Server flow:

```txt
uploaded asset
→ verify belongs to design
→ normalize replacement image
→ create user_replacement_asset
→ repair patch replace_image_src
```

Patch:

```ts
async function repairReplaceRasterAsset(request: any): Promise<MagicRepairPatch> {
  const layerId = request.target.layerId;
  const uploadedAssetId = request.input.uploadedAssetId;

  if (!layerId || !uploadedAssetId) {
    throw new Error("missing_layer_or_uploaded_asset");
  }

  /**
   * In production:
   * verify uploadedAssetId
   * normalize to PNG/WebP editor asset
   * create final design asset
   */
  const replacementAssetId = uploadedAssetId;

  return {
    schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",

    workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
    designId: request.designId,
    repairRequestId: request.id,

    baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,

    repairType: "replace_raster_asset",

    targetLayerId: layerId,

    ops: [
      {
        op: "replace_image_src",
        layerId,
        assetId: replacementAssetId,
        preserveTransform: true,
        reason: "User replaced raster asset",
      },
      {
        op: "set_object_props",
        layerId,
        props: {
          aiSource: "manual_user",
          aiRuntimeKind: "manual_object",
          aiDirty: true,
        },
        reason: "Layer now contains user-provided replacement asset",
      },
    ],

    repairedAssetIds: [replacementAssetId],

    warnings: [],

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}
```

Do not alter the clean background automatically here. If replacing a product exposes bad background, user should trigger background repair separately.

---

# 25.20 Repair: regenerate clean background

This should reuse Step 14 in target-bounded mode.

Input:

```txt
current runtime snapshot
selected foreground masks or target layer IDs
normalized image
existing raster candidates
```

Output:

```txt
new repaired_background_png
repair patch replace_image_src for clean background layer
```

Repair rule:

```txt
force outside-mask preservation again
never let generative repair mutate unmasked pixels
```

If Gemini Image is enabled later, still composite only inside mask. Gemini docs support image editing and semantic masking, but this model path must remain guarded and review-first. citeturn437366view2turn437366view1

Patch:

```ts
async function repairCleanBackground(request: any): Promise<MagicRepairPatch> {
  const backgroundLayerId =
    request.target.layerId ?? "layer_clean_background";

  /**
   * Implementation:
   * - load reconstruction/runtime snapshot
   * - build removal mask from selected target layers
   * - run Step 14 background reconstruction in target mode
   * - write repaired_background_png
   */
  const repairedBackgroundAssetId =
    await runTargetedBackgroundRepairAndReturnAssetId(request);

  return {
    schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",

    workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
    designId: request.designId,
    repairRequestId: request.id,

    baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,

    repairType: "regenerate_clean_background",

    targetLayerId: backgroundLayerId,

    ops: [
      {
        op: "replace_image_src",
        layerId: backgroundLayerId,
        assetId: repairedBackgroundAssetId,
        preserveTransform: true,
        reason: "Clean background regenerated",
      },
      {
        op: "set_object_props",
        layerId: backgroundLayerId,
        props: {
          aiDirty: true,
        },
        reason: "Background layer repaired",
      },
    ],

    repairedAssetIds: [repairedBackgroundAssetId],

    warnings: [],

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}
```

# 25.21 Repair: remask raster layer

Use when:

```txt
person/product cutout edge is wrong
mask includes background
mask misses object parts
```

Server flow:

```txt
target layer bbox
normalized image
existing mask
optional user brush hints
→ SAM/BiRefNet/Gemini segmentation proposal
→ Step 13 raster asset builder
→ repaired_raster_asset_png + repaired_mask_png
→ patch replace_image_src
```

Patch:

```ts
async function repairRasterMask(request: any): Promise<MagicRepairPatch> {
  const layerId = request.target.layerId;

  if (!layerId) {
    throw new Error("missing_layer_id");
  }

  const repairedAsset = await runTargetedMaskRepairAndReturnAsset({
    request,
    layerId,
  });

  return {
    schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",

    workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
    designId: request.designId,
    repairRequestId: request.id,

    baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,

    repairType: "remask_raster_layer",

    targetLayerId: layerId,

    ops: [
      {
        op: "replace_image_src",
        layerId,
        assetId: repairedAsset.editorAssetId,
        preserveTransform: true,
        reason: "Raster mask regenerated",
      },
      {
        op: "set_object_props",
        layerId,
        props: {
          aiSourceAssetId: repairedAsset.editorAssetId,
          aiDirty: true,
        },
        reason: "Runtime layer now uses repaired raster asset",
      },
    ],

    repairedAssetIds: [
      repairedAsset.editorAssetId,
      repairedAsset.maskAssetId,
    ].filter(Boolean),

    warnings: repairedAsset.warnings ?? [],

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}
```

Do not create a new layer by default. Replace the asset on the existing layer to preserve user layout.

# 25.22 Repair: revectorize shape

Use when:

```txt
shape raster fallback exists
vector candidate failed
user wants editable vector
```

Server flow:

```txt
source raster/fallback asset
→ Step 12 vector recovery target mode
→ validate vector render
→ if pass, return replace_object patch
→ if fail, return needs_review/fallback patch
```

Day-one safer implementation:

```txt
only allow primitive/vector repair when output maps cleanly to Fabric primitive/path
otherwise keep raster fallback
```

Patch output for successful vector repair:

```ts
async function repairVectorShape(request: any): Promise<MagicRepairPatch> {
  const layerId = request.target.layerId;

  if (!layerId) throw new Error("missing_layer_id");

  const vectorResult =
    await runTargetedVectorRepairAndReturnFabricObject(request);

  if (!vectorResult.passed) {
    return {
      schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",
      workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
      designId: request.designId,
      repairRequestId: request.id,
      baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,
      repairType: "revectorize_shape",
      targetLayerId: layerId,
      ops: [
        {
          op: "set_object_props",
          layerId,
          props: {
            aiDirty: true,
          },
          reason: "Vector repair failed validation; kept raster fallback",
        },
      ],
      repairedAssetIds: vectorResult.assetIds ?? [],
      warnings: ["vector_repair_failed_validation"],
      createdAt: Date.now(),
    };
  }

  return {
    schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",

    workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
    designId: request.designId,
    repairRequestId: request.id,

    baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,

    repairType: "revectorize_shape",

    targetLayerId: layerId,

    ops: [
      {
        op: "replace_object",
        layerId,
        object: vectorResult.fabricObject,
        reason: "Shape revectorized successfully",
      },
    ],

    repairedAssetIds: vectorResult.assetIds,

    warnings: [],

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}
```

Client-side `replace_object` should remain disabled until you implement/test it. Server can alternatively return `manual_review` until ready.

# 25.23 Repair: convert raster text to editable

Use when:

```txt
text was kept as raster fallback
user wants editable text
```

Server flow:

```txt
target raster text fallback crop
→ OCR
→ style estimation
→ render validation
→ text safety validation
→ if pass, return replace_object patch with Textbox JSON
→ if not pass, keep raster fallback
```

Hard rule:

```txt
Never convert text to editable unless Step 20-style safety passes on that crop.
```

Patch:

```ts
async function repairTextConversion(request: any): Promise<MagicRepairPatch> {
  const layerId = request.target.layerId;

  if (!layerId) throw new Error("missing_layer_id");

  const textResult =
    await runTargetedTextConversionAndReturnFabricObject(request);

  if (!textResult.passed) {
    return {
      schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",
      workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
      designId: request.designId,
      repairRequestId: request.id,
      baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,
      repairType: "convert_raster_text_to_editable",
      targetLayerId: layerId,
      ops: [
        {
          op: "set_object_props",
          layerId,
          props: {
            aiDirty: true,
          },
          reason: "Text conversion failed safety validation; kept raster fallback",
        },
      ],
      repairedAssetIds: textResult.assetIds ?? [],
      warnings: textResult.warnings ?? ["text_conversion_failed"],
      createdAt: Date.now(),
    };
  }

  return {
    schemaVersion: "ai-repair-patch.v1",

    workspaceId: request.workspaceId,
    designId: request.designId,
    repairRequestId: request.id,

    baseRevision: request.input.baseRevision,

    repairType: "convert_raster_text_to_editable",

    targetLayerId: layerId,

    ops: [
      {
        op: "replace_object",
        layerId,
        object: textResult.fabricObject,
        reason: "Raster text converted to editable text",
      },
    ],

    repairedAssetIds: textResult.assetIds ?? [],

    warnings: [],

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}
```

This is disabled until `replace_object` is supported safely client-side.

# 25.24 Repair patch client workflow

Client flow after repair request completes:

```txt
1. Listen to repairRequests/{repairId}.
2. When completed, load repairPatchAssetId.
3. Hydrate referenced asset URLs.
4. Apply patch to Fabric canvas.
5. Mark dirty.
6. Trigger manual_save or autosave_checkpoint.
7. Create repair_result version.
```

Do not apply a repair patch to a stale canvas.

Patch requires:

```txt
patch.baseRevision === current editor baseRevision
```

or user must explicitly apply as conflict resolution.

Create:

```txt
GET /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/repair-requests/{repairId}/patch
```

Behavior:

```txt
verify auth/appcheck
verify workspace access
load repair request
load repair patch asset
verify repaired assets belong to design
return patch
```

# 25.26 Repair result persistence

After applying a patch:

```txt
Step 23 autosave persists the repaired runtime Fabric JSON.
```

For repair completion, create a version:

```txt
source = repair_result
```

Recommended flow:

```ts
await autosaveController.flushManualSave()
```

or:

```txt
POST editor-save with saveKind = autosave_checkpoint
then create version source = repair_result
```

Do not rely on repair patch alone as final state. The actual editor state after repair is the Fabric runtime snapshot.

# 25.27 Targeted repair validation

Every targeted AI repair must run its own validation before returning a patch.

```txt
background repair
  outside-mask preservation
  seam risk
  hallucination risk

mask repair
  mask area sanity
  alpha coverage
  bbox bounds
  edge quality

vector repair
  render validation
  path complexity
  fallback attached

text conversion
  OCR/string safety
  protected token safety
  render validation

replacement upload
  MIME validation
  decode validation
  dimensions
  storage ownership
```

Do not return a patch for an unvalidated AI result.

---

# 25.28 Full reconstruction retry

Use only when targeted repair is insufficient.

Criteria:

```txt
visual validation failed catastrophically
many layers are low confidence
background + foreground interaction is broken
text recovery failed across many regions
z-order is widely wrong
```

Do not call full retry from a single bad layer.

Full retry creates:

```txt
new aiLayerJobs/{jobId}
new reconstruction document
new fabric manifest template
new editor runtime source
```

It does not overwrite current user-edited runtime unless user explicitly chooses to replace.

Layer panel action mapping:

```txt
text_raster_fallback
  Try convert to editable text

vector_editable + warning
  Restore raster fallback

raster_masked

  Restore fallback

unknown_confidence
```

Each action should show:

# 25.30 Undo rule

Repair must be undoable.

Day-one rule:

```txt
Before applying repair patch:
  create autosave_checkpoint or manual_save snapshot.

After applying patch:
  create repair_result snapshot.
```

This gives:

```txt
before repair
after repair
```

without building a custom operation-level undo system.

Repair APIs must verify:

```txt
auth user owns/has workspace access
repair target belongs to design
base revision is valid
uploaded asset belongs to design
fallback asset belongs to design
repair patch assets belong to design
runtime snapshot belongs to design
```

Never accept:

```txt
foreign asset IDs
signed URLs in patch
base64 image data in patch
unbounded prompts
repairing locked_reference
repairing another user’s design
```

# 25.34 Non-negotiable invariants

Step 25 is valid only if:

```txt
Every repair is explicit.

Fallback restoration is possible without AI.

Unsafe editable text repairs to raster fallback first.

AI repair results are validated before patch creation.

Repair outputs are patch assets, not silent state mutation.

Repair patch contains no signed URLs.

Repair patch contains no base64 images.

Repair patch references only design-owned assets.

Repair patch is applied only to matching runtime revision or explicit conflict flow.

Applying repair marks runtime dirty.

Step 23 persists repaired runtime state.

Repair result can create a version.

AiReconstructionDocument remains original AI snapshot.

Fabric manifest template remains original AI projection.

Full reconstruction retry creates a new job, not an overwrite.
```

---

# 25.35 Definition of done

Step 25 is complete when:

```txt
Layer panel can trigger fallback restoration.

Unsafe text can be downgraded to raster fallback.

Raster assets can be replaced by user upload.

Repair request docs exist.

Repair worker dispatch exists.

Repair patch assets are generated.

Client can load and apply repair patches.

Repair patch application marks canvas dirty.

Step 23 autosaves repaired runtime state.

Repair result versions can be created.

No repair mutates the original reconstruction document.

No repair stores signed URLs.

No unvalidated AI repair reaches the canvas.
```

Locked Step 25 architecture:

```txt
User/system repair request
→ explicit repair request doc
→ local fallback OR targeted repair worker
→ validated repair assets
→ repair patch JSON
→ client applies patch to Fabric runtime
→ Step 23 persists repaired runtime snapshot
→ optional repair_result version
```

Next is Step 26: **Exports, server rendering, and production output pipeline**.

Step 23 is the persistence boundary: editor Fabric runtime snapshots become immutable GCS assets, while Firestore keeps only pointers, revisions, and lightweight status metadata.

# Step 23 — Autosave, versioning, and edit persistence

Step 23 makes editor changes durable.

The locked rule:

```txt
Autosave persists Fabric runtime state.
Autosave does not mutate AiReconstructionDocument.
Autosave does not regenerate AiFabricManifestTemplate.
Autosave does not call AI repair.
```

This is where the user’s edits become saved design state:

```txt
Fabric canvas runtime
→ FabricRuntimeJson snapshot
→ GCS immutable asset
→ Firestore current pointer
```

Firestore must store only small pointers and status. Firestore documents have a hard 1 MiB limit, so full Fabric JSON snapshots belong in GCS, not Firestore. citeturn608326view0

---

# 23.1 What Step 23 owns

Step 23 owns:

```txt
local editor draft persistence
debounced autosave
server autosave API
immutable Fabric runtime JSON asset writes
edit-event asset writes
current design pointer update
revision conflict detection
manual save / version creation
restore latest autosave
multi-tab/session safety
Firestore autosave metadata
```

Step 23 does **not** own:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument mutation
AI repair
fallback restoration
background regeneration
text safety validation
visual validation
export
collaboration cursors
real-time multiplayer editing
```

---

# 23.2 Core persistence model

Use three layers.

```txt
1. Local draft
   IndexedDB
   immediate, offline-safe, fast recovery

2. Server autosave
   GCS FabricRuntimeJson snapshot
   Firestore current pointer
   debounced

3. Version snapshot
   GCS FabricRuntimeJson snapshot
   Firestore versions/{versionId}
   explicit save / periodic checkpoint
```

Do not make every autosave a user-facing version.

Correct:

```txt
autosave = current recoverable state
version = intentional checkpoint
```

IndexedDB is appropriate for local drafts because it stores significant structured data and blobs client-side, unlike Web Storage, which is suited only to smaller data. citeturn608326view3

---

# 23.3 Durable truth split

After Step 23, your design has two truths:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
  immutable AI reconstruction snapshot

FabricRuntimeJson
  current user-edited editor state
```

Never collapse them.

Wrong:

```txt
user edits text
→ mutate AiReconstructionDocument.layers[].text.value
```

Correct:

```txt
user edits text
→ save FabricRuntimeJson snapshot
→ AiReconstructionDocument remains provenance/audit truth
```

This preserves auditability:

```txt
What AI recovered
vs
What the user edited after recovery
```

# 23.5 Revision rule

Every server autosave must include:

```txt
baseRevision
sessionId
idempotencyKey
```

Server accepts the autosave only if:

```txt
request.baseRevision === design.current.revision
```

Then server writes:

```txt
design.current.revision = baseRevision + 1
design.current.fabricRuntimeJsonAssetId = new asset id
design.current.autosaveId = autosaveId
```

Use a Firestore transaction for this pointer update. Firestore transactions are atomic, retry on concurrent document changes, and apply writes only after the transaction succeeds. citeturn608326view1

Conflict rule:

```txt
if baseRevision < currentRevision
  save conflict autosave asset
  do not update design.current
  return 409 conflict
```

Do not overwrite another tab/device’s newer state.

```ts
    "versions",
    input.versionId,
    "fabric-runtime.json",
  ]);
}
```

Generated autosave/version assets are immutable. Use create-only Cloud Storage writes. Cloud Storage preconditions prevent writes from applying when the target object is not in the expected state, and `ifGenerationMatch: 0` is the right create-only guard. citeturn608326view2

```ts
    | "user_autosave_checkpoint"
    | "export_checkpoint";

  fabricRuntimeJson: FabricRuntimeJson;

  stats: EditorRuntimeStats;

  createdAt: number;
};
```

# 23.10 Compute runtime stats

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/autosave/compute-editor-runtime-stats.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  Canvas,
} from "fabric";

import type {
  EditorRuntimeStats,
} from "./autosave.types";

export function computeEditorRuntimeStats(
  canvas: Canvas
): EditorRuntimeStats {
  const objects = canvas.getObjects();

  return {
    objectCount: objects.length,

    layerCount: objects.filter((object) => object.aiLayerId).length,

    textObjectCount: objects.filter(
      (object) => object.aiEditableLevel === "text_editable"
    ).length,

    imageObjectCount: objects.filter(
      (object) =>
        object.aiEditableLevel === "raster_masked" ||
        object.aiEditableLevel === "raster_fallback" ||
        object.aiEditableLevel === "raster_clean_background" ||
        object.aiEditableLevel === "locked_reference"
    ).length,

    vectorObjectCount: objects.filter(
      (object) => object.aiEditableLevel === "vector_editable"
    ).length,

    manualObjectCount: objects.filter(
      (object) => object.aiRuntimeKind === "manual_object"
    ).length,

    dirtyObjectCount: objects.filter(
      (object) => object.aiDirty === true
    ).length,
  };
}
```

# 23.11 Local draft persistence

Use IndexedDB for immediate client recovery.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/autosave/local-draft-store.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  FabricRuntimeJson,
} from "../fabric-generator/fabric-generator.types";

import type {
  MagicEditorEditEvent,
} from "../editor-behavior/editor-behavior.types";

export type LocalEditorDraft = {
  key: string;

  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  sessionId: string;

  baseRevision: number;

  fabricRuntimeJson: FabricRuntimeJson;

  editEvents: MagicEditorEditEvent[];

  savedAt: number;
};

const DB_NAME = "magic-layers-editor-drafts";
const STORE_NAME = "drafts";
const DB_VERSION = 1;

export async function saveLocalEditorDraft(
  draft: LocalEditorDraft
) {
  const db = await openDraftDb();

  await putValue(db, draft.key, draft);

  db.close();
}

export async function loadLocalEditorDraft(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;
}): Promise<LocalEditorDraft | undefined> {
  const db = await openDraftDb();

  const key = localDraftKey(input);

  const value = await getValue<LocalEditorDraft>(db, key);

  db.close();

  return value;
}

export async function deleteLocalEditorDraft(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;
}) {
  const db = await openDraftDb();

  await deleteValue(db, localDraftKey(input));

  db.close();
}

export function localDraftKey(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;
}) {
  return `${input.workspaceId}:${input.designId}:${input.userId}`;
}

function openDraftDb(): Promise<IDBDatabase> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const request = indexedDB.open(DB_NAME, DB_VERSION);

    request.onupgradeneeded = () => {
      const db = request.result;

      if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(STORE_NAME)) {
        db.createObjectStore(STORE_NAME);
      }
    };

    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);

    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
  });
}

function putValue(
  db: IDBDatabase,
  key: string,
  value: unknown
) {
  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readwrite");

    tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).put(value, key);

    tx.oncomplete = () => resolve();

    tx.onerror = () => reject(tx.error);
  });
}

function getValue<T>(
  db: IDBDatabase,
  key: string
) {
  return new Promise<T | undefined>((resolve, reject) => {
    const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readonly");

    const request = tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).get(key);

    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result as T | undefined);

    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
  });
}

function deleteValue(
  db: IDBDatabase,
  key: string
) {
  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readwrite");

    tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).delete(key);

    tx.oncomplete = () => resolve();

    tx.onerror = () => reject(tx.error);
  });
}
```

Local draft is a recovery buffer, not the server truth.
