# 26.13 Export renderer

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/export/playwright-export-renderer.ts
```

```ts
import {
  chromium,
} from "playwright";

import sharp from "sharp";

import type {
  MagicExportRenderInput,
  MagicExportRenderResult,
} from "./export.types";

import {
  MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY,
} from "./export-policy";

export async function renderExportWithPlaywright(
  input: MagicExportRenderInput
): Promise<MagicExportRenderResult> {
  const rendererUrl = process.env.MAGIC_LAYERS_RENDERER_URL;

  if (!rendererUrl) {
    throw new Error("missing_magic_layers_renderer_url");
  }

  const manifest = input.runtimeManifest;

  const multiplier = Math.min(
    input.options.multiplier ??
      MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.dimensions.defaultMultiplier,
    MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.dimensions.maxMultiplier
  );

  const width = Math.round(
    input.options.width ??
      manifest.canvas.width * multiplier
  );

  const height = Math.round(
    input.options.height ??
      manifest.canvas.height * multiplier
  );

  assertExportDimensions({
    width,
    height,
  });

  const browser = await chromium.launch({
    args: ["--no-sandbox"],
  });

  try {
    const page = await browser.newPage({
      viewport: {
        width,
        height,
      },
      deviceScaleFactor: 1,
    });

    await page.goto(rendererUrl, {
      waitUntil: "networkidle",
      timeout: MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.renderer.timeoutMs,
    });

    await page.evaluate(
      async ({ runtimeManifest, width, height }) => {
        const win = window as any;

        if (!win.renderMagicLayersRuntimeManifest) {
          throw new Error(
            "Renderer page missing renderMagicLayersRuntimeManifest"
          );
        }

        const scaledManifest = {
          ...runtimeManifest,

          canvas: {
            ...runtimeManifest.canvas,
            width,
            height,
          },

          fabricJson: scaleFabricJsonToOutputSize({
            fabricJson: runtimeManifest.fabricJson,
            sourceWidth: runtimeManifest.canvas.width,
            sourceHeight: runtimeManifest.canvas.height,
            outputWidth: width,
            outputHeight: height,
          }),
        };

        await win.renderMagicLayersRuntimeManifest(scaledManifest);

        function scaleFabricJsonToOutputSize(input: any) {
          const scaleX = input.outputWidth / input.sourceWidth;
          const scaleY = input.outputHeight / input.sourceHeight;

          return {
            ...input.fabricJson,
            width: input.outputWidth,
            height: input.outputHeight,
            objects: input.fabricJson.objects.map((object: any) => ({
              ...object,
              left:
                typeof object.left === "number"
                  ? object.left * scaleX
                  : object.left,
              top:
                typeof object.top === "number"
                  ? object.top * scaleY
                  : object.top,
              scaleX:
                typeof object.scaleX === "number"
                  ? object.scaleX * scaleX
                  : object.scaleX,
              scaleY:
                typeof object.scaleY === "number"
                  ? object.scaleY * scaleY
                  : object.scaleY,
            })),
          };
        }
      },
      {
        runtimeManifest: manifest,
        width,
        height,
      }
    );

    await page.evaluate(async () => {
      if ("fonts" in document) {
        await (document as any).fonts.ready;
      }
    });

    const canvas = page.locator(
      "[data-magic-layers-render-canvas='true']"
    );

    const png = await canvas.screenshot({
      type: "png",
      timeout: MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.renderer.timeoutMs,
    });

    if (input.options.format === "png") {
      return {
        buffer: png,
        mimeType: "image/png",
        extension: "png",
        width,
        height,
        rendererName: "playwright_chromium",
      };
    }

    if (input.options.format === "jpeg") {
      const buffer = await sharp(png)
        .flatten({
          background: "#ffffff",
        })
        .jpeg({
          quality: Math.round(
            clampQuality(input.options.quality, "jpeg") * 100
          ),
        })
        .toBuffer();

      return {
        buffer,
        mimeType: "image/jpeg",
        extension: "jpg",
        width,
        height,
        rendererName: "playwright_chromium_sharp_jpeg",
      };
    }

    if (input.options.format === "webp") {
      const buffer = await sharp(png)
        .webp({
          quality: Math.round(
            clampQuality(input.options.quality, "webp") * 100
          ),
        })
        .toBuffer();

      return {
        buffer,
        mimeType: "image/webp",
        extension: "webp",
        width,
        height,
        rendererName: "playwright_chromium_sharp_webp",
      };
    }

    if (input.options.format === "pdf") {
      const pdfBuffer = await renderPdfFromCanvasPage({
        page,
        width,
        height,
        printBackground:
          input.options.pdf?.printBackground ?? true,
      });

      return {
        buffer: pdfBuffer,
        mimeType: "application/pdf",
        extension: "pdf",
        width,
        height,
        rendererName: "playwright_chromium_pdf",
      };
    }

    throw new Error(`unsupported_export_format:${input.options.format}`);
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
  }
}

async function renderPdfFromCanvasPage(input: {
  page: any;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  printBackground: boolean;
}) {
  await input.page.emulateMedia({
    media: "screen",
  });

  return input.page.pdf({
    width: `${input.width}px`,
    height: `${input.height}px`,
    printBackground: input.printBackground,
    margin: {
      top: "0px",
      right: "0px",
      bottom: "0px",
      left: "0px",
    },
  });
}

function assertExportDimensions(input: {
  width: number;
  height: number;
}) {
  const maxLongEdge =
    MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.dimensions.maxOutputLongEdgePx;

  if (
    input.width < MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.dimensions.minOutputWidthPx ||
    input.height < MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.dimensions.minOutputHeightPx
  ) {
    throw new Error("export_dimensions_too_small");
  }

  if (Math.max(input.width, input.height) > maxLongEdge) {
    throw new Error("export_dimensions_too_large");
  }
}

function clampQuality(
  value: number | undefined,
  format: "jpeg" | "webp"
) {
  const defaultValue =
    format === "jpeg"
      ? MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.quality.jpegDefault
      : MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.quality.webpDefault;

  const q = value ?? defaultValue;

  return Math.max(
    MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.quality.min,
    Math.min(MAGIC_LAYERS_EXPORT_POLICY.quality.max, q)
  );
}
```

The render shell uses Fabric in Chromium, then Playwright screenshots the canvas or generates a PDF. Playwright’s Page API supports screenshot capture and PDF buffer generation. citeturn483849view2

# 26.14 Export worker

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/export/run-export-request.ts
```

```ts
import {
  FieldValue,
  getFirestore,
} from "firebase-admin/firestore";

import {
  AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,
  AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
} from "../schema/constants";

import {
  bucketForMagicStorageRole,
} from "../storage/storage-buckets";

import {
  exportOutputAssetPath,
  exportRequestReportPath,
} from "../storage/storage-paths";

import {
  writeAiAsset,
} from "../storage/write-ai-asset";

import {
  loadExportRuntimeSource,
} from "./load-export-runtime-source";

import {
  renderExportWithPlaywright,
} from "./playwright-export-renderer";

import type {
  MagicExportRequestReport,
} from "./export.types";

export async function runExportRequest(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  exportId: string;
}) {
  const db = getFirestore();

  const exportRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${input.workspaceId}/designs/${input.designId}/exportRequests/${input.exportId}`
  );

  const designRef = db.doc(
    `workspaces/${input.workspaceId}/designs/${input.designId}`
  );

  const exportSnap = await exportRef.get();

  if (!exportSnap.exists) {
    throw new Error("export_request_not_found");
  }

  const exportRequest = exportSnap.data()!;

  await exportRef.update({
    status: "running",
    "progress.percent": 10,
    "progress.label": "Preparing export",
    updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
  });

  try {
    const designSnap = await designRef.get();

    if (!designSnap.exists) {
      throw new Error("design_not_found");
    }

    const design = designSnap.data()!;

    const runtimeManifest = await loadExportRuntimeSource({
      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      source: exportRequest.source,
      design,
    });

    await exportRef.update({
      "progress.percent": 40,
      "progress.label": "Rendering export",
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    const rendered = await renderExportWithPlaywright({
      runtimeManifest,
      options: exportRequest.options,
    });

    const outputAssetId = stableAssetId(
      input.exportId,
      `export-${exportRequest.options.format}`
    );

    const outputAsset = await writeAiAsset({
      storageRole: "exports",
      bucket: bucketForMagicStorageRole("exports"),
      storagePath: exportOutputAssetPath({
        workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
        designId: input.designId,
        exportId: input.exportId,
        assetId: outputAssetId,
        extension: rendered.extension,
      }),

      bytes: rendered.buffer,

      assetId: outputAssetId,

      kind: kindForFormat(exportRequest.options.format) as any,

      contentType: rendered.mimeType,

      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,

      width: rendered.width,
      height: rendered.height,

      source: "server_export_renderer",

      schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
      pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

      cacheControl: "private, max-age=31536000, immutable",
    });

    await exportRef.update({
      "progress.percent": 85,
      "progress.label": "Finalizing export",
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    const reportAssetId = stableAssetId(
      input.exportId,
      "export-report"
    );

    const report: MagicExportRequestReport = {
      schemaVersion: "ai-export-request-report.v1",

      exportId: input.exportId,

      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,
      userId: exportRequest.userId,

      source: exportRequest.source,

      options: exportRequest.options,

      outputAssetId: outputAsset.id,

      outputMimeType: rendered.mimeType,

      renderer: {
        name: rendered.rendererName,
        width: rendered.width ?? 0,
        height: rendered.height ?? 0,
        multiplier: exportRequest.options.multiplier ?? 1,
      },

      warnings: [],

      createdAt: Date.now(),
    };

    const reportAsset = await writeAiAsset({
      storageRole: "source",
      bucket: bucketForMagicStorageRole("source"),
      storagePath: exportRequestReportPath({
        workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
        designId: input.designId,
        exportId: input.exportId,
        assetId: reportAssetId,
      }),

      bytes: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2), "utf8"),

      assetId: reportAssetId,
      kind: "export_request_report_json" as any,

      contentType: "application/json",

      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
      designId: input.designId,

      source: "server_export_renderer",

      schemaVersion: AI_RECONSTRUCTION_SCHEMA_VERSION,
      pipelineVersion: AI_PIPELINE_VERSION,

      sourceAssetId: outputAsset.id,

      cacheControl: "private, no-cache",
    });

    await exportRef.update({
      status: "completed",

      output: {
        assetId: outputAsset.id,
        mimeType: rendered.mimeType,
        width: rendered.width ?? null,
        height: rendered.height ?? null,
        sizeBytes: rendered.buffer.byteLength,
      },

      reportAssetId: reportAsset.id,

      "progress.percent": 100,
      "progress.label": "Export completed",

      completedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    return {
      outputAsset,
      reportAsset,
    };
  } catch (error) {
    await exportRef.update({
      status: "failed",

      error: {
        code: "export_failed",
        message:
          error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown export error",
        retryable: true,
      },

      "progress.label": "Export failed",
      updatedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
    });

    throw error;
  }
}

function kindForFormat(format: string) {
  switch (format) {
    case "png":
      return "export_png";
    case "jpeg":
      return "export_jpeg";
    case "webp":
      return "export_webp";
    case "pdf":
      return "export_pdf";
    default:
      throw new Error(`unsupported_format:${format}`);
  }
}

function stableAssetId(exportId: string, label: string) {
  return `asset_${exportId}_${label}_${crypto.randomUUID()}`
    .replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "_")
    .toLowerCase();
}
```

Remove `as any` after patching your asset enum.

# 26.16 Download URL endpoint

Create:

```txt
GET /api/workspaces/{workspaceId}/designs/{designId}/exports/{exportId}/download
```

Behavior:

```txt
verify auth
verify App Check
verify access
load export request
require completed
sign output asset URL
return URL
```

```ts
export async function GET(
  req: NextRequest,
  context: {
    params: Promise<{
      workspaceId: string;
      designId: string;
      exportId: string;
    }>;
  }
) {
  const {
    workspaceId,
    designId,
    exportId,
  } = await context.params;

  const userId = await verifyAuthAndAppCheck(req);

  await assertWorkspaceAccess({
    workspaceId,
    userId,
  });

  const db = getFirestore();

  const snap = await db
    .doc(
      `workspaces/${workspaceId}/designs/${designId}/exportRequests/${exportId}`
    )
    .get();

  if (!snap.exists) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: "export_not_found" },
      { status: 404 }
    );
  }

  const exportRequest = snap.data()!;

  if (exportRequest.status !== "completed") {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: "export_not_ready" },
      { status: 409 }
    );
  }

  const outputAssetId = exportRequest.output?.assetId;

  const asset = await loadAssetRef({
    workspaceId,
    designId,
    assetId: outputAssetId,
  });

  const signed = await resolveAiAssetSignedUrl({
    asset,
    expiresInMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
    responseDisposition: `attachment; filename="${downloadFilename(exportRequest)}"`,
  });

  return NextResponse.json({
    url: signed.url,
    urlExpiresAt: signed.urlExpiresAt,
  });
}
```

Signed URLs should be short-lived for export downloads because anyone holding the URL can access the object while it is active. citeturn566776search0

---

# 26.17 Export UI behavior

Export UI flow:

```txt
User clicks Export
→ choose format/options
→ POST export request
→ show queued/running progress
→ listen to exportRequests/{exportId}
→ when completed, call download endpoint
→ browser downloads signed URL
```

Do not block the editor.

Do not use local canvas export as official output.

Client preview option:

```txt
Quick preview PNG can use canvas.toDataURL locally.
Official download must use export worker.
```

---

# 26.18 Export from unsaved changes

If editor is dirty:

```txt
show “Save before export”
→ flush Step 23 autosave
→ export accepted revision
```

Hard rule:

```txt
Do not export stale server runtime while the user has unsaved local edits.
```

Flow:

```txt
dirty canvas
→ autosave flush
→ update current.revision
→ create export request with source=current_runtime revision
```

If autosave conflict:

```txt
block export
show conflict resolution
```

---

# 26.19 PDF rule

Day-one PDF is raster-backed.

Implementation:

```txt
render canvas to exact pixels
place/render that output in a PDF page
or call page.pdf on the render shell page
```

Do not claim:

```txt
editable PDF text
vector-preserved PDF
print-ready CMYK
```

unless you build those specific paths.

Playwright’s `page.pdf()` generates a PDF using print CSS media by default; use `page.emulateMedia({ media: "screen" })` when you need screen-style output. citeturn483849view2

---

# 26.20 SVG export rule

Do not ship SVG export as official day-one output.

Reason:

```txt
current runtime may include raster images, shadows, text fallback, masks, filters, and manual objects.
Fabric SVG output can be useful but needs separate validation.
```

Later SVG export should be:

```txt
explicitly labeled beta
validated by re-rendering SVG to PNG and comparing against server render
```

---

# 26.21 Production output invariants

An export is valid only if:

```txt
source runtime is explicit
source revision is recorded
all image URLs are hydrated server-side
no signed URLs are stored inside export reports
renderer name is recorded
output asset is stored in exports bucket
output asset has immutable cache metadata
export request has completed status
download endpoint signs a temporary URL
```

---

# 26.22 Export failure handling

Failure cases:

```txt
runtime source missing
asset hydration failed
Fabric load failed
font load failed
renderer timeout
output dimensions too large
Cloud Storage write failed
PDF render failed
worker timeout
```

On failure:

```txt
exportRequests/{exportId}.status = failed
error.code set
error.retryable set
do not mutate design.current
do not delete source runtime
```

Retry should create a new export attempt or rerun the same request if idempotent.

---

# 26.23 Cost controls

Export is expensive compared to normal editor operations.

Controls:

```txt
limit max output dimensions
limit multiplier
queue exports
rate-limit per workspace/user
dedupe identical export requests when possible
expire signed download URLs quickly
do not store redundant thumbnails as exports
use Cloud Run concurrency carefully
```

Cloud Run Jobs can run longer workloads, but individual export requests should usually be Cloud Tasks to Cloud Run service. Use Cloud Run Jobs for batch export, bulk re-rendering, or high-resolution long-running tasks. citeturn566776search1turn483849view4

---

# 26.24 What Step 26 must not do

Do not:

```txt
export unsaved dirty state without saving
mutate AiReconstructionDocument
mutate generated Fabric manifest template
run AI repair
silently downgrade layers
store signed URLs
claim vector/PDF editability without a validated vector pipeline
use client canvas export as official output
```

I’m closing the loop with the production-hardening layer: monitoring, cost discipline, evaluation datasets, incident handling, cleanup, and continuous quality loops.

# Step 27 — Operations, monitoring, cost controls, QA datasets, and production hardening

Step 27 is the operating system around the entire Magic Layers pipeline.

The locked rule:

```txt
A Magic Layers system is not production-ready until every job, asset, model call, render, repair, export, validation failure, and cost driver is observable, bounded, and replayable.
```

This step does **not** add new layer functionality.  
It makes the system safe to run at scale.

This is where you prevent the feature from becoming:

```txt
expensive
un-debuggable
untrusted
slow
fragile
unbounded
impossible to improve
```

Firestore cannot be treated as a blob store because Firestore documents have a maximum document size of 1 MiB, so all large artifacts must remain in Cloud Storage with Firestore storing pointers and summaries only. citeturn839414search0 Cloud Storage lifecycle rules can automatically delete or transition objects based on bucket lifecycle configuration, which is required for cost control on intermediate assets. citeturn839414search1

---

# 27.1 What Step 27 owns

Step 27 owns:

```txt
pipeline observability
structured logging
job trace IDs
step timing
model call accounting
asset storage accounting
Firestore write accounting
Cloud Run / worker metrics
error aggregation
dead-letter handling
cost ledger
lifecycle cleanup
QA dataset creation
golden test suite
regression testing
release gates
quality dashboards
incident playbooks
retention policy
privacy redaction
```

Step 27 does **not** own:

```txt
new AI reconstruction logic
editor feature logic
repair logic
export rendering logic
autosave implementation
Fabric object behavior
```

Step 27 surrounds all previous steps and makes them operable.

---

# 27.2 Non-negotiable production principle

Every pipeline run must be answerable.

For any job, you must be able to answer:

```txt
What input image was used?
Which route was selected?
Which models ran?
How long did each step take?
How much did each step cost?
Which assets were created?
Which validation gates passed or failed?
Which text layers were unsafe?
Which foreground candidates were accepted/rejected?
Which background repair engine ran?
Which export renderer ran?
Which user/worker created each artifact?
Can this job be replayed?
Can this job be deleted safely?
```

If you cannot answer those questions, the system is not production-grade.

---

# 27.3 Operational source of truth

Use these durable records:

```txt
aiLayerJobs/{jobId}
  high-level status, progress, pointers, error summary

assets/{assetId}
  GCS object index and retention metadata

observabilityEvents/{eventId}
  optional low-volume structured operational events

repairRequests/{repairRequestId}
  repair lifecycle

exportRequests/{exportId}
  export lifecycle

versions/{versionId}
  user-visible saved versions

GCS JSON reports
  complete immutable reports for every pipeline pass

Cloud Logging
  structured logs for workers/API

BigQuery
  long-term analytics/evaluation sink
```

Do not put large event arrays or raw manifests in Firestore.

Cloud Logging sinks can route matching log entries to supported destinations such as BigQuery, where routed logs arrive in small batches and can be queried later. citeturn711068search0turn711068search15

# 27.5 Structured logger

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/ops/structured-logger.ts
```

```ts
import type {
  MagicLayersOpsEvent,
  MagicLayersOpsEventType,
} from "./ops-event.types";

export function createMagicLayersLogger(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId?: string;
  jobId?: string;
  userId?: string;
  traceId?: string;
}) {
  return {
    info(
      eventType: MagicLayersOpsEventType,
      fields: Partial<MagicLayersOpsEvent>
    ) {
      writeLog({
        ...base(input, eventType),
        ...fields,
        severity: "info",
      });
    },

    warning(
      eventType: MagicLayersOpsEventType,
      fields: Partial<MagicLayersOpsEvent>
    ) {
      writeLog({
        ...base(input, eventType),
        ...fields,
        severity: "warning",
      });
    },

    error(
      eventType: MagicLayersOpsEventType,
      fields: Partial<MagicLayersOpsEvent>
    ) {
      writeLog({
        ...base(input, eventType),
        ...fields,
        severity: fields.severity ?? "error",
      });
    },
  };
}

function base(
  input: {
    workspaceId: string;
    designId?: string;
    jobId?: string;
    userId?: string;
    traceId?: string;
  },
  eventType: MagicLayersOpsEventType
): MagicLayersOpsEvent {
  return {
    schemaVersion: "magic-layers-ops-event.v1",

    eventId: `ops_${crypto.randomUUID()}`,

    eventType,

    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
    designId: input.designId,
    jobId: input.jobId,
    userId: input.userId,
    traceId: input.traceId,

    status: "completed",

    severity: "info",

    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}

function writeLog(event: MagicLayersOpsEvent) {
  /**
   * Cloud Logging parses JSON written to stdout/stderr in many runtimes.
   * Keep logs structured and avoid dumping raw manifests or user content.
   */
  const payload = redactOpsEvent(event);

  if (payload.severity === "error" || payload.severity === "critical") {
    console.error(JSON.stringify(payload));
  } else {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(payload));
  }
}

function redactOpsEvent(event: MagicLayersOpsEvent): MagicLayersOpsEvent {
  return {
    ...event,

    error: event.error
      ? {
          ...event.error,
          message: truncate(event.error.message, 800),
          stack: event.error.stack
            ? truncate(event.error.stack, 2000)
            : undefined,
        }
      : undefined,
  };
}

function truncate(value: string, max: number) {
  return value.length > max ? `${value.slice(0, max)}…` : value;
}
```

Cloud Monitoring supports user-defined metrics, including metrics based on log entries via Cloud Logging. citeturn839414search2turn839414search10

# 27.6 Step timing wrapper

Every pipeline step must run through one wrapper.

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/ops/measure-step.ts
```

```ts
import {
  createMagicLayersLogger,
} from "./structured-logger";

export async function measureMagicLayerStep<T>(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  jobId: string;
  userId?: string;
  traceId: string;

  step: string;

  run: () => Promise<T>;

  labels?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
}): Promise<T> {
  const logger = createMagicLayersLogger(input);

  const startedAt = Date.now();

  logger.info("job_step_started", {
    status: "started",
    step: input.step,
    labels: input.labels,
  });

  try {
    const result = await input.run();

    logger.info("job_step_completed", {
      status: "completed",
      step: input.step,
      metrics: {
        durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
      },
      labels: input.labels,
    });

    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error("job_step_failed", {
      status: "failed",
      step: input.step,
      metrics: {
        durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
      },
      error: {
        code: error instanceof Error ? error.name : "unknown_error",
        message:
          error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error",
        retryable: classifyRetryableError(error),
        stack: error instanceof Error ? error.stack : undefined,
      },
      labels: input.labels,
    });

    throw error;
  }
}

function classifyRetryableError(error: unknown) {
  const message =
    error instanceof Error ? error.message.toLowerCase() : "";

  return [
    "timeout",
    "temporarily",
    "rate limit",
    "unavailable",
    "deadline",
    "network",
  ].some((term) => message.includes(term));
}
```

Patch every worker step to use this wrapper.

# 27.8 Cost estimator

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/ops/cost-estimator.ts
```

```ts
export type CostEstimateInput = {
  modelInputTokens?: number;
  modelOutputTokens?: number;

  storageBytesWritten?: number;
  storageBytesRead?: number;

  firestoreReads?: number;
  firestoreWrites?: number;
  firestoreDeletes?: number;

  renderMs?: number;

  exportOutputBytes?: number;
};

export function estimateMagicLayersCostUsd(
  input: CostEstimateInput
): number {
  /**
   * Keep constants configurable by env/admin config.
   * These defaults should be overwritten from pricing config.
   */
  const modelInputPer1MTokens =
    numberFromEnv("COST_MODEL_INPUT_PER_1M_TOKENS_USD", 0);
  const modelOutputPer1MTokens =
    numberFromEnv("COST_MODEL_OUTPUT_PER_1M_TOKENS_USD", 0);
  const renderPerHour =
    numberFromEnv("COST_RENDER_WORKER_PER_HOUR_USD", 0);
  const storagePerGbMonth =
    numberFromEnv("COST_STORAGE_PER_GB_MONTH_USD", 0);

  const tokenCost =
    ((input.modelInputTokens ?? 0) / 1_000_000) *
      modelInputPer1MTokens +
    ((input.modelOutputTokens ?? 0) / 1_000_000) *
      modelOutputPer1MTokens;

  const renderCost =
    ((input.renderMs ?? 0) / 3_600_000) * renderPerHour;

  /**
   * Storage cost is rough because true storage is time-based.
   * This cost record is a directional write-time estimate.
   */
  const storageCost =
    ((input.storageBytesWritten ?? 0) / 1_000_000_000) *
    storagePerGbMonth;

  return roundUsd(tokenCost + renderCost + storageCost);
}

function numberFromEnv(name: string, fallback: number) {
  const value = process.env[name];

  if (!value) return fallback;

  const parsed = Number(value);

  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : fallback;
}

function roundUsd(value: number) {
  return Math.round(value * 1_000_000) / 1_000_000;
}
```

Do not hardcode live pricing into source code. Pricing changes.

# 27.10 Alert rules

Create alerts for:

```txt
job failure rate > 5% over 15 minutes

visual validation fail rate > 3% over 30 minutes

text safety fail rate > 1% over 30 minutes

median job duration > 2x rolling baseline

p95 Step 19 render duration > threshold

export failure rate > 5%

repair request failure rate > 5%

Cloud Run memory near limit

Cloud Tasks queue oldest task age > threshold

GCS asset write failures > 0

Firestore contention/conflict spike

daily estimated cost > budget threshold
```

Cloud Tasks queues support retry configuration such as max retry attempts and intervals between retries, so task retry behavior should be explicitly set rather than relying on uncontrolled failure loops. citeturn953089search18

---

# 27.11 Worker dead-letter handling

Every async worker queue needs a failure sink.

For Pub/Sub-backed workers:

```txt
use dead-letter topics
```

Pub/Sub can forward messages to a dead-letter topic after a configured number of delivery attempts when subscribers cannot acknowledge messages. citeturn953089search2

For Cloud Tasks-backed workers:

```txt
maxAttempts finite
maxRetryDuration finite
log final failure
mark job/request failed
```

Never allow infinite retries on:

```txt
model hallucination failure
bad input asset
schema validation failure
text safety failure
visual validation failure
```

Retry only transient infrastructure failures.

---

# 27.12 Retention policy

Retention must be different by artifact class.

```txt
original upload
  retain until design deleted

normalized image
  retain until design deleted

locked reference
  retain until design deleted

reconstruction documents
  retain until design deleted

fabric manifest templates
  retain until design deleted

autosave runtime snapshots
  retain latest N and 30 days

edit event assets
  retain 30–90 days

intermediate masks/crops
  retain 7–30 days unless sampled for QA

visual validation render/diff
  retain 30–90 days

text safety diagnostic crops
  retain 30 days or less

repair patches
  retain with version if repair was applied

export files
  retain according to product policy

raw model responses
  retain short-term only, redacted where possible
```

Cloud Storage lifecycle management applies rules to current and future objects in a bucket, so use it for automatic cleanup of temporary prefixes. citeturn839414search1

---

# 27.13 GCS lifecycle rules

Create lifecycle config per bucket/prefix.

Example:

```json
{
  "rule": [
    {
      "action": {
        "type": "Delete"
      },
      "condition": {
        "age": 30,
        "matchesPrefix": [
          "workspaces/"
        ],
        "matchesSuffix": [
          ".debug.png",
          ".raw-ocr.json",
          ".raw-response.json"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "action": {
        "type": "Delete"
      },
      "condition": {
        "age": 14,
        "matchesPrefix": [
          "tmp/",
          "staging/"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Use prefix/suffix carefully. Do not accidentally lifecycle-delete original uploads or reconstruction documents.

Cloud Storage Object Versioning can preserve deleted objects as noncurrent versions until explicitly removed, which is useful for high-value buckets but can increase storage if not paired with lifecycle policy. citeturn711068search1

```ts
  stratification: {
    byRoute: true,
    byCanvasType: true,
    byFailureCode: true,
    byModelVersion: true,
  },
} as const;
```

The QA loop must bias toward failures and review cases. Random pass sampling alone will not improve the system.

# 27.17 Regression runner

Create:

```txt
src/lib/magic-layers/qa/run-regression-suite.ts
```

```ts
export type RegressionSuiteResult = {
  suiteId: string;

  commitSha?: string;

  samplesRun: number;

  passed: number;

  failed: number;

  failures: {
    sampleId: string;
    reason: string;
    metrics?: Record<string, number>;
  }[];

  createdAt: number;
};

export async function runMagicLayersRegressionSuite(input: {
  suiteId: string;
  sampleIds: string[];
  pipelineVersion: string;
}): Promise<RegressionSuiteResult> {
  const failures: RegressionSuiteResult["failures"] = [];

  let passed = 0;

  for (const sampleId of input.sampleIds) {
    const result = await runSingleRegressionSample({
      sampleId,
      pipelineVersion: input.pipelineVersion,
    });

    if (result.passed) {
      passed++;
    } else {
      failures.push({
        sampleId,
        reason: result.reason,
        metrics: result.metrics,
      });
    }
  }

  return {
    suiteId: input.suiteId,
    commitSha: process.env.GITHUB_SHA,
    samplesRun: input.sampleIds.length,
    passed,
    failed: failures.length,
    failures,
    createdAt: Date.now(),
  };
}

async function runSingleRegressionSample(input: {
  sampleId: string;
  pipelineVersion: string;
}) {
  /**
   * Implementation:
   * - load golden sample
   * - run pipeline in isolated test workspace
   * - run Step 19 and Step 20
   * - compare against expected thresholds
   */
  throw new Error("regression_sample_runner_not_implemented");
}
```

Regression outputs should be stored as test artifacts, not mixed with customer production data.

# 27.21 Schema migration policy

Create:

```txt

```

```ts
export type MagicLayersMigration<TInput, TOutput> = {
  from: string;
  to: string;
  migrate: (input: TInput) => TOutput;
};

export const magicLayersMigrationRegistry: MagicLayersMigration<any, any>[] = [
  /**
   * Add migrations here.
   */
];

export function migrateMagicLayersDocument(input: {
  schemaVersion: string;
  document: unknown;
  targetSchemaVersion: string;
}) {
  let current = input.document;
  let currentVersion = input.schemaVersion;

  while (currentVersion !== input.targetSchemaVersion) {
    const migration = magicLayersMigrationRegistry.find(
      (item) => item.from === currentVersion
    );

    if (!migration) {
      throw new Error(
        `missing_magic_layers_migration:${currentVersion}->${input.targetSchemaVersion}`
      );
    }

    current = migration.migrate(current);
    currentVersion = migration.to;
  }

  return current;
}
```

# 27.22 Security hardening checklist

Enforce:

```txt
Firebase Auth on every user API
App Check on every user API
workspace authorization on every request
asset ownership checks
no raw signed URLs in durable JSON
no base64 blobs in durable JSON
Cloud Storage security rules deny direct canonical writes
server-only service account writes canonical assets
worker endpoints require internal authentication
repair/export workers validate request state
rate limits per workspace/user
```

Firebase App Check protects custom backends by requiring requests to include valid App Check tokens, while Firebase Authentication identifies the user; both are complementary and should be used together. citeturn839414search7turn839414search3

## ChatGPT Response 038

<!-- assistant_message_ids: d1ec2db1-39e4-4d84-8072-d5a5087edfd0 -->

Yes. Before implementation, there are several things I would lock down. These are not optional if you want this to survive production.

# 1. Do not start with AI models

Start with the **contract spine**, not decomposition.

The first working implementation should prove this path:

```txt
known test image
→ synthetic/manual observation bundle
→ scene resolver
→ reconstruction document
→ Fabric manifest template
→ runtime hydration
→ canvas.loadFromJSON
→ autosave
→ export
```

Only after this works should you plug in Gemini/OCR/SAM/LayerD/vectorization.

Reason: if you start with models first, every bug becomes ambiguous:

```txt
Is the mask wrong?
Is z-order wrong?
Is Fabric mapping wrong?
Is storage broken?
Is asset hydration broken?
Is the schema wrong?
Is validation wrong?
```

You need deterministic fixtures before nondeterministic AI.

---

# 2. Treat the schema as the product core

The real moat here is not “we call a model.”

The real core is:

```txt
flat image
→ auditable design scene graph
→ safe editor projection
→ repairable runtime state
```

So the strongest implementation order is:

```txt
schema
storage
job orchestration
asset writer
observation bundle
reconstruction document
Fabric manifest
runtime hydration
validation
then AI engines
```

If the schema is weak, everything after it becomes expensive chaos.

---

# 3. Keep these truths separate forever

Do not collapse these into one document:

```txt
AiReconstructionDocument
  what AI reconstructed

AiFabricManifestTemplate
  generated editor import package

FabricRuntimeJson
  current user-edited design

ExportOutput
  final disposable output file
```

This separation is what preserves:

```txt
auditability
repairability
autosave safety
versioning
debugging
legal/content safety
```

If you mutate reconstruction every time the user edits, you lose provenance.

---

# 4. Do not persist signed URLs anywhere durable

This is a common fatal mistake.

Durable JSON must store:

```txt
magic-asset://assetId
```

Runtime JSON may temporarily hydrate to:

```txt
https://signed-gcs-url
```

Before autosave:

```txt
strip signed URLs back to magic-asset://
```

This applies to:

```txt
Fabric manifest templates
autosave runtime JSON
versions
repair patches
exports
support bundles
```

Signed URLs are runtime transport only.

---

# 5. Firestore is pointer/state only

Never store large JSON in Firestore.

Firestore should hold:

```txt
status
progress
asset ids
revision
summary metrics
error codes
small counters
```

GCS should hold:

```txt
observation bundles
reconstruction documents
Fabric JSON
autosaves
versions
model reports
validation reports
diff images
repair patches
exports
```

If you violate this, you will hit cost, document-size, read-amplification, and hot-document problems.

---

# 6. Validation gates are not “nice to have”

The product should not say “done” when AI finishes.

It should say “done” only after:

```txt
visual render validation passes or marks needs_review
text safety passes or marks needs_review/fail
```

The key trust rule:

```txt
No editable text may silently change meaning.
```

If text is unsafe:

```txt
fail or downgrade to raster fallback through explicit repair
```

Never let Gemini or any LLM decide that altered visible text is “close enough.”

---

# 7. The first version should be raster-first, vector/text selective

For highest user trust, default to:

```txt
raster fidelity first
editable text only when safe
vector only when validated
clean background only when conservative
```

Do not chase maximum editability at the cost of visual corruption.

The correct product behavior is:

```txt
“This object is editable.”
“This object is raster fallback.”
“This layer needs review.”
“This text was kept as original pixels for safety.”
```

That is more trustworthy than pretending every element is perfectly reconstructed.

---

# 8. Background repair is dangerous

Background reconstruction must be treated as a hidden helper, not a creative feature.

Hard rule:

```txt
unmasked pixels must remain identical
```

Every repair engine output must be composited like:

```txt
outside mask = original pixels
inside mask = repaired pixels
```

Do not allow semantic/generative background repair by default. Add it later behind a flag and review UI.

---

# 9. Do not create Fabric.Group by default

Logical groups are useful.

Fabric groups are dangerous too early.

Day-one behavior should be:

```txt
logical group metadata
layer panel nesting
ActiveSelection for group select
no fabric.Group
```

Only create real `fabric.Group` after your editor fully supports:

```txt
child editing
ungroup
undo/redo
serialization
z-order inside group
selection targeting
```

Otherwise grouping will break editability.

---

# 10. Build a replay harness before real users

Every job should be replayable from stored artifacts.

You need this immediately:

```txt
jobId
→ load input assets
→ load observation bundle
→ rerun scene resolver
→ rerun Fabric generation
→ rerun visual validator
→ compare outputs
```

Without replay, debugging AI failures becomes guesswork.

Also create 10–20 golden fixtures before implementation goes far:

```txt
simple poster
text-heavy menu
photo-heavy banner
logo/vector-like graphic
AI-generated poster
tiny text case
bad OCR case
complex background case
```

Each fixture should have expected thresholds:

```txt
min visual score
text exactness required
max layer count
expected route
```

---

# 11. Implement idempotency from day one

Every worker step must be safe to retry.

Use stable IDs where possible:

```txt
asset_${jobId}_${step}_${purpose}
```

And write assets with create-only/precondition behavior.

Every step should handle:

```txt
already completed
asset already exists
job cancelled
job failed
worker retried
partial previous output
```

Cloud workers will retry. Assume duplicate execution.

---

# 12. Cloud Run is the right heavy-worker default

For this pipeline, avoid putting heavy work inside normal Next.js routes.

Use:

```txt
Next.js API
  auth, request creation, status, signed URL endpoints

Cloud Run workers
  AI pipeline
  Python/OpenCV/SAM/LayerD
  Playwright render validation
  exports
  repair jobs
```

Firebase Functions can work for small orchestration, but image processing, Playwright, Python, GPU-adjacent work, and long exports belong in Cloud Run-style workers.

---

# 13. Model outputs must never be trusted directly

Every AI/model output must become:

```txt
observation
candidate
validated candidate
final layer
```

Never:

```txt
model output → Fabric object directly
```

That one rule prevents most catastrophic behavior.

For every model output, store:

```txt
source
model version
prompt version
confidence
bbox/mask/path/text
failure reasons
fallback
validation metrics
```

---

# 14. Repair is part of the product, not an edge case

A feature like this will always produce imperfect layers.

So the user experience must include:

```txt
restore fallback
downgrade text to raster
remask object
regenerate background
replace image
revectorize
open diagnostics
```

If you ship only “generate layers” without repair, the product will feel brittle.

---

# 15. Do not overfit to Canva’s promise

The technically correct claim is not:

```txt
“Recover original layers.”
```

The correct claim is:

```txt
“Convert a flat image into a safe, editable approximation with fallbacks.”
```

The first claim is mathematically impossible in many cases.

The second claim is defensible.

Build the product around:

```txt
faithful first render
editable where safe
fallback where uncertain
review where risky
repair where needed
```

---

# 16. Implementation spine I would use

Not “phases,” but dependency order:

```txt
1. Schema + asset writer + storage paths
2. Job orchestration + idempotent step runner
3. Synthetic observation bundle fixture
4. Scene resolver
5. Fabric generator
6. Runtime hydration + editor boot
7. Layer panel + metadata preservation
8. Autosave/versioning
9. Visual validator
10. Text safety validator
11. Raster fallback repair
12. Export worker
13. Real AI engines one by one
```

This still gives the full architecture from day one, but prevents AI uncertainty from hiding infrastructure bugs.

---

# 17. The first real AI target should be narrow

Do not start by supporting every poster.

Start with one controlled input class:

```txt
graphic poster / social banner
single page
reasonable resolution
English text first
no extreme tiny text
max 30 final layers
raster-first output
```

Then expand.

A controlled first target lets you tune:

```txt
thresholds
cost
latency
repair UX
validation gates
fallback behavior
```

without drowning in edge cases.

---

# 18. Keep latency expectations honest

A high-quality run may involve:

```txt
normalization
routing
OCR
segmentation
matting
inpainting
vectorization
Fabric generation
browser render validation
text safety OCR
```

That is not an instant feature.

So design UX around:

```txt
job queued
progress
preview when ready
open editor when safe enough
needs review state
repair actions
```

Do not block the whole product on synchronous generation.

---

# 19. Define “ready” precisely

Use this status logic:

```txt
failed
  unsafe or unusable automatic result

needs_review
  usable editor state, but one or more validations are weak

ready
  visual validation passed
  text safety passed
  no critical warnings

draft
  user has edited after generation/autosave
```

Do not call a design ready just because Fabric JSON exists.

---

# 20. My strongest caution

The biggest risk is not that the AI fails.

The biggest risk is that the system **pretends success when it should expose uncertainty**.

This feature will be trusted only if users feel:

```txt
the first render matches
text was not changed
fallbacks are available
bad layers are repairable
AI uncertainty is visible
exports are consistent
```

Optimize for trust, not magic.

---

# Final pre-implementation decision

Before writing production code, lock these six contracts:

```txt
AiAssetRef
AiObservationBundle
AiReconstructionDocument
AiFabricManifestTemplate
FabricRuntimeJson
MagicRepairPatch
```

Then implement one synthetic end-to-end path.

Once that path works, plug in the first real AI engine.

That is the cleanest way to build this without creating an unmaintainable AI-canvas system.

# The main recommendation

Add a **Prompt-to-Design Generation Layer** before Step 0.

Call it:

```txt
Generation Source System
```

It becomes another source input type, same as uploaded PNG/JPG.

Current source types:

```txt
user_upload_image
template_image
ai_generated_image
```

New flow:

```txt
User prompt
→ GenerationJob
→ GeneratedImageCandidate[]
→ Selected generated image
→ Magic Layers pipeline Step 0–27
```

But critically, the generated image should carry **intent metadata** into the layer pipeline.

Without intent metadata, your pipeline sees only pixels.

With intent metadata, your pipeline knows:

```txt
intended headline
intended CTA
intended brand name
intended price/date/address
canvas preset
style
expected subject
expected text regions
expected background behavior
generation model
prompt version
```

That makes OCR, text safety, grouping, z-order, and scene resolution much more accurate.

---

# Do not use Imagen as the strategic default

Given your stack is Firebase + Google AI, use Gemini Image / Nano Banana models as the forward path.

Firebase’s AI Logic docs state that Imagen models are deprecated and will shut down on June 24, 2026, and recommend migrating to Gemini Image / Nano Banana models. citeturn699303view1

For server-side production generation, default model strategy should be:

```txt
gemini-3.1-flash-image
  default prompt-to-poster/banner generator
  good speed/cost balance

gemini-3-pro-image
  use for premium/pro layouts, complex instructions, better text-heavy outputs

gemini-2.5-flash-image
  fallback/high-volume low-latency option if supported in your chosen access path
```

Google’s Gemini image docs describe Nano Banana 2 as `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, Nano Banana Pro as `gemini-3-pro-image`, and Nano Banana as `gemini-2.5-flash-image`. citeturn505808view1

Also use Remote Config / server-side model registry so you can switch model versions without redeploying the app. Firebase docs explicitly recommend Remote Config for changing model/version behavior without shipping a new app version. citeturn699303view1

# The biggest product decision: image-first vs design-first

You need two generation modes.

## Mode A — Image-first generation

```txt
prompt
→ generated flat poster/banner image
→ run full Magic Layers decomposition
→ editable approximation
```

This is simple and impressive, but lower control.

Use when:

```txt
user wants a creative poster
text is minimal
exact text is not business-critical
design is mostly visual
```

Risk:

```txt
AI-rendered text may be wrong
layout may be hard to decompose
background/object boundaries may be ambiguous
```

## Mode B — Design-first generation

```txt
prompt
→ structured design intent
→ generate background/visual without critical text
→ create Fabric text/vector/raster layers directly
→ optional decomposition only for generated visual elements
```

This is the better default for posters, banners, ads, menus, offers, and SMB creative.

Use when:

```txt
headline matters
price/date/address matters
brand name matters
CTA matters
editable text matters
```

Recommended default:

```txt
Design-first for business/marketing outputs.
Image-first for artistic/creative outputs.
```

This is the key difference between a toy generator and an editor-grade design system.

Do not change the 0–27 pipeline. Add this upstream.

# G0 — Generation request intake

Do not expose only one textarea internally.

UI can be simple, but backend should receive structured fields.

```ts

  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  prompt: string;

  designType:
    | "poster"
    | "banner"
    | "social_post"

    | "print_a4"
    | "custom";

    headline?: string;
    subtitle?: string;
```

# G1 — Prompt compiler

Use a text Gemini model to convert freeform prompt into a **DesignIntentManifest**.

Example:

```ts
type DesignIntentManifest = {
  schemaVersion: "design-intent.v1";

  promptRaw: string;

  promptNormalized: string;

  designType: string;

  canvas: {
    width: number;
    height: number;
    aspectRatio: string;
  };

  intendedText: {
    id: string;

    role:
      | "headline"
      | "subtitle"
      | "cta"
      | "price"
      | "date"
      | "business_name"
      | "address"
      | "disclaimer";

    text: string;

    importance:
      | "critical"
      | "normal"
      | "decorative";

    mustBeEditable: boolean;

    mustMatchExactly: boolean;
  }[];

  visualIntent: {
    subject?: string;
    background?: string;
    style?: string;
    mood?: string;
    colorPalette?: string[];
    composition?: string;
  };

  constraints: {
    avoidTinyText: boolean;
    avoidExtraText: boolean;
    noFakeLogos: boolean;
    noWatermarkText: boolean;
    leaveTextSafeAreas: boolean;
  };

  generationMode:
    | "design_first"
    | "image_first";
};
```

This manifest becomes a **first-class pipeline artifact**.

# G2 — Generation strategy selector

Decision logic:

```txt
if intendedText has critical fields
  use design_first

if prompt asks for menu, sale banner, ad, event poster, business flyer
  use design_first

if prompt asks for artistic poster with no exact text
  use image_first

if user asks for “editable text”
  use design_first

if user asks for complex typography as visual art
  image_first, but mark text as raster-art unless validated
```

Model selection:

```txt
default:
  gemini-3.1-flash-image

premium / complex / text-heavy:
  gemini-3-pro-image

high-volume / lower cost:
  gemini-2.5-flash-image where supported
```

Google’s docs say Nano Banana 2 is the go-to balanced image generation model, Nano Banana Pro is for professional asset production and complex instructions, and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image is optimized for speed/efficiency. citeturn505808view0

---

# G3 — Generation prompt builder

For design-first mode, the generation prompt should usually say:

```txt
Create only the background and visual composition.
Do not render text, letters, logos, words, numbers, watermarks, labels, signs, or typography.
Leave clean negative space for the headline and CTA.
```

Then your system creates Fabric text layers from `DesignIntentManifest.intendedText`.

This gives:

```txt
better text safety
better editability
cleaner Fabric output
lower OCR dependence
less need to de-render AI text
```

For image-first mode, where text is allowed, the prompt should include:

```txt
Render the exact following text only:
"SUMMER SALE"
"50% OFF"
"No extra text, no fake words, no watermark, no gibberish."
```

But image-first text must be validated before entering the editor.

# Important limitation: no transparent generation

Google’s image generation docs state the model does not support transparent background generation. citeturn505808view1

So do not build the generator UX around:

```txt
transparent stickers
transparent logos
transparent cutouts
```

Instead:

```txt
generate on white/solid background
→ remove background later using mask/matting pipeline
```

For assets/icons/stickers:

```txt
prompt white background
→ Step 9/11/13 extracts asset
→ Step 12 vectorizes if clean
```

# G4 — Image generation worker

Do not generate images directly from the browser for production.

Use:

```txt
Next.js API
→ create GenerationJob doc
→ Cloud Run worker
→ Google AI model call
→ store candidates in GCS
```

Reason:

```txt
cost control
rate limiting
abuse prevention
prompt logging/redaction
model version control
retry/idempotency
candidate validation
```

Firebase AI Logic can be useful, but production generation for your system should be server-orchestrated.

# G5 — Store multiple candidates

The image model may return good/bad variation quality.

Store candidates:

```ts
type GeneratedImageCandidate = {
  id: string;

  generationJobId: string;

  index: number;

  imageAssetId: string;

  width: number;
  height: number;

  model: {
    provider: "google";
    modelName: string;
    modelVersion?: string;
    promptVersion: string;

  prompt: {
    rawPrompt: string;
    compiledPrompt: string;
    negativePrompt?: string;

  validation: {
    decoded: boolean;
    aspectRatioMatched: boolean;
    textValidationLevel?: "pass" | "needs_review" | "fail";
    hasUnexpectedText?: boolean;
    visualQualityScore?: number;
  };

  selected: boolean;

  createdAt: number;
};
```

User can choose one candidate, or your system can auto-select the safest one.

# G6 — Generation validation before decomposition

Before running Magic Layers, validate the generated image.

Checks:

```txt
image decodes
dimensions match requested canvas/aspect ratio
no model error/refusal
no unexpected text in design-first mode
critical text matches intended text in image-first mode
image is not blank
image is not mostly noise
content policy pass
```

For text-heavy prompts:

```txt
OCR generated image
compare against DesignIntentManifest.intendedText
if mismatch:
  regenerate
  or switch to design_first
  or mark candidate failed
```

Do not send a text-broken generated poster into the layer pipeline and hope OCR fixes it.

```txt
clean negative space for text
```

# Critical integration with Step 20 text safety

For generated designs, Step 20 should compare editable text against:

```txt
intended_text observations
```

not only OCR.

Text safety priority:

```txt
1. intended_text from prompt/compiler
2. accepted text_candidate original OCR
3. layer.text.originalValue
4. layer.text.value
```

This is important.

If user prompted:

```txt
Create a sale poster saying "50% OFF"
```

and the generated image rendered:

```txt
"60% OFF"
```

you should not treat the generated pixel text as truth. The intended text is truth.

Better behavior:

```txt
design_first:
  generated image has no text
  Fabric text layer says "50% OFF"
  validation passes

image_first:
  generated image says "60% OFF"
  OCR mismatch
  candidate fails before decomposition
```

---

# Preferred generation strategy for editable posters

For anything business-like, use this architecture:

```txt
Prompt
→ structured intent
→ generate text-free background/visual
→ create native Fabric text layers
→ optionally generate decorative assets
→ visual validation
→ autosave/export
```

This may bypass a lot of layer decomposition because you already know the layers.

The best version is not:

```txt
AI generates flat poster
→ AI tries to recover layers
```

The best version is:

```txt
AI generates design intent and visual assets
→ system constructs layers directly
→ decomposition fills gaps only when needed
```

That is more controllable, cheaper, and safer.

No separate editor stack.

# Final position

This generator system should exist, but only if it is designed as a **design-source system**, not just an image generator.

The high-trust version is:

```txt
prompt intent is preserved
critical text is structured
generated image is validated
generated source enters same pipeline
text safety uses intended text
Fabric output uses same editor/autosave/export stack
```

The weak version is:

```txt
prompt → flat AI image → decompose blindly
```

That will look impressive in demos but fail on real business posters, menus, prices, dates, CTAs, and brand names.

The default should be:

```txt

= structured intent
+ generated visual/background
+ native Fabric text
+ optional decomposition
+ same validation gates
```

That makes the generator compatible with the full 0–27 Magic Layers architecture instead of becoming a second system you have to maintain.

# The only real difference between upload and generated source

## 1. User-uploaded image

The system knows only pixels.

```txt
user upload
→ normalize
→ route
→ OCR / segmentation / decomposition
→ infer everything from image
```

Text truth source:

```txt
OCR from uploaded image
```

So if the image says:

```txt
50% OFF
```

then Step 20 validates editable text against OCR/source pixels.

---

## 2. AI-generated flat image

The system knows:

```txt
pixels
+ prompt
+ generation metadata
+ intended text if user supplied any
```

Flow:

```txt
prompt
→ generated flat image
→ selected candidate
→ normalize
→ seed generation_intent observations
→ run normal Magic Layers pipeline
```

Text truth source:

```txt
intended_text from prompt if present
else OCR from generated image
```

Important example:

```txt
Prompt intended: "50% OFF"
Generated pixels: "60% OFF"
```

The system should **not** treat “60% OFF” as truth. It should mark the generated candidate unsafe or needs review.

---

## 3. AI-generated design

This is the best long-term path.

The system knows:

```txt
intended design structure
critical text
canvas preset
brand colors
style intent
generated visual assets
```

Flow:

```txt
prompt
→ design intent manifest
→ generate background/visual
→ create native text layers directly
→ optionally run decomposition for generated visuals
→ same Fabric editor
```

Text truth source:

```txt
DesignIntentManifest.intendedText
```

This is superior for posters, banners, ads, flyers, menus, offers, event graphics, and SMB marketing assets.

```txt
user-upload-source-adapter.ts
generated-flat-image-source-adapter.ts
generated-design-source-adapter.ts
source-package.types.ts
create-source-package.ts
register-source-package.ts
```

Each adapter must output the same `MagicSourcePackage`.

---

# Adapter 1 — User upload source

```ts
export async function createUserUploadSourcePackage(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  uploadAssetId: string;
}) {
  const normalized = await normalizeSourceImage({
    assetId: input.uploadAssetId,
  });

  return {
    sourceKind: "user_upload",

    originalAssetId: input.uploadAssetId,
    normalizedAssetId: normalized.normalizedAssetId,
    editorReferenceAssetId: normalized.editorReferenceAssetId,

    provenance: {
      createdBy: "user_upload",
      uploadId: input.uploadAssetId,
    },

    seedObservations: [],
  } satisfies Partial<MagicSourcePackage>;
}
```

No generation intent. The pipeline infers everything from pixels.

---

# Adapter 2 — AI-generated flat image source

```ts
export async function createGeneratedFlatImageSourcePackage(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  generationJobId: string;
  generationCandidateId: string;

  generatedImageAssetId: string;

  designIntentManifestAssetId?: string;
}) {
  const normalized = await normalizeSourceImage({
    assetId: input.generatedImageAssetId,
  });

  const seedObservations = await createGenerationSeedObservations({
    generationJobId: input.generationJobId,
    generationCandidateId: input.generationCandidateId,
    designIntentManifestAssetId: input.designIntentManifestAssetId,
    mode: "image_first",
  });

  return {
    sourceKind: "ai_generated_flat_image",

    originalAssetId: input.generatedImageAssetId,
    normalizedAssetId: normalized.normalizedAssetId,
    editorReferenceAssetId: normalized.editorReferenceAssetId,

    designIntentManifestAssetId:
      input.designIntentManifestAssetId,

    provenance: {
      createdBy: "google_ai_generation",
      generationJobId: input.generationJobId,
      generationCandidateId: input.generationCandidateId,
      designIntentManifestAssetId:
        input.designIntentManifestAssetId,
    },

    seedObservations,
  } satisfies Partial<MagicSourcePackage>;
}
```

This path still runs the full decomposition pipeline, but with better prior knowledge.

---

# Adapter 3 — AI-generated design source

This is the strongest path.

```ts
export async function createGeneratedDesignSourcePackage(input: {
  workspaceId: string;
  designId: string;
  userId: string;

  generationJobId: string;
  generationCandidateId: string;

  generatedBackgroundAssetId: string;

  designIntentManifestAssetId: string;
}) {
  const normalized = await normalizeSourceImage({
    assetId: input.generatedBackgroundAssetId,
  });

  const seedObservations =
    await createDesignFirstSeedObservations({
      generationJobId: input.generationJobId,
      generationCandidateId: input.generationCandidateId,
      designIntentManifestAssetId:
        input.designIntentManifestAssetId,
      normalizedAssetId: normalized.normalizedAssetId,
    });

  return {
    sourceKind: "ai_generated_design",

    originalAssetId: input.generatedBackgroundAssetId,
    normalizedAssetId: normalized.normalizedAssetId,
    editorReferenceAssetId: normalized.editorReferenceAssetId,

    designIntentManifestAssetId:
      input.designIntentManifestAssetId,

    provenance: {
      createdBy: "google_ai_generation",
      generationJobId: input.generationJobId,
      generationCandidateId: input.generationCandidateId,
      designIntentManifestAssetId:
        input.designIntentManifestAssetId,
    },

    seedObservations,
  } satisfies Partial<MagicSourcePackage>;
}
```

For design-first generated designs, you can seed:

```txt
background_candidate
intended_text
layout
palette
z_order
group_candidate
```

That means the scene resolver can create editable text directly without depending on OCR.

# Critical text truth logic

Patch Step 20 expected-text resolver.

Current logic:

```txt
text_candidate
→ layer.text.originalValue
→ layer.text.value
```

New logic:

```txt
intended_text observation
→ text_candidate
→ layer.text.originalValue
→ layer.text.value
```

Priority:

```txt
1. intended_text if sourceKind is AI-generated and text is critical
2. accepted text_candidate OCR
3. layer.text.originalValue
4. layer.text.value
```

This prevents the generated image model from becoming the truth source for prices, dates, names, CTAs, addresses, and offers.

---

# Generated design text rule

For `ai_generated_design`, critical text should be created as **native text layers**, not recovered from image pixels.

Correct:

```txt
prompt says:
  headline = "Grand Opening"
  CTA = "Book Now"

system creates:
  fabric.Textbox("Grand Opening")
  fabric.Textbox("Book Now")
```

Wrong:

```txt
image model renders text inside flat image
→ OCR tries to recover it
→ text safety tries to validate it
```

For business designs, do not outsource critical typography to the image model unless the user explicitly asks for image-only artwork.

---

# Source kind behavior table

| Source kind | Pixel source | Text truth | Pipeline behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_upload` | uploaded image | OCR/source pixels | full reconstruction |
| `ai_generated_flat_image` | generated image | intended text if provided, else OCR | full reconstruction + generation priors |
| `ai_generated_design` | generated background/visual | intended text manifest | seeded reconstruction, less OCR reliance |

# UX implication

The user-facing product can have two entry points:

```txt
Upload image
Generate design
```

But both end at:

```txt
Editable Magic Layers editor
```

Internally:

```txt
Upload image
→ UserUploadSourceAdapter
→ Magic Layers pipeline

Generate design
→ GenerationJob
→ GeneratedSourceAdapter
→ Magic Layers pipeline
```

Same editor. Same autosave. Same repair. Same export.

---

# Strong recommendation for generation default

For SMB/poster/banner use cases, default to:

```txt
ai_generated_design
```

not:

```txt
ai_generated_flat_image
```

Meaning:

```txt
generate visual/background
create important text as Fabric text
create shapes/vectors directly where possible
use decomposition only for generated visual pixels
```

This gives:

```txt
higher text safety
better editability
lower OCR dependence
cleaner layers
less repair burden
```

Use flat image generation only for:

```txt
artistic posters
image-only compositions
moodboards
non-critical typography
creative exploration
```

---

# Implementation order adjustment

Before Step 0, add:

```txt
S0. Source package abstraction
S1. User upload source adapter
S2. Generation job schema
S3. Generated image source adapter
S4. Generated design source adapter
S5. Seed observations from generation intent
```

Then run the same 0–27 pipeline.

Do not build the generator after the pipeline as a separate feature. Build source abstraction first so both paths are first-class.

---

# Final architecture

```txt
                 ┌────────────────────┐
                 │ User uploaded image │
                 └─────────┬──────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                 UserUploadSourceAdapter
                           │
                           ▼
┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────┐
│ Text prompt  │──▶│ GenerationJob         │
└──────────────┘   │ design intent + image │
                   └─────────┬────────────┘
                             │
              ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
              ▼                             ▼
 GeneratedFlatImageSourceAdapter   GeneratedDesignSourceAdapter
              │                             │
              └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                             ▼
                    MagicSourcePackage
                             │

                    ObservationBundle
                             │
                             ▼
                  Magic Layers Step 0–27
                             │

                    Fabric editor runtime
                             │
```

That is the correct structure.

Support both uploaded images and generated images, but unify them at the source-package boundary. Only the source adapter differs. Everything after that should be one platform.

## ChatGPT Response 041

<!-- assistant_message_ids: 518d8ffa-9eec-455c-883d-74e36c749f31 -->

Yes. There are a few things I would still lock before implementation. Most are not new features; they are constraints that prevent this from becoming an unstable AI-canvas system.

# 1. Define the product promise very carefully

Do not promise:

```txt
“Recover original Canva/PSD layers.”
```

Promise:

```txt
“Turn flat images or generated designs into a safe editable approximation with fallbacks.”
```

This matters legally, technically, and UX-wise. Original layers are not recoverable with certainty from flattened pixels. The product should be judged on:

```txt
first render fidelity
text preservation
safe editability
fallback availability
repairability
```

not on “perfect original layer recovery.”

---

# 2. Add an unsupported-result path

Some inputs should not become Magic Layers.

Examples:

```txt
dense documents
screenshots with tiny UI text
complex collages
low-resolution posters
watermarked images
overcompressed JPEGs
NSFW/unsafe content
highly ambiguous AI art
```

For these, the correct output is:

```txt
flat image opened as locked/reference/background
+ maybe simple crop/edit tools
+ “Magic Layers could not safely reconstruct this”
```

Not:

```txt
bad layers pretending to be editable
```

A refusal/fallback path is part of quality.

---

# 3. Treat text as sacred content

For this product, text is not decoration.

Text can be:

```txt
price
date
address
phone number
menu item
business name
CTA
legal disclaimer
offer terms
```

That means text safety must have a higher trust standard than visual similarity.

The hierarchy should be:

```txt
user-provided structured text
> generation intended text
> trusted OCR from source image
> layer text
> model guess
```

A model guess should never become truth.

This is especially important for generated posters/banners. For business designs, exact text should be created as Fabric text from structured intent, not rendered into the generated image and recovered later.

---

# 4. Font licensing is a real product constraint

We have discussed font matching, but the licensing side matters.

You need a controlled font catalog:

```txt
licensed fonts only
known web/render availability
same fonts in editor and renderer
fallback font rules
font confidence metadata
```

Do not let the system claim exact font recovery unless the font is actually available and licensed.

Practical rule:

```txt
fontFamily = best licensed match
fontConfidence = explicit
fallback raster crop = always available
```

This avoids a class of invisible production failures where the editor looks fine on one machine and exports differently on another.

---

# 5. The renderer is a security boundary

Your server renderer will load user-edited Fabric JSON.

Treat FabricRuntimeJson as untrusted input.

Before rendering/exporting, enforce:

```txt
allowlisted Fabric object types
allowlisted properties
no external image URLs
no javascript/data URLs
no unknown custom classes
no arbitrary SVG import
no remote fonts from user input
no huge dimensions
no huge object counts
no base64 blobs
```

Only hydrate:

```txt
magic-asset://assetId
```

to signed URLs for assets that belong to the same workspace/design.

This is one of the most important hardening points. The render worker should never become a browser that loads arbitrary user-controlled URLs or SVG payloads.

---

# 6. Do not let SVG become a Trojan horse

SVG is useful, but risky.

SVG can contain:

```txt
external references
embedded images
unexpected styles
huge path payloads
potential sanitizer issues
```

So for day one:

```txt
Do not import arbitrary SVG into Fabric runtime from user/model output.
Do not accept SVG-only vector candidates as editable unless parsed and sanitized.
Do not export SVG as canonical.
```

Use SVG as:

```txt
candidate artifact
debug artifact
best-effort export
```

not as trusted design truth.

---

# 7. Generated design should be design-first by default

For the generator, the default should not be:

```txt
prompt → flat image → decompose
```

The better default is:

```txt
prompt → structured design intent
→ generate visual/background
→ create Fabric text layers directly
→ run decomposition only where needed
```

This gives:

```txt
better editable text
lower OCR dependency
better text safety
cleaner layer structure
lower repair burden
```

Use flat AI image generation mainly for:

```txt
artistic posters
visual inspiration
non-critical text
image-only artwork
```

For SMB posters, banners, menus, flyers, and offers, design-first is the stronger architecture.

---

# 8. Brand assets must become canonical inputs

If this system is connected to business/public truth infrastructure, then brand data should not be random per design.

You want:

```txt
business name
logo
brand colors
approved fonts
menu items
hours
address
phone
website
offers
```

as structured inputs.

Then generated designs become an output of business truth, not arbitrary creative blobs.

This is strategically important. It turns the generator from:

```txt
generic Canva-like image tool
```

into:

```txt
business truth → publishable creative surfaces
```

That is a stronger long-term position.

---

# 9. Correction data is the compounding asset

When a user fixes a layer, do not only save the final Fabric state.

Also capture structured correction signals:

```txt
OCR text was wrong
font match was wrong
mask included background
background repair failed
vectorization too complex
z-order wrong
grouping wrong
user restored fallback
user remasked object
user replaced image
```

This becomes the dataset that improves:

```txt
routing
OCR thresholds
mask selection
vector acceptance
background repair
grouping
scene resolution
repair defaults
```

The correction loop is more valuable than raw model output.

---

# 10. You need a “flat-safe mode”

There should be a mode where the system outputs:

```txt
locked reference
editable text overlays if safe
simple background
minimal objects
```

rather than attempting full decomposition.

Use this when confidence is low.

This mode protects the product from bad AI outputs while still giving users value.

Example:

```txt
uploaded poster
OCR detects clear headline and CTA
segmentation is weak
→ keep original image as background
→ place editable text layers on top only if safe
→ mark as partial Magic Layers
```

This is better than noisy 40-layer garbage.

---

# 11. Browser memory budgets must be explicit

Fabric editors can degrade quickly when you have:

```txt
large PNG layers
many transparent cutouts
huge paths
large shadows
multiple 4K assets
high object count
mobile devices
```

Set hard budgets:

```txt
max final layers
max editor image long edge
max vector path count
max total editor asset bytes
max canvas pixels
max active object count
max history snapshots
```

When exceeded:

```txt
downgrade to raster fallback
merge decorations
hide advanced editability
show performance warning
```

Do not wait for the browser to fail.

---

# 12. Build a deterministic “known input” harness first

Before plugging in Google AI models, build fixtures that manually create:

```txt
observation bundle
reconstruction document
Fabric manifest
runtime canvas
autosave
export
validation
```

This gives you known-good outputs.

Then when AI is introduced, failures are isolated to AI/model steps, not storage/schema/Fabric/rendering.

This is the single most practical implementation advice.

---

# 13. Use one editor runtime, not separate runtimes

Both uploaded images and generated designs must land in the same editor state:

```txt
FabricRuntimeJson
```

Do not create:

```txt
generated-design editor
uploaded-image editor
template editor
```

One runtime means one:

```txt
layer panel
autosave
repair system
export system
versioning system
renderer
```

Source adapters differ. Everything after source package should be unified.

---

# 14. Add kill switches from day one

Feature flags should exist for:

```txt
Gemini image generation
design-first generation
flat-image generation
semantic background repair
text conversion to editable
vector repair
SVG export
replace_object repair patches
large-canvas export
```

If text safety failures spike or exports break, you need to disable risky paths without redeploying the whole app.

---

# 15. Separate “completed” from “ready”

A job can complete but still produce a design that needs review.

Use this status logic:

```txt
completed + ready
  visual passed
  text safety passed
  no critical warnings

completed + needs_review
  usable editor state
  one or more weak validations

failed
  unsafe or unusable automatic result
```

Do not treat every completed pipeline as ready.

This will prevent customer trust damage.

---

# 16. Avoid becoming a generic design tool too early

This is a strategic warning.

If this is connected to your broader SMB infrastructure direction, the generator should not become:

```txt
general-purpose AI art/design sandbox
```

It should be oriented around:

```txt
business-publishable creative outputs
menus
offers
announcements
event posters
hours updates
local ads
reputation/social graphics
discovery surfaces
```

That keeps it tied to business truth and distribution, not generic creativity.

The surface can look simple, but the system underneath should be business-data-aware.

---

# 17. Human review is not optional long-term

For production hardening, you need an internal review tool.

It should show:

```txt
original/source image
rendered reconstruction
diff heatmap
text safety report
layer panel
accepted/rejected candidates
repair history
export result
human labels
```

This is how you tune thresholds and improve model decisions.

Without human review, you will overfit to anecdotal failures.

---

# 18. You need a policy layer before generation

For prompt generation, add policy checks before model calls:

```txt
unsafe content
trademark/logo misuse
fake documents
medical/legal/financial claims
political persuasion if relevant
adult content
violent content
impersonation
watermark requests
copyrighted character/style issues depending on your policy
```

Even if the model has safety filters, your product still needs its own policy layer because you own the UX, logs, retries, and exports.

---

# 19. Prompt injection is less important than prompt ambiguity

A user saying:

```txt
ignore previous instructions
```

is not the main risk.

The main risk is ambiguous prompts:

```txt
make a sale poster
```

without structured truth for:

```txt
sale amount
business name
CTA
valid dates
address
```

So the prompt compiler should convert ambiguity into structured fields or ask the UI to collect them.

For business outputs, exact fields beat clever prompts.

---

# 20. The highest leverage product primitive is “Business Creative Source Package”

For generated and uploaded designs, define one object:

```txt
BusinessCreativeSourcePackage
```

It contains:

```txt
source image
source kind
business truth inputs
generation intent
brand inputs
prompt
model provenance
seed observations
```

This object is the bridge between:

```txt
MenuList/business truth
AI generation
Magic Layers reconstruction
Fabric editor
exports/distribution
```

That abstraction will age well.

---

# 21. Minimal first implementation I would trust

The first working build should support:

```txt
user upload image
AI generated design-first image/background
source package abstraction
raster-first reconstruction
native editable intended text
locked reference
clean background fallback
Fabric editor
layer panel
autosave
export PNG
visual validation
text safety
restore fallback
```

Do not start with:

```txt
PSD export
SVG export
real Fabric groups
advanced vector editing
multi-language OCR
transparent image generation
semantic background hallucination
full repair automation
```

Those can come later without changing the spine.

---

# 22. One sentence architecture

The correct system is:

```txt
Business or image source → source package → observations → audited reconstruction → Fabric runtime → validated editor state → repairable/exportable output.
```

Everything should serve that chain.

---

# Final caution

The most dangerous failure mode is not technical inability.

The dangerous failure mode is building an impressive demo that:

```txt
silently changes text
generates untraceable assets
stores expired URLs
exports from unsaved browser state
creates bad layers with no fallback
has no repair path
has no cost limits
has no replay/debug system
```

Avoid those, and the system can become durable infrastructure rather than a fragile AI feature.
